tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/attribuly) A free plan that covers the first $1,000 of recovered email revenue, then Capture at $450 a month and Recapture at $500. Rating 4.8 from 154 reviews. Note the shape: the free tier is metered on recovered revenue rather than on time, so it ends when the tool starts working.
tools.honest_knock: This is the most expensive app in its category on the Shopify store by a wide margin, and the jump is not gradual — free to $450 a month with nothing in between. It is also an add-on rather than a replacement: the pitch is explicitly that it recovers carts “Klaviyo misses” and syncs identity signals back into Klaviyo, so you are paying for this on top of an email platform you already pay for. Work out what $450 a month needs to recover before it breaks even, and compare that against simply improving the flows you already have.
tools.best_for: stores already running Klaviyo at volume, where a few percent more recovered carts is worth $450 a month and the identity-resolution layer has enough traffic to work with
tools.skip_if: your monthly email revenue is below roughly $5,000 — the entry price eats the gain — or you do not run Klaviyo, since the product is built around it

tools.name: Audiorista
tools.what_it_does: No-code platform for launching branded audio apps — podcasts, audiobooks, meditation and courses with subscriptions, on iOS, Android and web.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Demo is $29/mo and Lite $240/mo for iOS and Android apps. Business is $400/mo per app, plus a tiered variable fee from $0.80 per monthly active user. Enterprise sits on that same $400 per app with further fees based on services, features and commitment, and the plan card quotes an Enterprise floor of $5,000/mo. 30-day free trial. Demo carries all Lite features except publishing to the App Store and Google Play, and monetization is disabled on it — a preview tier rather than a product. Paid app sales, RevenueCat in-app subscriptions and Zapier webshop sync start at Lite; the web app, Stripe web payments and push-notification campaigns start at Business.
tools.honest_knock: The $29 Demo tier cannot actually publish to the App Store or Google Play — real branded apps start at $240 a month. The Business tier adds a per-active-user fee from $0.80 on top of $400 per app, so growth literally raises the bill — and Apple and Google's own store commissions still apply to in-app sales on top of everything.
tools.best_for: creators and media brands with a real audio catalog — podcasts, audiobooks, meditations, courses — ready to monetize subscriptions in their own branded apps
tools.skip_if: you are still validating an audio idea on a small catalog or budget: the tier that actually ships to the app stores starts at $240 a month, before store commissions
compare_with: Uscreen is the video-first heavyweight for creator apps; Audiorista is audio-native — leaner for podcasts and audiobooks, with per-user fees appearing at the Business tier

tools.name: Aura
tools.what_it_does: Dynamic repricing for Amazon and Walmart sellers — automated price strategy across marketplaces.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-28, checked line by line against their own pricing page; every figure below is the same as on 1 Aug 2026) Flat per account, not per seat, with unlimited listings on every tier. Starter $37/month ($451 a year), Essential $77 ($931), Plus $157 ($1,891), Pro $237 ($2,851) — annual saves 20%. The ladder is set by monthly sales volume, not by features: Starter up to $15K, Essential up to $50K, Plus up to $250K, Pro up to $1M. Marketplaces included: 2, 3, 4 and 6. Aura AI covers 250, 500, 1,000 and unlimited listings; Hyperdrive 10, 25, 50 and 100 allocations; user seats 1, 2, 5 and unlimited. Their table adds three things the earlier reading did not record: monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, workflows run 5, 10, unlimited and unlimited, and there is a 14-day free trial.
tools.honest_knock: The tier is decided by how much you sell, not by what you need. That is unusually honest as a model — a seller doing $10K a month is not subsidising one doing $900K — but it means your bill moves when your business does, in the same month, without you choosing to upgrade. Pass $15K and Starter stops being the plan you are on. Work out which band you land in the way the page measures it: their table says monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, so it is a sustained climb rather than a single spike that moves you up. Two smaller things: the marketplace count is a real cap (two on Starter, so Amazon plus one), and the AI listing allowance is per listing rather than per repricing action, so a large catalogue eats it faster than a busy one.
tools.best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers past the point where manual repricing costs more attention than it is worth, and whose monthly volume sits comfortably inside one band
tools.skip_if: your catalogue is small or your prices rarely need to move — repricing pays back on competition and volume, and at low volume the $37 is buying automation you could do by hand
compare_with: the direct repricing peers — compare on which marketplaces are included and where the volume band ends, not on the monthly sticker

tools.name: AutoWrite
tools.what_it_does: AI blog writer for Shopify with SEO scoring, scheduling and publishing. Free plan available. New to the App Store: zero reviews as of 18 Aug 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 in a browser on apps.shopify.com/autowrite, because the plan table renders client-side and a plain fetch returns nothing) Four tiers, metered on posts, images and workflows per month. Free: 10 posts, 10 images, 1 workflow, basic SEO. Starter $9: 30 posts, 30 images, 3 workflows, brand voices, auto-publish, expert SEO. Pro $29: 100 posts, 100 images, 10 workflows, product references, generation priority. Business $79: 300 posts, 300 images, 30 workflows, support priority. All charges are billed in USD every 30 days. Correction to our own earlier note: on 18 August we wrote that the listing showed no paid tiers, which was our reading failing on a client-side table, not the vendor withholding prices.
tools.honest_knock: The honest thing to say about this one is that there is nothing to judge yet: on 18 August 2026 the App Store listing showed a rating of 0.0 from zero reviews. Not one merchant has publicly reported using it. That is not a criticism of the product, it is a statement about the evidence — an AI blog writer that nobody has reviewed is a bet, and it should be priced as one. The category it sits in is also crowded with tools that have years of track record behind them.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that want to test AI-written blog posts with SEO scoring at no cost, and who treat the output as a first draft rather than as publishable copy
tools.skip_if: you need a tool with a track record — there is none here yet — or you publish content where accuracy matters enough that an unreviewed generator is a liability

tools.name: Auware
tools.what_it_does: AI-built, audience-specific Shopify pages: automatically generates a personalized page per buyer persona — not just landing pages but advertorials, listicles, comparison and product (PDP) pages — with targeted headlines, social proof and FAQs, plus per-segment analytics. Built to lift ad conversion for DTC brands. No code.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Auware publishes a price after all: $99 a month on auware.com, alongside a 1-click Shopify install with a 30-day free trial that needs no card. Our earlier note said the paid rate was only visible inside the Shopify app — that is no longer the case, and the $99 figure has been on the site since at least early July. Their own pitch compares that with page builders charging up to $499 a month, and the plan is positioned as the full feature set from day one rather than a gated entry tier. Billing still runs through Shopify, so confirm the current rate in the app before committing.
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately narrow — Shopify-only and built around segmented paid traffic. If you send everyone to one page or don't run audience-segmented ads, the core 'a page per persona' value doesn't really kick in. It's also newer and less battle-tested than general builders like PageFly.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores running segmented paid campaigns (different personas, interests, offers) who are currently sending all that traffic to one generic page
tools.skip_if: you're not on Shopify, you don't run audience-segmented paid ads, or you just want a flexible general-purpose page builder
compare_with: the general page builders that make one page for everyone

tools.name: Ava AI
tools.what_it_does: AI phone agent for Shopify stores: answers support calls 24/7 — order lookup, edits and refunds mid-call — and runs outbound abandoned-cart recovery calls, with recordings, transcripts and its own business number. Priced by call minutes.
tools.pricing: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/ava-ai and avasales.ai) Three paid tiers, no free plan, each with a 7-day trial. Support is $29 a month and includes 100 call minutes, then $0.10 a minute; Recover is $99 a month with 400 minutes and $0.08 over; Scale is $499 a month with 1,500 minutes and $0.07 over. The headline price is really a minutes bucket: a store with real call volume pays the overage, so cost tracks conversation length, not seats. Estimate your monthly call minutes before you compare — at heavy volume the effective bill can sit well above the tier price.
tools.honest_knock: The monthly price is a minutes allowance, not a flat fee — every minute past the bucket bills at $0.07 to $0.10, so a busy support line can cost far more than the headline. And keep the vendor's marketing at arm's length: Ava launched in September 2025 with just six App Store reviews, and the promoted 21–24x ROAS figures are the vendor's own, not independently verified. There is no free plan, only a 7-day trial.
tools.best_for: Shopify DTC and cash-on-delivery stores with real inbound call volume that want 24/7 phone support and outbound cart-recovery automated, and are comfortable with per-minute economics
tools.skip_if: low-call-volume or thin-margin stores where per-minute overage can dwarf the base fee, and anyone who needs a proven track record — the review base is tiny (six) and the app is under a year old
compare_with: Ringly and Ava both put an AI voice agent on a Shopify store's phone line; Ava leans into live order actions and outbound recovery with per-minute pricing, while alternatives like Ringly, CallFlows and Fin differ mainly on minute rates and how much they do beyond answering. Compare on expected call minutes, not sticker price

tools.name: AWeber
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing and automation for small businesses and creators: drag-and-drop newsletters, prompt-built landing pages, autoresponders and sign-up forms, AI writing help, and since August 2026 a ChatGPT plugin and Claude connector that read a whole automation back with its engagement numbers.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Genuinely free plan (up to 500 subscribers); Lite shows $12.50/mo and Plus $20/mo at 500 subs (annual billing; both scale by subscriber count). The ~$899 flat Unlimited tier is served to about one visitor in eighteen rather than withdrawn: on 5 Sep 2026 we loaded the pricing page 18 times in fresh cookie-less browsers, 17 returned Lite and Plus with no flat tier and one returned a three-card variant with “Go Unlimited” at $899/mo for unlimited subscribers, so it exists but you cannot count on seeing it. AWeber runs aggressive limited-time launch promos (an ‘87% off’ banner striking $599 to $79 at research time) — treat banner prices as promos, not list prices. AWeber's own affiliate newsletter of 5 September 2026 describes a single paid plan, 'AWeber Pro', starting at $16.15 a month billed annually, and does not name Lite or Plus at all; the pricing page served us Lite and Plus the same day, so the plan names appear to be mid-change. Check the live page before quoting a tier name. Re-checked 6 September 2026 in twelve cookie-less loads: the pricing page named Free, Lite, Plus and Unlimited on all six of its loads, so the flat Unlimited tier that showed once in eighteen loads the day before was served every time; the free-email-marketing page named only Free. No load carried a plan called Pro and the newsletter figure of $16.15 appeared nowhere; the entry amounts read $12.50 and $20.00.
tools.honest_knock: The free and low tiers are generous, but Lite and Plus prices climb with your subscriber count, so budget for growth. It's a dependable, no-frills veteran — just not the most modern automation on the market.
tools.best_for: small businesses and creators who want reliable, simple email marketing with a genuinely usable free tier
tools.skip_if: you need advanced, behaviour-driven automation — newer tools go deeper for the money

tools.name: BabyLoveGrowth
tools.what_it_does: AI SEO/GEO content automation — auto-publishes optimized articles, builds backlinks and runs keyword research, aimed at fast hands-off organic growth for lean teams.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-05 on babylovegrowth.ai/pricing from a European connection, where it prices in euros) Two plans, both billed yearly. Grow is €75 a month, billed €900 a year, shown against a struck-through €247: 30 branded AEO/SEO articles a month, auto-publishing to WordPress, Shopify and eight more CMSs, $800 a month of backlinks from the partner network, AI-visibility optimisation and a site audit. Scale is €224 a month, billed €2,691 a year, against a struck-through €599: everything in Grow plus a dedicated SEO/GEO specialist for two hours a month, three extra content languages and early beta access. Both start with a 3-day free trial and can be cancelled at any time. History: in August 2026 the page quoted about $99 and $299 a month billed monthly; the current page bills the year up front and prices in your local currency.
tools.honest_knock: The honest concern here isn't the price — it's the model. Auto-publishing 30 AI articles a month and building $800+ in backlinks monthly is exactly the scaled-content-and-links pattern Google's spam policies (Helpful Content, link-spam) are written to catch. It can lift metrics short-term; on a brand you're building for years, it's a real durability risk. The 90-day money-back guarantee is a genuine plus that offsets some of that.
tools.best_for: solo founders and lean startups who want hands-off SEO content velocity fast, are comfortable with AI-generated articles at scale, and value the 90-day guarantee as a safety net
tools.skip_if: you're building a long-term brand where a spam-update hit would hurt, or you operate in a YMYL/regulated niche where thin AI content is genuinely risky — human-in-the-loop tools fit better there
compare_with: Frase keeps a human in the loop — AI that assists writing you still edit and own; BabyLoveGrowth goes full-automation for pure velocity. The trade-off is speed now versus durability against Google's next spam update

tools.name: BackupMaster
tools.what_it_does: Automatic daily backups for Shopify: products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventory, with 365-day retention and one-click restore; Pro adds downloadable copies, Google Drive sync and store duplication for staging. The free tier is for Shopify Partner dev stores only; live stores run $19, $39 or $79 a month for 300, 600 or 1,500 orders, 10% off annually.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/backup-master) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Agency is free to install but only for Shopify Partner development stores before they are transferred to a client, with all features enabled for three months. Essentials $19 a month or $205.20 a year, a 10% saving, covers stores up to 300 orders a month. That is automatic daily backups of products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventories, restore of supported items, 365-day retention and unlimited cloud storage. Pro $39 a month or $421.20 a year covers up to 600 orders a month and adds downloadable backup copies, Google Drive sync and duplication of data for staging or expansion. Plus $79 a month or $853.20 a year covers up to 1,500 orders a month, and adds multi-store pricing, detailed audit logs, external portal access, a custom backup time and priority support. The listing says higher-volume plans exist on the vendor's own pricing page without printing what they cost. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer BackupMaster, Bondi, NSW, Australia; the app launched 4 August 2017, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in English and German, and had 108 reviews at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
The listing header says free to install, and there is a free tier, but it is not for you unless you are an agency: Agency is limited to Shopify Partner development stores before they are handed over to a client. For a live store the entry price is $19 a month and it buys 300 orders a month.

Restore is described throughout as restoring supported items, and nowhere does the listing say which items are not supported. That phrase is carrying a lot of weight in a product whose entire promise is that you can undo a mistake. Ask for the exclusion list before you rely on it, and run one real restore into a development store rather than discovering the boundary during an incident.

The most useful review on the page is the critical one. In April 2026 a merchant asked for exports over SFTP to storage the vendor does not control, on-demand backups before risky changes, configurable retention and languages beyond English and German. The same merchant noted that a second store costs extra here where some rivals include one. None of that is damning; it is a fair map of where this app currently stops. Worth adding to the same note: your store data sits with a vendor in Australia, which belongs in your processing register whatever you decide.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores under roughly 1,500 orders a month that want the whole store backed up daily — metafields, metaobjects and translations included — without anyone having to remember to trigger it
tools.skip_if: you need backups exported to storage you control on the entry tier, an on-demand backup before every risky change, or a written list of what restore does not cover

tools.name: Barcodes Talk
tools.what_it_does: Authentic UPC and EAN barcodes for retail and Amazon listings. Buy GS1-sourced barcodes for your products as a one-time purchase, without an annual GS1 membership.
tools.pricing: One-off purchase, no subscription and no renewal, read on barcodestalk.com on 5 September 2026: a single barcode is $5, 10 are $15 ($1.50 each), 100 are $45 ($0.45 each), 1,000 are $180 ($0.18 each), 25,000 come out at $0.048 each and 100,000 at $3,500 ($0.035 each). The unit price drops fastest between one and a hundred codes.
tools.honest_knock: The honest caveat is about fit, not the codes. Some large retailers and brand registries — notably certain Amazon Brand Registry and big-box requirements — increasingly ask for a GS1-issued prefix tied to your own company, and a third-party barcode (legitimate and globally unique as it is) may not satisfy that specific gatekeeping. For most marketplaces and independent retail it's completely fine and far cheaper; just confirm your channel's exact requirement first.
tools.best_for: sellers and small brands listing on marketplaces or in independent retail who want authentic, one-time-cost UPC/EAN barcodes without an annual GS1 membership
tools.skip_if: your target retailer or brand registry explicitly requires a GS1-issued company prefix in your own name — then buy direct from GS1
compare_with: GS1 costs more and can carry ongoing fees, but it's the only route when a channel demands a prefix registered to your company

tools.name: Beautiful.ai
tools.what_it_does: Presentation builder whose templates lay themselves out as you type. Pro is about $12/month billed annually but $45 month-to-month — a steep gap — and the constraints that make decks look consistent also block pixel-level custom layouts.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-02 on the vendor's own pricing page) Pro is $14.50/mo billed annually, up from $12 in our July and August 2026 captures ($45 for a one-off month); Team about $40/user/mo annual ($50 monthly) with brand controls and shared libraries; Enterprise custom for 20+ seats. A single one-off presentation can be bought for ~$45; 14-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The smart-template engine is the feature and the fence: decks look polished with zero design skill precisely because the system constrains you, so pixel-perfect custom layouts and heavy brand exceptions fight the tool. And note the billing gap — $14.50/mo annual becomes $45 month-to-month, one of the steeper monthly premiums around. If your organisation lives in PowerPoint workflows, test the import/export round-trip before committing.
tools.best_for: founders, sales and small teams that want consistently good-looking decks fast, where design consistency matters more than pixel-level control
tools.skip_if: you need intricate custom layouts or complex animations (designers want full control), or your whole company workflow is deeply PowerPoint-native
compare_with: Gamma is the AI-native rival with a freer canvas — Beautiful.ai's edge is disciplined, on-brand consistency at speed

tools.name: Beefree
tools.what_it_does: RGE Studio (formerly Beefree — renamed 14 May 2026): drag-and-drop email and landing-page design. Build responsive, on-brand emails fast and export clean HTML to any major ESP, no coding required. Beefree remains the company name and the name of its separate developer SDK; the builder itself now lives under reallygoodemails.com.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (verified 21 Jul 2026 on reallygoodemails.com/pricing) Sold as RGE Studio since the 14 May 2026 rebrand. Starter free — up to 10 designs, 6 exports/mo, landing-page builder, custom subdomain, 20GB/mo image traffic, unlimited users but no roles or permissions. Professional $25/mo billed yearly ($30/mo monthly) — unlimited designs and folders, unlimited reusable blocks, 2 editing users plus 4 view-only, AI writing assistant. Business $134/mo billed yearly ($160/mo monthly) — 2 editing users plus 10 view-only, 2 workspaces, approval workflows, advanced brand controls, QA assistant. Enterprise: custom, quoted by sales. The free trial is 15 days on the Business plan. The embeddable Beefree SDK is a separate product on its own price list (developers.beefree.io) and is not covered by these numbers.
tools.honest_knock: Read the seat row before the price row. Professional and Business both cap at two full editing seats, so a "mid-sized team" plan at $134/mo annual still buys two people who can actually build. Everyone else lands in view-only slots — four on Professional, ten on Business — or an Enterprise quote. The free Starter is the odd one out: unlimited users, but with no roles or permissions at all. Exports are metered at six a month, rather than the unlimited free tier its old reputation suggests. And the naming is a live tripwire. Since 14 May 2026 the builder is RGE Studio at reallygoodemails.com, while Beefree remains the company name and the name of the separate developer SDK. So check which product a plan or invoice actually refers to. It is purely a creation environment that never sends, so it always sits on top of your ESP. Worth it when the ESP's native editor is the bottleneck — agencies, multi-brand teams, ESP migrations — and duplicated effort when it isn't.
tools.best_for: agencies and in-house teams shipping email at volume across brands or ESPs — a dedicated builder with approvals, brand controls and one-click push to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Pardot and HubSpot, sitting above whatever you send with
tools.skip_if: solo senders whose ESP editor already copes — you would be paying for a second tool to do a job your sending platform already does, and you still need the ESP because RGE Studio sends nothing itself
compare_with: Stripo or your ESP's own editor
Stripo is the head-on builder rival — compare template depth, export connectors into YOUR sending stack, and how many real editing seats each plan actually gives you

tools.name: Beehiiv
tools.what_it_does: Newsletter platform with growth, automation, SEO and monetisation tooling, priced by subscriber count. You keep 100% of paid subscriptions where Substack takes 10%; the trade is a steeper start than Substack's near-zero setup and built-in discovery.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-16 from beehiiv's own machine-readable pricing file at beehiiv.com/pricing.md, which states USD) Subscriber-based, and you keep 100% of paid subscriptions — beehiiv takes 0%, against Substack's 10%, leaving only Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30. Launch is $0 up to 2,500 subscribers with unlimited sends. At up to 1,000 subscribers Scale is $49/mo billed monthly or $517 a year (about $43/mo), Max $109/mo or $1,151 a year (about $96/mo). At 10,000 subscribers Scale is $109/mo or $1,151 a year; at 50,000 it is $249/mo or $2,629 a year. The ladder tops out at 100,000 subscribers ($329/mo Scale, $459 Max) and Enterprise is custom above that.
tools.honest_knock: Next to Substack it's more to learn. Substack's built-in discovery network and dead-simple setup are easier if you're starting from zero with no audience and don't care about automation or SEO. Beehiiv's depth is the point, but it's a steeper start.
tools.best_for: newsletter operators who want growth tools, automation, SEO control and ad/referral monetisation — and to keep 100% of subscription revenue
tools.skip_if: you're a beginner starting from zero who wants the simplest setup and Substack's built-in discovery, and don't need automation or SEO

tools.name: BidX
tools.what_it_does: Amazon-advertising automation from German vendor BidX GmbH: bid and budget automation, campaign creation, dayparting and target-ACOS rules for Sponsored Products, Brands and Display, with Amazon DSP and Marketing Cloud reporting and organic-plus-paid share-of-voice tracking in the same dashboard.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-06, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, EUR view) Amazon PPC is sold in three tiers, and every one of them is a monthly fee plus an unspecified percentage of connected ad spend. They are Self Service Platform €495/month, Managed Platform €1,995/month and Managed Service €4,995/month. The tiers differ mainly in how much of a human you get. That is one monthly strategy call on Self Service, up to two calls and up to 10h of assistance a month on Managed Platform, and up to four calls and up to 32h on Managed Service. Amazon DSP is priced separately on the same page: Self Service €495/month and Managed Service €995/month, again plus a percentage of ad spend. Amazon Marketing Cloud is sold as reporting: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The Share of Voice add-on covers the first 100 keywords free and charges $250 a month per additional 500 keywords. All prices are net with VAT added on top, and the page states that plans are based on an annual commitment paid monthly; the FAQ adds that new customers can take a paid three-month proof-of-concept period first. Walmart Managed Service, high ad-spend volumes and large agencies are contact-sales. Sellers under €10,000 a month in ad spend are pointed to a separate product, BidX Essential, whose own landing page at get.bidx.io/essentials lists $195/month for up to $10K in monthly ad spend — a flat fee with no percentage attached.
tools.honest_knock:
The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print. Every Amazon PPC and DSP tier ends with “+ % of connected ad spend per month”, and that percentage appears nowhere — not on the tier cards, not in the footnotes, not in the FAQ. So €495 is a floor, not a price, and nobody spending real money on Amazon ads can work out their monthly cost from this page. Ask for the percentage in writing, and ask whether it is charged on all connected spend or only on what BidX manages, before you get as far as a contract.

The second thing to price is the commitment. The page states plans run on an annual commitment paid monthly, and the FAQ confirms it: the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path on offer is a paid three-month proof of concept. There is no free trial. That makes the cheapest visible door €5,940 a year net of VAT before a cent of the percentage — a very different proposition from the €495 the eye lands on.

Two smaller inconsistencies worth noticing, because they tell you how carefully the price list is maintained. On a page priced in euros, the one add-on with a hard number is quoted in dollars ($250 per extra 500 keywords), so ask which currency you are actually billed in. And BidX Essential — the $195/month product they route smaller sellers to — lives on a completely separate landing page carrying a 2024 copyright line and a different phone number. It is not listed among the tiers on the pricing page itself, so confirm it still exists at that price before you plan around it.
tools.best_for: brands and agencies already spending well past €10,000 a month on Amazon ads, who want bid, budget and campaign automation, Amazon DSP and AMC reporting in one platform with a named growth manager attached. It also suits teams who value a German vendor with EU invoicing, SEPA and direct debit, and support in English and German
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is under roughly $10K a month, because BidX itself routes you to a different product at that size. Skip it too if you want to try before you commit: there is no free trial, the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path is a paid three-month proof of concept. And skip it if you need your total cost on paper before a sales call, because the percentage of ad spend is unpublished — or if you advertise mainly outside Amazon and Walmart
compare_with: the closest peer we cover, and the comparison is unusually clean because both charge a fee plus a percentage of ad spend — the difference is how much of that they will tell you up front. Teikametrics publishes both halves: $149/month billed annually (or $179 monthly) under $10K of ad spend, and 3% of ad spend above $10K on the Advanced tier. BidX publishes the monthly fee and withholds the percentage on every tier. At the small end the gap is stark too: Teikametrics' entry plan is self-serve at $149, while BidX's answer under $10K is the separate Essential product at $195/month. Model both at your own real monthly spend rather than at the headline, and get the BidX percentage in writing before you compare — without it the two are not comparable at all. Verify both current price lists yourself; ours were read on 2026-08-06.

tools.name: Bill.com
tools.what_it_does: Accounts-payable and receivable automation for finance teams with real approval chains. Priced per user from about $45/month, with transaction fees stacked on top — roughly $0.49 ACH, $1.99 cheque, $9.99 international wire, 2.9% card.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Accounts-payable and receivable plans priced per user: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise. The separate Spend and Expense product is $0 per user per month. Transaction fees stack on top of the seat, and are where the real cost hides. ACH or ePayment is $0.59, a mailed check $1.99, an international USD wire $19.99, and an international FX wire or a virtual card free. Instant payment is 1.0% with a $9.99 minimum and a $100 maximum, and Pay Faster ACH $11.99. Expedited checks are $24.99 overnight, $19.99 two-day and $14.99 three-day. Paying by card costs 2.9%, and the receiver pays 2.9% on credit or debit card payments.
tools.honest_knock: Per-user pricing plus per-transaction fees means the real cost depends on team size and payment volume — it's built for finance teams with genuine AP workflows and is overkill if you pay a handful of bills a month.
tools.best_for: growing companies with real accounts-payable volume and approval chains that want to automate bill pay and sync to accounting
tools.skip_if: you pay only a few bills a month — your accounting software or a free tool like Melio's base plan covers it without per-seat fees
compare_with: the free-to-start AP alternative for smaller volumes

tools.name: BillingNow
tools.what_it_does: Invoicing and expense tracking with AI — unlimited invoices, expenses, clients and users, at $9.99 a month or $99.90 a year, made in Geneva.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-20, read on their own site) Two plans, both carrying the identical feature list with no limits: $9.99 a month, or $99.90 a year which the page itself works out to $8.33 a month and labels 'Save 17%'. Both include unlimited invoices, expenses, client relations, users, estimates and credit notes, plus payment tracking, tax rates, PDF export and the AI assistant. There are no per-user fees and no feature-gated tier. The trial is 3 days and the page states three separate times that no credit card is required to start it. SOC 2 Type II certified with European-standard compliant invoices.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is genuinely refreshing — two plans, same features on both, unlimited users, no per-seat maths. The honest watch-out is the trial length rather than its terms: three days is short for migrating billing into a new tool, and the practical constraint is that there is no import path. The help centre documents CSV and Excel export but no import, so an existing client list has to be retyped — which is more than three days of work for anyone with a real book. It is also a young product from a small Geneva maker, so weigh ecosystem depth and longevity before you move your billing history in.
tools.best_for: freelancers and small teams that want unlimited invoicing, expenses and client management with zero per-user maths — users are unlimited on both plans, so a five-person team pays $2.00 a head
tools.skip_if: you need accountant-grade features, payroll or deep integrations (the incumbents' ecosystems are bigger), or you have an existing client list to bring across — the help centre documents export but no import, so every client has to be retyped
compare_with: FreshBooks is the polished incumbent with tiered plans and client limits; BillingNow’s single flat unlimited plan undercuts it hard — you trade ecosystem depth for radical simplicity

tools.name: Birch
tools.what_it_does: Ad automation for performance marketers (formerly Revealbot): rule-based optimization, automated scaling and creative insights across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat — run and optimize ad campaigns on autopilot.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026, formerly Revealbot) Essential about $49/mo and Pro about $99/mo, both with a $10k monthly ad-spend ceiling; overages meter (~0.49% Essential, ~1% Pro of excess spend, monthly billing only); Enterprise custom with no cap. 14-day free trial, two months free on annual.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is that pricing tracks your ad spend. The tidy $49/$99 tiers assume you stay under a $10k monthly ceiling, and past it you either pay spend-based overages or move to custom Enterprise — so a scaling advertiser's real cost rises with their budget. It's also a power tool: rule-based automation across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat rewards advertisers who know what to automate, and can amplify mistakes if your rules are wrong. For hands-on performance marketers, it's a serious time-saver.
tools.best_for: performance marketers and agencies running real ad budgets who want rule-based automation, scaling and creative insights across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat
tools.skip_if: you run small, simple campaigns a native ads manager handles fine, or you're not comfortable defining automation rules (bad rules scale bad decisions)
compare_with: Madgicx or the native ad managers
comparable ad-automation platforms — Birch's edge is granular rule automation; compare on spend-based pricing at your budget

tools.name: Bitdefender
tools.what_it_does: GravityZone endpoint protection for small business, managed from one console. Roughly $57–96 per device per year at list on an annual plan. The first year is promotional and renews higher, so budget for the renewal rate rather than the intro.
tools.pricing: Read on their own product pages, 6 September 2026, where a configurator prices each tier by device count and term. At 10 devices for one year the list prices are GravityZone Small Business Security $324.99, Business Security $384.99 and Business Security Premium $879.99 — $32.50, $38.50 and $88.00 per device per year. A 30% discount is applied by default on all three, bringing them to $227.49, $269.49 and $615.99. Small Business Security at 5 devices for one year is $169.99 list, $118.99 discounted. Add-ons are priced separately: at 10 devices, Web Access and Device Control $41.99 and Network Attack Defense and Risk Management $41.99 on Small Business Security, Setup & Go $224.99, and Essential: Tips & Best Practices $54.99 a seat. Enterprise Security, Defense XDR and MDR are contact-sales.
tools.honest_knock: Like most antivirus, the first-year price is a promo — renewals run notably higher, so budget for the renewal rate, not the intro. It's consistently top-rated on protection, so the real trade-off is cost, not efficacy.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want top-tier, independently-validated endpoint protection managed from one console
tools.skip_if: you're a solo user with basic needs — built-in OS defenses plus good habits may be enough before you pay for a business console
compare_with: Microsoft Defender for Business or ESET

tools.name: Bitscale
tools.what_it_does: GTM data layer that sits on top of your CRM: enrich records through waterfalls across 100+ B2B sources, track buying signals and run AI agents against the result. Free tier at 200 credits; paid from $349 a month for 15,000.
tools.pricing: (read 1 September 2026 on bitscale.ai/pricing) The meter is credits, and every tier carries the same 100+ data sources. Free is $0 with 200 credits, no card required, capped at 20 action columns per grid. Growth is $349 a month billed monthly for 15,000 credits, with unlimited actions and inbound integrations like RB2B, Factors and Vector. Booster is $799 for 50,000 credits and adds 50 action columns per grid, curated scraping scripts, a private Slack channel and Salesforce integration. Enterprise is quote-only but publishes a floor most vendors hide: annual billing at $15,000 and above, adding SOC 2 and SSO, priority support and custom credit volumes. Annual billing takes 10% off. The number to watch is the step from Free to Growth: 200 credits to 15,000 is a seventy-five-fold jump with nothing in between, so a small team that outgrows the free tier has no gentle next rung -- the bill goes from nothing to $4,188 a year in one move.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is real and needs no card, which makes Bitscale unusually easy to judge for yourself before paying. What to check during that trial is not the feature list but your own burn rate: 200 credits go quickly once a waterfall tries three sources per record, and the next rung is $349. Work out what one enriched record actually costs you in credits, multiply by your real monthly volume, and compare that against what you pay your current vendors combined. That is the only comparison that settles it, and Bitscale gives you the free tier to run it.
tools.best_for: sales and RevOps teams that already run enrichment across several vendors and want the waterfall, the signals and the CRM sync in one place, with enough monthly volume to put 15,000 credits to work
tools.skip_if: you enrich a few hundred records a month -- the free 200 credits or a per-lookup tool costs a fraction -- or you need a flat, predictable bill, because credits are consumption and consumption moves with your prospecting
compare_with: the flexible enrichment platforms -- Clay is closest in shape, and Apollo publishes its prices, which makes it the honest benchmark for what Bitscale credits really cost you

tools.name: Bitvavo
tools.what_it_does: Dutch-regulated, euro-native crypto exchange with deep EUR pairs and an API for automation. No subscription — the base tier under €100k monthly volume runs about 0.15% maker and 0.25% taker, dropping through ten volume tiers. Sign up via our link for €10K fee-free.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own fees page) No subscription — you pay per trade. EUR markets (Category A) run ten volume tiers. It is 0.15% maker / 0.25% taker below €100,000 of 30-day volume, then 0.10%/0.20% from €100,000, 0.09%/0.18% from €250,000, 0.08%/0.16% from €500,000 and 0.05%/0.14% from €1,000,000. Above that: 0.03%/0.12% from €2,500,000, 0.01%/0.10% from €5,000,000, 0.00%/0.08% from €10,000,000, 0.00%/0.04% from €25,000,000 and 0.00%/0.02% above €100,000,000. USDC markets (Category B) are a separate schedule from 0.05% maker and taker, and stablecoin pairs (Category C) from 0.10%; Bitvavo states that stablecoin trades do not count towards the 30-day volume that sets your tier. Deposits are free by SEPA, iDEAL/Wero, Apple Pay and Bancontact; a credit card costs 1%, PayPal 2% and EPS or Giropay 1.75%. Margin positions carry a separate hourly borrowing fee, published at 0.0023% an hour on every listed asset, plus a 2% fee if the position is liquidated.
tools.honest_knock: The honest caveats are crypto-wide, not Bitvavo-specific: fees are only part of the cost (spread matters on small orders), and no exchange removes market risk — the platform being cheap and MiCA-regulated doesn't make the assets safe. Note the disclosure: this is one of the few tools here we genuinely run — our own trading system executes on Bitvavo — which is experience, but also means we're an actual customer, not a neutral bystander.
tools.best_for: EU-based traders and builders who want a MiCA-regulated, euro-native exchange with low tiered fees, deep EUR pairs and a solid API for automation
tools.skip_if: you're outside the EU (it's euro-centric), you trade exotic altcoins it doesn't list, or you need derivatives-first infrastructure
compare_with: Kraken is the classic global peer; Bybit leans derivatives — Bitvavo's edge is euro on/off-ramps and EU regulation

tools.name: Blinq
tools.what_it_does: Digital business cards shared by QR code or link, with contacts syncing into your CRM. A free plan covers two cards; Business is about $4.99/user/month annual with a five-user minimum, and the event lead-capture add-on starts near $199/month.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). For individuals, Premium is $9.99 a month billed monthly or $7.33 billed annually. For teams, Business is $6.99 per user a month billed monthly or $4.99 per user billed annually, with a 5-user minimum, adding CRM sync, templates and custom reporting. Enterprise is custom. A lead-capture add-on for events starts around $199/mo. Note the individual plan costs more per person than the team plan — if there are five of you, the team tier is both cheaper per head and more capable.
tools.honest_knock: The core product is honestly cheap — the price jump hides in the event lead-capture add-on (~$199/mo), which is where teams that live on trade shows actually get value. And a truth about all digital cards: the wow factor works precisely because adoption is still low; the durable value is the CRM sync (contacts flowing automatically into your pipeline), so judge Business tier by that integration, not by the tap-to-share trick.
tools.best_for: teams and field-sales orgs that want consistent, branded digital cards with contacts syncing straight into the CRM — and events teams via the capture add-on
tools.skip_if: you're an individual (the free tier honestly covers you), or your networking volume doesn't justify per-user pricing
compare_with: the digital-card peer set — compare CRM integrations and whether you need hardware (NFC cards) versus pure app

tools.name: Blocky
tools.what_it_does: Shopify fraud filter that blocks visitors and orders by country, IP (v4 and v6), email, name, address and phone, with an AI bot blocker for TOR, proxy and VPN traffic that gets past reCAPTCHA, country redirects, a right-click blocker and visitor analytics. The free tier is for development stores only; live stores run $9.99 for country blocking, $16.99 with IP blocking or $19.99 for the identity and bot filters, 30% off annually. Not sold to Shopify Plus stores.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/blocky-simple-country-blocker) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Development Stores is free but only for development and partner stores; it carries all Pro features and starts billing on upgrade. Basic $9.99 a month or $83.92 a year, a 30% saving: enforcement inside the checkout page, unlimited country blocking, a fully customisable blocked page and online support. Advanced $16.99 a month or $142.71 a year adds unlimited IP blocking for IPv4 and IPv6, an IP whitelist and a geolocation country redirector. Pro $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year adds blocking by email, name, address and phone, the Bot Killer for TOR, proxy and VPN traffic, an add-ons blocker, a right-click blocker and unlimited visitor analytics traffic logs. All three paid tiers carry the same restriction in their own plan text: all stores except for Shopify Plus stores. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched 7 April 2021, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in eleven languages, and had 324 reviews at the time of writing, 5% of them one-star.
tools.honest_knock:
Read the plan text before you read the badge. The App Store header says a free plan is available; that free plan is Development Stores, for development and partner stores only, and it starts charging the moment the store goes live. All three paid tiers then carry the line 'all stores except for Shopify Plus stores', so if you are on Plus this app is not sold to you. Check that with the developer before you plan around it.

A blocker is a blunt instrument, and the review distribution shows it: 324 reviews, 89% of them at the top rating and 5% at the bottom — fifteen one-star reviews. Rules that stop fraud also stop customers. A blocked country catches the expat who genuinely wanted to buy; a VPN rule catches the privacy-minded shopper. The tuning is yours to do, continuously, using visitor analytics that only the Pro tier includes.

And it prevents rather than recovers. Nothing here disputes a chargeback that has already landed or claws back an order that already shipped. For that you need a separate dispute tool, which is a second subscription on top of this one.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores below Plus that are losing time to bot traffic, repeat fraudsters or orders from regions they do not ship to, and want blocking rules they control rather than a full security suite
tools.skip_if: you are on Shopify Plus, where the paid plans exclude you outright, or you need chargebacks disputed and revenue recovered rather than visitors kept out

tools.name: Bokun
tools.what_it_does: Booking management for tours and activities, by Tripadvisor. Manage availability, channel sales and online bookings in one place — built for experience businesses.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) A free version plus paid plans from about $49/mo (Start). Service fee on direct bookings varies by plan (~1.5% Start, 1.25% Plus, 1% Premium); crucially, zero Bokun booking fee on Viator reservations. Free trial available.
tools.honest_knock: Bokun is a Tripadvisor/Viator company, and that's both the draw and the lock-in. Distribution to Viator and 2,600+ resellers is excellent, but you're building your booking backbone inside one OTA's ecosystem, and the per-booking service fee on direct sales is a real cut on top of the subscription. If most of your business is direct, weigh that fee; if you live on OTA distribution, the Viator advantage is hard to beat.
tools.best_for: tour, activity and experience operators who want booking management plus wide OTA distribution (Viator, GetYourGuide and more) from one dashboard
tools.skip_if: you're a tiny operator taking a handful of direct bookings where the fees and setup outweigh the reach, or you want to stay off OTA rails entirely
compare_with: close tour-booking peers — compare direct-booking fees and how much you rely on Viator/Tripadvisor distribution

tools.name: Bolt Business
tools.what_it_does: Business travel and mobility management. Give your team expense-tracked rides and travel with centralized billing and reporting.
tools.pricing: No subscription, no activation cost and no minimum commitment (re-verified 2026-08-20 on Bolt's own business page): you pay per ride or rental taken, with consolidated monthly billing, spend limits and policy controls included. One line the marketing does not carry, but Bolt's own support pages do: Bolt charges a service fee on every trip made with the business payment method, billed at the start of the following month. On credit card it is deducted automatically and does not appear on the individual trip invoice — it arrives as a separate service fee statement on the 3rd of each month; on postpaid it sits on the monthly invoice. The amount is not published. Still commitment-free to pilot, but ‘you only pay for the rides’ is not the whole bill.
tools.honest_knock: The honest boundary is geography: Bolt's network is Europe/Africa-centric across 600+ cities, so US-only operations should look elsewhere, and ride availability varies by city — pilot it on your team's actual routes. Pricing is dynamic like all ride-hailing; the business layer adds control and receipts, not fixed corporate fares, so budget-predictability comes from your spend limits, not from locked prices.
tools.best_for: companies with European/African travel footprints that want employee rides centrally billed, policy-controlled and expense-integrated — at zero platform cost
tools.skip_if: US-only operations (network coverage), or you need guaranteed fixed-price corporate transport contracts
compare_with: the direct rival — Uber wins on US/global coverage, Bolt typically on per-ride cost in its home markets; run both where they overlap

tools.name: BookX
tools.what_it_does: Shopify appointment booking that lives in the storefront: Calendly-style slots for services, classes, rentals and events, with staff and multi-location schedules, deposits and partial payments, and the money taken at your own checkout. Bookings are unlimited on every tier — the ladder is gated on locations and team members. Free covers 1 service and 1 team member; Starter $9.99 a month or $107.99 a year, Growth $19.99 or $203.99, Business $39.99 or $407.99, for 5, 10 and 20 locations and team members. Read 8 Sep 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/appointment-booking-bookeasy and checked against the vendor's own pricing section on logbase.io, which lists the same tiers) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is locations and team members rather than bookings — every tier, the free one included, carries unlimited bookings. Free costs nothing and covers one service and one team member, minute or hour scheduling, lead and buffer time, email notifications, timezone and multi-language support, blockout dates and slots, and live support by chat, email and Zoom. Starter is $9.99 a month or $107.99 a year (10% off) and lifts that to five locations and team members with unlimited services, full-day, multi-day and bundle bookings, Google Calendar and Zoom, book-now-pay-later and partial payments, customer reschedule and cancel, and a universal booking button. Growth is $19.99 or $203.99 a year (15%) for ten locations and team members, deposits and multi-payment options, workflows and a custom email sender, Shopify Flow and POS, seasonal pricing and advanced bundle and multi-day conditions. Business is $39.99 or $407.99 a year (15%) for twenty locations and team members, the all-in-one booking widget, two-way Google Calendar sync per team member, advanced seasonal pricing, Klaviyo and webhook integrations and priority support. Every paid tier has a 14-day free trial. What the table does not publish is what happens above twenty locations or team members: the ladder simply ends there.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is a demonstration rather than a plan. One service and one team member means a salon with two stylists, or a studio running two class types, is already on Starter — so treat $9.99 a month as the real entry price, not zero. From there the ladder is gated on locations and team members rather than on how much you actually book: five, ten and twenty at $9.99, $19.99 and $39.99. A busy single-location business therefore pays the same as a quiet one, which is generous, while a small chain climbs the ladder for reasons that have nothing to do with volume. Above twenty locations or team members the published table stops and you have to ask. And the whole thing only exists inside Shopify — the calendar rides on your storefront, checkout and POS — so there is nothing here for a business that takes bookings anywhere else.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants running appointment-based services — salons, studios, clinics, rentals, classes and events — who want the booking calendar inside the store they already sell from, with staff and multi-location schedules and payment taken at the Shopify checkout.
tools.skip_if: you do not sell on Shopify; you need a booking system that stands on its own website and payment flow so customers who never visit your shop can still book; or you run more than twenty staff or locations and want a published price before you commit.
compare_with: SimplyBook.me is a standalone booking platform with its own booking page, client records and payment providers, and it works whatever you sell on. BookX makes sense the other way round: you are already committed to Shopify and you want the calendar, the staff schedule and the money to sit inside that storefront instead of beside it. The trade is reach against integration — SimplyBook.me can take a booking from someone who never sees your shop, BookX cannot, but BookX takes the payment through the checkout you already run and keeps the appointment in the same admin as the order

tools.name: Bookyourdata
tools.what_it_does: B2B email lists and verified contact data on demand. Build targeted prospect lists with verified business emails and pay only for the contacts you need.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) Pay-as-you-go, no subscription: one credit is one full contact. The published pack table runs 250 credits for $99 ($0.40 each), 500 for $159, 1,000 for $299 ($0.30), 2,500 for $599 and 5,000 for $799 ($0.16). From there it goes 10,000 for $999 ($0.10), 25,000 for $2,099 ($0.08), 50,000 for $3,699 ($0.07), 100,000 for $5,499 ($0.05) and on up to 2,500,000 for $24,999 ($0.010), with anything larger quoted. New accounts get a Free Pack of 10 credits once, with no card. Credits never expire and the 97% deliverability guarantee refunds credits, not money. BeSpoke, the hand-built private list service, is priced separately from $499 for 1,000 records.
tools.honest_knock: The model is honest — no subscription, credits keep, bad data refunded — so the real scrutiny belongs on usage. Bought lists are only as good as your targeting and your sending infrastructure, and cold-emailing purchased contacts has legal boundaries that vary by country, GDPR territory especially. The data being accurate doesn't make the campaign compliant; that part is yours.
tools.best_for: sporadic, project-based prospecting where a subscription would idle — buy exactly the verified contacts you need, when you need them
tools.skip_if: you prospect continuously at volume (subscription databases price better), or your market is EU-consumer-adjacent where purchased-list outreach gets legally delicate
compare_with: subscription databases vs pay-per-contact — the crossover is usage frequency; occasional buyers win with BookYourData, daily prospectors with Apollo

tools.name: Boulevard
tools.what_it_does: Booking, point of sale and client management for salons, spas and self-care businesses.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per location per month: Essentials $140 (shown as discounted from $176), Premier $234 (from $293), Prestige $328 (from $410). Enterprise is a bespoke quote. Paid add-ons sit on top, also per location — the page lists items at $45 and $65 per month per location, ePrescribe at $45 per prescriber, and email marketing at $0.01 per email beyond the included allowance. Every tier's button is 'Get a demo': there is no self-serve checkout at any price.
tools.honest_knock: Two things about this price list. It is per location, so the arithmetic for a second salon is not a volume discount, it is double — and the add-ons are per location too, which compounds it. And every listed price is shown struck through against a higher 'normally' figure, footnoted on 18 August 2026 as a limited-time summer offer for new customers only. Treat the higher number as the list price a renewal may return to, and the lower one as an introductory rate with an end date you should ask about. The third thing is not a price at all: you cannot buy this without booking a demo. That is a signal about how the deal is done, and it means the published numbers are a starting point rather than a checkout.
tools.best_for: salons, spas and clinics with staff to schedule and a front desk to run — the per-location pricing works out fine for one busy site
tools.skip_if: you are a solo practitioner with a calendar and a card reader, because the entry tier at $140 a month is priced for a team, and multi-location owners should price the add-ons per site before comparing
compare_with: the standing comparison in salon and spa software — compare per-location totals with your add-ons switched on, not the entry sticker

tools.name: Bouncer
tools.what_it_does: Email-list verification sold as credits that never expire: $8 per 1,000 (also the minimum purchase), falling to about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume. Unknowns and duplicates are not charged. Treat 'accept-all' domain results as unverified.
tools.pricing: Email verification credits, pay-as-you-go and never expiring (re-verified 2026-08-11): $8 per 1,000, which is also the minimum purchase, then $35 per 5,000, $60 per 10,000 and $250 per 50,000. Above that it runs $400 per 100,000, $750 per 250,000, $1,250 per 500,000 and $2,000 per 1,000,000 - about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume. The same calculator offers a monthly-subscription mode for verification that Bouncer states is discounted against pay-as-you-go; it publishes no fixed monthly tiers, so price it at your own volume. 100 free credits to test; duplicates and 'unknown' results aren't charged. The $25/$125/$250 per month tiers are the separate Deliverability Kit, and Shield is a separate real-time product.
tools.honest_knock: Not charging for unknowns and duplicates is genuinely fair — many rivals do. The honest framing for any verifier: it removes invalid addresses, which protects deliverability, but it can't make a cold list warm or a purchased list legitimate. Verify before every big send (lists decay measurably per month), and treat 'accept-all' domain results as the gamble they are, not as verified.
tools.best_for: email marketers and outbound teams that clean lists regularly and want accurate verification with fair credit mechanics (no expiry, no double-charging)
tools.skip_if: you send rarely to a stable opt-in list (occasional pay-as-you-go beats any subscription), or your problem is content/reputation rather than list hygiene
compare_with: the verification peer set — accuracy claims are near-identical; compare per-1,000 rates at your volume and the unknown/duplicate billing policy

tools.name: Bread & Butter
tools.what_it_does: Lead-intelligence platform with server-side tracking: captures the full visitor journey from the first visit, then enriches, scores and nurtures the moment someone submits an email — verified identities instead of IP-based company guesses. 30-day full trial, then a genuinely usable freemium tier; Pro from $49 per website.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against breadbutter.io) (2026) Fully functional 30-day free trial that moves to a freemium tier after (200 lead profiles, unlimited traffic). AI Enabled Pro $49 per month PER WEBSITE: full AI lead intelligence, enrichment, intent scoring, nurture and attribution with 5,000 lead profiles. AI capacity scales via add-on blocks: +$49/mo per Scale-AI-Enrichment block (+10,000 compute credits) and +$89/mo per deep-profile-research block (100 → 300 profiles/month). Enterprise is custom.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters to watch: it prices per WEBSITE (multi-site setups multiply the $49) and the AI features run on compute-credit blocks that stack as usage grows. On privacy, refined twice in open dialogue with the vendor (16 Jul 2026, verified against their docs). The anonymous journey IS tracked from the first visit, server-side via their site plugin. So ad-blockers and Safari’s ITP don’t strip it the way they kill client-side scripts — the vendor estimates 30-50% of high-value traffic is lost to client-side blocking. What stays dormant until someone submits an email is identity resolution — the ‘hand-raise’ that connects the captured history to a verified person. You still owe normal GDPR care on enriched data, and the real trade-off is simply this: no IP-based guessing at which company an anonymous visitor works for.
tools.best_for: marketing and revenue teams that want engaged visitors — people who filled a form or left an email — automatically enriched, scored and nurtured, on a genuinely usable freemium tier
tools.skip_if: you want IP-based company guessing at anonymous visitors — that’s a different tool class (Leadfeeder-style) with a different accuracy and compliance profile — or you run many small sites, where per-website pricing adds up
compare_with: Leadfeeder guesses the company behind anonymous IPs — useful when it lands, though remote work and VPNs often return an ISP instead; Bread & Butter tracks behaviour server-side from the first visit and resolves identity when a visitor hands over an email. Pick by what your sales team acts on: company guesses or verified people

tools.name: Breezy HR
tools.what_it_does: Recruiting and applicant tracking made simple. Post jobs to 50+ boards, manage candidates on a visual pipeline, and automate scheduling and screening.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A genuinely permanent free Bootstrap plan: one open position, unlimited users. Paid, annual against monthly: Startup $157/mo or $189, Growth $273/mo or $329, Business $439/mo or $529, plus a custom-quoted Pro tier. Every paid tier includes unlimited users and unlimited positions, which is what separates it from per-seat applicant tracking. Onboarding is a separate product, starting at $49/mo for automated role-based workflows that sync with the ATS.
tools.honest_knock: The jump from free (one position) to the first paid tier is steep if you only hire occasionally — the free plan is genuinely usable, so live in it until you're filling several roles at once.
tools.best_for: small teams hiring for a few roles at once that want a visual, drag-and-drop pipeline without enterprise-ATS pricing
tools.skip_if: you hire once or twice a year — the free single-position plan is plenty, and the paid jump only pays off with concurrent open roles

tools.name: Brevo
tools.what_it_does: Email, SMS and a light CRM, priced by monthly send volume rather than contact count — cheaper for a large list you email selectively. Free forever at 300 emails a day with unlimited contacts; paid from about $9/month. Model your real send volume if you mail frequently.
tools.pricing: Read on brevo.com/pricing on 6 September 2026 with the currency switched to US dollars and the yearly tab open (the page prices the same tiers in euros from the EU, at roughly 7, 15 and 499 a month): Free at $0 with 300 emails a day; Starter from $9 a month for 5,000 emails, or $8.08 on yearly billing; Standard from $18 ($16.17 yearly) adding marketing automation and A/B testing; Professional from $499 ($449 yearly, from 150,000 emails) with multi-user access and contact scoring; Enterprise on quote. Email volume, not contact count, is the meter, so every tier climbs with your monthly sends. The Sales Essentials CRM is billed separately from about $27 a month.
tools.honest_knock: Charging by sends rather than contacts is genuinely cheaper for big lists you email infrequently — but the free daily cap and add-on fees mean high-frequency senders should model their real send volume first.
tools.best_for: businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size
tools.skip_if: you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency

tools.name: Bright Data
tools.what_it_does: The web data platform trusted by enterprises. Collect public web data at scale with proxies, ready-made datasets and scraping APIs — fuel for your market research and AI projects.
tools.pricing: Usage-based (re-verified 11 Aug 2026): residential proxies start at $4.00/GB with no commitment, against a struck-through $8 — the $2.50/GB rate the overview page leads with is the $1,999/month tier, not the entry price; datacenter from $0.90/IP and ISP from $1.30/IP. API side: Unlocker, Crawl and SERP APIs from $1/1k requests (free tiers available), Scraper APIs $0.75/1k records (sale; list $1), Data Firehose $0.20/1k, Datasets from $250/100k records; managed offerings from $1,500/mo (Managed Data Acquisition) and Retail Insights from $2,000/mo.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise-grade web data infrastructure at enterprise-grade prices — the per-GB meter looks small until you multiply by real scraping volume, and the committed tiers only pay off if your usage is steady. The bigger honest note is compliance: Bright Data is strict about KYC and use-cases (a feature, not a bug), and whatever you collect still has to respect the target sites' terms and applicable law. Budget legal thought alongside the gigabytes.
tools.best_for: data teams and enterprises with real, ongoing web-data needs (pricing intelligence, market research) that justify committed volume and pass use-case vetting
tools.skip_if: you need occasional small scrapes (Browse.ai-class tools or datasets are far cheaper), or your use-case wouldn't survive a compliance review
compare_with: the premium proxy/data peers — compare effective per-GB at your committed volume and the quality on your specific target sites

tools.name: Browse.ai
tools.what_it_does: No-code web scraping and data extraction. Turn any website into an automated data pipeline or spreadsheet automatically.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against browse.ai) Credit-metered (2026): Free ~50 credits/mo (2 sites); Personal about $19/mo annual (12,000 credits/yr, 5 sites); Professional ~$69/mo annual (60,000 credits, 10 sites); Premium custom (600k+ credits, managed). A credit ≈ 10 extracted rows; premium sites cost more credits.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest realities of no-code scraping. Credits burn faster than expected: row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter, so monitor a big site daily and do the math first. And scrapers break when sites redesign — robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.
tools.best_for: ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers
tools.skip_if: you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot
compare_with: close scraping platforms — Apify is more developer-oriented; compare credit math on YOUR row volumes and site list

tools.name: BrowserAct
tools.what_it_does: No-code web scraper and browser-automation bots from one prompt, with managed browsers, residential proxies and CAPTCHA solving in one credit pool. Free tier with 1,500 credits; Basic $13/month on yearly billing ($20 monthly) for 10,000 credits, up to Advanced $96/$200 for 100,000. Monthly billing costs up to twice the yearly rate.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-02 on browseract.com/pricing, both billing tabs open) A credit-metered subscription with a free tier. Free Trial is $0 with 1,500 credits on signup and 5 free local browser profiles. Basic is $13 a month on yearly billing ($156 a year) or $20 month-to-month, for 10,000 credits a month, 10 simultaneous tasks, up to 5 static proxies and 10 local browsers. Essential is $56 a month yearly ($672) or $100 monthly, for 50,000 credits, 20 tasks, 25 static proxies and 50 local browsers. Advanced is $96 a month yearly ($1,152) or $200 monthly, for 100,000 credits, 40 tasks, 50 static proxies and 100 local browsers. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial (1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 credits respectively) and access to extra credit packs. The meters are published on the same page: a workflow step costs 5 credits, a local fingerprint browser 100 credits, residential proxy traffic 5,000 credits per GB; static proxies are priced by location and tier without a figure, and the cloud browser is free for a limited time. Seen inside the app on 2026-09-04, on first login: a trial panel offering Basic at $16, Essential at $70 and Advanced at $120 a month with the public monthly prices struck through, i.e. an in-app discount of 20 to 40 percent that the pricing page does not show.
tools.honest_knock: The yearly toggle wears a -20% badge, but the arithmetic on the page is steeper than that: Basic is $13 yearly against $20 monthly (35% less), Essential $56 against $100 (44% less) and Advanced $96 against $200 (52% less). Read the other way, paying month to month costs up to twice the yearly rate. And the 'as low as' figures under the meters do not come from these tiers either: at Advanced a credit works out to about $0.00096, so a 5-credit workflow step is roughly $0.0048, not the advertised $0.0032 -- that lower number must belong to a credit pack whose price the page does not show. In our own test the meter itself was honest at account level (1,500 to 1,174 credits over one build and two runs, reconciling exactly with the history list), but the same Bot cost 21 credits on one run and 27 on the next for identical output, and the task panel briefly reported 0 credits for a run the list priced at 21.
tools.best_for: teams that need a reusable web scraper or browser bot without writing selectors, want the browsers, residential proxies and CAPTCHA handling managed for them, and can commit to yearly billing -- at $13 a month Basic is a cheap way to run a few scheduled bots
tools.skip_if: you will bill month to month (you pay up to double), your jobs are proxy-heavy (one gigabyte of residential traffic is 5,000 credits, half of Basic's monthly pool), or you need a published overage rate before you commit, because the credit-pack price is not on the page
compare_with: Both turn a website into a scheduled, reusable data robot without code. Browse.ai is the older name and prices per robot run on a credit ladder that starts at $19 a month on annual billing, $48 monthly; BrowserAct starts lower at $13 yearly and bundles managed browsers, residential proxies and CAPTCHA solving into the same credit pool. If your bottleneck is blocked pages, BrowserAct's infrastructure is the difference; if it is simply extracting a table on a schedule, either does the job and Browse.ai has the longer track record.

tools.name: BuddyPunch
tools.what_it_does: Time clock and employee time tracking for hourly teams. Track hours, breaks, PTO and overtime with GPS and photo punch-in, and export payroll-ready reports.
tools.pricing: Per user plus a base fee, read on buddypunch.com/pricing on 5 September 2026: Starter $5.99 per user a month, Pro $7.99 and Advanced $13.99, each with a $19 base fee a month. Scheduling is $1 per user on Starter (included from Pro), real-time GPS $2 per user, onboarding and task checklists $4 per user, extended data retention $2 per user; the payroll add-on is $8 per user plus a $49 base fee a month. 14-day free trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: That flat $19 base fee makes it pricey for very small teams — at three or four users the base fee dominates the bill, so it's better value once you're past a handful of employees.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid teams that need straightforward employee time tracking with GPS and payroll-ready exports
tools.skip_if: you're a team of two or three — the fixed base fee makes the per-head cost sting until you scale up

tools.name: BugHerd
tools.what_it_does: Visual bug tracking and website feedback. Let clients and teams point-and-click to report issues right on the page, turned into trackable tasks.
tools.pricing: Standard about $42/mo (5 members), Studio ~$67/mo (10), Premium ~$125/mo (25), plus custom Enterprise — all with unlimited projects and unlimited client users; annual billing runs $500/$800/$1,500 per year (two months free), extra members $6.60/user/mo billed annually ($80 a year each). Free trial. Prices in US dollars before tax (re-verified 2026-09-05; unchanged since our July read). The MCP server and the other AI features now sit inside the Standard plan on the pricing page, still marked beta.
tools.honest_knock: The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly: your clients report for free as guests, but everyone on your side who works the feedback needs a seat, so a growing agency steps up tiers. It's deliberately a visual-feedback layer, not a full project-management or dev-issue tracker — most teams run it alongside Jira/Trello rather than instead of. The new MCP feature is genuinely interesting but currently beta: treat AI-agents-triaging-your-feedback as a bonus to evaluate, not the reason to buy.
tools.best_for: web agencies and site teams that want clients to point-and-click feedback directly on the page — and, new in 2026, want AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and others) to read, triage and action that feedback via BugHerd's MCP server, free in beta
tools.skip_if: you don't work with external clients or website revisions (a plain issue tracker is enough), or you need deep dev-workflow tracking that belongs in Jira
compare_with: close visual-feedback rivals — BugHerd currently stands out with its MCP/AI-agent integration; compare per-seat costs at your team size

tools.name: Buzz.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered outbound platform: prompt it and it finds intent-ready buyers, writes multichannel sequences and books the meetings — per-seat plans with monthly credit allowances and a free start.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-05) Teams: Core is $79 per seat a month with 500 credits a month, AI Employee $695 per seat a month with 5,000 credits; both are billed monthly and show a $0 setup fee, footnoted 'waived on prepaid annual'. Enterprise is custom: 25,000 credits a month, five seats included and a $2,500 setup fee. An 'Annual, 25% off' toggle sits above the cards, but the page kept showing the monthly figures when we switched it, so treat the annual price as unpublished until sales confirms it. A White-label tab adds Core White Label at $1,000 a month with 20 seats included, billed annually, and AI Employee White Label at $250 per seat a month billed annually with a five-seat minimum (advertised as 64% off, 'save $445 a seat'), 25,000 credits a month and a $2,500 setup fee on both. Free start on Core. History: in August 2026 the page said Core $125 (launch offer $75 for three months) and AI Employee $795 with a warning it would move to $1,000; on 2 September we read $79 and $695 and wrote that the credits were no longer stated and that one plan carried the $2,500 fee — on 5 September the credits are stated per plan and the $2,500 fee sits on Enterprise and the white-label plans, not on Core or AI Employee.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters run at once: seats AND credits — the seat price includes a credit allowance (500 a month on Core, 5,000 on AI Employee, read 5 September 2026), and real outbound volume means credit packages on top, so budget past the sticker. Watch the moving numbers too: the page changed twice this summer — a $75 teaser, then $79 a seat; $795 with a promised rise to $1,000, then $695 — and the $2,500 setup fee now sits on Enterprise and the white-label plans, so decide on the total for the plan you are actually offered, not the sticker. And the honest fundamental for any AI-SDR: it only books meetings as good as your list and offer, so keep a human reviewing what goes out in your name.
tools.best_for: GTM teams that want AI to run outbound end-to-end — prompt-driven prospecting of intent-ready buyers, multichannel sequences and meeting booking without adding SDR headcount
tools.skip_if: you send low-volume, hand-crafted outreach (per-seat-plus-credits is overkill), or you're not ready to QA an AI that writes to your market on your behalf
compare_with: Reply.io is mature multichannel sequencing you drive yourself and lemlist leads on deliverability and personalization — Buzz.ai's pitch is the autonomous AI-SDR layer that does the driving for you

tools.name: Bybit
tools.what_it_does: Crypto exchange covering spot, perpetuals and options. No subscription — spot is 0.1% maker and taker for non-VIP, derivatives around 0.02% and 0.055%, with volume tiers cutting lower. Funding rates on perpetuals are a recurring cost the fee table does not show, and availability differs per country.
tools.pricing: No subscription — per-trade fees, re-verified 2026-09-05 against Bybit's own fee schedule, which the page says was last updated on 2 September 2026. At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker; perpetuals and futures 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker; options 0.0200% maker and 0.0300% taker. The VIP ladder cuts those toward zero — at Supreme VIP spot is 0.0300% maker and 0.0450% taker, derivatives 0.0000% maker and 0.0300% taker, options 0.0050% and 0.0150%. Note that the top derivatives maker rate is zero rather than a rebate: we found no negative maker fee in the published table. That base table is not the only one, and the others start higher: fiat-crypto spot pairs cost 0.2000% taker and 0.1500% maker under $100,000 of 30-day volume, the Spot Adventure Zone and xStocks 0.2000% both ways at VIP 0, and Pre-Market Perpetuals and the Innovation Zone 0.0400% maker and 0.1000% taker — so a new account trading the newest listings pays about double the headline rate. Your VIP level is set by your asset balance, your 30-day average net borrowing or your trading volume over the past 30 days, whichever qualifies you higher, and it refreshes daily at 07:00 UTC.
