Bybit adds that actual rates can vary by region and points you to your own My Fee Rate page.
tools.honest_knock: Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways, and funding rates on perpetuals are a real recurring cost the fee table doesn't show. Regulation-wise, check what Bybit may offer in YOUR jurisdiction before funding an account — availability and product range differ per country, and that's the part most fee comparisons skip.
tools.best_for: active traders who want deep liquidity, low derivatives fees and a broad product range (spot, perps, options) with volume-tiered discounts
tools.skip_if: you're a buy-and-hold beginner (a simple euro-native exchange is safer territory), or derivatives aren't available to you locally
compare_with: Bitvavo is the euro on/off-ramp specialist, Kraken the regulated all-rounder — Bybit wins on derivatives depth

tools.name: Calilio
tools.what_it_does: Cloud phone system with international numbers and call menus, from about $12/user/month annual on Standard. Numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active team's real bill sits above the per-seat price.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Standard $15 per user/mo, or $12 billed annually ($144 a year); Premium $35 per user/mo, or $28 annually ($336 a year); Enterprise custom. Annual billing saves 20%. Each plan includes a stated value of free calls and SMS/MMS to US and Canada numbers — $6.75 on Standard and $33.74 on Premium — and beyond that calls and SMS draw from a credit balance, with numbers billed separately. Standard suits solopreneurs and small businesses; Premium is aimed at growing businesses, franchises and call centres.
tools.honest_knock: The subscription is the platform, not the talking: numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active calling team's real bill sits meaningfully above the per-seat sticker — model a month of your actual call volume before comparing vendors. It's a young player in a crowded VoIP field; the price is keen, so test call quality on your real routes in the trial.
tools.best_for: startups and small teams that want a modern, affordable cloud phone system with international numbers and clean dashboards
tools.skip_if: you need a battle-tested enterprise contact center with deep integrations and SLAs, or your call volume makes metered credits unpredictable
compare_with: close low-cost VoIP rivals — compare the metered call rates on the countries you actually call, not the seat price

tools.name: CallHippo
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven business phone system. Virtual numbers in 50+ countries, power dialer, call analytics and AI agents — set up your sales and support calling in minutes. Its omnichannel inbox threads voice, WhatsApp, SMS, email, Instagram and Telegram into one conversation per customer.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page in euros) Starter €19/user/mo, Professional €29 and Ultimate €39 on monthly billing for a 1-4 user team, above a genuinely free Basic tier where you pay only for the numbers. Unlimited landline and mobile minutes start at Starter with 100 SMS; call recordings, AI voicemail transcription and multilingual IVR at Professional with 500 SMS; smart DID, multilevel and holiday routing at Ultimate with 1,000 SMS. 10-day free trial on the paid tiers. The page carries selectors for currency, number region and team size plus a yearly toggle, and the tiers are priced per currency rather than converted — the same grid read in dollars on 19 July 2026 showed $19, $30 and $42. Call-centre 'Pro Suite' tiers run $32-48/user/mo annual and Enterprise is custom at 50+ users. AI copilot, AI voice agent and CNAM are paid add-ons.
tools.honest_knock: 'Unlimited calling' is unlimited to the US and Canada — international minutes meter separately, so teams calling Europe or Asia should price their real destinations first. The plan grid is busy (two suites, add-ons for the dialer and AI), which makes comparisons slippery: list the five features you actually need and find the cheapest tier that truly contains all five.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious sales/support teams wanting virtual numbers in 50+ countries with a free entry point and CRM integrations
tools.skip_if: your calling is mostly international at volume (metered minutes stack up), or you want one simple plan without add-on shopping
compare_with: the budget-VoIP peer group — decide on per-country call rates and which features are add-ons vs included

tools.name: CallRail
tools.what_it_does: Call tracking and attribution — which campaigns, keywords and ads produce phone calls and form leads. Plans run about $50–195/month, but included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest and overages meter at roughly $0.05 a local minute. It is an attribution layer, not a phone system or CRM.
tools.pricing: Four plans, read on callrail.com/pricing on 5 September 2026, each 'plus usage': Lead Tracking $55 a month, Lead Tracking Complete $105, Lead Conversion $165 and Lead Conversion Complete $215; on yearly billing the same four read $50, $95, $150 and $195 a month (read 6 September 2026; the page states “Save up to 10% with a yearly plan”). Voice Assist (the AI answering agent) is a separate add-on from $95 a month for 50 calls, then $1 a call. Usage past the included allowance is metered: extra local numbers $3 each, local minutes $0.06, toll-free numbers $5. Users are unlimited on every plan. 14-day free trial.
tools.honest_knock: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling — the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.
tools.best_for: marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution
tools.skip_if: you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight
compare_with: WhatConverts or a platform's native tracking
comparable attribution tools — compare on included minutes and how your real call volume meters

tools.name: Campaign Monitor
tools.what_it_does: Email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management for brands and agencies. Priced per contact rather than per send: Essentials at 10,000 contacts runs about $89/month, so dormant subscribers bill like active ones. Automation depth is lighter than dedicated platforms.
tools.pricing: Contact-based, on three tiers — Lite (with a monthly send cap of about five times your contact count), Essentials (unlimited sends) and Premier (priority and phone support). We could not re-verify a plan amount on 2026-08-16. The page publishes no plan price until you pick a contact count in its slider. The only figure in the page itself is the Website Builder add-on, at €9 a month from an EU address — our July and August captures both read the same line as $10. There is no free plan; the trial runs 30 days with 500 contacts. Older readings put Lite around $12-13 a month and Essentials around $29-31 at 500 contacts, climbing steeply with list size — treat those as indicative and take your own figure from the slider. Note also that the product is now listed as Campaign Monitor by Marigold.
tools.honest_knock: You pay for contacts, not sends — so a large, quiet list costs the same as a large, active one, and dormant subscribers are literally a line item. Clean your list before comparing prices anywhere. Campaign Monitor's strength is polished, agency-friendly email; its automation depth is lighter than dedicated marketing-automation platforms, so know which of the two jobs you're actually buying.
tools.best_for: brands and agencies that want beautiful, reliable email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management, priced per contact
tools.skip_if: you need deep behavioral automation and CRM-grade journeys (ActiveCampaign-class tools fit better), or your list is large but low-engagement — prune first
compare_with: Mailchimp is the closest general peer, ActiveCampaign wins on automation depth — compare at YOUR list size, since contact pricing diverges fast

tools.name: Campaigner
tools.what_it_does: Email and SMS marketing for mid-market senders with larger lists. The useful features start high — automation and API only arrive on Essential at about $179/month, while Starter at $59 is a sending tool rather than an automation platform. Contact-based pricing bills dormant subscribers too.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-05 on campaigner.com/pricing) Campaigner prices by contact count and bills per account, not per user: a slider sets the tier and there is no separate monthly/annual toggle. Two self-serve plans: Essentials from $14 a month at 1,000 contacts ($38 at 5,000, $158 at 25,000, $409 at 100,000) and Advanced from $35 a month at 1,000 contacts ($70 at 5,000, $258 at 25,000, $649 at 100,000), plus a quote-only Custom tier. Essentials excludes automation workflows and conversion tracking but includes the REST API, webhooks and SFTP; landing pages, sub-accounts and white-label are Custom only. SMS/MMS is not bundled into any plan: pay-as-you-go from $0.009 per message, sold through sales. Reputation Defender is an add-on at 20% of plan cost. The 30-day trial is full-feature but takes a card and auto-charges when it ends. History: until July 2026 the page carried a Starter/Essential/Advanced ladder at about $59, $179 and $649 a month; the current ladder starts far lower and moves with the contact count.
tools.honest_knock: Two paragraphs of fine print worth reading. Automation workflows and conversion tracking only arrive on Advanced (from $35 a month at 1,000 contacts) — Essentials is a sending tool with an API, not a marketing-automation platform — and the trial auto-converts to paid if you do not actively cancel, which tells you something about the retention strategy. Contact-based pricing also means dormant subscribers bill like active ones; prune first.
tools.best_for: mid-market senders with larger lists that want mature email plus SMS workflows and are comfortable at the Essential tier and up
tools.skip_if: you're small (the useful features start at $179/mo) or you dislike card-required auto-converting trials on principle
compare_with: Campaign Monitor shares the polish, ActiveCampaign beats it on automation depth — compare at your real list size and feature floor

tools.name: Capsule
tools.what_it_does: Deliberately simple CRM for small businesses: contacts, pipeline and tasks. Free for 250 contacts and two users, then about $21/user/month on Starter. The simplicity is the product — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on capsulecrm.com/pricing over a US connection) Four tiers, each quoted per user a month on annual billing: Free for two users and 250 contacts, then Starter at US$18, Growth at US$36 and Advanced at US$54, all with a 14-day trial that needs no card. Contacts are the ladder — 250, 30,000, 60,000 and 120,000 — with pipelines, project boards and reporting opening up alongside. Our earlier note listed five tiers topping out at an Ultimate plan around $75; the page we read today shows four and stops at Advanced. The figures render client-side, so treat these as our dated reading and take yours from the live page. A Marketing add-on is sold beside the CRM, and the AI features can be switched off in your account.
tools.honest_knock: Capsule's simplicity is the product: it deliberately does less than the CRM giants, which is why small teams actually use it. The honest flip side — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out at the top tiers, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it. Buy it to finally have a CRM the team fills in; plan a migration path if you're heading toward enterprise process complexity.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want a clean, genuinely simple CRM for contacts, pipeline and tasks — one the team will actually keep updated
tools.skip_if: you need marketing automation, complex territory logic or enterprise reporting (bigger platforms exist for a reason)
compare_with: the SMB-CRM peer group — Capsule wins on calm simplicity, Pipedrive on pipeline power; pick by which your team will really use

tools.name: Carbon6
tools.what_it_does: A suite of Amazon seller tools sold per product rather than as one subscription: Seller Investigators (FBA reimbursement recovery), ChargeGuard (1P vendor recovery for chargeback fees, shortages and accruals), PixelMe, DSP Prime and PPC Entourage (advertising), SoStocked (demand and inventory planning), ScanUnlimited (wholesale sourcing), plus ManageByStats, D8aDriven, AMZAlert and SellerAssist. Ownership matters here: SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 in Feb 2025 and folded the 1P deduction-recovery work into spscommerce.com, then transferred the 3P Amazon-seller business to Carbon6 on 30 Jun 2026 — the suite is sold under the Carbon6 brand again, with the partner programme rebranding from SPS to Carbon6 on 24 Aug 2026 and commission terms unchanged.
tools.pricing: What we can verify on the vendor’s own pages today (re-checked 26 Aug 2026): carbon6.io/pricing now redirects to the tool list, so there is no suite-level price at all. SoStocked has dropped its two-tier ladder — where on 21 Jul it listed ProfitFlow at $97/mo and ProfitFlow + Inventory at "starting at" $250/mo, it now shows a single Inventory + Profit plan at "starting at" $175/mo with a free trial. ScanUnlimited lists a free Limited tier and Unlimited at $70/mo, or $60/mo on the annual plan ($720/yr, marketed as two months free); the Unlimited Plus tier that sat above it at $1,080/yr is no longer on the pricing page. The off-Amazon advertising tool is listed as PixelMe by Carbon6 again rather than SPS Ad Performance, and it publishes no price. The 3P FBA-reimbursement service is a contingency arrangement: Seller Investigators by Carbon6 states a 25% commission charged only after Amazon has deposited the recovered funds, stated twice on its own site (re-read 26 Aug 2026), after a free 48-hour audit with no obligation. Our older suite-level figures — entry tools from about $49/mo, PixelMe from about $500/mo with a 6-month minimum, and $300-500+/mo for a working stack — stay withdrawn: none of those is verifiable against a live authoritative source today.
tools.honest_knock: The honest headline here is not pricing but ownership — and it has moved again, this time in the reader's favour. SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 for roughly $210M on 7 Feb 2025 and retired the brand into spscommerce.com. On 30 Jun 2026 it sold the entire 3P (Amazon marketplace seller) revenue-recovery business for $9.5M cash, booking an estimated $20M loss, and named no buyer at the time. There is a name now. The partner-programme notice we received on 17 Aug 2026, from Carbon6's own partnerships contact, states that SPS transferred ownership of the 3P business to Carbon6 and that commission terms and payouts are unchanged. It also states that existing links were redirected to the Carbon6 tool sites on 14 Aug 2026, and that the programme itself rebrands from SPS to Carbon6 on 24 Aug 2026. Reading carbon6.io on 17 Aug 2026 matches that: the whole suite is on sale there again as "by Carbon6". Read the two purchase numbers carefully, because they are not the same thing. The $210M bought the whole Carbon6 stack; the $9.5M was the 3P arm alone, and offloading it at a book loss seventeen months in still tells you how it performed. What remains undisclosed is who stands behind the Carbon6 entity itself, so the question is answered one level down and no further. Two more things to hold. Reuters reported on 23 Jun 2026 that SPS hired Morgan Stanley to explore a sale of itself under activist pressure, with talks early and no deal assured. And the 1P side is no longer a clean split, because SPS kept the deduction-recovery business it bought while Carbon6's own site now lists ChargeGuard for Amazon 1P vendor recovery. Ask which entity your 1P work would sit with before you sign. For 3P reimbursements the July advice has expired — you can name the counterparty on your contract again.
tools.best_for: Amazon sellers who want reimbursements, advertising, inventory and sourcing tools from one vendor and are content to buy them tool by tool — the suite trades under the Carbon6 brand again since 30 Jun 2026, so there is a named counterparty on the contract
tools.skip_if: you want one flat subscription and one invoice: this is a suite priced per tool, each with its own contract, and the pieces have moved between owners twice since Feb 2025 — check which entity your existing agreement actually names before you add another one
compare_with: Helium 10 is the flat-priced seller suite with published tiers, and GETIDA is the independent FBA-reimbursement specialist. Against a suite that has changed hands twice in eighteen months, both still win on continuity. The owner question itself is no longer open, though: the 3P business trades as Carbon6 again since 30 Jun 2026, on unchanged commission terms

tools.name: Castmagic
tools.what_it_does: Turns recorded audio and video into a stack of ready-to-use assets: transcripts in 60+ languages, show notes, summaries, newsletters, social posts, clips and audiograms, with custom prompts and an AI chat across your whole library. Billed annually at $19, $48 or $139 a month for 30, 100 or 400 transcribed hours; Business & Scale starts at $699 a month by demo.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on castmagic.io/pricing) Three published tiers plus an enterprise band, and the page opens on annual billing with a 'Save 30%' label, so every headline number is the annual rate. Hobby: $19 a month billed annually, $239 a year, 30 transcribed hours, up to 3 Spaces, 50GB storage, 3 seats, no API access, no onboarding call. Starter: $48 a month billed annually, $579 a year, 100 transcribed hours, 10 Spaces, 250GB, 5 seats, API access, onboarding call. Team: $139 a month billed annually, $1,669 a year, 400 transcribed hours, 25 Spaces, 1TB, unlimited seats with 5 included and extras at $159 a year or $19 a month each, priority support. Business & Scale: from $699 a month and $999 a month, by demo, for custom volume, seats, storage, SLA and dedicated support. Unlimited AI outputs, re-generations, media clipping and audiograms are on all three published tiers, as are 60+ transcription languages, a 10GB maximum file size and the Zoom, Google Drive, Zapier, RSS and YouTube/TikTok/Instagram imports. The monthly-billing prices are behind a toggle that the page does not put in its source, so the only thing we can state about them is what the page states: annual saves 30%. And the hours need care. The table calls them 'transcribed hours (library total)' and the FAQ 'a growing library of transcribed hours that you build up over time', which never actually says whether the allowance renews each month or is a running ceiling. Extra hours can be bought at any time on every tier.
tools.honest_knock:
The prices on the page are the annual prices. The toggle sits on 'Annually — Save 30%' by default, so $19, $48 and $139 are what you pay when you commit for a year; monthly billing costs more and the page does not show how much until you flip it. That is a normal enough pattern, but it means the number you remember from the pricing page is not the number you pay for a month-to-month subscription.

The hours are the part to pin down before you subscribe. The comparison table labels them 'transcribed hours (library total)', and the FAQ describes 'a growing library of transcribed hours that you build up over time'. That wording fits a monthly allowance and a lifetime ceiling equally well, and the difference between the two is enormous. 30 hours every month at $19 is a bargain for a weekly podcast. 30 hours in total is about seven episodes, and then you are buying top-ups. Ask before you pay, and ask what happens to the hours when you downgrade.

And the social proof does not agree with itself. The homepage hero says 'Loved by 100K+ podcasters and creators'; the pricing page on the same site says '75k+ Creators Served' and '75,000+ Creators & Businesses'. Both cannot be current. It is a small thing, and the kind of small thing that tells you which numbers on a marketing site have been checked recently. Treat the 100K, the 10M minutes and the named logos as marketing, and judge the product on the trial.
tools.best_for: content teams, agencies and serious podcasters with a steady flow of recorded audio or video who want a transcript plus a stack of derived assets — show notes, newsletters, social posts, clips — from every upload, and who record enough hours to fill a tier
tools.skip_if: you record occasionally, you only need an accurate transcript and nothing downstream of it, or you need a month-to-month price you can read off the page before you sign up

tools.name: ChatGPT AI Product Description
tools.what_it_does: Bulk copy generator for Shopify from Profitonium: product descriptions, titles, meta tags and image alt text for thousands of products at once, in 30+ languages, with custom instruction templates and automatic descriptions on import. Free tier gives 100 credits a month; paid runs $19, $49 or $249 a month for 2,000, 11,000 or 110,000 credits. Live since 2021, rated 4.9 over 466 App Store reviews.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/automated-description-writing) Four tiers, priced in credits per month. Free Trial: 100 credits a month. Basic $19 a month or $190 a year (save 17%): 2,000 credits, product descriptions, titles and meta descriptions, formatted descriptions, automatic descriptions on import. Standard $49 a month or $399 a year (save 32%): 11,000 credits, same feature list. Pro $249 a month or $1,990 a year (save 33%): 110,000 credits, same list plus priority video-call support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Every paid tier carries the same strapline — 'Only $1 per 100 Descriptions' — and it only holds at the bottom of the ladder: $19 for 2,000 credits is 95 cents per hundred, $49 for 11,000 is 45 cents, $249 for 110,000 is 23 cents. So the $1 is a ceiling on the cheapest plan rather than a rate, and it assumes one credit equals one description, which the listing never states. That is the central gap in this pricing: nowhere does the page say what a title, a meta description or an alt text costs in credits, or what the 'Pro Features' that use product images, metadata and web search cost extra. Developer Profitonium, Adugodi, Bangalore; the app launched 12 March 2021, holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge and carries a 4.9 average over 466 App Store reviews.
tools.honest_knock:
First, the name is not a name. 'ChatGPT AI Product Description' describes a category, and on its own listing page Shopify shows 'ChatGPT‑AI Product Description' — a different app by a different developer, also 4.9, also 331 reviews, also with the Built for Shopify badge. Two more competitors on the same page use nearly the same words. Check the developer is Profitonium before you install, because the App Store search results for this phrase are a thicket.

Second, the credit is undefined and it is the only thing you are buying. Four tiers, one variable, no definition — and the '$1 per 100 descriptions' line repeated on all three paid plans is not the rate on two of them.

Third, and the one that costs real money if it goes wrong: this app edits your live store. Its permissions cover product descriptions and titles, Online Store pages and theme, files, locales, Shopify Markets settings, translations and navigation. Bulk generation across thousands of SKUs is exactly the operation you cannot eyeball, and nothing on the listing describes versioning, a preview queue or a rollback. The 466 reviews are genuinely strong: 96% five stars, one two-star, no one-stars, and the substantial ones come from merchants with 30,000 SKUs and over a year of use. But every one of them describes a merchant who was happy with the output, not one who needed to undo it. Export your product CSV before the first bulk run. That is your rollback.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with catalogues in the thousands that need descriptions, titles, meta tags and alt text written in bulk and in several languages, and have the discipline to check a sample before running the whole catalogue
tools.skip_if: you have a small catalogue where 100 free credits a month already covers the new arrivals, or your product copy is a differentiator you would rather write by hand

tools.name: Checkr
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered background check and screening platform for hiring: fast criminal, employment and identity verification with automated adjudication and ATS integrations — speeds up onboarding while staying FCRA-compliant.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Pay-as-you-go per report, no subscription: Basic $29.99, Essential $59.99 and Complete $94.99 per report, with Enterprise quote-only. Tenant screening is priced separately at $24.99, $34.99 and $44.99 per report, and personal checks start from $49.99. Add-ons stack on top: MVR report $9.50 per check, identity verification $4.99 per check, employment verification $59.95 and income plus employment $64.95, billed per verification with no commitment or contract.
tools.honest_knock: The headline per-check price is rarely what you actually pay — passthrough fees vary wildly by county and search type, so budget for the effective cost, not the advertised one. It's overkill unless you hire at real volume.
tools.best_for: companies hiring hourly or gig workers at volume that need fast, API-driven, compliant background checks
tools.skip_if: you hire only a handful of people a year — a one-off check from a simpler provider costs less hassle than onboarding a screening platform

tools.name: ChemiCloud
tools.what_it_does: Lightning-fast cloud hosting with free migrations, daily backups, and 24/7 expert support. Perfect balance of performance and affordability for growing businesses.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-02) Shared hosting starts at $1.95/mo on the September campaign: ChemiCloud's Back to Build sale runs from 2 September 4:00 AM EST to 30 September 11:59 PM EST and prices Starter, Pro and Turbo at $1.95, $2.95 and $3.49 a month on the 36-month term, or $3.49, $4.49 and $4.95 on 12 months. We read it on changeover day, with the outgoing 10th-birthday sale still on the hosting page behind a countdown of under twelve hours at $1.49, $2.49 and $3.49, so the entry price rises by 46 cents as that clock runs out. What did not move in either sale is the renewal, and that is the number that matters: $11.95, $17.95 and $21.95 a month for Starter, Pro and Turbo. Across the rest of the range, reseller starts at $17.95/mo (Kickstart, regular $34.95), managed cloud VPS at $32.95/mo (Cloud 1, regular $59.95, on a 7-day money-back guarantee rather than 45 days), and managed WordPress at $25/mo with a $1 first month, or $12.50/mo billed yearly. Shared plans include a free first-year domain on the 36-month term, free SSL, daily backups and free migration.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the one every budget host shares: the headline price is an introductory rate, and renewals land roughly three times higher, so judge it on the renewal cost, not the sign-up teaser. Support and performance reviews are genuinely strong for the price band, but this is shared/managed hosting — if you need serious dedicated resources or enterprise SLAs, you'll outgrow the cheap tiers. Great value to start, just enter with eyes open on renewal.
tools.best_for: small businesses, freelancers and growing sites that want fast, well-supported managed shared or WordPress hosting at a low starting price
tools.skip_if: you need enterprise-grade dedicated infrastructure and SLAs, or you'll be unhappy when the low intro rate renews at standard pricing
compare_with: comparable managed hosts — ChemiCloud competes hard on intro price and support; compare renewal rates and performance for your stack

tools.name: Circle
tools.what_it_does: Community platform for creator businesses: discussions, courses, events, memberships and messaging in one branded home — plus a no-code website builder, branded iOS/Android apps, email marketing, a member CRM, built-in payments and AI agents that answer member questions.
tools.pricing: (2026) Professional about $89/mo billed annually ($129 monthly), Business $199/mo annual, Enterprise around $419/mo annual, plus a custom Circle Plus tier for fully branded apps. On top of the subscription Circle takes a commission on every sale you make through the platform (roughly 2% on Professional, 1% on Business, 0.5% on Plus) plus standard Stripe/PayPal processing, and the Email Hub is a paid add-on around $99/mo for 10,000 contacts. 14-day free trial, but no always-free option.
tools.honest_knock: The sticker is only the entry: Circle keeps a commission on every sale on top of Stripe's processing fees, and email marketing is a separate add-on — so a monetized community's real bill runs meaningfully past the plan price. Model it at your actual sales volume before choosing a tier.
tools.best_for: creators and brands running a paid community — courses, memberships, events and discussions in one branded home, with a built-in payments stack and even branded mobile apps
tools.skip_if: you only need a casual chat space (Discord-style) or your margins are thin on high sales volume — the platform commission plus processing fees stack against you
compare_with: Skool wins on radical simplicity and flat pricing, Mighty Networks on affordable entry; Circle wins on breadth: branded apps, email, CRM, AI agents and a real payments stack

tools.name: Claap
tools.what_it_does: AI sales intelligence that records calls without putting a bot in the meeting, then turns them into CRM fields, follow-up emails, deal scoring and coaching. Basic is free; Pro is €24 per license a month on annual billing (€30 monthly); Business, which holds the CRM and coaching features, is €48 (€60 monthly) and quote-led.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-04 on claap.io/pricing, both billing toggles and the full comparison table) Priced per license per month, in euros, with no dollar column anywhere on the page. Basic is €0: 10 videos per user, 300 minutes of recording in total rather than per month, calendar and conference-call sync, 99-language transcript, basic AI summary, the Chrome recorder extension and a collaborative workspace, capped at 5 licenses, no guests, one team, one channel, 3 video uploads and 3 months of recording storage. Pro is €24 per license a month billed yearly or €30 monthly: unlimited recordings, 1,000 minutes a month, 500 AI credits per license pooled across the workspace, advanced AI summaries, meeting insights, AI video editing, 10+ integrations, speaker and video insights and private channels, with 50 licenses, 50 guests, 10 uploads a month and 2 years of storage. Business is €48 per license a month yearly or €60 monthly: unlimited recording time, 1,000 AI credits per license, Claap AI across all meetings, CRM auto-complete, AI-generated emails, AI coaching, deal insights, smart tables, admin recording controls and priority support, with 50 uploads a month and 3 years of storage. Enterprise is a custom price and adds SSO through Okta, SCIM provisioning, unlimited Basic licenses, white-glove onboarding and migration support. Basic carries a Try for free button and Pro a Start now button; Business and Enterprise both say Contact us, and the pricing FAQ states that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team.
tools.honest_knock:
The four tiers sell two different products, and only one of them is self-serve. Pro at €24 is the recorder and note-taker. Everything Claap actually markets itself on — CRM auto-complete, AI coaching, deal insights, asking Claap AI a question across all your meetings — starts at Business, €48 per license a month on annual billing, and Business is the only paid tier with no Start now button: it says Contact us. The pricing FAQ closes the other door too, stating that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team. So the features you came for cannot be bought or tested without a sales conversation.

Your recordings also expire. Storage runs 3 months on Basic, 2 years on Pro and 3 years on Business; only Enterprise is unlimited. If the call archive is meant to be your evidence trail, that is a deletion date on your own data, and it is in the comparison table rather than in the plan cards.

Two smaller things worth reading twice. The AI credits that power the summaries and coaching — 500 per license on Pro, 1,000 on Business, pooled across the workspace — have no published top-up rate anywhere on the page, so there is no way to price a heavy month before you commit. And the free tier's 300 minutes is a total, not a monthly allowance: it is a sample, not a plan you can sit on.
tools.best_for: revenue teams that want every call captured without a notetaker bot joining the meeting, and want those calls to end up as CRM fields, coaching and deal signals rather than as transcripts nobody reopens — with enough seats to make a sales conversation worth having
tools.skip_if: you want to buy and test the product yourself, because the tier with the CRM and coaching features is quote-led and even its trial runs through sales; you need a long retention window, since recordings age out after 2 or 3 years below Enterprise; or you need to be billed in dollars
compare_with: Both record and transcribe meetings and both sit in our database, but they aim at different jobs. Fireflies is the cheaper, broader meeting assistant: it joins the call as a bot, transcribes and summarises, and works for any team that takes notes. Claap is built for revenue teams specifically, records without a bot in the conversation, and puts its money on what happens after the call — CRM fields, deal scoring against MEDDIC or BANT, coaching. Pick Fireflies if you want meetings captured cheaply across the company; pick Claap if your problem is an empty CRM and untrained reps, and you can live with the sales-led purchase.

tools.name: Claude
tools.what_it_does: Anthropic's AI assistant for writing, coding, analysis and long-document work — strong reasoning and a careful, direct tone rather than an eager-to-please one. Free tier plus Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans, and a per-token API (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) for builders.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-27 on their own pricing page) The free tier is $0. Pro is $17/month with the annual discount ($200 billed up front) or $20 billed monthly, and includes Claude Code and unlimited projects. Max starts at $100/month for 5x or 20x the usage of Pro per five-hour session. Team is for teams of 2 to 150: a standard seat is $20/seat/month billed annually ($25 monthly), and a premium seat is $100/seat/month billed annually ($125 monthly) for 5x the usage of a standard seat, adding Claude Code and Claude Cowork. Enterprise self-serve is $20/seat plus usage billed at API rates, so cost scales with the models and tasks the team runs; larger contracts are custom via sales. The API is separate and billed per token across the Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models, with platform features priced on top: Managed Agents at $0.08 per session-hour of active runtime, web search at $10 per 1,000 searches, and code execution beyond the 50 free hours a day at $0.05 per hour per container.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is usage limits: even on Pro you can hit a ceiling mid-session on a heavy day, and the step up to Max is a real $100 to $200 a month — you're buying headroom, not extra features. It also doesn't generate images, so if that's your main need it's the wrong tool, and its third-party plugin ecosystem is smaller than ChatGPT's.
tools.best_for: developers, writers, analysts and researchers who want best-in-class reasoning, coding and long-document work — and a model that's careful and direct rather than eager to please
tools.skip_if: you mainly need image generation or the widest third-party plugin ecosystem (a general assistant like ChatGPT fits better there), or you're a light user the free tier already covers
compare_with: ChatGPT leads on image generation and third-party plugins, Gemini on native Google Workspace integration — Claude's edge is reasoning depth, coding, long context and writing quality

tools.name: Clay
tools.what_it_does: Waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows for go-to-market teams. It enriches rather than sends, so you still need a separate email tool. From about $185/month (Launch, 2,500 credits) to $495 (Growth), with credit spend that is hard to forecast and a two-to-four-week learning curve.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page; the model has changed since most write-ups, ours included) Clay now meters two things separately: actions and data credits, and each plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier. The entry paid plan is $167/mo billed monthly, starting at 15,000 actions a month. The volume ladder runs $60, $150, $200, $290 and $540 a month for 15K, 40K, 60K, 100K and 200K actions monthly. Billed annually, the same ladder starts at $54/mo for 180K actions a year and runs to $486/mo for 2.4M. The recommended plan is $446/mo starting at 40,000 actions a month, expanding from $185/mo annually. Data credits are a separate meter again: from $125/mo for 2,500 credits a month up to $2,125/mo for 50,000, or $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.
tools.best_for: modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it
tools.skip_if: you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users

tools.name: ClickUp
tools.what_it_does: The 'everything app' for project and work management. Centralize your tasks, docs, sprints, and team communication in one hub.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page with both billing tabs open) A Free Forever plan with unlimited tasks but 60MB of storage; Unlimited $7 and Business $12 per user/month billed yearly, which are $10 and $19 billed monthly; Enterprise is quote-only. AI is priced on top of the plan: Brain AI $9 and Everything AI $28 per user/month.
tools.honest_knock: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Powerful and cheap per seat, but only if you'll actually configure and adopt it.
tools.best_for: teams that want one highly customizable app for tasks, docs, goals and reporting and will invest in setting it up
tools.skip_if: you want something simple your team adopts in a day — ClickUp's depth becomes overwhelm for a light use case

tools.name: Clonable
tools.what_it_does: Creates a continuously-translated clone of your existing website — fast multilingual versions that stay synced as your site changes, without rebuilding it.
tools.pricing: Read in a browser on clonable.net/pricing on 5 September 2026 (the page blocks plain fetches), monthly view in euros: Free at €0 for 1 clone and up to 20 translated pages (50 pages for €25 a month), Business €49 for 3 clones and 400 pages, Pro €79 for 5 clones and 1,200 pages, Expert €249 for 10 clones and 5,000 pages, Premium €999 for 20 clones and 50,000 pages. An extra clone with its pages is €25 a month (€50 on Expert and Premium); optional setup assistance is €250 (€1,000 on Premium). Annual billing is cheaper and there is a separate ladder for online stores.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest caveats. First, it's a continuous subscription, not a one-time translation — you pay ongoing to keep the translated clone synced with your site. Second, it's machine translation under the hood, so quality varies by language pair; always have a native speaker spot-check high-stakes pages. (Public pricing was gated at research time — confirm current tiers yourself.)
tools.best_for: businesses that want a fast, continuously-updated translated version of an existing website without rebuilding it as a multilingual site
tools.skip_if: you need human-quality translation for legal, medical or brand-critical copy, or you only need a one-off translation rather than an ongoing synced clone
compare_with: Weglot is the established website-translation layer with published pricing; Clonable positions as a full continuously-synced clone — both are subscription localization, and both need a human spot-check on quality

tools.name: Cloro
tools.what_it_does: API that reads AI search engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini, Grok, AI Overview and Google Search — and returns the sources and citations behind every query as structured JSON.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on cloro.dev/pricing) Credit-metered, and the credit table matters more than the plan price. Free is $0 for 500 credits a month, one concurrent job and one seat. Paid runs Lite $30 (37,500 credits, $0.80 per 1k, 10 concurrent jobs), Hobby $100 (250,000, $0.40, 20 jobs) and Starter $250 (650,000, $0.39, 50 jobs). Above that come Growth $500 (1,350,000, $0.37, 75 jobs) and Business $1,000 (2,800,000, $0.36, 100 jobs). Then four Enterprise steps run from $2,000 to $5,000, where the rate falls to $0.31 and concurrency reaches 255. Seats are unlimited from Lite up. What a request costs varies by engine. ChatGPT full response is 7 credits, ChatGPT web search 5, Copilot 5, and AI Overview including the SERP 5. Grok is 4, AI Mode 4, Gemini 4, Perplexity 3, and Google Search and Google News 3 plus 2 per extra page. A synchronous call adds 2 credits on top of all of those.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is a sampler, not a trial of the real thing: 500 credits is about 100 async ChatGPT answers at the 5-credit rate we were actually charged, and their table lists 7 for a full response. Fewer, if you call it synchronously — and one concurrent job means you queue. Anyone running a daily visibility check across a hundred keywords burns through it in about two days. Read the credit table before the price table — the same $100 buys 250,000 credits, which is 35,700 full ChatGPT calls or 83,000 Perplexity ones, so your engine mix decides your bill more than your plan does.
tools.best_for: SEO and marketing teams who need AI-search visibility as structured data — who gets cited for which query on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Google's AI Overview — rather than as a dashboard someone else designed
tools.skip_if: you want a finished rank-tracking dashboard rather than an API; this returns JSON with markdown, sources and citations, and you build the reporting yourself

tools.name: Close
tools.what_it_does: Sales CRM unifying calling, email and SMS in one inbox, for teams that live on the phone. Seats run about $9 (Solo) to $139 (Scale) per user/month billed annually, and call, SMS and Power Dialer credits bill separately on top — a $99 plan can land nearer $160 once a rep dials all day.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page) Per-seat: Solo $19, Essentials $49, Growth $109 and Scale $149 per user/mo, or $9, $35, $99 and $139 billed annually. No free plan; the trial runs 14 days and close.com states no credit card is required, with $5 of calling and enrichment credits included, and the page carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. AI credits are pooled per tier (500 a month on Solo, then 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 per user up to 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000). Call minutes, SMS and dialer credits are billed separately, and can meaningfully raise the real cost. Outbound calls run about $0.02 a minute, phone lines start at about $1 a month, and premium numbers are $19 a month per line. The Call Assistant add-on is $50 a month per organisation plus $0.02 a minute.
tools.honest_knock: The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.
tools.best_for: inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place
tools.skip_if: your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you

tools.name: CloudTalk
tools.what_it_does: Cloud call centre with call routing, analytics and CRM integrations, from €19/user/month on annual billing (Expert €49 needs at least three licences). AI voice agents are separate subscriptions from €99/month for 200 minutes, and number rental plus outbound minutes stack on top of the seat price.
tools.pricing: Lite €19, Starter €25, Essential €29 and Expert €49 per user/mo on annual billing, and Expert needs at least 3 licences (re-verified 2026-08-16). The add-ons are where the bill grows: Power Dialer €15 per user/mo (already included in Expert), Parallel Dialer €39 per user/mo, AI Conversation Intelligence €9 per user/mo. AI voice agents are separate subscriptions: AI Receptionist from €99/mo with 200 minutes, AI Specialist €349/mo with 1,000 minutes, and above 10,000 minutes a month custom pricing CloudTalk advertises as low as €0.15 per minute. There is a 14-day trial that includes 50 AI voice agent minutes. Note the page quotes us in euros from an EU address while the same page carries a $99 figure for the same AI bundle. CloudTalk told us on 31 August 2026 that this is deliberate rather than a display error: they hold the same number in both currencies instead of converting at the exchange rate, so €99 and $99 buy the same bundle. Confirm the currency at your own checkout.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price is only part of it — number rental, outbound minutes and the AI add-ons stack on top, so a call-heavy team's real bill runs above the plan rate. Solid CRM integrations, but model your call volume first.
tools.best_for: support and sales teams that want a cloud call center with strong CRM integrations and call analytics
tools.skip_if: you make only occasional calls — a basic VoIP line or your CRM's built-in dialer costs far less

tools.name: CloudTask
tools.what_it_does: Managed marketplace for LATAM go-to-market hires — SDRs, BDRs and similar — with payroll and compliance handled. $299/month membership, plus an all-in monthly rate per hire that is not published. Direct Hire instead costs 30% of first-year salary.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-19, read on their own pricing page) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No. There is a one-time $299 deposit to start your search. That is the only fee outside the models above.” — and the deposit applies toward your buyout or your first placement. Direct Hire costs 20% to 30% of first-year base salary, paid once and quoted per role, with a 6-month replacement guarantee (one replacement, same job description) and US W2 employment available. Managed Staffing is billed as one all-in monthly rate per person covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that decides what this costs. It carries a 24-month replacement guarantee with replacements not capped, and time and activity tracking on by default, which the hire agrees to before matching and you can switch off when you post the role. Graduating a managed hire onto your own payroll is possible after six months for a one-time placement fee quoted at that moment; no amount is published. Health and equipment benefits are available on request on Managed Staffing only.
tools.honest_knock: The $299 is the honest part and also the small part: their FAQ calls it a one-time deposit to start a search, denies any monthly platform fee, and says it goes toward your first placement. What you will actually spend is the all-in monthly rate per hire, and that figure appears nowhere on the pricing page — you get it after you talk to them, once you are already invested in the process. Work out before you start what a comparable LATAM salary is on your own, so you can see what the managed layer costs on top. The exit is worth reading twice too. After six months you can graduate a managed hire onto your own payroll, but the placement fee for doing so is quoted at the time and no amount is published. So the price of keeping the person is a number you cannot check in advance.
tools.best_for: companies hiring GTM roles — SDRs, BDRs and similar — who want LATAM talent without setting up their own payroll and compliance in another country, and who value the 24-month replacement guarantee
tools.skip_if: you only need one hire ever, where Direct Hire's one-time 20-30% fee is cleaner than a managed monthly rate; also skip it if you cannot get the all-in monthly rate in writing before you commit
compare_with: the comparison worth doing, because they solve overlapping problems from opposite ends. Deel publishes its floors and handles employment for people you already found; CloudTask finds the people and wraps employment around them, but does not publish the all-in rate. Decide by whether your bottleneck is sourcing or paperwork, then insist on the missing number

tools.name: Cloudways
tools.what_it_does: Managed-hosting layer that rents you servers on DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS or Google Cloud through one dashboard, with the stack, caching, staging, cloning, backups and 24/7 platform support pre-built on top. You buy a server and put as many sites on it as it holds — no per-site plans and no visit metering — billed hourly and invoiced monthly in arrears with no contract. The trade is control: Cloudways' own documentation states there is no root access and no bring-your-own cloud account, so the server lives in Cloudways' name. Owned by DigitalOcean since September 2022.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on cloudways.com/en/pricing.php, DigitalOcean tab) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required. Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract — and the hourly figure is the one that decides the bill: every card divides its monthly price by 672 hours, so $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan. The page now opens on DigitalOcean's Premium (NVMe) column, where Micro is 1GB RAM / 1 vCPU / 25GB NVMe / 1TB bandwidth at $14/month, Small 2GB / 1 vCPU / 50GB NVMe / 2TB at $28, Medium 4GB / 2 vCPU / 80GB / 4TB at $54 and Large 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB at $99. Two of those have moved since July: the entry machine is now half the size for three dollars more (July's Micro was 2GB / 50GB at $11), and the 8GB plan went from $88 to $99. Switch the column to Standard and that same 2GB / 50GB box reads $11 a month — but the hourly figure printed underneath it, $0.0357, works out to $24 at the 672-hour month the other cards use, so the two numbers on that one card cannot both be right; read the live estimate before you commit. Bought direct from DigitalOcean on the same day, an 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB droplet lists at $0.07143 an hour, $48 a month. Add-ons are monthly and separate: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN from $4.99 per domain, Site Manager from $3 per app, Malware Protection from $4 per app, Rackspace email $1 per mailbox, DNS Made Easy $0.50 per domain, offsite backup storage $0.033 per GB. Advance Support is $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, with a limited-time flat rate of $25/month advertised on the page today; the $500 Premium Support tier we recorded in July is no longer listed there. Cloudways Autonomous, the separate autoscaling product, now prices at $35, $240 and $995 a month where July's page showed $99, $199 and $399, and it meters unique visits and bandwidth rather than RAM (30k visits and 100GB on Small, 70k and 200GB on Medium) with a 3-day free trial. Markups on AWS and Google Cloud still cannot be calculated because Cloudways does not publish the underlying instance types. A site-wide banner advertises 40% off for four months until 15 September 2026 — promotions move, so read the live price. US list prices, excluding tax.
tools.honest_knock: "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is. Cloudways' own support page puts infrastructure and platform work in the included tier but treats application help as guidance only. Plugin and theme troubleshooting, database work and performance tuning sit behind Advanced Support at $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum. On a small server that add-on costs more than the server it supports. Content changes, custom code debugging and code audits stay out of scope on every tier, paid ones included. The deeper catch is ownership: Cloudways documents that you get no root access and cannot use your own cloud credentials, so the machine sits in Cloudways' account — you cannot fire the management layer and keep the server, you migrate. And read the billing terms before you rely on it: their help centre states that an unpaid invoice restricts server access and can lead to the server and its backups being deleted, with backups kept for only 14 days after deletion.
tools.best_for: agencies and PHP shops running many sites who want servers managed but not metered. One server holds as many sites as it can carry with no visit caps, billing is hourly and post-paid with no annual term, and Magento and Laravel are first-class alongside WordPress. It suits teams who genuinely do not want anyone patching kernels at 2am
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable in a terminal, or you run a single small site. Going direct to the cloud provider with your own control panel keeps the server in your own account for materially less. And one low-traffic site is better served by shared hosting, or by a per-site managed host that bundles CDN and application support. Cloudways also has no email hosting of its own, reselling a Rackspace add-on instead
compare_with: Going direct on DigitalOcean with your own control panel

DigitalOcean owns Cloudways and sells both sides, which makes this the honest comparison: the same 8GB machine is $48/month as a droplet and $99/month wrapped in Cloudways. Add DigitalOcean's own daily backups and a control-panel licence and a like-for-like self-managed box lands nearer $75-80, so the real premium is smaller than the sticker gap suggests. The decisive difference is not price but ownership: with your own droplet the account and root are yours and you can drop the panel and keep the server, whereas leaving Cloudways is a migration

tools.name: Cloze
tools.what_it_does: AI shopping assistant for Shopify: a chat widget wired to your live catalogue, inventory and knowledge base that answers product questions, compares items, tracks orders and hands off to a human. Free for 25 conversations a month; paid runs $49, $99 or $199 a month on the App Store, with extra conversations at $0.10. New listing: no reviews yet as of 19 Aug 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19, re-verified unchanged 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/cloze, listed as “Cloze: AI Shopping Assistant”) Free plan available: 25 AI conversations a month, up to 100 synced products, core assistant customisation and 7 days of conversation history. Paid tiers are Starter $49, Pro $99 and Scale $199 a month, each with $0.10 per additional AI conversation and a 3-day free trial. Starter covers 250 conversations a month and 1,000 synced products, with full customisation and 30 days of insights. Pro covers 750 conversations and 10,000 products with advanced insights and 90 days of history, and Scale 2,000 conversations, unlimited products, a year of history and priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing before you install. The vendor's own site, cloze.bot/pricing, advertised a different and cheaper ladder on the same day: Free forever with 50 conversations a month, Pro $29 a month and Business $79 a month. On that page both paid tiers say unlimited conversations rather than a monthly allowance. Our link goes to the App Store listing, so the $49/$99/$199 ladder, with its caps of 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations, is what you pay when you install there. The screenshot further down is their own page exactly as we captured it. Developer Optify, Lyon, France; the app launched 24 April 2026, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and had no reviews at all at the time of writing. Re-read on 4 September 2026: both ladders still stood exactly as described above, and the listing had gained its first review — a single five-star note left on 14 August 2026 by a French store eight days in.
tools.honest_knock: Two things to weigh, and the first is the price itself. On the same day, the App Store listing sold this at $49, $99 and $199 a month for 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations. The vendor's own site sold it at $29 and $79, with unlimited conversations on both paid tiers. The screenshot below is that page. Two prices and two different meters for one product is not a discount you can claim, it is an inconsistency to ask about before you pay. The second is the track record, or the absence of one. The app launched 24 April 2026 and, as of 4 September 2026, carries exactly one review — five stars, left after eight days of use. So there is next to no merchant experience to lean on, and the “Built for Shopify” badge is a technical bar, not a verdict on the answers. Also note what a conversation costs when it goes wrong. An assistant wired to live inventory and order tracking is answering with your data, and the free tier's 25 conversations a month is enough to test the tone but not enough to see it handle a bad day. The 3-day trial on paid plans is short for a support tool.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a catalogue big enough that shoppers ask which item to buy, who want a chat assistant that reads live inventory and hands off to a person, and who will watch the transcripts
tools.skip_if: your support volume is low, or you want proof from other merchants before you put an AI in front of customers — there are no reviews yet

tools.name: Clutch
tools.what_it_does: B2B services marketplace — submit a free project brief and get matched with verified, best-fit agencies for your project, no research required.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read in their own help centre) Free for buyers. Clutch's help centre describes the Project Brief as the buyer's route in and says it goes to up to 9 service providers that best match your project requirements, with no fee named anywhere in that flow. Clutch is a B2B services marketplace — the providers being listed pay for visibility, the buyer does not. A free provider profile covers the listing, client review collection, badges and widgets, contributed content, awards eligibility and a profile on sister-site The Manifest; Sponsorship, Featured Listings and Clutch Verified are the paid upgrades on top.
tools.honest_knock: It's genuinely free to submit a brief — but be clear on what it is: a lead-generation marketplace, not a neutral directory. Your brief goes straight to agencies who will reach out to pitch you, and providers pay to be visible and matched. It's a fast way to shortlist vetted agencies; just expect the outreach that comes with it.
tools.best_for: businesses that want to skip manual agency research and get matched quickly with vetted, best-fit service providers for a specific project
tools.skip_if: you already have trusted agency relationships, or you'd rather research independently without agencies contacting you
compare_with: G2 and traditional directories make you scroll and compare yourself; Clutch's brief-matching narrows it to a handful of vetted providers fast — the trade-off is that it's a matching marketplace where you'll field agency outreach

tools.name: Code Bulk Discounts
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app (by Optizio) that turns a discount you have already created into thousands of unique codes and exports them as CSV for email and SMS campaigns. Free covers 500 lifetime codes; Pro is $14.99 a month for unlimited codes.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/code-bulk) Two plans, billed in USD every 30 days. Free costs nothing and covers 500 lifetime codes with CSV export. Pro is $14.99 a month and lifts that to unlimited codes per month, with the same CSV export; both plans say they work with most discount applications. The plan table lists no annual rate, no free trial on Pro and no per-code charge, so the monthly figure is the whole cost.
tools.honest_knock: Read the free plan's number twice, because the word doing the work is 'lifetime': it is 500 codes in total, not 500 a month. One influencer drop or one email segment can spend the whole allowance in an afternoon, and after that the only way on is $14.99 a month — so the free tier is a sample, not a plan. What the app does is also narrower than the word 'discounts' suggests. It takes a discount you have already created and multiplies it into unique codes you export as a CSV. It does not create the discount rule, does not send the codes to anyone, and does not report which ones were redeemed, so it sits between your discount settings and your email or SMS tool and needs both of those to be worth anything. The 4.9 rating also rests on 40 reviews, which is a thin record next to the app's peers.
tools.best_for: shopify stores that already run email or SMS campaigns and need thousands of unique, single-use codes generated out of one existing discount and handed over as a CSV
tools.skip_if: you need one or two codes, which Shopify's own discount screen already gives you at no cost — or the campaign itself is what you want, because this app generates and exports the codes and stops there
compare_with: Both come out of the Shopify discount aisle and both generate bulk codes, but they are priced for different problems. Code Bulk Discounts does one job — turn an existing discount into unique codes and export them — and asks $14.99 a month once the 500 lifetime free codes run out. Kite treats bulk codes as one feature among many and puts them behind $29 a month, with the code ceilings rising by tier. So if codes are the whole requirement, Code Bulk is the cheaper and simpler answer and there is nothing to grow into. If you also want the discount mechanics themselves — free gifts, BOGO, tiered pricing, progress bars — Code Bulk cannot build any of them and Kite is the one that can.

tools.name: Cognism
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact data with a GDPR focus — phone-verified mobile numbers and intent signals.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Two named plans, Standard and Pro, both stated to include 5 seats, with everything routed to 'Talk to sales' and 'Get a personalised quote'. The model is credit-based — their own wording is that 1 credit equals 1 revealed contact — with credits included in the subscription per seat, but no allowance is published. CRM Enrichment is sold standalone or as an add-on; Data-as-a-Service is priced by volume and delivery method.
tools.honest_knock: No price, no credit allowance, and a five-seat minimum on both named plans. That combination means the smallest deal is five seats of something you cannot price, so budget conversations start with a sales call rather than a number. The credit model is the part to nail down: one credit reveals one contact, so your real cost per usable lead is the credit price divided by your connect rate, and neither figure is published. Before the call, work out how many contacts a month you actually reveal — that is the only number that lets you judge the quote you get. And it is worth asking whether unused credits roll over, because nothing on the page says.
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams in Europe who need mobile numbers that are actually verified and care about GDPR provenance — that is the specific thing this is better at
tools.skip_if: you are one or two people prospecting, because both named plans include five seats; also skip it if your market is US-only, where the data advantage is smaller and cheaper options exist
compare_with: the standing comparison in B2B data — Apollo publishes its prices, which makes it the honest starting benchmark for whatever Cognism quotes you

tools.name: CometChat
tools.what_it_does: In-app text, voice and video chat infrastructure to embed into your own software — secure and scalable, with a free developer plan and, via the new Air release, fully on-prem or air-gapped deployment for regulated enterprises.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against CometChat's own machine-readable pricing reference, which they publish for AI agents and last verified themselves on 2026-05-20; USD) Build is free for development: all features, up to 100 users and 25 concurrent connections, no card. Paid Chat plans are priced by monthly active users. Billed yearly, shown as a monthly equivalent: at 1,000 MAU Basic is $239 and Advanced $359; at 10,000 MAU Basic $299, Advanced $399 and Enterprise $999; at 25,000 MAU $699 and $949; at 50,000 MAU $1,349 and $1,649. Paying monthly costs about 20% more — $298.75 and $448.75 at 1,000 MAU. Above 50,000 MAU everything is quote-only. Concurrency is included at 5% of your MAU on Basic and Advanced and 10% on Enterprise. On overage CometChat charges $0.10 per extra MAU (falling at higher tiers) or $1 per extra concurrent connection — and where both are exceeded it bills the higher of the two, not both. Enterprise has no listed overage; usage above the plan is upgraded to the appropriate plan instead. Messages and storage are unlimited on every plan, and message retention is 6 months across the board, extendable at extra cost.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing cliff is the honest headline: from a 100-MAU free tier straight to ~$239/mo is a brutal jump for an early-stage app, and users report plan structures changing under them. Model your MAU growth curve and the overage math before you architect around it. Chat infrastructure is sticky by nature; the time to compare vendors is before launch, not after.
tools.best_for: product teams that want proven in-app text/voice/video chat with SDKs for every major framework, without building messaging infrastructure themselves
tools.skip_if: your app is pre-revenue with growing users (the free-to-paid cliff will hit mid-growth), or chat is peripheral enough that a support widget covers it
compare_with: the premium chat-SDK peers — all three are MAU-priced; compare at YOUR projected MAU including overages, not at the entry tier

tools.name: Compliancely
tools.what_it_does: Compliance and verification API for US businesses and individuals: real-time and bulk IRS TIN matching, KYB business verification, USPS address and Secretary of State lookups, Form I-9 and E-Verify, consent-based IRS tax transcript retrieval, and ongoing OFAC, watchlist and FATCA monitoring. Built by Zenwork, the company behind Tax1099.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-29, re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. Billed annually, Essential 25 is $16.95/mo for 25 monthly TIN verifications ($0.67 per match), Essential 50 $32.54/mo ($0.65), Essential 75 $45.79/mo ($0.61), Plus 100 $57.99/mo ($0.57) and Plus 250 $135.04/mo ($0.54). Switch the toggle to monthly billing and the same five tiers read $19.95, $38.49, $53.95, $67.95 and $159.95 per month, at $0.79 down to $0.63 per match. The page advertises 15% off for annual billing, and the real gap holds at roughly 15% on every tier. Enterprise is quote-only. Everything else Compliancely sells carries no public price at all: the business verification and credit-risk report packages, address verification, Form I-9, IRS tax transcripts and income verification each end in Contact Sales or Book a Demo rather than a number. Compliancely's partner team told us on 5 August 2026 that the published tiers are meant for buyers up to roughly 3,000 checks and that anything above that moves to a custom quote — that threshold is theirs, not a number the pricing page states. They confirmed on 11 August 2026 that buyers over that line are sent to their demo-request form at compliancely.com/demo-request, where the quote is written by hand; there is no published rate card for that range at all.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a dozen. Every tier you can actually buy online is an allowance of TIN verifications. The moment you want the things the homepage leads with — KYB business verification, credit-risk assessment, address verification, Form I-9 and E-Verify, IRS tax transcripts, OFAC and watchlist monitoring — the button changes from Get Started to Contact Sales. So the compliance stack this tool is pitched as has no advertised cost, and the number you can see is the smallest part of it. The second thing to read carefully is that the tiers are allowances rather than rates. You commit to a monthly verification count up front, and the per-match price moves against the smallest buyers. It is $0.79 a check on the cheapest month-to-month plan versus $0.54 on the largest annual one — a 46% spread that falls the wrong way for anyone testing the product at low volume. If your usage is lumpy — a filing-season spike and eleven quiet months — an allowance you buy every month is the wrong shape, and the prepaid option the page offers as a third toggle is worth asking about before you subscribe.
tools.best_for: finance, tax and HR teams with a steady monthly volume of US identity and business checks, who would rather buy TIN matching, KYB, I-9 and sanctions screening behind one API than integrate three separate vendors. It suits those willing to run a sales conversation to price the modules beyond TIN matching
tools.skip_if: you need a handful of one-off verifications a year. The cheapest plan still bills a monthly allowance whether you use it or not, and the per-match rate is at its worst down there. Also skip it if you need the full cost of a compliance stack on paper before you talk to a salesperson, since only the TIN-match tiers are published
compare_with: the honest head-to-head is Checkr, which owns one slice of what Compliancely does — employment and identity screening — and owns it with the more mature product and public self-serve pricing. If background checks are the job, Checkr wins; Compliancely is the broader bet when IRS TIN matching and KYB sit at the centre of the workflow rather than hiring. Tax1099 belongs in the conversation for an odder reason: it is family. Zenwork, Inc. is named in Compliancely's own footer and builds Tax1099 too, so the filing product and the verification product come out of one house — complements rather than rivals, and worth raising as an integration question before you price either. Verify both current price lists yourself; ours were read on 2026-07-29.

tools.name: Connecteam
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one app for managing deskless teams. Scheduling, time clock, tasks, training and team chat for hourly and frontline workforces.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) The free tier is real and not a trial: the Small Business Plan is $0 for life, covers up to 10 users and includes all hubs and features. Above that you buy per hub — Operations, Communications or HR — and each hub is priced for the first 30 users with a per-user surcharge after that. The published per-user rates run from $0.50 to $5.00 a month depending on hub and tier, with the yearly and monthly columns shown side by side. The cheapest paid entry is well under a dollar per user a month at the Basic level, which is why the headline looks so low against competitors. Price it per hub you will actually switch on, not per user.
tools.honest_knock: The free-for-10 plan is one of the most generous in the category, but the three-hub structure means costs can stack if you need all of them — price the specific hubs you'll actually use, not the full bundle.
tools.best_for: deskless and frontline teams (shift work, field crews) that need scheduling, a time clock and comms in one app, on the free-for-10 plan
tools.skip_if: your whole team sits at desks with email and Slack — this is built for the frontline, and a general PM tool fits an office better

tools.name: Consensus
tools.what_it_does: AI search across peer-reviewed literature: it reports what published studies found, not whether those studies are sound. A free tier covers basic search; Pro is about $15/month, or roughly $10 billed annually. Study quality and conflicting results still need your own judgment.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) Consensus blocks plain fetches of its pricing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount, so today's figures are not independently confirmed. Our dated reading: a free tier with essential search; Pro about $15/mo, or roughly $10/mo billed annually, with unlimited Pro searches and 15 Deep searches; a Deep tier adding around 200 Deep searches for power users; Teams and Enterprise quoted. The unit that matters is Deep searches rather than seats — that is what the tiers ration.
tools.honest_knock: It searches peer-reviewed literature, which is its strength and its boundary: it can tell you what published studies found, not whether those studies are good. Study quality, sample sizes and conflicting results still need your judgment, and the AI summary layer can smooth over genuine scientific disagreement. Treat it as a dramatically faster literature scan, not an oracle; click through to the papers that matter.
tools.best_for: researchers, clinicians, students and writers who want evidence-backed answers drawn from peer-reviewed papers instead of the open web
tools.skip_if: your questions are practical/commercial rather than research-based (a general AI assistant fits), or you need full systematic-review rigor (this accelerates it, not replaces it)
compare_with: the research-AI peer set — Consensus leans consumer-friendly consensus summaries; Elicit leans structured extraction for reviews

tools.name: Consentmo
tools.what_it_does: Shopify consent app that geolocates the visitor and shows the right GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA or LGPD banner, with Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok signals, cookie scanning and data-request pages — plus an accessibility widget and scanner from the Plus tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier. Free plan; Standard $10 a month or $100 a year, Plus $37 or $370, Enterprise $64 or $640. Read 8 Sep 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/gdpr-backpack and on the vendor's own consentmo.com/pricing, which list the same four tiers) Billed in USD every 30 days, with a 7-day free trial on each paid tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier, the free one included, so the ladder gates features rather than traffic. Free costs nothing and covers the cookie banner and preferences, the data-request and Do-Not-Sell pages, one banner language and one cookie scan a month, with minimal Consentmo branding on the banner. Standard is $10 a month or $100 a year (17% off) and adds unlimited cookie scans, multi-region compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA and others), Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok integrations, US opt-out signals, script blocking, multilingual banners with automatic detection, automatic Google Drive backups and removal of the branding. Plus is $37 or $370 a year and is where the accessibility side starts: web accessibility (ADA/WCAG), smart geotargeting, the EU withdrawal page for Directive 2023/2673, automated monitoring, scheduled scans, AI cookie categorisation, advanced analytics and full CSS customisation. Enterprise is $64 or $640 a year for IAB TCF 2.3, cross-domain consent sharing, a checkout banner for Shopify Plus, Hydrogen and headless support, A/B testing, an alt-text manager, bot and crawler protection and priority support.
tools.honest_knock: Read the ladder before you budget $10 for this. The two things the listing leads with — web accessibility and a smart, region-specific banner — are not on Standard; they start at Plus, $37 a month, which is 3.7 times the entry price. A Shopify Plus store that wants a banner on the checkout needs Enterprise at $64, and so does anything headless or on Hydrogen. The accessibility side is a widget and a scanner: it overlays controls and flags issues, but it does not change the theme markup underneath, which is where an accessibility audit actually looks — treat it as a first layer, not as a remediation. And the free tier puts Consentmo's own branding on the banner your visitors see first.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants selling into several jurisdictions who want one app to carry the cookie banner, the consent signals the ad platforms now demand, and a first layer of accessibility — and who go in knowing that the region-aware banner and the accessibility tools sit on the $37 tier.
tools.skip_if: you sell outside Shopify; you need one plain cookie banner in one country, which the free tier or your theme already covers; or you need an actual accessibility audit and repair of your theme rather than a widget and a scanner.
compare_with: these two only look alike on the accessibility line. accessiBe sells accessibility as its whole product, on any site, and goes deeper than a widget; Consentmo sells consent as its whole product and adds accessibility from the $37 tier up. So if accessibility is the reason you are shopping, Consentmo's Plus tier is a starting layer rather than a replacement. If consent is the reason, the two are not in the same market at all: the cookie banner, the geotargeting and the Consent Mode integrations are what Consentmo is for, and they are not what accessiBe sells

tools.name: Contractor Foreman
tools.what_it_does: Construction management — estimating, scheduling, daily logs and financial tracking — priced per company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier. Annual runs $49/month for one user up to $332 for unlimited; quarterly billing costs about 26% more and Basic is annual-only.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 28 Aug 2026 on their own pricing page; all plan prices unchanged since 1 Aug 2026) Priced for the company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier, and every plan opens with 30 days free before the first bill. Annual: Basic $49/month ($588 a year, 1 user), Standard $105 ($1,264, 3 users), Plus $166 ($1,997, 8 users), Pro $221 ($2,654, 15 users), Unlimited $332 ($3,984, unlimited users). Quarterly costs more for the same plans: Standard $132/month ($395 a quarter), Plus $206 ($619), Pro $282 ($845), Unlimited $415 ($1,245). Basic is not offered quarterly. Their own wording: the fee listed is the fee for the company as a whole.
