Card payments taken through the built-in Stripe integration are billed separately at 2.9% + $0.30 a transaction (3.9% + $0.30 for Amex, 1% + $0.30 capped at $10.00 for ACH).
tools.honest_knock: Credit where it is due first: this is company pricing with unlimited projects and no per-user overage inside your tier, which is rare in construction software and genuinely cheaper than per-seat rivals for a crew. The catch is the billing term. Quarterly costs 26% more than annual on the same plan — $132 against $105 on Standard — and Basic is not sold quarterly at all, so the cheapest way in requires a year paid up front. The user counts are the real ladder: 1, 3, 8, 15, unlimited. A five-person crew is not on Standard at $105, it is on Plus at $166, so count your licence holders before you compare against anything else.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size contractors who want estimating, scheduling and daily logs in one place and can commit to a year — the company-wide fee makes it cheap per head once you have a crew
tools.skip_if: you are a sole trader with a handful of jobs, because Basic at $49 a month annual is real money against a spreadsheet and a calendar — though the 30-day trial and the conditional 100-day refund mean trying it costs nothing but your time
compare_with: the standing comparison in construction software — compare total company cost at your crew size, since the per-seat rivals overtake this quickly

tools.name: Convert
tools.what_it_does: Privacy-first A/B testing platform — experiments, personalization and feature rollouts, priced by tested users. Via our link: an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (standard is 15 days).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-21 on their own pricing page) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr), and includes 100K tested users a month; Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo annually ($5,040/yr), and includes 1M a month; Enterprise on request. Overuse is metered — $399 per extra 100K on Growth, $699 per 250K on Pro, and it can be switched off — and each additional custom domain costs $1,000/year. Convert deliberately ships no heatmaps or exit popups, calling this a best-of-breed strategy, and charges no extra fee for its integrations.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them — and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399. One thing people misprice, and it is not the test itself: everyone expects an experiment to end when the subscription does. The trap is the winner. Convert describes itself as a client-side tool where “adding just one snippet of code on your site will then do all of the magic”. So a winning variant you leave running in the visual editor is not a change to your site — it is a rendering by their script. Ship the winner into your own code, or you are paying rent on a result you already bought.
tools.best_for: CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites
tools.skip_if: your traffic is modest — statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use — or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it
compare_with: VWO is the broad experimentation suite where testing is one module; Convert focuses squarely on A/B testing with GDPR-first positioning — compare the add-on costs (API, domains) on both before deciding

tools.name: CrankWheel
tools.what_it_does: No-download screen sharing for sales calls — a prospect clicks a link and sees your screen on any device. Deliberately narrow: no video conferencing, webinars or collaboration. The free plan covers one user and 15 meetings a month; Solo is about $29/user/month.
tools.pricing: (read on crankwheel.com/pricing, 2026-08-21) A free plan with no payment details required — unlimited usage for the first 15 days, then up to 15 sessions a month for life. Solo is $29/month for one user with unlimited usage, up to 30 viewers per share and up to 10 video-conferencing participants. Team starts at $99/month for unlimited users sharing 100 meetings a month, rising in steps: Team 200 $194, Team 500 $467, Team 1000 $882, Team 2000 $1,562. Busy User discount plans cost less for a capped number of users — Team 100 at $59 for three users, Team 500 at $287 for fifteen. Enterprise is quoted per year and the page prints no figure. A meeting counts at 40 seconds with a viewer, or when you create a share link or segment, or on an Instant Demo call.
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately narrow — instant, no-download screen sharing for sales calls — so it's excellent at that one job and thin everywhere else: no full video-conferencing suite, no deep collaboration or webinar tooling. Mind which plan caps what: the free plan drops to 15 sessions a month after the first fortnight and Team puts everyone on a shared pool of 100, while Solo is the one paid tier with unlimited usage. If you want an all-purpose meeting platform, this isn't it; if you want prospects to see your screen in seconds with zero friction, that focus is exactly why it works.
tools.best_for: sales reps, insurance agents and consultants who need prospects to view a screen instantly with no download or install, on any device
tools.skip_if: you need full video conferencing, webinars or team collaboration (Zoom/Meet fit better), or your call volume stays under the free tier
compare_with: general meeting platforms — CrankWheel's edge is zero-friction, no-download instant sharing for live sales, not full conferencing

tools.name: Crazy Egg
tools.what_it_does: Website optimization with heatmaps, scroll maps, session recordings and A/B testing — see how visitors behave and lift conversions with data.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-21, read on their own pricing page) Three plans, all billed annually, with a 30-day free trial and — in the vendor's words — no overages, ever. Analytics starts at $29/month and scales on tracked pageviews across 5,000, 50,000, 150,000, 500,000 and 1,000,000 a month, starting at 50 recordings. Growth starts at $99/month, but its slider starts at 50,000 pageviews rather than 5,000, and includes 500 recordings plus A/B testing, CTAs and targeting by device type. Enterprise is quoted. Note a conflict in the vendor's own material: their machine-readable pricing.md still lists an older Starter/Plus/Pro/Enterprise ladder at $29/$99/$249/$599 with different pageview allowances. The live pricing page is the one we read for the figures above.
tools.honest_knock: The entry plan is thin on recordings — 50 a month against Hotjar's far more generous free tier. And A/B testing is not in it at all: that starts on Growth at $99, whose pageview slider begins at 50,000 rather than 5,000. Heatmaps need manual per-page setup and annual-only billing locks you in. Like all these tools it's diagnostic — it shows what's broken, it doesn't fix it. Worth knowing before you treat a result as banked: Crazy Egg states it can run A/B tests “after implementing just a small code snippet directly on the website”, which means a winning variant is served by that snippet rather than written into your pages. Stop paying and the original page is what visitors get. Move the winner into your own templates once a test settles.
tools.best_for: lean marketing teams that want heatmaps, recordings and built-in A/B testing in one consolidated tool — noting that testing starts on the $99 plan, not the $29 one
tools.skip_if: you want generous recordings, automatic heatmaps and qualitative feedback — Hotjar's free tier and product depth suit product teams better

tools.name: Credit Repair Cloud
tools.what_it_does: Software for running a credit-repair business: client management, dispute automation and letter workflows. It is not a tool for repairing your own credit. Plans run from about $49/month (Personal) to $599 (Enterprise), scaling by active clients and seats.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-21 against the vendor's own pricing page, and now with the published limits rather than approximations) There are five plans, priced monthly. Personal is $49 for 1 user and up to 3 friends and family, and Start $179 for up to 3 users and 300 active clients. Grow is $299 for 6 users and 600 clients, and Scale $399 for 12 users and 1,200 clients. Enterprise is $599 for 24 users and 2,400 clients. Annual billing takes 20% off and is shown as a monthly equivalent on the four business tiers: $143.20, $239.20, $319.20 and $479.20. Every plan carries a 30-day free trial, the vendor states it charges no startup fees, and monthly plans have no long-term contract while annual plans require a one-year term.
tools.honest_knock: This is business-in-a-box software for starting a credit-repair company, not a tool that repairs your own credit — the price only makes sense if you're actually building a client business on it. The middle tiers jump fast as you add clients and seats, and success depends far more on your sales and compliance discipline (credit repair is a regulated space) than on the software. Buy it as an operator, not a consumer.
tools.best_for: entrepreneurs building or running a credit-repair business who need client management, dispute automation and done-for-you letter workflows
tools.skip_if: you just want to fix your own personal credit (you don't need this), or you're not prepared for the sales and compliance work a client business demands
compare_with: Dispute Fox or Client Dispute Manager
comparable credit-repair business platforms — compare on client limits and automation depth at your stage

tools.name: CrowdStrike
tools.what_it_does: Endpoint protection built around a cloud-delivered agent: antivirus, EDR and threat hunting.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-28, taken from the bundle table on their pricing page; the three published per-device rates have not moved since 1 Aug 2026) Priced per device. Falcon Go $7.99 per device per month, or $59.99 per device billed annually — capped at a maximum of 100 devices. Falcon Pro $14.99 monthly or $99.99 annually per device. Falcon Enterprise $19.99 per device per month, or $184.99 per device billed annually — a rate the 1 Aug reading recorded as unpublished. Larger tiers and managed services are quote-only. The free trial is a single 15-day Falcon Free Trial covering Next-Gen Antivirus, Device Control and Express Support, not a trial of each paid tier. Annual subscriptions are billed in full at the start of the term and can be cancelled within 30 days for a full refund.
tools.honest_knock: Two numbers decide whether this is for you, and neither is the headline. The first is the 100-device ceiling on Falcon Go: it is not a soft limit you grow through, it is the point where you change product. The second is the annual rate, which is worth doing the division on — $59.99 a year against $7.99 a month is $95.88, so annual saves 37%, one of the larger annual discounts in security software. Beyond that, be honest with yourself about which tier you are comparing: Go is antivirus with a good agent, and the endpoint detection and response that CrowdStrike is famous for starts at Pro. Comparing Go against a full EDR product from a competitor is comparing the wrong things.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size companies that want a serious endpoint agent without running a security team — Falcon Go is genuinely priced for businesses under 100 devices
tools.skip_if: you are under ten devices and already run a maintained operating system with its built-in protection, because at that size the management overhead outweighs the gain; also skip Go if you actually need EDR, since that starts a tier up
compare_with: SentinelOne or Microsoft Defender for Business
the direct endpoint peers — Defender is often already in your Microsoft licence, so price that first before comparing per-device rates

tools.name: Databox
tools.what_it_does: Centralized KPI dashboards. Pull data from all your software tools into one clean interface to monitor your business health. A free Skills Marketplace adds guided analyses on top: the paid-ads skill standardizes every ad channel into one efficiency table with CPA gauges against your own targets, judged per funnel role. A native MCP server (mcp.databox.com) puts those metrics inside ChatGPT or Claude — ingest data and query it in plain language. It runs on every paid plan, not on Free, and its queries spend from the same monthly AI-credit pool as Genie.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) There is a free plan: Free at $0 with 3 data sources, 1 user, 1 dashboard or report and 50 AI credits a month. Paid tiers, billed annually: Analyst $64/mo (5 data sources, 1 user, 500 AI credits), Pro $159/mo (3 sources included, $5.60/mo per extra, unlimited users, 1,500 credits), Growth $399/mo (4,000 credits, 15-minute sync) and a custom tier. AI credits are one shared monthly pool for the Genie assistant and the MCP server, so heavy AI use is what moves you up a tier rather than seats.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing model bites: Pro connects only 3 data sources, so the per-source fees stack up fast — and for agencies juggling many clients with diverse tools it gets expensive. Power users may also find the custom-metric and data-modelling depth limited next to a full BI tool.
tools.best_for: SMBs and agencies that want clean KPI dashboards from 130+ one-click integrations without building them by hand
tools.skip_if: you only need one or two data sources (the per-source fees add up), or you want deep custom data modelling — a free tool like Looker Studio fits better

tools.name: Datarails
tools.what_it_does: Excel-native FP&A platform for finance teams. Consolidation, planning, reporting and dashboards built on top of the spreadsheets you already use, with governed data behind them.
tools.pricing:
(read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be. The page frames that as a feature: “Get a custom quote tailored to your needs. Complete cost transparency, with no consultant fees—ever.”

What the page does publish is the shape of the ladder, and it is unusually explicit about what changes between tiers. The comparison table lists the same feature set on all three plans: reporting, planning, dashboards, Data Mapper, Lookups, Workflows, Submit Button, File Boxes, Filters, version control, the Datarails AI Suite, the FinanceOS AI Connector and permissions. Only two rows differ. Professional gives 1 integration and 2 users with standard support. Premium, marked most popular, gives 2 integrations and 5 users with premium support, and adds AI Storyboards, described as board decks in one click. Expert gives 3 integrations and 15 users with premium support, plus one “additional product included” — the line beyond FP&A runs to Datarails Month-End Close, Datarails Cash, Datarails Spend Control and Datarails Desk, and the page does not say which of those the extra slot may be spent on.

So the meter is seats and connected systems, not features. The page states no currency, no billing period, no minimum term and does not say whether a quote is annual, and there is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup: the only entry point on every page of the site is Request Demo or Request Quote. Treat any Datarails figure you have seen quoted elsewhere as unverified — on 25 August 2026 the vendor's own pricing page contains no amount at all.

One of those unpublished terms the vendor will answer if you ask. On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grows, and that adding modules or capabilities beyond the core platform can carry an extra cost that depends on the scope of the expansion. That is the vendor's own account rather than a published rate, so it belongs in your quote in writing — but it does answer the term question the pricing page leaves open.
tools.honest_knock: You cannot find out what it costs without talking to sales, and the entry plan is smaller than it looks: Professional covers 2 users and 1 integration, so a finance team of three, or one that needs both the ERP and the CRM connected, is priced into the next tier before the conversation starts. There is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup anywhere on the site — every path ends at Request Demo — so there is no way to try it quietly before procurement is involved.
tools.best_for: Excel-bound finance teams that have outgrown the spreadsheet plumbing but not the spreadsheets — consolidating several entities or data sources into one governed set of numbers, with planning, reporting and dashboards on top, while the models stay in Excel
tools.skip_if: you are a single-entity company whose budget lives in one workbook, or a team of two that just needs a dashboard — the quote-only sales motion and the tier caps cost more in elapsed time than the problem is worth at that size
compare_with: the honest comparison is against the other Excel-native FP&A platforms rather than against Excel itself; what is distinctive here is that every tier carries the same feature set — consolidation, planning, dashboards, the AI suite and the connector — so the ladder buys seats, integrations and, at the top, a second product from the wider line rather than capabilities

tools.name: Deel
tools.what_it_does: Global hiring, payroll and EOR platform — pay contractors and employees compliantly in 150+ countries, from $49 per contractor per month, with HR tools and US PEO options.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Pricing is per worker and demo-led, and each product is priced separately. HR and hiring tools start at $14 per worker a month. Contractor management is $49 per contractor a month, or $325 per month per Contractor of Record if you want Deel to carry the compliance risk. US PEO starts at $125 per employee a month. And EOR, where Deel employs your international hire, starts at $599 per employee a month. There is a free demo and final quotes come through sales. The spread is the point: the same headcount costs $14 or $599 a month depending on which relationship you need, so identify the employment model before comparing vendors.
tools.honest_knock: Every price is a ‘starting at’ and every button says ‘book a demo’ — the real bill depends on countries, benefits and add-ons, and only firms up in a sales conversation. And know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not software — worth it in unfamiliar jurisdictions, expensive where you could open your own entity.
tools.best_for: companies hiring internationally without local entities — contractors paid compliantly in 150+ countries, or full EOR employment where you need someone on the ground fast
tools.skip_if: your team is all-domestic (a local payroll tool is far cheaper), or you hire enough people in one country that opening your own entity beats paying per-employee EOR fees forever
compare_with: Gusto is the friendly US-payroll incumbent for domestic teams; Deel is built for global — contractors, EOR and payroll across 150+ countries. Pick by where your people are

tools.name: Deputy
tools.what_it_does: Workforce management for hourly and shift-based teams: rota building, time clocking, timesheet approval and labour-law compliance, with payroll and HR integrations.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-31, read in a live browser session on deputy.com/pricing with both billing toggles) Three plans, per user per month and excluding tax. On annual billing Lite is $5, Core $6.50 and Pro $9; switch the toggle to monthly and the same three read $5.50, $7.25 and $10. Add-ons are billed monthly on top. HR is $2 per user, Messaging+ $1.95 per user and Analytics+ $1.50 per user, and the last two are included in Pro. Deputy Payroll enabled by Paycor is $8 per user plus a $49 monthly base fee, available only on annual Core and Pro plans in the US. The page also states a minimum monthly spend of USD $30 / AUD $30 / GBP £20 per invoice on the monthly Lite, Core and Pro plans. Lite and Core start with a free trial; Pro is Contact us rather than self-serve.
tools.honest_knock: The minimum monthly spend is the number to check before anything else: at $5.50 per user on monthly billing, a team of fewer than about six people still pays the $30 floor, so the headline per-user price is misleading at small scale. Beyond that, the plan you probably want is not the one you first price — auto-scheduling, demand forecasting and labour budgets sit in Core, and SSO, custom access levels and location hierarchies only in Pro, which has no public self-serve checkout. The add-ons stack per user as well, and the payroll add-on is US-only and annual-only.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses — hospitality, retail, healthcare, any hourly workforce — that need rostering, clocking and labour-law compliance in one system and have enough staff to clear the minimum spend
tools.skip_if: you run a small salaried desk team: the $30 monthly minimum means you pay for roughly six users whether you have them or not, and salaried staff rarely need shift-level clocking at all

tools.name: Descript
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered video and podcast editor: edit media by editing the text transcript — cut, overdub and remove filler words like editing a doc — with screen recording, AI voice cloning and an AI assistant (Underlord) built in.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free plan with 60 minutes a month and watermarked 720p exports. Paid, per person per month, annual against monthly: Hobbyist $16 / $24, Creator $24 / $35, Business $50 / $65, with annual billing saving up to 35%. Media hours and AI credits are capped per tier: roughly 10, 30 and 40 hours a month, and 400 to 1,500 credits. So the meter that matters is footage rather than seats — a weekly podcast can outgrow Hobbyist on hours long before it needs the features above it.
tools.honest_knock: It's per-editor pricing with two meters running underneath: media hours AND monthly AI credits. Heavy podcast or video volume burns through the caps fast, and the free tier watermarks 720p exports — model your real production hours before picking a tier. The API changes the arithmetic rather than escaping it. Their own API page states access is included for paying users at no additional cost, but the work it does draws from the same AI credits and media minutes — so automating a pipeline burns the caps faster, not slower. It also stops just short of the finish — the same page says direct media file exports are not supported yet, so the export step stays a manual one in the app. (read on their own API page, 2026-08-14)
tools.best_for: podcasters and video creators who want to edit by editing the transcript, cutting, overdubbing and stripping filler words as easily as editing a doc. It also suits teams who want those same edits triggered from code or from an AI assistant via Descript’s API and MCP connector rather than from the app
tools.skip_if: you need frame-precise, effects-heavy editing (a traditional NLE fits better) or your monthly volume blows past the media-hour caps
compare_with: Riverside wins on recording-quality-first workflows, CapCut on quick social edits; Descript wins on the text-based editing workflow itself

tools.name: Devs.ai
tools.what_it_does: Build and ship AI agents and apps across many models without engineering work. The seat price is the smaller half of the bill: Personal includes $10 of model usage a month and Business $21, metered on top — and the plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate once it runs out.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-26, read in a live browser session on devs.ai/home/pricing with both billing toggles) Devs.ai does publish its pricing — on the marketing site at devs.ai/home/pricing, not at the app's /pricing route, which bounces you to a login screen. Free is $0 forever, but Agent Builder and App Builder appear there in "Core" rather than "Full" form, data upload is capped at 2 GB, and workflows, APIs and integrations are marked absent. Personal is $15 per seat / month billed annually or $18 billed monthly; Business is $30 per seat / month annually or $36 monthly; Enterprise is a custom annual contract. The seat fee is not the whole bill: Personal includes $10 of usage per month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. Data upload runs 2 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB and custom across the four tiers. Team governance and collaboration start at Business, while SSO (OpenID/SAML), access control lists, custom connectors and white-labelling are Enterprise-only. Separately, Devs.ai told us by email on 5 August 2026 that organisations upgrading to a paid Personal or Business plan can earn up to $100 in usage credits for completing setup steps: starting a conversation, creating an agent, connecting an integration, deploying an app. The credits are shared org-wide and do not expire. Enterprise is excluded, and orgs already on a paid plan before July 2026 are not enrolled by default. That last paragraph is the vendor's own statement to us, not something we found published on the pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is the smaller half of the bill. Personal includes $10 of usage a month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. The plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate you pay once it runs out — which is exactly the number you need to forecast a real workload. The free plan is a demo rather than a working tier: both builders are limited to "Core", and workflows, APIs and integrations are absent entirely, which is much of what would make the platform useful past a first agent. And for a product sold on IT governance, the governance controls are the ones you cannot buy with a card — SSO, access control lists and white-labelling sit on the Enterprise tier, behind a custom annual contract.
tools.best_for: teams that want to prototype and ship AI agents and apps across multiple models without engineering overhead, and that can absorb model usage metered on top of the per-seat fee
tools.skip_if: you need SSO, access control lists or white-labelling without going through an Enterprise contract, or you need one predictable all-in bill rather than a seat fee plus metered usage
compare_with: the agent-builder field — all three meter model usage differently on top of their base price, so compare on the metered layer rather than on the seat fee

tools.name: Dext
tools.what_it_does: Receipt and invoice capture that extracts the data and feeds it into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage. It is the capture layer, not accounting software, so you still need one of those. From about £24/month on Starter, and extraction accuracy varies enough to need manual correction.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-21, read in a browser on dext.com/en/business/pricing because the price panel renders client-side) Dext has moved off named tiers: you choose a region and a billing period, then slide an allowance. The base of 250 documents a month and 5 users costs $25.21 per month billed annually ($302.50 a year) or $31.50 monthly in the Rest of the World, £30 monthly in the UK, €31.50 in the EU and A$42 in APAC, all excluding tax. The annual discount is stated as up to 20% everywhere except the UK page, which says up to 19%. Add-ons are billed separately: AI Assist $10.5 a month until 31 October, Commerce Lite from $7.50 and Vault free for 100MB then from $4. Line Item Extraction and Supplier Statement Extraction are from $20.50 a month or $0.50 per document, and Bank Statement Extraction from $13.00 a month or $0.32 per document. Plans include 10 sheets of bank statement extraction, 5 line-item documents and 5 supplier statement extractions as free credits, and the free trial is 14 days with no payment details required.
tools.honest_knock: It's a data-capture layer, not accounting software — it feeds Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, so you still need one of those. Extraction accuracy varies and sometimes needs manual fixes, the UI is tricky for beginners, the mobile app is more limited than desktop, and sole traders find it pricey.
tools.best_for: accountants, bookkeepers and growing businesses drowning in receipts who want fast, accurate capture flowing straight into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage
tools.skip_if: you're a sole trader with few receipts (pricey for low volume), or you want all-in-one accounting — Dext only does the capture layer
compare_with: the free-with-Xero and the do-it-yourself routes

tools.name: Dify
tools.what_it_does: Source-available platform for LLM apps and agent workflows: visual builder, RAG pipelines, model-agnostic. The Community Edition is free of a software fee to self-host, but you own the servers, updates and reliability. Managed Dify Cloud runs $59/month on Professional, priced per workspace.
tools.pricing: Source-available and free of a software fee to self-host — the Community Edition ships under the Dify Open Source License, a modified Apache 2.0 with additional conditions — while the managed Dify Cloud adds a free Sandbox, Professional at $59/mo ($590/yr) and Team at $159/mo ($1,590/yr), each priced per workspace (2026). Self-hosting still costs you infrastructure, model usage and any commercial licence those terms require. Cloud plans include message credits for supported model providers; once those run out you connect your own provider API key and pay that provider directly.
tools.honest_knock: 'Free' self-hosting isn't free — you own the servers, updates and reliability, and model usage bills separately once the included message credits run out. Dify Cloud takes that infrastructure work off your hands, but every cloud plan is a single workspace, and multiple workspaces, SSO and a commercial licence sit in quote-only Enterprise. It's powerful, but self-hosting it well needs technical comfort.
tools.best_for: technical teams that want to build and ship LLM apps and agents on a source-available platform they can self-host and control
tools.skip_if: you want a no-maintenance, non-technical builder — a fully managed no-code AI tool saves you the infra and upkeep
compare_with: Flowise or a managed platform like Lindy.ai
other LLM-app builders, self-host or managed

tools.name: Diginius
tools.what_it_does: Digital marketing and e-commerce performance platform. Manage PPC, analytics and product feeds to improve online sales and visibility.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-21 on diginius.com/pricing/, business pricing) Essential $75 USD a month for 2 users, Pro $250 for 5 users, Core $500 for 10 users and marked Most Popular, Business by contact with sales. The FAQ on the same page confirms a 20% discount for annual payment. The plan limits scale with the price. SEO keywords run 25 / 500 / 1000 / custom, and SEO site pages 1000 / 5000 / 10000 / custom. Lead Intelligence leads run 10 / 25 / 50 per week, and Bombora intent leads 10 / 50 / 100 per week. Contact info credits run 25 / 50 / 100 per month, and support goes from email only to a dedicated customer success rep. The trial banner advertises 30 days including 100 intent leads a week and 100 contact credits, but the mobile plan card on the same page says 14 days.
tools.honest_knock: All-in-one marketing dashboards live or die on data depth per module. Diginius bundles PPC, SEO, lead intelligence and reporting affordably, but specialists — a dedicated SEO suite, a dedicated PPC optimizer — go deeper in their lanes. So buy it as consolidation for a lean team, not as a replacement for expert-grade tooling in your primary channel. Verify the integrations you depend on (especially Microsoft Ads, its historical strength) in the trial.
tools.best_for: lean teams and agencies that want PPC, SEO and lead intelligence consolidated in one affordable dashboard instead of five subscriptions
tools.skip_if: your growth lives in one channel where a specialist tool's depth pays for itself, or you need enterprise analytics rigor
compare_with: the specialist suites — deeper per channel at higher cost; Diginius wins on breadth-per-dollar for generalists

tools.name: Digit
tools.what_it_does: Inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system for manufacturers and distributors. Starter $400/month with 5 users, Growth $750, Professional $1,300, extra users $63 each. Watch the add-ons: a third integration is $100 to $125 a month, and API or MCP access is $125 each.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-05 in a rendered browser on their own pricing page) Four tiers with three published: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15, and Enterprise on quote. Extra users are $63/month each on every tier. Paying quarterly takes 10% off — $360, $675 and $1,170 a month, shown with the quarter total beside it — and annually 20%, which is $320, $600 and $1,040 with the year total beside it; the page now opens on Monthly, so the first figure you see is the real monthly rate. Two integrations are included on every plan. The third and each one after it is where the page disagrees with itself: the Integrations block says $100 a month, the FAQ on the same page says $125, and the add-on cards side with the FAQ — API access $125 a month, MCP access $125, push notifications and webhooks $63, all the same price on Starter, Growth and Professional. Customer portals are $18.75 per portal per month on every tier, Enterprise included. We have asked Digit which integration price is the one they bill.
tools.honest_knock: The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling, and the add-ons are where an inventory system quietly doubles. Two integrations are included — but a working setup usually means an accounting package and a webshop, which is your two, and then Amazon or a second sales channel is another $125 a month by the FAQ (the integrations block on the same page still says $100; we have asked which one bills). Want the API, or your data inside an AI assistant? $125 a month each. A Starter customer on QuickBooks, Shopify and Amazon with API access is at $650 a month on the FAQ's numbers, $625 on the block's, before adding a sixth user. Price the whole configuration you actually need, not the tier.
tools.best_for: manufacturers and distributors outgrowing spreadsheets who need inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system, and who genuinely need lot tracking and traceability rather than just wanting them
tools.skip_if: you are a small operation where $400/month for five users is heavy against what a warehouse module in your existing accounting package would cost; also skip it if your integration list is long, because the per-connection model punishes exactly that — $100 to $125 a month for every integration past the second, depending on which part of their pricing page you read
compare_with: the natural head-to-head for manufacturers leaving spreadsheets. Both cover inventory and production; the difference shows up in how they charge for the edges. Price the full configuration you need on each — every integration, the API if you want it — because Digit's per-connection add-ons — $100 to $125 a month for each integration past the first two, and $125 for API or MCP access — are where the tier price stops being the price

tools.name: Disputifier
tools.what_it_does: Chargeback automation for Shopify: submits dispute evidence for you, buys chargeback alerts that refund incoming disputes before they land, and screens orders for fraud and late shipments. Free to install; recovery costs 20% of every won chargeback (capped at $250 a win), alerts run $17-$27.50 each and the two prevention add-ons $0.05 an order.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/disputifier and on disputifier.com/pricing) Free to install, with everything billed on use. The listing shows a single plan — Basic, free to install, with a 7-day risk-free trial — and names two charges: chargeback fighting at 20% of won-back revenue, and chargeback alerts from $17 to $27.50 per alert. All charges are billed in USD. The vendor's own pricing page fills in the rest. Recovery is 20% of the recovered amount with the fee capped at $250 per win — win a $50 chargeback and they debit $10 — while fraud prevention is $0.05 per order and 'order not received' prevention another $0.05 per order. Alerts are sold there as custom volume-based pricing by quote, so the $17-$27.50 band on the listing is the only public number for them. There is no monthly subscription anywhere in this: the bill is a function of how many disputes and orders you have, so it cannot be read off the pricing page in advance. Developer Disputifier, 294 Trillium Way, Clayton, North Carolina; the app launched 23 September 2020 and carries a 4.5 average over 84 App Store reviews.
tools.honest_knock:
Free to install is doing a lot of work here. All four services bill per event — a fifth of each recovery, $17 to $27.50 an alert, five cents an order twice over — so the cost lands after the fact and scales with exactly the thing you are trying to reduce. Model your worst chargeback month before you switch alerts on, not your average one.

The reviews deserve a straight look too. The 4.6 average across 88 reviews, read again on 22 August 2026, is not a middle: 89% are five stars and nine of the eighty-eight are a single star, with almost nothing in between. The most recent one-star, from June 2026, describes a security incident at the vendor and a dispute over unpaid invoices and billing descriptors; Disputifier replied in July that it does not block merchants from moving providers and disputes the account of the charges. We have not verified either side and are not taking one. What the pattern does show is where the friction sits: merchants either rate this perfect or fall out with it over invoices, not over whether disputes were won.

And know what alerts cannot reach. Coverage depends on the shopper's bank and card: smaller issuers do not participate, Amex and Discover frequently cannot be set up, Klarna alerts do not exist yet and PayPal alerts are recent. The prevention rate the vendor quotes is a ceiling for a well-covered card mix, not a promise for yours.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a chargeback problem big enough to cost real money and nobody in-house to fight disputes, who would rather pay a share of what is recovered than a monthly fee
tools.skip_if: your dispute volume is low or lumpy, you need a predictable monthly bill, or your margins are high enough that auto-refunding an alerted order costs more than losing the occasional dispute

tools.name: Dondy
tools.what_it_does: WhatsApp marketing and support for Shopify on the official WhatsApp Business API: abandoned-cart recovery, campaigns to Shopify segments, automated order messages, a shared inbox and an AI chatbot for sales and support. Free for the chat button; $6.99 a month for manual messages, $79.99 for automation and campaigns, $159.99 with the AI chatbot, plus Meta's own per-conversation charges from $0.0126.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/dondy-marketing-ai, listed as “Dondy: WhatsApp Marketing+Chat”) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Free: a WhatsApp chat button with unlimited conversations, custom size and location, and prefilled messages. Pro $6.99 a month or $67.10 a year, a 20% saving: premium button designs, a WhatsApp widget, text customisation, product URLs in messages, custom hours, reports, and abandoned-cart and order-confirmation messages you send manually. Power Automation is $79.99 a month or $719.88 a year, a 25% saving. It carries automated abandoned-cart recovery, WhatsApp marketing campaigns, customisable automated messages, bulk messaging to Shopify segments, an inbox with Shopify integration and the official WhatsApp Business API. It includes 1,000 one-click messages every 30 days, and quotes WhatsApp rates starting at $0.0158 in the US on top. Elite $159.99 a month or $1,439.88 a year adds an AI chatbot for sales and support, AI corrections and training, AI product recommendations, a five-agent WhatsApp inbox, green-tick verification assistance, a VIP account manager and unlimited WhatsApp flows. It carries the same 1,000 included messages and rates starting at $0.0126. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and Meta's per-conversation charges are separate from all of it. Developer Dondy, Givatayim, Israel; the app launched 15 March 2023, is available in five languages, and had 774 reviews at the time of writing, 3% of them one-star.
tools.honest_knock:
The free plan is a chat button. It is a decent chat button, and conversations through it are unlimited. But none of the marketing this app is named for is in it. Automated cart recovery, campaigns and the official API begin at $79.99 a month, and the $6.99 tier in between only lets you send those same messages by hand.

You will also get two bills. Dondy charges the subscription; Meta charges per conversation on the WhatsApp Business API. Dondy can only tell you the rate starts at $0.0158 or $0.0126, because the real figure depends on the country you are messaging and the type of conversation. A thousand one-click messages a month are included on the two top tiers; past that, your monthly total is not knowable from this listing, and a campaign to a large segment is exactly the kind of thing that produces a surprise. Model it against your own list size and destination countries before you send one.

The rest is Meta's rulebook, not Dondy's. Opt-in, message templates and sender quality are governed on WhatsApp's side, so approval and reach are not things this app can promise you whatever you pay it. The review record is strong — 774 reviews, 91% at the top rating — and it still contains 21 one-star reports, which is the ordinary shape of a channel where a misfired broadcast is not an unsubscribe but a block.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores whose customers already live in WhatsApp — much of Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia — that want cart recovery, order updates and campaigns on the official API without leaving the Shopify admin
tools.skip_if: your customers are on email and SMS, or you need one predictable monthly figure: Meta's per-conversation charges sit on top of every paid tier here

tools.name: doola
tools.what_it_does: Business formation and compliance made easy. Launch your US LLC or C-Corp from anywhere globally, complete with banking and tax management.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 1 September 2026 on doola.com/pricing) The August sale has ended, so these are the list prices again. Starter is $297 a year plus state fees and covers LLC or C-Corp formation, EIN, a registered agent and a US address; state filing fees run $50 to $500 depending on the state, and they are yours, not doola's. Pulse bookkeeping comes with a 30-day trial and renews at $300 a year. Tax and Compliance, the tier the page marks Most Popular, is $1,999 a year plus state fees. Business-in-a-Box is $2,999 a year, or $329 a month, plus state fees. doola's own FAQ states that all plans are billed annually. Worth knowing for timing: through 31 August the page ran an automatic discount of up to $750 that could not be combined with anything else, which showed $222, $1,499 and $2,249 for those three tiers. That window closed on 31 August, which is precisely why our reader code applies again from 1 September.
tools.honest_knock: Formation is the cheap part; the recurring bookkeeping and tax tiers are where the real cost sits, and state fees are extra on top of doola's price. Convenient especially for non-US founders, but a local accountant may be cheaper once you're established.
tools.best_for: founders (often non-US) who want US LLC/C-Corp formation, EIN and compliance handled in one place without the paperwork
tools.skip_if: you're a US resident comfortable filing formation yourself — the state fee plus a cheap registered agent costs far less than the bundle
compare_with: other formation services, or doing it yourself

tools.name: Drip
tools.what_it_does: Ecommerce email and onsite marketing built around your store's order data — segments, abandoned-cart and welcome playbooks, pop-ups and A/B testing, with one-click links to Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce. Priced purely on list size from $39/month for 2,500 people, 14-day trial without a card. Two things the headline price hides: chat support only starts at $99/month, and the promised unlimited sends turn into a hard cap of twelve emails per contact per month somewhere above 25,000 contacts (read 12 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-12, read off their own pricing calculator; every rung on the slider re-verified 2026-08-22 and unchanged) One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. 2,500 people is $39, then $49 at 3,000, $59 at 3,500, $69 at 4,000, $79 at 4,500, $89 at 5,000, $99 at 6,000, $109 at 7,000, $169 at 12,500, $369 at 25,000, $699 at 50,000, $1,299 at 110,000 and $1,949 at 175,000. Above roughly 175,000 the number disappears and the page says “Let’s chat”, so the top of the range is quote-only. The trial is 14 days and takes no card, but Drip states unlimited sends are switched off during it. Two things the ladder does not advertise. Chat support is not included at the entry price: up to 5,000 people the line reads “Email support”, and “Chat and email support” only appears from $99 (6,000 people) — their FAQ says the same in words. And “Unlimited email sends” stops being literally true as you climb. It still says unlimited at 30,000 people, but at 30,001 the same line reads “390,000 email sends”, at 50,000 “600,000”, at 110,000 “1,320,000” and at 175,000 “2,100,000” — in every case exactly twelve sends per contact per month. Every plan carries the same feature set otherwise, including up to 50 workflows and unlimited sub-accounts, so what you buy going up the ladder is list capacity, not capability.
tools.honest_knock: The word “unlimited” quietly expires. At the prices most small shops pay, the send allowance really is uncapped. But the switch has an exact address: unlimited holds to 30,000 people, and from 30,001 the bullet becomes a hard number — 390,000 sends there, 600,000 at 50,000 people, twelve per contact per month. Drip never flags the switch. If you run a daily-deal or high-frequency list, do the arithmetic before you migrate: twelve sends per contact is generous for a monthly newsletter and tight for anything that mails several times a week. The second thing to price in is support. The page sells one product at every level, but you cannot talk to anyone in chat until $99/month; below that it is email only, which is a real difference on the day a broken automation is sending to the wrong segment.
tools.best_for: an online store on Shopify, WooCommerce or BigCommerce that already has order data worth segmenting and wants ecommerce playbooks — abandoned cart, welcome series, post-purchase — without assembling them by hand. The pricing model suits a list that grows steadily and mails at a normal cadence, because you pay for people rather than per seat or per feature, and every plan carries the whole feature set
tools.skip_if: you are not selling online: Drip says an ecommerce store is not required but that the platform is built for one, and you would be paying for the half you cannot use. Skip it too if your list is large and you mail often, because the send allowance caps at twelve per contact per month once you are past the small tiers. The same goes past 175,000 people, where the published ladder ends and pricing becomes a conversation
compare_with: the comparison Drip picks itself — it publishes a Drip vs. Klaviyo page — and the one most ecommerce teams actually make. Both price on list size and both live off store data; the practical question is what the send allowance and the support line look like at your volume, which is where Drip's ladder is unusually easy to read and unusually quiet about the twelve-sends ceiling

tools.name: Dripify
tools.what_it_does: Cloud-based LinkedIn outreach automation — drip sequences of connection requests, messages, InMails and profile views, with configurable daily limits and a built-in email finder. From $39 per user/month billed annually, 7-day free trial without a card.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page — note that dripify.io now redirects to dripify.com) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all six numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here, and the page now prints the daily quotas instead of calling them 'limited': Basic sends 20 connection requests, 30 messages, 10 Sales Navigator InMails and 100 profile views a day, against 75, 100+, 30 and 200+ on Pro and Advanced. Basic is also capped at one drip campaign; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales.
tools.honest_knock: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control sits on the $79 Advanced tier. It is the feature Dripify names as its best protection, and it adjusts your pace automatically. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.
tools.best_for: sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session
tools.skip_if: anyone whose LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or anyone tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that
compare_with: the closest head-to-head — both are cloud-based with a regional dedicated IP, so the 'cloud versus extension' framing you will read in affiliate roundups does not actually separate them. The real difference is the pricing model: Expandi sells one Business plan with everything included at $99 per user a month, 20 percent off annually, while Dripify tiers both quotas and safety features. Watch the $39-versus-$99 gap that roundups quote — that is Dripify's annual rate against Expandi's monthly one. Month against month it is $59 to $99 versus $99, and at the top of Dripify's range the two cost the same. Both price lists read on 2026-07-24; verify them yourself before you buy.

tools.name: Dripshipper
tools.what_it_does: Private-label coffee and tea dropshipping for Shopify: they roast, bag and ship from their own US facilities within 3-5 business days, with your brand on the packaging. Starter $30 a month or $240 a year, Professional $99, Elite $197, all with a 14-day trial and per-order product and shipping cost on top.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/dripshipper, listed as “Dripshipper: Coffee & Tea”) Starter $30 a month, Professional $99 and Elite $197, each with a 14-day free trial. Starter is also sold annually at $240 a year, which is $20 a month for the same tier. Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.7 from 142 App Store reviews. Developer The Doughty Organization.
tools.honest_knock: Read the ladder before you climb it. Starter already carries unlimited orders, unlimited products and automatic fulfilment — the whole product, in other words. Professional at $99 adds live monthly training, priority support and a success manager; Elite at $197 adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. You are buying people, not capability: nothing above Starter makes the coffee ship faster or cost less per bag. The annual rate is the move worth noticing in the other direction, since $240 a year against $30 a month is a third off the same tier. Beyond that the model is narrow by design — one product category, roasted and shipped from their own US facilities in 3-5 business days, with no route to source elsewhere or negotiate the per-order cost.
tools.best_for: someone who wants a turnkey private-label coffee or tea brand on Shopify — their roasting and packaging, your label on the bag — and is content to stay inside one product category
tools.skip_if: you want product breadth, fulfilment outside the US, or control over sourcing and packaging cost — this is a single-supplier pipeline and the higher tiers only add coaching

tools.name: DropGenius
tools.what_it_does: Generates a Shopify dropshipping store — products, branding and copy — as a starting template, not a finished business. Monthly runs $39 to $299, and annual billing drops Starter. Trustpilot sat near 1.6/5 at research time, with recurring complaints about charges after cancellation.
tools.pricing: Re-verified 6 September 2026 on their own pricing page, unchanged since August. Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 14-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). The meter is catalogue size: Starter 25 unique products, Pro 250 unique plus 25 premium, Empire 10,000 and 10,000, Unicorn 25,000 and 25,000. Their own FAQ still quotes an older $39.99-$299.99 range plus a $1.99 one-time store-creation fee, so the marketing copy and the pricing table disagree.
tools.honest_knock: We have to be blunt here: DropGenius carries a very poor Trustpilot rating (around 1.6/5 at research time), with recurring complaints about charges continuing after cancellation and refund difficulty. An AI-generated store in 30 seconds is also just a starting template — the product selection, marketing and margins remain entirely your problem. If you proceed: pay attention to cancellation mechanics from day one, screenshot everything, and treat the Renewal Radar as mandatory equipment.
tools.best_for: absolute beginners who want a pre-built Shopify dropshipping store scaffold in minutes and understand it's a starting point, not a business
tools.skip_if: anyone uncomfortable with the documented billing complaints — or expecting an AI-generated store to sell by itself
compare_with: building on Spocket directly (same ecosystem) gives you the supplier network without the store-generator layer — and cleaner reviews

tools.name: Dryground AI
tools.what_it_does: Full-stack AI implementation services: helps businesses design and integrate AI across their tech stack — for teams that want AI built and shipped, not just advised.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-17, read in a browser because the site renders client-side and a plain fetch returns only the title) There is no public pricing anywhere, and we checked before saying so. /pricing, /plans, /services, /about and /contact all return 404. The words “pricing”, “price” and “$” appear zero times on the homepage, and the navigation carries no pricing entry at all — it runs Solutions, Products, Verticals, Case Studies, Research, Book a Consultation. Tiers do exist with no numbers attached: the AI Velocity line is described as “six tiers from pilot to full enterprise transformation” on 90-day outcome cycles. Budget this as a consulting engagement scoped per project, not a subscription you can read off a page.
tools.honest_knock: This is consulting, not a tool you log into: best when you want AI designed and built for you, not when you'd rather DIY with software. Read the headline numbers carefully too. The 20-50% efficiency and 10-20% revenue figures on their homepage carry the caption “2025 industry benchmarks”, so they describe the market rather than this firm's own results. And the case studies underneath them name no clients.
tools.best_for: businesses that want AI solutions built for them as a services engagement rather than assembling tools themselves
tools.skip_if: you're looking for self-serve software with published pricing — this is custom, quote-based consulting

tools.name: Easy Advanced Translations
tools.what_it_does: AI Shopify store translation (by Northwest): translate products, collections, theme text, metafields and even hard-coded and third-party-app text across languages, with a choice of engine (its own, Google, OpenAI or DeepSeek), image translation, protected terms and Shopify Markets support.
tools.pricing: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/advanced-translation) Four tiers, all monthly. Free installs at no cost and gives you unlimited AI if you bring your own OpenAI or DeepSeek key, or free built-in AI for a small quota (50 products, 50 metafields, 100 variants, 5 articles). Starter is $4.99, Basic $14.99 and Pro $29.99, each raising the free-AI quota (100, 400 and 800 products respectively) — or, again, unlimited if you supply your own key. The model's real pivot is that key: bring your own and you pay the AI provider's token costs directly for unlimited volume; rely on the built-in free AI and you are capped per tier.
tools.honest_knock: The 'free AI' is heavily quota-limited — 50 products on Free, up to 800 on Pro — so a genuinely multilingual catalogue pushes you either to a paid tier or to your own OpenAI/DeepSeek key, where you pay token costs separately on top of the subscription. Auto-translation of new or changed content is reserved for the higher plans. And the track record is thin: 5.0 stars but only nine reviews, the app launched in July 2025, and it carries no 'Built for Shopify' badge — cheap and promising, but unproven.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid Shopify stores that want affordable, full-store AI translation — including images and third-party-app text — and are comfortable bringing their own OpenAI or DeepSeek key for unlimited volume
tools.skip_if: large catalogues that want predictable all-in pricing without managing API keys or quotas, merchants who require a proven app with a large review base, or enterprises needing SLA and support guarantees
compare_with: Weglot is the established, higher-priced incumbent for Shopify translation; Easy Advanced Translations undercuts it sharply and translates deeper into theme and third-party text, but with a young nine-review record and a bring-your-own-AI-key model rather than Weglot's all-in pricing. Pick Weglot for a proven managed service, this for price and depth if you will manage a key

tools.name: Easy Bundles
tools.what_it_does: Shopify bundle builder for build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price, volume and subscription bundles, with bundle inventory synced across Shopify and 3PLs and POS support. Priced on bundle sales rather than orders: free up to $500 a month, Essential $29 up to $3,000, Growth $49 up to $5,000, Scale $99 up to $10,000, with 14-16% off on annual billing. 4.9 stars over 1,216 reviews as of 4 Sep 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is the part that matters: you are charged on bundle sales, not on orders, products or staff. The free plan is free to install and covers up to $500 of bundle sales a month. Essential is $29 a month or $299 a year and lifts that to $3,000; Growth is $49 or $499 a year up to $5,000; Scale is $99 or $999 a year up to $10,000. Annual billing saves 14% to 16% depending on the tier, and every paid tier has a 15-day free trial. Features climb the same ladder: free gives mix-and-match, fixed and volume bundles with templates and a custom or template design; Essential adds the single-step and multi-step bundle builders, landing-page templates, search and filtering, and multi-currency and multi-language support; Growth adds advanced discount logic, custom personalisation fields, add-ons, free gifts and subscription bundles; Scale adds AI-generated designs, advanced analytics, one-to-one onboarding and an account manager on Slack. Two things the block does not say are worth noting before you commit. It does not publish what happens when you pass $10,000 of bundle sales in a month, and it does not publish an overage rate; the plan table simply ends there and links out to see all pricing options.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is tied to the thing the app is supposed to grow. A revenue meter reads as generous at the bottom — $500 of bundle sales a month free is a real trial, not a crippled one — but it means every tier upgrade is triggered by the app working, and the published ladder stops at $10,000 a month with no stated overage. A store doing well on bundles has to ask what comes next rather than read it, and that is the wrong moment to be negotiating. Maturity is not the concern here: the app has been on the App Store since 15 September 2022 and carries 4.9 stars over 1,216 reviews as of 4 September 2026. The concern is where the money goes as you succeed. Two smaller things: the features most merchants picture when they think bundles — guided build-your-own-box, subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts — sit on Growth at $49, not on the free plan, and the recent reviews that praise the app most warmly also praise the support team by name, which is a compliment to people rather than to a product that never needs them.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who want build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price or volume bundles live in days rather than sprints, with bundle inventory syncing across Shopify and 3PLs and bundles that also sell through POS — and whose bundle revenue is still small enough to sit comfortably inside a published tier
tools.skip_if: your bundle sales already run past $10,000 a month, because that is where the published ladder ends and the overage is not disclosed; or you need one straightforward fixed or mix-and-match bundle, which Shopify's own free first-party Bundles app already covers
compare_with: Shopify ships a free, first-party bundles app that handles fixed and mix-and-match bundles with no meter on your revenue, and for a store that wants one simple bundle that is the cheaper answer and always will be. Easy Bundles is worth the $29 to $99 when the bundle is an experience rather than a SKU — a guided build-your-own-box or gift-box flow, subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts, bundle landing pages in several currencies and languages — and when you want the bundle stock to stay in step with your 3PL without anyone reconciling it by hand

tools.name: EasyDMARC
tools.what_it_does: DMARC, SPF and DKIM monitoring — stop others sending email as your domain.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on easydmarc.com/pricing over a US connection, on the Organizations tab with annual billing on) Plus is $US 44.99 a month, or $US 35.99 billed annually, for 2 domains, three months of report history and one invited user. Premium is $US 89.99, or $US 71.99 annually, for 4 domains, a year of history, TLS reports and a dedicated CS manager on the yearly plan. Enterprise is quoted and carries three years of history, unlimited users and managed services. Annual billing is marked as 20% off plus bonus features, and MSPs and MSSPs get a separate tab with their own ladder. The number that actually sets your tier is monthly email volume: each card has its own selector, running 100,000 to 1,000,000 messages on Plus and up to 5,000,000 on Premium, so the headline is the floor for the smallest bracket. We first read these as euro amounts from the Netherlands on 1 Aug; the figures do not convert — €44.99 there is $44.99 here.
tools.honest_knock: You are buying domains and history, not features. Plus covers two domains; a company with a main domain, a marketing subdomain and a legacy domain it forgot about is already over. And the history window is the part that bites later: three months on Plus means that when you are investigating a spoofing campaign that started in the spring, the reports are gone. The page also does not say what happens when you pass the message volume. Their own FAQ does: you lose access to your reports and dashboard rather than being billed for overage. That is a harsher failure mode than an overage charge, and worth knowing before you size the plan.
tools.best_for: anyone who sends email from their own domain and has not yet got DMARC to enforcement — the reporting is the part that makes that safe rather than guesswork
tools.skip_if: you have one domain, send little email, and are willing to read raw XML reports yourself, because the free tier plus patience covers the same ground
compare_with: the direct DMARC-platform peers — compare on domains included and history retention, not on the feature list

tools.name: EcomXray
tools.what_it_does: Shows cost price, gross margin, current stock and net units sold over 30, 90 and 365 days for every Shopify product, with restock advice from real sales velocity. The analytics are free; Pro at $29 a month adds in-place product editing, SEO fields, an activity log and a Chrome extension.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/ecomxray) Two tiers. Free: product analytics inside Shopify, cost price and gross margin, net units sold over 30, 90 and 365 days with refunds, cancellations and test orders excluded, 30-day restock recommendations and a revenue rank for top products. Pro is $29 a month, with a 14-day free trial. It carries everything in Free plus editing product name, description and price in place, SEO fields with automatic URL redirects, publishing to channels and managing collections. There is also a full product activity log, and a Chrome extension showing stock value and editing on your storefront product pages. There is no annual rate on the listing. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer aMemory ApS, Ellegardvej 36, Sonderborg, Denmark; the app launched 20 July 2026.
tools.honest_knock:
The split between the two tiers is unusually clean, and worth seeing clearly: everything this app is described as doing, the margins, the net units, the restock advice, is free. The $29 buys editing, not insight. If you are happy making changes in the Shopify admin you already have, the free plan is the whole product and the paid one is a convenience layer over it.

The track record is the real caveat. The app launched on 20 July 2026 and has no reviews at all yet. Nothing is known about how it behaves at scale, how it handles a catalogue in the tens of thousands, or how quickly support answers, because nobody has said so in public.

And its numbers are only as good as your cost prices. Gross margin comes out of Shopify's own cost-per-item field, so if that field is empty or stale across your catalogue, the margin column is decoration. Fill the cost prices in first, then judge the app.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size Shopify merchants who want cost price, gross margin, clean net unit sales and restock advice inside the admin instead of exporting to a spreadsheet
tools.skip_if: you sell across several channels and need cross-platform inventory sync, you already run a dedicated inventory or MRP system, or you want an app with a public track record longer than a month

tools.name: eDesk
tools.what_it_does: E-commerce helpdesk: one unified inbox for Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email, with order data and an AI Agent that bills per resolved outcome. Free plan; paid from $39/agent/mo (annual).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free plan to start; Essential $39 per agent/mo, Growth $89 (recommended), Professional $119, Enterprise custom — all billed annually, with monthly billing 20% higher ($49 against $39 on Essential). The AI Agent is included on every paid tier, but its automated resolutions bill separately at $0.99 per outcome: you pay when it actually resolves a query, not per attempt. eDesk claims the agent can automate up to 65% of support across channels, so model the outcome fee against your ticket volume — at 1,000 resolved tickets a month that is $990 on top of the seats.
tools.honest_knock: There are two meters, and the second one is easy to miss. The per-agent price is the entry ticket, but the AI Agent charges $0.99 for every automated resolution on top. That is great when it deflects real tickets, but it is a variable line item that scales with your support volume — model it against your ticket count before assuming a flat bill. And the honest fundamental for any e-commerce helpdesk: the value is only as good as your marketplace integrations actually syncing — test Amazon/eBay/Shopify connections with your real accounts during the free trial.
tools.best_for: e-commerce and marketplace sellers who want one unified inbox across Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email — with order data and AI-assisted replies where support and revenue overlap
tools.skip_if: you run a non-commerce SaaS or service business (general helpdesks fit better and cheaper), or your ticket volume is low enough that a shared inbox already copes
compare_with: Gorgias is the other big e-commerce helpdesk, deepest on Shopify; eDesk leans harder into marketplaces (Amazon, eBay) and per-outcome AI pricing — pick by where your orders actually live and how you want the AI billed

tools.name: ElevateForward
tools.what_it_does: An operational execution and alignment platform (Elevate Studio) for scaling companies, structured in three layers — Strategy (set priorities and initiatives), Execution (track initiatives, workstreams, ownership and KPIs), and Momentum (adoption, change management and follow-through). It turns strategy into structured, visible execution rather than task lists.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-21, read on their own pricing page) The prices are published, despite the consultative first impression, and the report figures have not moved since our 12 August reading. An Elevate Insight Report is $500, a bundle of three is $1,350 at a 10% discount, and the Elevate Studio tiers render at $250, $500 and $750 a month. Those three are Elevate Strategy, Elevate Execution and Business Enablement, the last still marked coming soon. A report is scoped to one focus area you choose, delivered within five business days of submission, with up to two rounds of feedback-based adjustments and a review consultation included. Treat the monthly figures as provisional: each price sits in a pair of spans whose second value reads $1,500 per report. For the three monthly tiers those second values are $8, $16 and $149. The page carries no visible label for either state, so which figure a given buyer is shown cannot be settled from the markup.
tools.honest_knock: It's a strategy-to-execution layer, not a task app or a dashboard — so the value only lands if leadership actually adopts the framework. 'Operational alignment platform' is also a fuzzy, crowded label, so press them on the concrete deliverables (the diagnostics, KPI blueprints and execution plans) before committing.
tools.best_for: scaling companies where growth is outpacing alignment — leadership lacks execution visibility and strategic initiatives keep stalling halfway
tools.skip_if: you already have solid execution discipline, or you just want a simple task or project tool — this is a strategy-and-alignment layer, not a to-do list
compare_with: an EOS/Traction-style operating system plus your existing PM and BI tools
the pieces EF tries to combine into one

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what_it_does: Market-leading AI voice platform: hyper-realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing, sound effects and conversational agents — plus a developer API and, since August 2026, a hosted MCP connector that runs inside Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Free tier to test voices before you pay.
tools.pricing:
(re-verified 3 Sep 2026 on elevenlabs.io/pricing) Every rate held for a second month. Free $0 with 10k credits/mo; Starter $6/mo (30k credits, commercial license); Creator $22/mo — first month 50% off at $11 — with ~121k credits. Then Pro $99/mo (~600k credits, 44.1kHz PCM), Scale $299/mo (~1.8M credits, 3 workspace seats) and Business $990/mo (~6M credits, 10 seats). Extra usage runs roughly $0.36 down to $0.17 per additional minute depending on tier.

Two things the plan cards do not put next to the price. Annual billing is sold as ten months rather than twelve — the FAQ writes it out as annual price = monthly price × 10, which works out to $5 for Starter, $18.33 for Creator, $82.50 for Pro, $249.17 for Scale and $825 for Business. And credits are shared across every product, so speech, music, dubbing and video all draw down the same monthly balance. On a paid plan unused credits roll over for up to two months — the balance caps at three times the monthly quota — but downgrading or cancelling forfeits whatever is left at the end of the cycle, and the free plan has no rollover at all.
tools.honest_knock: Credits are the meter and retakes are the tax — you are charged per generation request, and a regeneration is only free while the content and settings are unchanged, so real usage lands well above the calculator estimate. And read the free-tier fine print: $0 gets you 10k credits to play with, but no commercial license — anything you publish commercially needs at least the $6 Starter. Voice realism genuinely leads the market; niche names and jargon can still need manual retakes, so run your hardest paragraph through the free tier before subscribing.
tools.best_for: creators, developers and product teams that want the most realistic AI voices available — voiceovers, audiobooks, dubbing, conversational agents and a well-documented API
tools.skip_if: you generate hours of long-form audio on a tight budget (credit math punishes volume — flat-hour tools or the TTS built into your video editor may be enough), or you need acted emotional range only a human voice actor delivers
compare_with: Murf counters with studio workflow and per-language breadth, Descript bundles voice into a full video/podcast editor — ElevenLabs' edge is raw voice realism and the developer API

tools.name: EmailListVerify
tools.what_it_does: Email verification with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits — bulk list cleaning, real-time API, inbox-placement testing and free DMARC/SPF tools, plus a credit-based email finder.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on emaillistverify.com/pricing, read from the page's own JSON-LD offer data) Pay-as-you-go credits that never expire: 1,000 for $5 ($0.005/check), 5,000 for $17 ($0.0034), 10,000 for $27 ($0.0027), 25,000 for $54 ($0.00216), 50,000 for $98 ($0.00196), 100,000 for $186 ($0.00186). Monthly subscription at the same volumes: 5,000 for $16 ($0.0032), 10,000 for $25 ($0.0025), 25,000 for $49 ($0.00196), 50,000 for $89 ($0.00178), 100,000 for $168 ($0.00168), 250,000 for $346. The subscription discount runs from 5.9% at 5,000 credits to 9.7% at 100,000, so it grows with volume rather than being a flat rate. API included at every level; the email finder costs 5 credits per address found at medium-or-higher confidence. Free tools: email validator, inbox-placement test, DMARC/SPF generators. Note that /llms.txt and /pricing.md both serve the 404 page under an HTTP 200, so the JSON-LD on the pricing page is the machine-readable source here.
tools.honest_knock: The $5 entry pack is the most expensive way to buy: $0.005 per check versus $0.00196 at the 50k tier — a 2.5x spread that rewards guessing your volume upfront. And the email finder quietly consumes 5 credits per found address, so a 1,000-credit pack finds 200 emails, not 1,000.
tools.best_for: teams cleaning real sending lists before campaigns — bulk verification at volume rates, with credits that never expire
tools.skip_if: you verify tiny batches occasionally (the entry rate is the worst per-check price), or you mainly want prospecting — the finder burns credits five at a time
compare_with: Bouncer leans into deliverability polish and EU data residency; EmailListVerify wins on raw per-check price at volume, with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits

tools.name: Emergent
tools.what_it_does: AI app builder. Describe what you want and Emergent builds full-stack web apps for you — an agentic, credit-based platform that turns prompts into working software with no manual coding.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on emergent.sh/pricing) Free $0 (10 credits/mo); Standard $20/mo, or $17/mo billed annually, for 100 credits (the page states a $36 annual saving, 15%); Pro $200/mo, or $167/mo billed annually, for 750 credits (a $396 saving, 16.5%). Above Pro the ladder is quote-only: Business and Enterprise both show 'Custom' and route to Book a demo, adding RBAC, SSO, shared workspaces and co-editing (Business) and user-level credit limits, audit logs, self-hosted database support, VPC deployment and priority SLAs (Enterprise). The $300/mo Team tier with 1,250 shared credits is no longer offered. Credits meter the work -- simple changes 1-2, medium features 5-10, complex refactors 10-20+ -- which comes from earlier research and was not re-confirmed on the 31 Aug read of the pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: The real cost is credit consumption, not the flat sticker -- a genuinely complex app burns 10-20+ credits per big change, so serious builders move up tiers faster than the price list implies. Now do the division, because Emergent's own pricing page doesn't. Standard is $20 for 100 credits, so 20 cents a credit. Pro is $200 for 750, which is 26.7 cents.
