Moving up a tier makes every unit of work more expensive, not less: Pro costs 33% more per credit than Standard, and annual billing keeps the gap (17 cents against 22.3). That is the opposite of the volume discount the ladder looks like -- you are buying a 1M-token context window, custom agents and priority support, not cheaper work. And there is nowhere cheap to go above it: Business and Enterprise are both quote-only, so passing 750 credits a month means a sales call rather than a bigger plan. Check what your month actually needs before you upgrade; one Standard month plus purchased extra credits may beat one Pro month. AI-generated code still needs a human eye: review it for security, correctness and maintainability before anything touches real users.
tools.best_for: founders, PMs and builders who want to turn a prompt into a working full-stack web app or MVP fast, without writing the code themselves
tools.skip_if: you need a hardened, security-audited production system with no human review, or your usage would burn through credits faster than the value returns
compare_with: close AI app-builder rivals — compare credit economics and output quality on the kind of app you actually build

tools.name: Employment Hero
tools.what_it_does: Modular HR, payroll and recruitment platform for small and mid-size employers.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-28, read on their own pricing page at employmenthero.com/pricing/) EVERY PRICE ON THAT PAGE IS AUD EXCLUDING GST — the page states it in its own disclaimer. It is the Australian page; separate pages exist for the UK, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia and Canada, and there is no US one. Sold as separate modules rather than one plan. Recruitment: a free ATS tier at A$0 that includes 50 complimentary AI video interviews as a one-off trial, then A$199, A$359, A$639 and A$959 a month for 50, 100, 200 and 300 interviews. Those are annual-billing rates — the disclaimer gives A$2,388 a year for the 50-interview plan at a 20% discount, against A$249 a month on monthly billing. Interview credits reset monthly, unused credits do not roll over, and overage is billed automatically with no hard cap. No HR or payroll subscription is required for Recruitment. HR Essentials A$10 per employee per month, HR Engage A$14; HR Elite and Employment Unlimited are quote-only. There is no standalone payroll tier on the page any more: payroll sits inside Employment Unlimited, and Managed Payroll is an add-on at A$20 per employee per month with a A$400 monthly minimum. Other add-ons, each per employee per month with a stated monthly minimum: Chat A$2 (min A$20), Rostering and Time and Attendance A$4 (A$40), HR Advisory A$14 (A$280), Learning 10-course bundle A$8 (A$80), LMS Plus A$17 (A$170), EAP Standard A$8 (A$80), EAP Premium A$10 (A$100). A minimum of 10 Users applies, billed on the higher of the users named in your agreement or the active users. Every price on the page carries an asterisk. CHANGED SINCE 1 AUG 2026: the standalone Payroll module at $10 per employee recorded then is no longer on the page, and the currency was not recorded as AUD.
tools.honest_knock: There is no such thing as the Employment Hero price, and the first thing to fix is the currency: the pricing page is the Australian one, its disclaimer says every figure is AUD excluding GST, and there is no US page. Then the structure. HR, recruitment, chat and payroll are separate subscriptions, most of them per employee, with a stated minimum of ten users underneath — so a six-person company is billed for ten. Payroll no longer carries its own price at all: it is inside the quote-only Employment Unlimited tier, or an A$20-a-head add-on with a A$400 floor. And the recruitment tiers meter AI video interviews rather than people, with credits that reset monthly, do not roll over, and overage billed automatically with no hard cap.
tools.best_for: Australian and New Zealand employers who want HR and payroll from one vendor and will genuinely use both, where the per-employee rate beats separate systems
tools.skip_if: you are budgeting in US dollars — the page is Australian, in AUD excluding GST, with no US equivalent — or you only need one of the modules, since each is sold separately and priced as though you are buying the platform
compare_with: the usual comparison — build the total for the modules you actually need at your headcount, and convert before you compare: Employment Hero publishes in AUD excluding GST while both of those publish in USD

tools.name: EngageBay
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one CRM, marketing, helpdesk and live chat for small teams — a genuine free tier (250 contacts) and per-user suites that undercut the big names.
tools.pricing:
(re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 250 contacts with email marketing, CRM, helpdesk and live chat, and the plan card adds that it is free for teams of up to 15 members. All-in-One suite per user/month on monthly billing: Basic $14.99 (500 contacts), Growth $64.99 (5,000 contacts, marketing automation), Pro $119.99 (50,000 contacts). Those three rates are unchanged since our July reading, but the Pro contact allowance is not what we recorded then: it is a 50,000-contact cap, not unlimited.

Read the toggle before you read the number. The page defaults to a biennial ‘15% off’ display (Basic $12.74, Growth $55.24, Pro $101.99) with a yearly ‘8% off’ step in between ($13.79, $59.79, $110.39), so the friendly figure in the headline assumes you prepay two years. Single bays (Marketing or CRM & Sales) start at $11.04/user/mo on that same biennial display.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is contacts AND seats at once: prices are per user, and each tier caps contacts — Basic’s 500 contacts fills fast, and the Growth jump is steep ($15 → $65 per user). The advertised ‘starts at $12.74’ assumes biennial prepay — two years upfront for the friendly number. Real automation only starts at Growth.
tools.best_for: small teams that want CRM, email marketing, helpdesk and live chat in one affordable suite — the free tier is a genuine trial-for-life, and it undercuts HubSpot hard at small scale
tools.skip_if: your contact list is big (per-tier caps push you up fast) or you need best-of-breed depth in one area — all-in-one means good-at-everything, not best-at-anything
compare_with: Keap is the automation-first veteran at a higher price point; EngageBay is the budget all-in-one with a real free tier — pick Keap for automation depth, EngageBay for breadth per dollar

tools.name: Envoy
tools.what_it_does: Workplace platform for visitor sign-in, desk and room booking, deliveries and emergency notifications.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page and their platform page) Five products, each metered differently and all billed annually. Visitors: Basic free, Premium $362 per location per month, Enterprise quote-only. Emergency Notifications $2 per user per month. Reservations $5 per bookable resource per month. Screens $12 per device per month. Deliveries $250 per delivery location per month. All five amounts are unchanged since 1 August 2026, and the pricing page now publishes the Visitors Premium rate in JSON-LD with a billingDuration of one year. The line 'Price excludes platform fee' appears exactly four times, on Emergency Notifications, Reservations, Screens and Deliveries — not on the Visitors card. The platform page supplies the shape of that fee without its number: the platform is required to use Envoy products, it is 'priced as a flat annual fee', and it has its own Premium and Enterprise tiers that you choose before adding modules. That page also lists visitor management as one of the modules. Invoicing by ACH is offered only on Enterprise or with three or more Premium Yearly locations.
tools.honest_knock: None of the prices on that page is a price you can budget from. Four of the five product cards are followed by 'Price excludes platform fee', and the platform page says outright that the platform is required to use Envoy products and is charged as a flat annual fee — with its own Premium and Enterprise tiers to pick first, and no number published anywhere. That is the first thing to ask for. The second is how the meters stack, because they are all in different units: per location, per user, per bookable resource, per device, per delivery location. An office with forty bookable desks, six screens and one delivery point is paying on four clocks at once: $362 for the location, $200 for the desks, $72 for the screens and $250 for deliveries. That is $884 a month before the platform fee, and before emergency notifications at $2 a head. Price the combination you actually want, not the product you came for.
tools.best_for: companies with a real office and a front desk problem — visitor compliance, desk booking and deliveries in one system, where the per-location price is spread over enough employees to be worth it
tools.skip_if: you are remote-first or have one small office — a visitor log and a shared calendar cover the same ground, and the per-location floor is priced for buildings rather than teams
compare_with: the direct workplace-platform peers — compare the total across every module you would switch on, and get all three to name their platform fee

tools.name: Essential Loyalty
tools.what_it_does: Shopify loyalty and rewards app metered on loyalty-influenced orders rather than total orders, with VIP tiers and referrals on the free plan.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/essential-loyalty-rewards-program) Four tiers, and the meter is the whole decision. It counts loyalty-influenced orders — repeat sales and referrals — rather than every order your store takes, which the plan text states outright. Free covers up to 250 of those and is unusually complete: the point program, VIP tiers, a referral program, twelve-plus ways to earn points, product, cart, popup and account placements, built-in email notifications with Klaviyo, and discount, gift, shipping and credit rewards. Starter is $10 a month for up to 500, adding a dedicated loyalty landing page, full customisation, Shopify Flow, POS support for in-store loyalty and 24/7 human support. Essential is $24 for up to 1,500, adding loyalty status on the customer orders and profile pages and points in product cards. Growth is $79 for unlimited loyalty orders, with API integrations on request, white-glove onboarding and priority support. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps; the app runs in twenty languages and works with Checkout, Customer accounts, Shopify POS, Shopify Flow, Judge.me, Klaviyo and Omnisend. Rating 5.0 from 438 reviews, of which 430 are five-star and one is one-star.
tools.honest_knock:
Two things to read closely before you pay. The meter is honest — loyalty-influenced orders, not all orders — and that is genuinely in your favour, but it also means you cannot work out your tier from your order count. A store doing 3,000 orders a month with little repeat business may sit on Free; one doing 800 with a loyal base may not. Measure your repeat and referral orders for a month before you choose.

The second is an oddity on the listing itself. The free plan advertises an 'Advanced loyalty point program' while Starter at $10 advertises a 'Free loyalty point program', which read literally means the paid tier offers less on that line. It is almost certainly a labelling slip rather than a real downgrade, but it is the kind of line worth confirming with support before you upgrade for it.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with genuine repeat business that want a loyalty programme priced on the orders it influences rather than on total volume — and stores selling in person too, since POS support arrives at $10 and the free tier carries VIP tiers and referrals
tools.skip_if: your customers buy once and rarely return, because a loyalty programme has nothing to work with and the free tier shows you that within a month; or you need API work from the start, since integrations are 'on request' and only on the $79 tier

tools.name: Evey Events
tools.what_it_does: Sell event tickets straight from your Shopify store: unlimited events and ticket types, QR check-in, attendee data at checkout. Free to install at $1 per ticket; the monthly plans buy a lower per-ticket rate.
tools.pricing: (read 1 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/event-tickets) Four tiers, and every one of them charges twice: a monthly fee and a fee per ticket processed. Lite is free to install and takes $1.00 per ticket. Growth is $19 a month and $0.75. Standard, the tier the store marks Popular, is $49 and $0.50. Professional is $189 and $0.25. The paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. Feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations and the multi-vendor dashboard live.
tools.honest_knock: Nobody gets caught by the monthly fee here; they get caught by the per-ticket one. On Lite the app is free to install and then takes a dollar off every ticket you sell, which is invisible until you sell volume and then is the largest line on the invoice. Work out your monthly ticket count before you install anything, because that single number picks your plan: under 76 stay on Lite, 76 to 120 move to Growth, 120 to 560 move to Standard, above that Professional. Getting this wrong is not a small error -- at 300 tickets a month the gap between the best and worst choice is about $65 every month.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that sell tickets alongside products and want attendees, orders and customer data in one place instead of reconciling a separate ticketing platform against the shop
tools.skip_if: ticketing is your actual business rather than a sideline -- a dedicated platform gives you seating, promoter tools and box-office features that a Shopify app is not trying to match -- or you sell so few tickets that any per-ticket fee is friction you don't need
compare_with: the real comparison is not another Shopify app but Eventbrite or similar -- Evey wins when keeping attendees inside your store data matters more than box-office depth

tools.name: Evolve
tools.what_it_does: AI-native training and enablement platform for enterprises: an LMS with branded academies, an AI course generator, job-skill simulations with AI counterparts, an assessment center and performance analytics — used by 100+ deployed enterprises.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on evolveplatform.ai) No public price list -- there is no /pricing page and the call to action across the site is 'Book an intro'. The platform is modular by design and the quote is built from which modules you contract and how many seats: Evolve LMS, Course Generate, Evolve Studio course builder, Assessment Center, Knowledge base and Simulations -- six independent but connected products, not four. Budget for an enterprise-tier commitment.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for large organizations — the site lists 100+ deployed enterprises like Carlsberg and Danone — and the sales-led, quote-only motion reflects that: there is no self-serve tier to trial quietly, so smaller teams can't just kick the tires before procurement gets involved.
tools.best_for: enterprises and scale-ups that need structured, measurable training rolled out across hundreds of employees — branded academies, AI-generated courses, job-skill simulations and assessment in one platform
tools.skip_if: you're a small team that just needs a course builder or a lightweight LMS — the enterprise machinery and the procurement process are more than the job requires
compare_with: the established enterprise-LMS names win on integration marketplaces and long track records; Evolve wins on AI-native course generation and built-in job simulations with AI counterparts

tools.name: Expandi
tools.what_it_does: LinkedIn and email outreach automation for sales teams and agencies — smart limits, warm-up and multi-account management.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) 7-day free trial, no free plan. Business is $99 per month month-to-month; paying a year up front takes 20% off, which their own page describes as two months free, so roughly $79 a month equivalent. Pricing is per seat and Expandi states that the discount grows with the number of seats you buy, so a multi-seat agency quote is not simply the seat price multiplied. Higher tiers add role and permission management and centralised billing. Taxes vary by country and are added on top.
tools.honest_knock: There is no free tier and no cheap entry — Expandi starts at $99 a month per seat, and the friendlier $79 assumes annual commitment. It's also LinkedIn automation, which sits in a grey zone against LinkedIn's own terms: powerful for outreach, but a platform-risk you own.
tools.best_for: sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn (and email) outreach at scale who want smart sending limits, warm-up and multi-account management
tools.skip_if: you send occasional connection requests (LinkedIn's native tools suffice), or you're uneasy about automation against LinkedIn's terms of service
compare_with: lemlist is the multichannel outreach all-rounder with a big template community; Expandi is the LinkedIn-automation specialist — sharper for that channel, no free tier, and the usual platform risk

tools.name: ExpertEx
tools.what_it_does: A unified AI studio: chat across multiple models (GPT-4, Gemini), generate images, video and voice, and reuse prompts — multilingual, all in one workspace.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 in a live browser on expertex.ai/pricing -- plain fetches return an empty page, so this is the first reading we have of the real ladder) There are four credit tiers, monthly against yearly with two months free. Starter is $10 or $7 for 1,000 credits, and Premium $30 or $20 for 3,000. Ultra is $75 or $45 for 7,500, and Professional $250 or $149 for 25,000. Paid three-day trials sit alongside them at $1 for Premium (1,000 credits), $2 for Ultra (2,000) and $5 for Professional (5,000), with full access and cancellation before renewal. The page's own calculator prices the work at 25 credits per product photo, 250 per short video ad and 2,000 per full reel, and reels require Ultra or above. Credits roll over month to month while the subscription is active and are lost on cancellation; you can top up on demand or upgrade mid-month, with upgrades prorated immediately and downgrades taking effect at the next billing date. Prompt Builder is free to use before subscribing.
tools.honest_knock: The plan cards and the calculator on the same page do not agree, and the gap is large enough to pick the wrong tier. Starter is sold as 65 product photos and 10 short video ads a month on 1,000 credits; at the calculator's own rates that work costs 4,125 credits, four times the allowance. The card numbers only reconcile if each is taken alone, and at roughly 15 credits a photo and 100 a video. The same 4.2x mismatch repeats on every tier, so it is a systematic difference rather than a typo. Ask which rate governs before you buy, because the calculator will steer you to a plan two rungs above what the card implies. The second thing to price is that this is a credit product with no free tier. Prompt Builder is free; generating is not. And the cheap trials ($1, $2, $5) are three days rather than a month -- enough to test output quality, not enough to test a monthly workflow. And the fundamental one: AI product photography is judged on whether the output is publishable without a retoucher. Run your own worst product through the trial -- a reflective bottle, a garment with fine texture -- rather than the kind of thing that looks good in every demo.
tools.best_for: online stores that need a steady stream of product photos and short video ads and would otherwise pay a studio or a freelancer per shoot -- the e-commerce studio pushes results straight to the live store on Ultra and above
tools.skip_if: you need one hero shoot a year (a photographer is cheaper and better), your products are hard to render convincingly, or you want a free tier to evaluate on -- generating always costs credits

tools.name: Expertise AI
tools.what_it_does: AI sales agent for B2B websites. Replaces a static chatbot with a live, RAG-grounded agent that holds buying conversations, qualifies visitors and routes them to reps or calendar slots — HubSpot-first, with visitor intelligence.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-03; the ladder itself is unchanged since our 15 August read, but the Business conversation allowance is not) The ladder was rebuilt since our July read: the Growth tier at $500/mo is gone, and Business is now $2,000/mo instead of $1,250. What is left is three tiers. Free Preview costs nothing and covers 1 AI agent, 10 conversations and up to 50 training materials. Business is $2,000/mo on both monthly and yearly billing. It adds conversations for websites with up to 50,000 monthly visitors — the table labels this "Limited", and unlimited conversations now sit on Enterprise — up to 500 training materials, visitor intelligence, proactive live chat in HubSpot, 2-way HubSpot sync, 3 playbooks, a webhook and implementation by their team. Its Voice AI carries 300 voice minutes a month, and $0.25 per minute after that. Enterprise is on quote, adding extra agents, Salesforce and Marketo, SSO, active engagement, API access and dedicated hosting. Two side products are priced separately on the same page: the booking system is free or $30/mo ($24/mo billed yearly), and the Expertise Assistant is free, $50/mo per user ($40 billed yearly) or custom.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is that there is no middle any more. When we re-read the pricing page on 15 August 2026, the $500/mo Growth tier had been withdrawn. So the ladder runs straight from a Free Preview capped at 10 conversations to Business at $2,000/mo. And everything that makes the product genuinely powerful — visitor intelligence that de-anonymizes traffic, the 2-way HubSpot sync, Voice AI — sits on that paid tier. There is no way to grow into it gradually. It's also a RAG agent, so it's only as good as the docs you feed it: give it thin content and it can answer buyers confidently but wrong. Strong for HubSpot-centric B2B teams; less compelling if you're not in that ecosystem.
tools.best_for: B2B software teams (especially HubSpot-first) that want a live AI sales agent to qualify website visitors, hold buying conversations and route leads to reps
tools.skip_if: you're not running B2B demand-gen through a CRM like HubSpot, or a simpler support chatbot covers your needs at a fraction of the Business-tier cost
compare_with: close conversational-sales/AI-agent platforms — Expertise AI leans HubSpot-first B2B; compare on visitor-intelligence features and tier pricing

tools.name: ExpertSender
tools.what_it_does: E-commerce marketing automation with a built-in customer data platform: email, SMS, web and mobile push plus on-site messages, behavior-triggered workflows, product recommendations and segmentation on unified store data.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Quote-based with a documented floor: their site lists pricing starting around $450/mo, scaling with volume and channels, and they explicitly target stores with at least 30,000 unique monthly visits. No free tier — a free consultation is the entry point.
tools.honest_knock: The $450/mo floor and the 30k-monthly-visits target make this an established-store tool, not a starter one: below that traffic the platform can't pay for itself, and there is no self-serve plan to test it cheaply first.
tools.best_for: e-commerce stores from 10,000+ monthly visitors (the vendor's own stated ICP) and high-volume senders doing 100k+ emails a month, who want email, SMS, push and on-site messaging on one unified customer data platform with a managed, dedicated-partner setup
tools.skip_if: your store is still building traffic or you want self-serve, pay-as-you-grow email marketing — a Klaviyo-class tool is the lighter, cheaper start
compare_with: Klaviyo and Omnisend win on self-serve onboarding and ecosystem breadth for smaller stores; ExpertSender wins on managed service and a unified CDP for bigger catalogs

tools.name: Fast Bundle
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that covers every bundle format from one place — fixed bundles, mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks and AI frequently-bought-together — on product pages, in the cart and in POS. Metered on the sales your bundles generate rather than on catalogue size: free under $500 a month, then $19, $49 and $139, with $299 for uncapped bundle revenue. Shopify pulled the app after a July 2026 security incident and relisted it on 30 July.
tools.pricing:
(read 2026-08-24 on apps.shopify.com/fast-bundle-product-bundles, listed as “FBP | Fast Bundle & Upsell App”, and on fastbundle.co/pricing) The meter here is not your catalogue, your traffic or your seats — it is the revenue your bundles themselves generate. The listing is free to install and shows four tiers. Development stores are free to install and free to run. Standard (1K) is $19 a month or $180 a year and covers up to $1,000 of monthly bundle sales. Standard (3K) is $49 a month or $468 a year for up to $3,000. Standard (10K) is $139 a month or $1,380 a year for up to $10,000. All three paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial and the same feature list: unlimited bundles, upsells and cross-sells, mix and match, volume-discount upsell, BOGO and Buy X Get Y, unlimited AI frequently-bought-together, product add-ons, 24/7 English support and the AI bundle image generator. The App Store states all charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing page adds a fifth tier the listing never shows: Enterprise at $299 a month or $2,988 a year, described as limitless monthly bundle revenue, with automatic bundle detection in the cart, Shopify POS integration, minor specialised customisations, priority onboarding with an account manager and a five-minute support target against Standard's thirty. That page also prices the annual commitments as effective monthly rates — $15, $39, $115 and $249 — under a “2-MONTHS FREE” label, and it is the only place the free plan is described in full: all six bundle types, 24/7 support, available to development stores and “eligible merchants”, and capped at $500 in bundle sales a month. Its comparison table shows what the free tier gives up: volume discounts and product add-ons on selected products only rather than collections or the whole catalogue, no AI frequently-bought-together across all products, no multilingual translation, no subscription-app integration, and a “Powered by Fast Bundle” credit left on your storefront.

Fast Bundle's own FAQ defines the metered revenue as sales through bundles, volume discounts, product add-ons, mix and match, Buy X Get Y, frequently bought together and other offers created with the app, and states that exceeding your plan's monthly bundle revenue limit means upgrading to keep campaigns running. Developer Fast Bundle, listed at 13353 Commerce Parkway, Unit 2353, Richmond, BC, Canada; the app launched on 26 November 2020, the vendor's site claims 22,400 merchants, and the listing carried 3,031 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
The most important thing about this app is not on its App Store listing. On 17 July 2026 Fast Bundle detected what its own status page calls a security attack; Shopify removed the app from the App Store as a precaution and deactivated it on existing stores, so merchants found it simply gone. It was restored to limited visibility on 30 July and fully searchable again on 3 August, after Shopify reviewed an incident report and a third-party vulnerability and penetration test. The vendor states its investigation and testing found no indication that any customer, store or shopper data was accessed, exposed or leaked, and that 2,405 stores had reinstalled by early August. Shopify's own words, quoted on that page, are that the app “has been restored to limited visibility”.

Nobody outside the process can verify what was reached, and neither the vendor nor Shopify has published the technical detail. What is verifiable is the shape of the disruption: a storefront-facing app pulled without warning, deactivated on live stores, and roughly two weeks coming back. If your bundles carry your average order value, that is the risk you are underwriting — not because it is likely to recur, but because it has happened once and the app sits in the path to checkout.

The review record needs reading with that date in mind. 5.0 from 3,031 reviews is exceptional, and the breakdown is 3,000 at five stars against 19 at one. But most of that history predates July 2026, and Shopify app ratings skew high because merchants are prompted for them. What an average cannot tell you is how a vendor handles an incident, and on that the status page is the better evidence: dated, specific, quoting Shopify directly, and correcting its own earlier estimates in public. That is a good sign about communication rather than about security.

One practical hazard came out of the outage and has not gone away. While the app was delisted, other apps renamed themselves to include “Fast Bundle” — the vendor names Fast Bundle Offer, BOGO, BYOB; Sparrow Fast Bundle Upsell App; and Rabbit Fast Bundle & Upsell — and Shopify subsequently delisted three of them. Searching the App Store for the name is therefore not a reliable way to find this app. Install from the listing slug, fast-bundle-product-bundles, and check that the developer reads Fast Bundle.

Finally, the listing's data grant is broad even for this category: it edits customers and customer tags, products, inventory and collections, orders including third-party fulfilment and order edits, discount codes and promotions, Shopify Functions cart transforms, the checkout page and Online Store pages. Cart transforms are how a bundle becomes a single line item, so the scope is explicable, but an app with write access to your discounts and your checkout page belongs in your processing register and in whatever review you run after an incident like July's.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who want every bundle and upsell format from one app — mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks, AI frequently-bought-together — priced against what those offers actually earn rather than a flat fee, and who are comfortable with an app that Shopify delisted for two weeks in July 2026 and then restored
tools.skip_if: you need one bundle type only, where a single-purpose app costs less than the metered ladder; you sell in person, since Shopify POS support sits behind the $299 Enterprise tier; or an app in your path to checkout having been pulled and deactivated once, however well handled, is a risk you cannot carry

tools.name: Fastmail
tools.what_it_does: Private, ad-free email hosting with your own domain. Fast, secure email, calendars and contacts from an independent provider that doesn't mine your data. From 1 August 2026 you pick EU (Amsterdam) or US data residency, encrypted at rest on Fastmail's own servers — note that EU data is initially still replicated and backed up to the US while that infrastructure matures.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on fastmail.com/pricing over a US connection, with their country selector on United States and the 12-month term chosen) Individual is $5 a month, or $60 for twelve months, with 60 GB of storage for one person. Duo is $8 a month ($96 a year) for two inboxes and 120 GB. Family is $11 a month ($132 a year) for up to six people and up to 360 GB, at 60 GB each. The page also sells 24- and 36-month terms, so the twelve-month figure is the middle of three commitments rather than the cheapest one.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying for what the free giants monetize differently: no ads, no profiling, real support and standards-first email (JMAP/IMAP everywhere). The honest limits: it's email/calendar/contacts, not a Workspace-style office suite, so document collaboration lives elsewhere, and migrating decades of Gmail habits (filters, integrations) takes a weekend of care. For owning your address on your own domain, it's the boring, excellent choice.
tools.best_for: individuals and small businesses that want fast, private, ad-free email on their own domain with proper support and masked-email aliases
tools.skip_if: your team lives in Google Docs/Drive collaboration (Workspace bundles that), or free mail genuinely serves you and privacy isn't a priority
compare_with: Proton leads on E2EE, Workspace on suite breadth — Fastmail wins on speed, standards support and price for pure email

tools.name: Feedvisor
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven Amazon and retail-media optimization: dynamic repricing, ad automation and analytics for brands and larger sellers on Amazon and Walmart.
tools.pricing: Feedvisor publishes no price, and we checked that again on 2026-09-03. feedvisor.com/pricing returns a 404. Their own llms.txt lists every public page and contains no pricing page and no amount. The plan comparison at feedvisor.com/plans does publish a tier structure — Professional, Premium and Enterprise for price optimisation, Feedvisor and Feedvisor Plus for advertising, and a single Enterprise tier for brand optimisation — but every column ends in Request Demo rather than a figure. One correction to what we wrote before: the sentence we attributed to Feedvisor, that pricing is hybrid and varies with catalogue size, ad spend and complexity, is no longer anywhere on their site. The platform has been rebranded to Agentis and that wording went with it, so we no longer put those words in their mouth. Every figure you will read elsewhere, including the roughly $100 a month entry tier and the roughly $1,500 a month for the full platform that we carried before, comes from third parties or from sales conversations rather than from Feedvisor. Treat those as indicative only, and expect a sales call.
tools.honest_knock: The honest structure: the $100 tier is a limited on-ramp, and most of what Feedvisor is famous for (the algorithmic Buy-Box strategy that holds prices UP, ad management, analysts) lives behind the $1,500+ top tier — this is enterprise software for serious catalogs, priced accordingly. If your Amazon revenue can't absorb that as a small percentage, simpler repricers are the rational choice.
tools.best_for: mid-market and enterprise Amazon sellers with large catalogs where algorithmic repricing and ad optimization move real revenue
tools.skip_if: you're a small seller (rule-based repricers cost a tenth), or your margins are set by factors repricing can't touch
compare_with: the accessible repricer tier — far cheaper, rule-plus-AI based; Feedvisor's edge is holding price ceilings, not just winning races to the bottom

tools.name: Filevine
tools.what_it_does: Case management for law firms: matters, intake, depositions, e-signature and AI document work.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Their own wording: all packages are custom built for your team's needs. The page describes five products — LOIS (AI features), Matters, Intake, Depositions and Signatures — and routes everything to a sales team for a custom quote. No per-user cost, no minimum seats, no contract length and no implementation fee is published, which is unchanged since 1 August 2026. What the page does name now is a free way in: LOIS Explore, described as a free tier of LOIS for AI-powered legal research and drafting, with a trial that takes no credit card.
tools.honest_knock: Nothing is priced, so everything is negotiable — which cuts both ways. In legal software the number that usually surprises people is not the per-seat rate but implementation: data migration from your existing case system, template configuration and training, quoted separately and often as a one-off in the thousands. That figure is absent here along with everything else. Ask for it as its own line, ask what the contract length is, and ask what happens to your matter data if you leave. A custom quote is fine; a custom quote you cannot compare against a rate card is what you are trying to avoid.
tools.best_for: law firms past the point where a general project tool works, with enough matters that case-specific workflows and intake tracking pay back a negotiated annual contract
tools.skip_if: you are a small practice wanting a published price to compare — this category will not give you one, and simpler practice-management tools do publish theirs
compare_with: the standing comparison in legal case management — both publish per-user prices, which makes them the honest benchmark for whatever Filevine quotes

tools.name: Finale Inventory
tools.what_it_does: Inventory and warehouse management for e-commerce and wholesale: multi-channel stock sync, purchasing and barcode workflows that scale with order volume.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on finaleinventory.com/pricing) Essentials starts at $499/mo (positioned for 1-2 warehouses); Growth starts at $799/mo and adds the Mobile Barcode WMS module plus email, phone and Zoom support; Enterprise is custom pricing on request and adds API and EDI access, premium support with SLAs and a dedicated account manager. Both published figures are 'starting at' and no per-tier order, SKU or user cap is published -- the vendor's FAQ says overage means additional usage fees or a plan upgrade, with the thresholds written into your agreement. Every plan routes through Request a Demo; there is no self-serve signup or trial. Most customers sign 12-, 24- or 36-month terms. Standard onboarding is included and go-live is quoted at 2-6 weeks. Stated platform ceilings: up to 300 users, 1.5 million orders per month and 1.5 million products. The Self-Starter tier at around $99/mo that our earlier record described is no longer on the pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for real warehouse volume and priced that way: Essentials starts at $499 a month and Growth at $799, with Enterprise quoted. There is no self-serve tier and no published order or user cap -- every plan goes through Request a Demo, most customers sign 12- to 36-month terms, and API and EDI access are Enterprise-only. If you do a few dozen orders a month, this is far more inventory engine, and far more cost, than the job needs.
tools.best_for: e-commerce and wholesale operations with real order volume that need multi-channel stock sync, purchasing and barcode-driven warehouse workflows
tools.skip_if: you're a low-volume store where your sales platform's built-in inventory is enough, or you want a slick modern UI over deep functionality
compare_with: comparable multi-channel inventory platforms — weigh by which sales channels and integrations you actually run

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes your calls across Zoom, Google Meet and Teams — searchable notes, action items and CRM sync, so nobody takes minutes by hand.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Free $0 — unlimited transcription, limited AI summaries, 400 mins storage per team, 20 AI credits. Pro $18/seat/mo month-to-month or $10/seat/mo billed annually — unlimited AI summaries, 8,000 mins storage per seat, 20 AI credits. Business $29/seat/mo month-to-month or $19/seat/mo billed annually — unlimited storage, 30 AI credits. Enterprise $39/seat/mo, annual only — 50 AI credits, SSO/SCIM, HIPAA, private storage. CORRECTION to the previous dossier: $10 and $19 were carried as the price; they are the annual rates and month-to-month is 80% and 53% higher. Enterprise was missing entirely. The AI-credit ladder (20/20/30/50) means Pro adds no AI credits over the free plan.
tools.honest_knock: The advertised $10 and $19 are annual-billing rates; month-to-month is $18 and $29. And AI credits are capped on every tier — Pro carries the same 20 a month as the free plan, so upgrading to Pro buys recording and storage rather than more AI. If you mainly want real-time in-Zoom captioning and simple English notes, Otter is the simpler pick.
tools.best_for: teams that want every meeting transcribed and searchable automatically — the free unlimited-transcription tier is genuinely rare
tools.skip_if: your meetings involve sensitive topics where an AI notetaker joining calls raises consent or confidentiality questions — check policy first

tools.name: Flatpay
tools.what_it_does: Card terminals, POS systems and online payments for physical shops across Europe, sold with on-site installation and 24/7 support. One flat rate on every card type: 1.49% on the terminal, 1.69% on the POS tiers, with daily payouts and no monthly subscription. Read their separate price list before you sign, though: it carries a £995 minimum monthly turnover with a £39 charge when you miss it, £410 for a replacement terminal, and POS installation from £995 to £2,495 — all excluding VAT (read 13 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-13, read off flatpay.com/en-gb/pricing and their separate /pricelist page) Flatpay charges one rate per transaction on every card type, with no monthly subscription. The card terminal is 1.49% and costs £0 to start. The three point-of-sale tiers all run at 1.69% and differ only in what you pay up front for onboarding and installation: £995 for mobile POS, £1,495 for POS Pro and £2,495 for POS Premium. Every one of those four prices applies only below £200,000 in annual card turnover; above it, all four say “custom rate — contact sales”, so the published ladder is for smaller merchants only. Included on all plans: 24/7 support, daily payouts and a customer portal. The part that needs reading is the price list, which is linked from the footer rather than from the pricing page. It sets a **minimum monthly turnover of £995** and charges **£39 in any month you fall short** — assessed annually, so seasonal businesses are explicitly in scope. It also lists £410 for a replacement terminal, £25 to re-onboard after a change in business registration, and hardware separately: tablet £495, printer £495, cash drawer £200. All of those figures exclude VAT. One inconsistency worth raising with their salesperson: the pricing page puts POS Pro onboarding at £1,495 while the price list quotes a “Pro POS bundle” at £1,995 — a £500 gap between two pages on the same site.
tools.honest_knock: “Zero monthly fees” is the headline, and there genuinely is no subscription — but there is a floor. Miss £995 of card turnover in a month and you are charged £39, which for a quiet month is the same thing as a monthly fee wearing a different hat. Do the sum before you sign: a shop turning over £500 on cards pays £7.45 in transaction fees and then £39 on top, so the cost of taking cards is six times what the rate suggests. The rate itself is straightforward and the terminal really is free to start, so this is a good fit for a busy till and a poor one for a market stall, a seasonal business or anyone whose card volume swings. And the four-figure POS installation charges are real money that the “no hidden fees” promise sits directly above — they are disclosed, but they are not what most people picture when they read that line.
tools.best_for: a physical shop, café or bar with steady card turnover above £995 a month that wants one predictable rate on every card type instead of a pricing table full of card categories. The on-site installation and 24/7 support suit an owner who would rather not configure hardware, and daily payouts help if cash flow is tight
tools.skip_if: your card takings are small or seasonal: the £995 monthly minimum and the £39 shortfall charge punish exactly that pattern, and the price list says the assessment is annual so a quiet winter still counts. Skip it too if you are online-only — this is built around physical terminals and an in-person sales visit — or if you turn over more than £200,000 a year on cards, because then every published price is replaced by a quote
compare_with: not a like-for-like rival — Payoneer moves money for online and cross-border businesses while Flatpay sells the terminal on your counter — but it is the comparison our readers reach for when they ask what taking payments actually costs. The useful contrast is structural: Flatpay publishes one flat percentage and hides the conditions in a separate price list, where the fee that catches people out is a turnover floor rather than a per-transaction surprise

tools.name: FlexiQuiz
tools.what_it_does: Online quiz and test maker for educators, trainers and businesses: build graded exams, assessments and simple courses with certificates, timed tests, question banks and analytics — from a genuinely free tier.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on flexiquiz.com/Home/Plans; the monthly-billed rates were read from the page's own billing-toggle script, the yearly rates from the rendered cards) Free: 20 responses a month, no card required. Essentials $25/mo billed monthly or $17/mo billed yearly ($204/yr) -- 500 responses a month, 1 administrator, unlimited quizzes and questions, question bank, live quizzes, auto grading. Premium $39/mo monthly or $25/mo yearly ($300/yr) -- 2,000 responses a month, 2 administrators or trainers, learning paths, selling quizzes and courses, custom certificates, embedding, self-registration. Enterprise $89/mo monthly or $60/mo yearly ($720/yr) -- 25,000 responses a month, 15 administrators or trainers, APIs and webhooks, single sign-on, white-label emails, custom CSS, 100 custom groups, 24/7 priority support. Enterprise+ is tailored and quoted by sales. Yearly billing works out 32-36% cheaper than monthly, which is more than the 'save over 25%' the toggle advertises. Purchases over $300 can be invoiced for bank transfer or cheque against an additional $50 fee.
tools.honest_knock: The monthly response caps are the business model: 20 on free, 500 on Essentials, 2,000 on Premium and 25,000 on Enterprise -- one viral quiz or one big exam cohort and you're shopping a tier up. The per-response price falls steeply as you climb ($0.034, $0.0125, $0.0024 on yearly billing), so the ceiling is the thing to price, not the sticker. Administrator seats are capped separately at 1, 2 and 15, and sharing a login is against the terms.
tools.best_for: educators, trainers and small teams that want professional graded quizzes, exams and simple courses — with certificates, timed tests, question banks and analytics — without building out a full LMS
tools.skip_if: you need a complete learning platform with deep integrations, or your volumes run past a few thousand responses a month — the caps make it the wrong shape
compare_with: the generic form tools win on price and ubiquity for simple surveys; FlexiQuiz wins on exam features — grading, certificates, timed tests and question banks

tools.name: Flippa
tools.what_it_does: Marketplace for buying and selling online businesses, SaaS, apps and domains. Self-serve, so the due diligence is yours. Sellers pay a listing fee from about $29 plus a success fee starting near 3% — a bracket rate on the whole sale price, not a marginal one.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-03 on their own pricing page, USD) Sellers pay an upfront listing fee plus a success fee when the business sells, and BOTH change with the asking-price band. The success fee is 10% on every band up to $499.9K, then 9% from $500K, 8% from $1M, 7% from $5M, 6% from $10M and 5% at $50M+. The listing fee is not one figure either: on a sub-$10K asset it is $29 flat for a 60-day term, $49 flat for a boosted three-month listing, or $199 per six months for Premium; from $10K the ladder is $49, $399 or $599 per six months; from $50K it is $129, $399 or $699. From $100K upward there is no self-service option at all — Flippa routes those to its own brokers at a single upfront $399 to $1,499 for a six-month brokerage term, with the success fee still on top. Buyers browse free — AI matching, Deal Room, FlippaPay, escrow and multi-currency are all included — and a paid buyer subscription ($49 a month or $490 a year, up from $388 a year in our July and August 2026 captures) adds 21 days of exclusive early access to new listings valued over $10,000. Payment charges are published too: FlippaPay from 1% and Escrow.com from 1.2%.
tools.honest_knock: The real cost is the success fee, and it's a flat bracket rate on the whole sale price, not marginal — a mid-five-figure sale can hand over a four- to five-figure commission. Flippa is also a self-serve marketplace: more listings, but more due-diligence burden on you. Verification and quality vary, so buyers must vet hard and sellers should expect tyre-kickers. It's reach and liquidity, not a white-glove broker.
tools.best_for: buyers and sellers of small-to-mid online businesses, SaaS, apps and domains who want the largest marketplace and are comfortable doing their own due diligence
tools.skip_if: you're selling a large, premium business where a dedicated broker's vetting and negotiation earns its higher fee, or you want a hands-off sale
compare_with: brokered marketplaces that vet harder and charge more — better for larger, cleaner exits; Flippa wins on reach and low entry cost

tools.name: Flocksy
tools.what_it_does: A dedicated creative team for one flat monthly fee. Unlimited graphic design, video editing, motion graphics and web design — your marketing never waits on a freelancer again.
tools.pricing: Flat monthly plans priced by dedicated creative hours per business day: $1,199/mo for 2h/day, $1,699 (3h/day), $2,199 (4h/day), $2,599 (5h/day), $2,999 (6h/day), $3,399 (7h/day) and $3,799/mo for 8h/day, each billed annually and shown per month (re-verified 2026-09-03; every annual rate unchanged since 6 August, and the monthly and quarterly ladders are now published beside them at $1,699 to $5,899 a month). Plans start at 2 daily hours and scale to 8, with custom teams beyond that; month-to-month costs more — on the 4h/day plan Flocksy prices annual billing as saving $10,800/yr versus monthly. The pricing page carries a money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: 'Unlimited' means unlimited queue, not unlimited throughput: work happens at your plan's daily capacity, so a big launch week still needs planning, and turnaround expectations are where subscription-design relationships sour. The economics are simple and honest — against even one freelance designer's day rate, the math works IF you feed it steady volume; if your design needs are sporadic, a flat monthly fee is paying for silence — unused hours do bank, but only for 30 days.
tools.best_for: marketing teams and agencies with steady, recurring creative volume (ads, social, video edits) that want predictable flat-fee capacity instead of freelancer wrangling
tools.skip_if: your design needs are occasional or spiky (pay per project instead), or you need one senior specialist deeply embedded in your brand
compare_with: the unlimited-design subscription peers — compare real turnaround and daily capacity at equal price, not the 'unlimited' word

tools.name: folk
tools.what_it_does: Lightweight, collaborative CRM for managing contacts and relationships. Centralize your network and personalize outreach without the bloat. A mobile app (Contacts by folk) adds on-the-go search, one-tap contact capture with business-card scanning, voice notes and interaction tracking across WhatsApp, LinkedIn, email and calendar.
tools.pricing: $30/member/month on Standard, $60 on Premium and from $100 on Enterprise when billed monthly; billed yearly those drop to $24, $48 and from $80 per member per month — 20% off — for $288, $576 and $960 per member per year (re-verified 2026-09-03; every figure held). The same page publishes euro rates: 27€, 54€ and from 83€ monthly, 22€, 43€ and from 67€ yearly, for 259€, 518€ and 804€ a year. The free trial is two weeks and needs no credit card; folk's own FAQ says an account that does not upgrade is blocked rather than deleted at the end, and that the trial can be extended by a week on request. The published caps: email enrichment 500 a month on Standard, 1,000 on Premium and custom on Enterprise; AI magic fields 2,000 and 5,000; account sync one per member and five per member.
tools.honest_knock: One gap has closed and one has not. folk now has a mobile app — the pricing table carries a Mobile app row ticked on all three plans — so the browser-only complaint is out of date. Automation still bites: Zapier and Make are marked Premium and Enterprise only, so Standard has no automation route at all, and the table shows no native multi-step workflow anywhere. Enrichment is capped at 500 a month on Standard and 1,000 on Premium, and email sequences need at least Premium.
tools.best_for: small sales teams, agencies and VC/partnership teams who want a clean, fast-to-set-up CRM with a great LinkedIn enrichment extension
tools.skip_if: you're a solo founder who needs your network on your phone, or you need real workflow automation and reporting — folk is lightweight by design

tools.name: Foxit
tools.what_it_does: PDF editing, OCR and organising priced under Acrobat: $129.99 per user per year for the desktop editor, or $159.99 for Editor+, which now bundles Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year. A perpetual licence is $209.99 once, and the AI Assistant stays a $49.99/year add-on.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 1 Sep 2026 on the Foxit pricing pages and the eSign JSON-LD) PDF Editor is $129.99 per user per year, or from $10.99 per user per month, with a 14-day free trial that asks for no card. PDF Editor+ is $159.99 per user per year and bundles what used to be a second bill: mobile apps, AI Smart Redact, cloud storage and Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year. A perpetual licence, Foxit PDF Editor 14, is $209.99 once per user for Windows or macOS, covering editing, conversion, OCR, forms and security but not the AI Assistant, Smart Redact, the document management system or any cloud feature. Every Editor seat carries 300 free AI credits per user per month; the paid AI Assistant tier is $49.99 a year for 2,000 credits a month per user, credits reset monthly and do not roll over, and the add-on is not sold for perpetual licences. Standalone eSign still exists and the pricing page prints it in its JSON-LD: Essentials is $120.00 a year with 250 envelopes and 10 templates for one dedicated user, Business is $300.00 per licence a year with unlimited envelopes and a five-licence minimum, so $1,500 is the smallest Business order; volume licensing starts at 30 licences and is quoted. Foxit publishes a volume discount of up to 30% for larger teams. An education discount is applied automatically at checkout when you register with a school email address; Foxit does not publish the rate. Foxit states the comparison figures are US list rates.
tools.honest_knock: Foxit's pitch is being the honest fraction of Acrobat's price, and on the headline numbers it delivers. The catch used to be that e-signing was always a second subscription. As of our 28 August 2026 reading that is only true below Editor+, which now includes Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year. The trap has moved rather than gone: buy the $129.99 Editor, then find you need signatures, and Editor plus standalone eSign Essentials is $249.99 a year against $159.99 for the Editor+ that bundles it. AI is still an add-on at $49.99 a year beyond the 300 monthly credits, and it is not sold for perpetual licences at all. Price the basket, not the first line.
tools.best_for: individuals and businesses that want full PDF editing, OCR and organizing at a fraction of Acrobat's subscription — especially multi-seat deployments
tools.skip_if: you only read and occasionally annotate PDFs (free readers cover it), or your org is contractually deep in the Adobe ecosystem
compare_with: Acrobat is the incumbent at 2-3x the price; PDF-XChange undercuts further on Windows — Foxit balances polish, platform breadth and price

tools.name: Frase
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered SEO content writing and optimization. Research, outline, write, and optimize articles that rank — all in one place.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Frase's own machine-readable pricing file) The headline figure is the yearly rate; paying month to month costs about 25% more, and both are shown on the page. Starter $39/mo billed yearly against $49/mo monthly: 1 seat, 1 site, 10 articles and 50 audit pages a month, Content Guard watching 10 pages. Professional $103/mo yearly against $129/mo monthly: 3 seats, 5 sites, 40 articles and 250 audit pages, extra seats $29/mo. Scale $239/mo yearly against $299/mo monthly: 5 seats, up to 10 domains, 100 articles and 1,000 audit pages, Content Guard watching 300 pages, extra seats $29/mo. The trial is 7 days with no credit card. FraseCMS hosting is included free up to 100,000 page views a month; moving the blog to your own domain is $19/mo on top of a paid plan, or $99/mo at a million page views. On Starter, Frase stops at the limit rather than billing you extra; on Professional and Scale you can switch on pay-as-you-go capacity, so there the sticker price is a floor rather than a ceiling.
tools.honest_knock: The article quotas pinch if you publish at volume (overage docs bill each), and it's a research-and-optimization tool, not a magic ranking button — it speeds up briefs, it doesn't replace the writing or the backlinks.
tools.best_for: content teams and SEOs who want to speed up research, briefs and SERP-driven optimization in one workflow
tools.skip_if: you publish only occasionally — the monthly quota and subscription outweigh the time saved for a handful of articles

tools.name: FreshBooks
tools.what_it_does: Invoicing and accounting aimed at freelancers and service businesses, priced by billable clients.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page) Every amount is unchanged since 1 August 2026. The prices shown are 90% off for three months. Lite $2.30 a month promotional, $23 regular, 5 billable clients. Plus $4.30 promotional, $43 regular, 50 billable clients. Premium $7 promotional, $70 regular, unlimited clients. Select is quote-only. Team members are $11 a month each on every tier, with 2 included on Select. Two add-ons sit in the fine print: Advanced Payments $20 a month and Payroll $40 a month plus $6 per user. The page prints the promotional saving beside each tier — $62.10 on Lite, $116.10 on Plus, $189.00 on Premium — which is exactly three months of the difference and confirms the discount runs three months and no longer. Separately, there is a 30-day free trial, and FreshBooks promises a full refund if you contact them within 30 days of purchase.
tools.honest_knock: Two things multiply the number you first see. The promotional rate is 90% off for three months, so Lite is $23 rather than $2.30 from month four. And the meter is billable clients, not invoices or revenue: Lite stops at five, which a freelancer with a handful of retainers passes in their first good quarter, and the step to fifty clients is $43. Then people cost extra on top at $11 each, so a two-person studio on Plus is $54 a month rather than $43. Payroll is a separate $40 plus $6 a head, which is the line most people miss when they compare this against a bookkeeping tool that includes it.
tools.best_for: freelancers and small service firms who bill time and want invoicing that chases payment for them — the client cap is generous enough at Plus for most one-person businesses
tools.skip_if: you have more than a handful of clients and only need invoicing — the client cap is what pushes you up the ladder here, and flat-priced invoicing tools do not care how many clients you have
compare_with: the standing comparison — FreshBooks is friendlier for service billing, the other two are stronger accounting; compare on post-promotional price plus your team count

tools.name: Freshchat
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered customer messaging from Freshworks: live chat and chatbots across your website, app, WhatsApp and Instagram, with a unified agent inbox and automation that deflects repetitive questions.
tools.pricing: Read 1 Sep 2026 on freshworks.com/live-chat-software/pricing/ (USD fields of the page own plan data). Free is $0 for up to 10 agents. Per agent per month: Growth $19 billed annually or $23 monthly, Pro $49 or $59, Enterprise $79 or $95. Freddy AI is a separate bill, and both rates are published: the Freddy AI Copilot add-on is $29/agent/mo billed annually ($35 monthly), and Freddy AI Agent sessions cost $49 per 100 sessions beyond the 500 complimentary sessions each paid account receives once. Other add-ons on the same page: Freshcaller at $15/$39/$69 per agent per month annually ($18/$47/$83 monthly) on Growth/Pro/Enterprise, campaign contacts at $100, connector app tasks at $80, and day passes at $2/$7/$12.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is genuinely useful for small teams, but AI features and higher-tier routing sit behind paid plans and add-ons — and being part of the wider Freshworks suite means you'll be nudged toward the full platform.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid support teams that want live chat and messaging with a real free tier to start
tools.skip_if: you need a full help-desk and ticketing system, not just chat — look at a complete support suite instead of bolting on channels

tools.name: Freshservice
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered IT service management (ITSM) from Freshworks: cloud help desk, ticketing, asset management and workflow automation to run IT support and internal service desks without heavy ITIL overhead.
tools.pricing: Per agent, read 1 Sep 2026 on freshworks.com/freshservice/pricing/ (USD fields of the page own plan data, so not a euro reading): Starter $19/agent/mo billed annually or $29 monthly; Growth $49 or $59; Pro $99 or $119; Enterprise $139 or $167 -- Enterprise is no longer quote-only. Monthly billing costs 53% more on Starter and about 20% more on every tier above it. Metered on top of the seat: Freddy AI Copilot $29/agent/mo (Pro and Enterprise), orchestration transactions included at 1,000/2,000/5,000/20,000 per account per month with extra packs at $250 per 1,000, an e-signature pack at $90 for 30 signature credits, project management licences at $15/user/mo, a Business Agent add-on at $49 and connector app tasks at $80. Every tier includes the ITAM Growth package and 100 ITAM Growth asset units; further units are bought separately.
tools.honest_knock: The $19 headline rarely survives contact with a real deployment: the ITSM features most IT teams buy for (change/problem management, deeper analytics) live at Pro, and the modern extras — AI agent sessions, orchestration runs, asset counts — meter separately. Price the tier that contains your must-haves plus realistic AI usage, not the starter row. Within that honesty, it's one of the fastest ITSM tools to actually stand up.
tools.best_for: IT teams that want proper ITSM (incidents, assets, changes, service catalog) running in weeks, without enterprise-suite implementation pain
tools.skip_if: you need a simple shared helpdesk (Freshdesk-class is cheaper) or you're at the scale where ServiceNow's depth is genuinely required
compare_with: JSM undercuts for dev-centric teams; ServiceNow rules the enterprise — Freshservice wins the mid-market on speed-to-value

tools.name: Freshworks
tools.what_it_does: Suite of separately-sold products: Freshdesk support, Freshservice IT, Freshsales CRM, Freshchat and Freshcaller.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing pages) The main Freshworks pricing page still carries no prices at all — it lists the products and links out to each one, and that list has grown to nine: Freshdesk Omni, Freshdesk, Freshchat, Freshcaller, Freshservice, Freshservice for Business Teams, Freshsales, Freshsales Suite and Freshmarketer. On Freshdesk the annual rates are unchanged since 1 August 2026: Growth $19 per agent per month, Pro $55, Enterprise $89, billed annually. What has changed is that the monthly column is now published: Growth $23, Pro $66, Enterprise $107 per agent per month, billed monthly. The page's SAVE 20% badge overstates the gap — $19 against $23 is 17.4%, $55 against $66 is 16.7%, $89 against $107 is 16.8%. Freddy AI Agent is included with the first 500 sessions; additional sessions are $49 per 100. Freddy AI Copilot is a separate add-on at $29 per agent per month annually, or $35 monthly, on Pro and Enterprise only. Day passes are $2, $7 and $12 per pass on Growth, Pro and Enterprise. Connector app tasks are $80 per 5,000 tasks. The 14-day free trial starts you on Enterprise.
tools.honest_knock: Freshworks is not a product, it is nine of them behind a pricing page that contains no price. Once you find Freshdesk's own page, two things sit on top of the number. Freddy AI Copilot — the AI the marketing leads with — is $29 per agent per month extra, 53% on top of a Pro seat, and it is not sold on Growth at all. And the Freddy AI Agent that is included stops after 500 sessions; beyond that it is $49 per 100 sessions, so a busy queue turns the included allowance into a metered bill. The SAVE 20% badge on the annual toggle is really 17%. If you want support and IT and CRM, price three subscriptions, not one.
tools.best_for: teams who want a support desk that is cheaper per agent than the category leaders and will genuinely use the annual commitment — Growth at $19 is real value if ticketing is all you need
tools.skip_if: you want the AI-first product the marketing describes without doing the arithmetic, because that configuration is $55 plus $29 an agent annually, or $66 plus $35 if you take the monthly column
compare_with: the standing comparison — price all three with the AI add-on switched on, because that is where they separate

tools.name: FullEnrich
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact enrichment with waterfall data. Find verified emails and direct phone numbers for prospects by combining 15+ data sources in one lookup.
tools.pricing: (slider re-read 1 Sep 2026 on fullenrich.com/pricing from a Dutch exit; the USD amounts are the 26 Aug 2026 US reading, unchanged in structure) Pro is priced off a credit slider rather than a fixed tier: $55/mo at 1,000 credits a month, printed as $0.055 per credit, and $720/mo at 15,000 -- $0.048 each, so the rate drops as you commit to more. The slider runs from 500 credits to over 100,000. Enterprise is quoted. The free trial is 50 credits with no credit card, and inviting team members earns more. What a credit buys is the part worth reading and it did not change: one work email costs 1 credit, a personal email 3, a reverse email lookup 1, and a mobile number 10, so a list that needs phone numbers burns through ten times faster than the headline suggests. Credits roll over three months on monthly billing and twelve on annual. One caution for anyone checking these numbers from outside the US: the page localises. From the Netherlands the slider prints 0.055 euro per credit while the recommended-plan card on the same page still prints $720/mo, and the page structured data declares USD with a 0 to 500 range. Read the currency next to the number before comparing.
tools.honest_knock: The pay-on-success model is refreshingly honest, but note the 10x: phone numbers eat credits ten times faster than emails, so a calling-heavy motion consumes budget quickly — model your email/phone mix. As an orchestration layer over 15+ providers, its hit rate genuinely beats single databases; the flip side is you're paying a premium per contact versus querying one source that might have sufficed.
tools.best_for: outbound teams that need maximum find-rates on emails and especially mobile numbers, and prefer paying only for verified hits
tools.skip_if: you only need emails at volume (single-source tools are cheaper per hit), or your ICP data lives fine in one database already
compare_with: Clay orchestrates flexibly at platform prices; dedicated finders undercut on email-only — FullEnrich's edge is the waterfall hit-rate on phones

tools.name: Gamma
tools.what_it_does: Turns a prompt or rough notes into a deck, document or webpage draft. Credit-metered: the free tier gives 400 one-time credits and carries Gamma branding, Plus is €10/month (€8 on annual billing) for 1,000 monthly credits, read 16 Aug 2026 from an EU address. Output still needs a human pass for high-stakes decks.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-26 in the browser, and unchanged from our 16 Aug reading; the page is client-rendered and serves a bot challenge that our capture cannot pass, so there is no dated screenshot beside this. Served to us in euros from a Dutch address, so your own checkout may quote dollars) Free €0 with 400 one-time credits at signup and up to 10 slides per generation. These are the individual plans, monthly / annual per seat per month. Plus is €10 / €8 with 1,000 monthly credits and Gamma branding removed. Pro is €24 / €18 with 4,000 credits, API access and up to 10 custom domains. Ultra is €86 / €77.33 with 20,000 credits and the most advanced models. Read the annual column carefully: that €77.33 is not a rate Gamma charges but €928 a seat a year divided by twelve, and the same arithmetic sits behind €8 and €18. On the business side Team is €18 per seat a month (€216 a year) with 6,000 credits per seat, Business €35 (€420 a year) with 10,000 credits and SSO, and Enterprise is custom. Annual billing is advertised as saving up to 25%.
tools.honest_knock: The credit model means heavy generation eats your monthly allowance, and outputs still need a human polish for high-stakes decks — it's a brilliant first-draft engine, not a finished-deck button. The free tier's watermark pushes you to paid quickly.
tools.best_for: anyone who wants to turn a prompt or notes into a good-looking presentation, doc or webpage draft in minutes
tools.skip_if: you need pixel-perfect, brand-controlled decks — you'll spend the saved time re-polishing the AI output
compare_with: other AI and template presentation tools

tools.name: Gelato
tools.what_it_does: Global print-on-demand platform: design, produce and ship custom products (apparel, wall art, mugs, photo books) locally in 30+ countries with no inventory — integrates with Shopify, Etsy and WooCommerce.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-03 on gelato.com/subscription-plans in a browser session, every figure unchanged since 26 August; the site serves a bot challenge that our capture cannot pass, so there is no dated screenshot beside this) Free is $0 forever with two connected stores and two account users. Gelato+ is $29.99 a month, or $19.99 a month billed annually, and lifts both of those to unlimited while adding Personalization Studio, the AI tools and up to 33% off products year-round. Platinum is quoted, with custom discounts, a rewards programme and a dedicated implementation service. Note where those figures live: gelato.com/pricing publishes no subscription rates at all — it explains how payment works, with no upfront fees and no commission — and the plan table sits on /subscription-plans. The rates are in dollars even read from Europe. Gelato+ pays for itself on product discounts rather than features, so the question is order volume, not which tools you want.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is genuinely usable, so the honest question is only whether Gelato+ earns its fee — and that depends entirely on volume: below ~10 orders a month the discounts won't cover the subscription. Its real edge is local production in 30+ countries (fast, cheaper international shipping), but that means quality and product availability can vary slightly by region and print partner. Sample your key products before scaling.
tools.best_for: creators and stores selling custom products internationally who want local production in many countries to cut shipping time and cost, with no inventory
tools.skip_if: you sell only a handful of orders a month (stay on the free plan) or your customers are concentrated in one country where a single-hub competitor is simpler
compare_with: the major POD alternatives — Gelato's differentiator is its global local-production network; compare product range and per-item cost for your catalog

tools.name: GeoStock
tools.what_it_does: Shows per-location stock on the product page plus a store-locator map, so shoppers can see which branch has the item. From $9.99 a month, Plus $29.99. It displays inventory rather than managing it.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/product-inventory-information) From $9.99 a month, with a free trial. Base Plan $9.99 and Plus Plan $29.99. Rating 4.8 from 71 reviews. Developer sohkal llc.
tools.honest_knock: Know what this is before you buy it: despite the name it is a storefront widget, not an inventory system. It displays the stock you already track in Shopify per location, and adds a store-locator map — it does not manage, forecast or reconcile anything. If you came looking for multi-location inventory management, that is a different category and a different budget. What it does do well is close a specific gap: a shopper who can see that a nearby store has the item is a shopper who does not abandon.
tools.best_for: retailers with physical locations who want shoppers to see per-store stock and find the nearest branch on the product page itself
tools.skip_if: you are online-only — there are no locations to show — or you need actual inventory management, which this is not

tools.name: Geotargetly
tools.what_it_does: Geo-targeting toolkit — location-based redirects, content swaps, popups and personalization by country, state and city, priced by traffic volume.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) 14-day free trial. Six tiers, priced in USD: Dev $12/mo, Startup $24, Growth $49, Business $99, High Traffic $199, Enterprise from $349 — billed yearly $9, $19, $39, $79, $159 and from $279. Amounts unchanged; the yearly rates for High Traffic ($159) and Enterprise (from $279) are new to this dossier, which previously listed only the first four. All plans include country, state and city-level targeting. The meter is PAGEVIEWS, not visitors (the previous dossier said visitors): the FAQ states a pageview is consumed for every page visit, and that pageviews are consumed separately for each product in use; Geo Links consumes one on link click only. On quota exhaustion you get 2 days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop, with email alerts at 30%, 10%, 5% and 0%. Per-tier pageview quotas are NOT reliably readable: the page's JSON-LD repeats '500,000 pageviews/month' for every monthly tier and '6,000,000 pageviews/year' for every yearly tier, which cannot be right, and the visible ladder is a slider not present in the served HTML. Its priceValidUntil is stale (2025-12-31).
tools.honest_knock: The meter is pageviews, not visitors, and each product consumes its own pageview on the same page visit — so a redirect plus a popup bills twice. Run out and you get two days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop. The friendlier advertised numbers are the yearly rates; month-to-month runs about 25% higher. And the dependency worth pricing in: the rules run from a script you drop into your site, so they exist only while that script is served. Stop the subscription and every visitor sees the same page again, wherever they are.
tools.best_for: marketers personalizing redirects, content blocks and popups by visitor location — country to city level — without engineering work
tools.skip_if: your traffic is small enough for a hand-built redirect, or your CDN/edge stack already covers the basic geo-cases you need
compare_with: VWO is the full experimentation suite where geo is one dimension; Geotargetly is the geo-specialist — leaner and cheaper when location is the whole job

tools.name: GetResponse
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing with landing pages, automation and webinars in one suite, priced by contact count. Starter is €16/month (€13.12 billed annually) and allows a single automation workflow; unlimited workflows start on Marketer at €54. The better rates need long commitments.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page, in euros, quoted at 1,000 contacts) Free plan: 1,000 landing-page visitors a month, AI tools capped at 3 uses, webinars capped at 10 attendees, GetResponse branding retained, and premium features stop after 14 days. Starter €16/mo or €13.12/mo billed annually: 1 automation workflow, up to 3 users. Marketer €54/mo or €44.28 annual: unlimited workflows, 5 users, ecommerce tools, advanced segmentation, abandoned-cart recovery. Creator €62/mo or €50.84 annual: website builder, course creator up to 500 students, webinars up to 100 attendees. Enterprise quote-only, adding SMS, dedicated IP and 1,000-attendee webinars. Annual billing saves a stated 18%, and prices step up at 1k, 2.5k, 5k, 10k, 25k, 50k and 100k contacts. One currency warning: GetResponse's own FAQ on that same page quotes the entry plan at $19 a month for 1,000 subscribers while the plan grid served us euros — check which currency your own checkout uses before you budget.
tools.honest_knock: Priced by contact count, so the entry number climbs as your list grows, and the best value only shows on long (annual/24-month) commitments. A solid all-rounder, but you lock in to get the good rate.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want email plus landing pages, automation and webinars in one affordable suite
tools.skip_if: you only need basic broadcasts — a leaner tool costs less without the extra modules you won't use

tools.name: Getscreen
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based remote desktop and remote-support software: connect to any computer with no client install, share one-click access links, transfer files and record sessions — for IT teams, MSPs and remote support.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-02) Business rates on getscreen.me/en/pricing/plans/ are quoted on annual payment, which the page marks 16% off. The figures were first read over a US connection on 2026-08-26 as dollars and have not moved since; from a Dutch connection the same numerals print as euros, so the currency symbol follows the visitor region rather than the price. The business subscription bills on two meters at once, and quoting only the first understates it: Standard is $4.17 per technician a month plus $0.08 per device, Advanced $6.67 plus $0.13, and Enterprise $8.33 plus $0.17. Advanced and Enterprise add unlimited client invitations. Free plan (2 devices); paid tiers add one-time quick connections (Advanced) and white-label, roles and mass-device management (Enterprise) — plus a one-time Personal Lifetime Deal around $149, which sidesteps the recurring fees of rivals like TeamViewer (~$50/mo).
tools.honest_knock: AnyDesk tends to feel faster and lower-latency, and TeamViewer carries the heavier security/compliance certifications (HIPAA, SOC 2).
