Getscreen's real edge is being fully browser-based — nothing to install on the other person's machine — and cheaper, especially with the lifetime deal.
tools.best_for: IT and support people who want browser-based remote access without installing software on the other person's machine — at a fair price or a one-time fee
tools.skip_if: you need the absolute lowest latency (AnyDesk) or heavy compliance certifications like HIPAA/SOC 2 (TeamViewer)
compare_with: the faster and the more enterprise-secure rivals

tools.name: Gixo
tools.what_it_does: Seven separate AI workspaces — decks, articles, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal drafts and books — each sold on its own plan. Published floors run from $10 a month for Quill, Lumen and Prism to $49 for Arc, with a 14-day trial on six of the seven and no bundle price.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-19, read in a live browser on their own pricing page) Gixo is not one product but seven, each sold separately, and the pricing page publishes only a floor for each. Quill (articles and content), Lumen (decks) and Prism (visuals and infographics) start at $10 a month. Business (briefs and decisions) and Folio (books and long-form) start at $19. Lex (legal and compliance) is from $29, and Arc (proposals from RFPs) from $49. Six of the seven advertise a 14-day free trial and Quill's is explicitly no-card; Folio instead lets you plan or import a book free and charges monthly to draft. There is no bundle price and no published tier ladder: the pricing page says exact plan details sit on each product page, and the product pages we read carried none — they point you at the plan list inside the app. Quill, Lumen, Business, Arc and Lex can also be bought through Microsoft Azure Marketplace, with private offers for procurement.
tools.honest_knock:
Two things about this pricing are worth reading twice.

The first is that seven products means seven subscriptions. Gixo is priced per deliverable, not per company. So the moment a team needs decks and articles and a proposal it is buying Lumen plus Quill plus Arc — $10 + $10 + $49, or $828 a year at the published floors — rather than one plan. That is a fair trade if you genuinely need one of them and a poor one if you need three, because there is no published bundle to fall back on. Ask about a multi-product bundle before you subscribe to the second product, not after.

The second is that every number above is a floor and nothing else is public. “Plans from $10/month” is all Gixo publishes: what a higher tier costs, and what the entry tier actually allows in generations, seats or exports, is on neither the pricing page nor the product pages. You find that out inside the product. So run the 14-day trial at the volume you actually expect rather than on a sample, because the tier you land on is the price you will pay, and right now it is a guess.
tools.best_for: teams that want one dedicated, source-grounded tool per deliverable — a deck tool, a content tool, a proposal tool — and would rather buy them separately than bend one generic generator into every shape
tools.skip_if: you want a single flat AI subscription covering writing and design together, or you cannot justify stacking three narrow products to cover what one all-in-one tool does under one price
compare_with: Gamma and Beautiful.ai do one job — turn a prompt into a presentable deck — and publish a single per-seat price you can multiply in your head. Gixo spreads the same AI drafting across seven separately priced products covering decks, content, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal work and books, so it reaches further and costs more to assemble. If decks are the whole job, the single-purpose tools are simpler and cheaper; if you want the same draft-review-export flow across several deliverables, that breadth is the thing Gixo actually sells. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 19 August 2026.

tools.name: Glide
tools.what_it_does: No-code app builder — now sold as Glide Classic, next to the newer GlideOS — that turns spreadsheets and databases into working business apps: internal tools, client portals and field apps, with workflows and an API.
tools.pricing: (Classic re-verified 2026-09-03 in a live browser session on both tabs and both billing toggles, unchanged since 2026-08-04; the GlideOS plans were re-read the same day after a restructure) The classic spreadsheet-to-app builder still has a genuinely free tier: unlimited drafts, one editor, up to 25k rows. Its paid plans are unchanged, but they now live on glideapps.com/classic/pricing instead of the main pricing page. On the individual tab, Explorer starts at $19 per month billed yearly or $25 billed monthly (one app, 100 personal users, 250 updates, up to 25k rows) and Maker at $49 per month billed yearly or $60 monthly. On the business tab, Business starts at $199 per month billed yearly or $249 monthly, with unlimited apps, 30 users included, 5,000 updates and up to 100k rows. Extra users are $5 each on annual billing and $6 on monthly, and extra updates cost 2 cents each. Enterprise is quote-only. VAT is added at checkout, and Business comes with a 14-day free trial. Glide now sells two products from two pages. What glideapps.com/pricing shows today is GlideOS, the newer AI builder, on its own separate subscription, and its plan ladder was rebuilt between our August and September readings. The Free, Solo and Team tiers we recorded on 4 August 2026 are gone; as read on 3 September 2026 the ladder is Free, Basic at $25 per month, Plus at $50, Pro at $125 and a quote-only Enterprise. Free carries 2 team members, 10 projects and limited credits, with no published apps. Basic adds 100 credits, 2 published apps and 1 enabled workflow. Plus gives 250 credits, 3 team members, 5 published apps, 20 projects and 5 workflows, with credit bundles up to 10,000 a month. Pro starts at 5 team members with 500 credits, 50 credits included per member, unlimited published apps and workflows, premium integrations and the option to build with your own agent over MCP. Two things that used to be on the page are not any more: the $10 per additional member above five, and Glide's note that annual GlideOS plans were coming. So the GlideOS prices are still monthly only, and what a sixth seat costs is no longer published. Credit top-ups are capped at one a month on Basic and two on Plus, and are unlimited on Pro and Enterprise. One caveat on the row ceilings, from Glide's own partner team on 18 August 2026. The 25k limit applies to synced spreadsheet sources regardless of plan type, and the 100k+ figures apply to their Big Table data source. So which ceiling you hit is set by where the data lives as much as by what you pay. They also confirmed the Individual and Business tabs on the pricing page are audience segmentation rather than two halves of one plan ladder.
tools.honest_knock: Glide meters updates, not just seats. Your bill tracks how busy the app is rather than how many people own a licence. A write-heavy workflow can pass the included 5,000 updates and add 2 cents each without anyone changing plan. The jump from Maker to Business is also steep: $49 to $199 per month on annual billing, and the row ceiling only moves from 25k to 100k. Per Glide's partner team on 18 August 2026, those ceilings track the data source rather than the plan. 25k applies to synced spreadsheet sources whatever you pay, and the 100k+ figures belong to their Big Table source. So an upgrade alone does not lift a spreadsheet-backed app past 25k rows. The pricing page is hard to read for a reason Glide does not dispute. Asked about the Individual and Business tabs, the same team called them audience segmentation. They agreed on 18 August 2026 that the comparison tables confuse, because they never put all plans side by side. And there is a trap before any of that arithmetic applies: everything above describes the classic builder, but the free signup button on glideapps.com does not lead there. We pressed it on 7 September 2026 and landed in GlideOS, the newer AI product, which meters credits instead of updates, starts at $25 a month instead of $199, and describes its free tier only as “limited credits” with no number anywhere in the pricing page or the app. Read the classic prices, click sign up, and you are evaluating something else.
tools.best_for: teams that already run operations out of spreadsheets and want a real app on top — internal tools, field data capture, client portals — without hiring a developer
tools.skip_if: you need heavy custom logic or a high-write consumer app: the update metering punishes exactly that shape of workload, and anything beyond the published ceilings is a quote-only conversation

tools.name: Goflow
tools.what_it_does: Multichannel e-commerce operations: orders, inventory, listings and shipping across all your marketplaces in one dashboard. Goflow Core is free forever (500 orders, 3 users) and automates Amazon MCF fulfilment for TikTok Shop orders; the vendor states eligible orders may qualify for 35% savings on Amazon MCF rates (vendor mail, 27 Jul 2026). Goflow lists 250+ integrations across marketplaces, shipping, 3PL and accounting (goflow.com, 12 Aug 2026), and a nocnoc integration keeps Latin American listings, inventory, orders and fulfilment in sync from inside Goflow (vendor mail, 5 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 3 Sep 2026 on goflow.com/pricing; Scale changed, the rest held) Goflow Core is free forever at $0/mo with no credit card, covering 500 orders, 3 users, 1,000 newly created listings and every Goflow feature. Paid tiers add unlimited channels, users, integrations and listings — Launch $499/mo (750 orders), Scale $979/mo (5,000 orders plus wholesale/EDI orders; on 12 Aug this tier was $1,449 for 10,000 orders, so it has been cut in price and in volume), Enterprise custom — and Enterprise is the one annual commitment, twelve months, where every other paid plan is month-to-month. Billing is month-to-month with no setup or implementation fees, but EDI, SFTP and AS2 connections carry a one-time setup and testing fee of typically $500-1,300 per connection. There is no free trial and no discount programme — the free Core plan is the trial (vendor mail, 12 Aug 2026).
tools.honest_knock: Every tier ships the whole platform — you pay for volume, not unlocks — and Core really is free forever, so 500 orders a month costs $0. The catch is the cliff above it: orders past the Core allowance are paused until you upgrade, and the next step up is $499/mo. Goflow also states you cannot move back down to Core once you go paid. Budget the EDI setup separately: $500-1,300 one-time per connection, multiplied by the number of retail partners.
tools.best_for: multichannel e-commerce operations with serious order volume that want orders, inventory, purchasing, listings and shipping unified — including EDI retail
tools.skip_if: you sell on one channel only (a single-channel tool costs a tenth), or your volume sits just past the free Core allowance but nowhere near what the $499/mo Launch tier is worth
compare_with: the multichannel-ops peer set — compare at your order volume and count the EDI connections you'll actually need

tools.name: Gorgias
tools.what_it_does: Helpdesk built for ecommerce: tickets, automations and an AI agent, priced by volume rather than by seat.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 28 Aug 2026 on their own pricing page; every figure below unchanged since 1 Aug 2026) Not priced per agent — their own line. Two meters that stack. Starter is $40/month all in: a $10/month helpdesk with 50 tickets included and $0.40 per ticket beyond, plus the AI Agent at $30/month with 30 automated interactions and $1.50 per interaction beyond. Basic is $90/month month-to-month or $77/month billed annually ($924 a year), including 300 tickets and 30 automated interactions, with the same $0.40 and $1.50 overage rates. Pro is $550/month month-to-month or $471/month billed annually ($5,652 a year). Higher tiers scale the ticket allowance; their own framing is 50 to 5,000 tickets a month.
tools.honest_knock: Never priced per agent is a real advantage and worth saying plainly: your whole team can be in the inbox without the bill moving. The cost sits on two meters instead, and both bite. Tickets beyond your allowance are $0.40 each, so a bad week costs money rather than attention. And the AI agent — the thing the homepage leads with — is a separate $30 a month on the entry plan, which is three times the helpdesk it sits on. Automated interactions past 30 are charged at $1.50 each. So the honest entry price for the product as advertised is $40, not $10. Count a normal month's tickets and a busy month's, and price both.
tools.best_for: ecommerce support teams with seasonal or spiky volume, where per-agent pricing punishes you for having enough people on a busy week
tools.skip_if: your volume is steady and low — 50 tickets a month is the entry allowance, and below that a shared inbox costs nothing; also skip the AI agent until you know your automated-interaction count, since that is the meter that runs away
compare_with: the standing comparison — Gorgias wins when your team is larger than your ticket volume suggests, and loses when your volume is high and steady

tools.name: GrapeLeads
tools.what_it_does: Lead-finding for web developers and agencies — surfaces local businesses without websites from Google Maps, with contact details, on signup credits.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own buy-credits page) Pay-as-you-go credit packs, bought once rather than subscribed to: Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 credits ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 credits ($0.51). Bulk pricing is on request and signing up gives 20 free credits. Credits measure work, not leads: one credit starts a search and one more is charged for every filtered result, so a search that returns 20 matching businesses costs 21 credits. The vendor also states that unused credits carry a 50% bonus when its 2.0 app ships. Mind the URL — the price list lives at /buy-credits/ while the /pricing link 404s, which is how we had this down as unpriced until now.
tools.honest_knock: You are billed per result, not per usable lead: one credit opens the search and one more is charged for every business it returns, so a broad filter burns credits whether or not the results are worth calling. The packs are small enough that this is cheap to test ($28 for 50 credits) but it is the wrong shape if you want volume prospecting at a predictable monthly cost — there is no subscription at all. The site also still 404s its own /pricing link while the real list sits at /buy-credits/, which is an odd look for a tool sold to web professionals. And the niche (Google-Maps businesses without websites) is the real product: judge the data on one pack before you go further.
tools.best_for: web developers, designers and agencies prospecting local businesses that do not have a website yet — surfaced from Google Maps with contact details
tools.skip_if: you sell to companies that already have an online presence, or you want transparent pricing before creating an account
compare_with: Bookyourdata sells verified B2B contact lists pay-as-you-go at published rates; GrapeLeads is the niche specialist for no-website local businesses — smaller pond, sharper spear

tools.name: Gravity Forms
tools.what_it_does: Self-hosted WordPress form builder with conditional logic, payments and deep integrations. Licences run about $59/year for one site up to $259 for unlimited. WordPress-only, and much of the advanced power sits in paid add-ons that can add $99–349/year.
tools.pricing: Annual WordPress licences, read 1 Sep 2026 on gravityforms.com/pricing/: Basic $59/yr (1 site), Pro $159/yr (3 sites, payment add-ons such as Stripe, Square and PayPal Checkout), Elite $259/yr (unlimited sites, WordPress Multisite, priority support and every first-party add-on). No renewal rate is published on the page. The third-party extensions most advanced builds lean on are separate purchases with their own ladders: Gravity Perks $59/$169/$299 a year for 1/3/unlimited sites, Gravity Flow $99/$299/$447 for 1/3/50 sites, and GravityKit $119 for GravityView, $199 for GravityView Pro and $396 for the All Access Pass (all three were discounted for a first year at the time of reading).
tools.honest_knock: Two honest notes. It's a WordPress-only plugin — no WordPress, no Gravity Forms — and its real power often lives in paid add-ons and third-party extensions, so a genuinely advanced setup can cost more than the base license suggests. It's developer-friendly rather than beginner-slick; non-technical users may find hosted builders more polished. For a WordPress site, though, it's the reliable gold standard.
tools.best_for: WordPress site owners and developers who want powerful, self-hosted forms with conditional logic, payments and deep integrations they fully control
tools.skip_if: you're not on WordPress, or you want a hosted drag-and-drop builder with no plugin maintenance
compare_with: hosted SaaS builders that are slicker and platform-agnostic; Gravity Forms wins on WordPress control and a flat annual cost

tools.name: Guesty
tools.what_it_does: Property management for short-term and vacation rentals: bookings, guest messaging, channel distribution and pricing in one dashboard. Guesty Lite is roughly $9/month plus about 1% per reservation for one to three listings; Pro and Enterprise are custom-quoted. Heavy for a single listing.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Guesty Lite is $9/mo PER LISTING plus ~1% per reservation, for 1–3 listings; Pro covers 4–199 listings and Enterprise 200+, both quote-only. 14-day free trial of Lite. CORRECTIONS to the previous dossier: (1) the $9 is per listing, not a flat fee covering one to three listings; (2) the price is set by country. The page's geo-pricing table puts US, GB, AU, NZ, CA, MX and ~28 other markets at $9 both monthly and yearly (no annual discount), with country groups at $20/$29, $18/$26 and $16/$23 yearly/monthly, and a fallback of $27 yearly / $39 monthly for any country not listed — so the headline $9 is a major-market price and much of the world pays three to four times it. (3) The Pro and Enterprise listing bands (4–199, 200+) were not previously recorded. VENDOR SELF-CONTRADICTION, confirm before relying: the geo-price note reads '+1% per reservation | Including PriceOptimizer', while the same page's feature table lists Guesty PriceOptimizer as an 'Add-on' on Lite, Pro and Enterprise alike. Also add-ons rather than inclusions on Pro: Trust Accounting, GuestyPay, Fraud & Chargeback Management, GuestVerify, Damage Protection, Liability Coverage. Lite excludes owner management and the owners portal, rate strategies and promotions, phone support and a dedicated CSM, and processes payments through Stripe only.
tools.honest_knock: Pricing runs higher than leaner rivals, onboarding has a learning curve, and some users flag support — it earns its keep at scale, but it's heavy for a single listing.
tools.best_for: hosts with 1-3 listings starting on Guesty Lite (~$9/mo + ~1% per reservation) who may grow into the full property-management platform
tools.skip_if: you want quote-free scaling — Pro and Enterprise are custom-priced, so growth means a sales conversation

tools.name: Gusto
tools.what_it_does: Payroll, benefits and HR in one friendly platform. Automated tax filings, employee onboarding and time tracking — run payroll for your whole team in just a few clicks.
tools.pricing: Read in a browser on gusto.com/pricing on 5 September 2026 (the page blocks plain fetches): Simple $49 a month plus $6 per person for single-state payroll, Plus $80 plus $12 per person with multi-state payroll, next-day pay and time tracking, Premium $180 plus $22 per person with a dedicated service advisor and HR experts. Contractor Only is $35 a month plus $6 per contractor, with the base fee waived in the current promotion. No contracts, free setup, cancel any time.
tools.honest_knock: The base-plus-per-employee model is transparent but adds up, and Gusto is US-only — excellent for straightforward US payroll and benefits, but not the pick for international teams or complex multi-entity HR.
tools.best_for: US small businesses that want genuinely easy full-service payroll, benefits and tax compliance in one place
tools.skip_if: you employ people outside the US or need enterprise, multi-entity HR — Gusto is built for US SMB payroll

tools.name: Healthie
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one practice management and EHR for health, wellness and nutrition providers: scheduling, telehealth, secure messaging, billing and a branded client portal — plus a full API (GraphQL + webhooks) for automation. Built to scale with group practices.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page; yearly billing saves 10%) The entry tier is far lower than most summaries suggest: Core is $19.99/mo billed monthly or $18 billed yearly, Essentials $49.99 or $45, Plus $129.99 or $115, and Group $149.99+ or $135+ per month. Enterprise scales above that. Two costs sit outside the tier and matter for a practice: additional team members are $50 per clinician per month, and the ClaimMD billing integration starts at $30 a month. There is a 14-day free trial, and full API access sits above the standard group tier.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest limits: it's pricier than alternatives with thin mid-tier options, and several users report slow customer service (sometimes a week or more to reply). It really only pays off at scale — solo or tiny practices get more value, more simply, elsewhere.
tools.best_for: growing group practices (10+ clinicians) in health, wellness and nutrition that need multi-provider scheduling, telehealth and a real API to automate operations
tools.skip_if: you're a solo practitioner or tiny team who wants the simplest, cheapest setup — SimplePractice is easier and lighter for that
compare_with: the simpler, cheaper solo-focused rival — but with no API

tools.name: Heard
tools.what_it_does: Done-for-you bookkeeping and taxes built for therapists and a growing range of health-and-wellness practices — SLPs, dieticians, chiropractors, audiologists, coaches, massage and physical therapists: monthly books, quarterly tax estimates, annual filing and S-corp support by specialists who know the niche.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) Three plans, billed upfront per year with the monthly equivalent shown: Lite $129/mo or $1,548 a year, Essential $169/mo or $2,028, Premium $255/mo or $3,060. Lite covers done-for-you bookkeeping, financial reports and quarterly and annual tax support for solo sole proprietors; Essential adds personal tax preparation and filing; Premium is for group practices and S corps and brings payroll in as an add-on. Annual tax prep and filing is a $750 one-off add-on on Lite. Two costs sit outside the plan price: catch-up bookkeeping, required when you join, at $99 for each month you have been in business this year (advertised in September 2026 as a 50% limited-time offer), and payroll for S corps. The page now also offers a 30-day free trial of any plan, card required, $0 due today. Heard bundles business banking at no extra cost, advertised with 2.5% APY and $3M of FDIC insurance.
tools.honest_knock: Mind the fine print between tiers: the entry plan does not include your annual tax filing (a ~$750 one-off on Lite), it is annual billing only, and messy back-months cost extra as catch-up fees. Price the tier that actually includes filing.
tools.best_for: therapists and health-and-wellness practice owners — SLPs, dieticians, chiropractors, audiologists, coaches, massage and physical therapists — who want books, quarterly estimates and filing handled by specialists who know their niche
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable doing your own books in a general tool at a fraction of the price, or your business sits outside the health-and-wellness practice niche
compare_with: Bench wins on general small-business bookkeeping breadth, a good local CPA on complex situations; Heard wins on therapy-practice specialization and S-corp guidance

tools.name: Hello Bar
tools.what_it_does: Sticky bars, popups, slide-ins and full-screen takeovers for lead capture, with A/B testing and targeting rules. The meter is popup views rather than signups, so a traffic spike raises the bill however few emails you captured. Reported tiers start near $29–39/month for roughly 50k views.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-03 against hellobar.com/pricing) Hello Bar publishes exact prices, so the ranges we carried before were wrong: they were the monthly and the annual rate side by side. Paid tiers meter monthly popup VIEWS. Growth is $39 a month billed monthly or $29 billed annually, up to 50,000 views a month; Premium $69 or $49, up to 150,000; Elite $129 or $99, up to 500,000, with unlimited seats. The annual feature table states the same quotas as 600,000, 1.8 million and 6 million views a year. Starter is $0 forever with 5,000 views in total rather than per month. The view limit applies per website, and only a custom agency or enterprise plan can move it to a per-account basis. No credit card is needed to start, and first-time customers on an annual plan get a 30-day money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is views, not results: every visitor who sees a popup counts against your quota, so a traffic spike raises the bill regardless of how many emails you actually captured — a busy site outgrows the entry tier fast. And the honest fundamental of every popup tool: it amplifies an offer, it doesn't create one. A weak lead magnet with a beautiful popup is still a weak lead magnet, and aggressive full-screen takeovers can cost more goodwill (and Core Web Vitals) than they capture.
tools.best_for: content sites, blogs and stores that already have traffic and a genuinely worthwhile offer, and want sticky bars, popups and slide-ins with A/B testing to convert more of that traffic into subscribers
tools.skip_if: your traffic is still small (fix distribution first — a popup on 200 visitors captures almost nothing), or your list-building runs through gated content and landing pages rather than on-page interrupts
compare_with: close popup-tool rivals — compare the view-quota math at your real traffic level, since that's what you're actually billed on

tools.name: HelpCenter
tools.what_it_does: Shopify helpdesk with live chat and an AI FAQ builder: email, chat and Messenger in one ticket queue, plus SEO-friendly FAQ pages. Free to install; paid from $5.99 to $49.99 a month.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-08-29 on apps.shopify.com/helpcenter) Free to install, and the meter is tickets rather than agents — Basic already gives unlimited support agents, then bills for every ticket over the allowance. Free covers 10 tickets a month and charges $0.25 for each one after that. Basic is $5.99 a month or $59.99 a year, a 17% saving, and covers 50 tickets, then $0.16 each. Standard is $19.99 or $199.99 a year for 300 tickets, then $0.15. Advanced is $49.99 or $498.96 a year for 1,000 tickets, then $0.10. Every paid tier carries a 14-day free trial and all charges are billed in USD. Which means the headline $5.99 only holds to 50 tickets a month: at 300 tickets Basic works out at $45.99, because the 250 over the allowance add $40 — while Standard includes those same 300 for $19.99. Price the tier against your own ticket count rather than the entry rate. The App Store lists it as “SB: Helpdesk, Live Chat & FAQs” from Shark Byte, Inc — the product calls itself HelpCenter, so you will see both names. Rating 4.5 from 243 reviews.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is the hook and the FAQ builder is the reason people stay. But the meter is tickets, not agents: Basic hands you unlimited support staff and then charges $0.16 for every ticket past fifty. At 300 tickets a month that is $45.99, against $19.99 for the Standard tier that includes them outright — so check your own ticket volume before you treat $5.99 as the price. One dependency worth knowing: translating FAQs into other languages is handed off to a separate app (LangShop), so a multilingual store is two subscriptions, not one.
tools.best_for: small Shopify stores that want ticketing, live chat and a searchable FAQ page from one app rather than bolting three together
tools.skip_if: you already run a general helpdesk like Zendesk or Freshdesk for a business wider than the store — this is Shopify-shaped, not company-shaped

tools.name: HiBob
tools.what_it_does: HRIS with onboarding, time-off and people analytics, built for scaling mid-size companies. Quote-only, per employee per month: third-party estimates cluster in the mid-teens, plus a one-off implementation fee reported at roughly 10–20% of the annual value. Get the number in writing.
tools.pricing: Quote-only, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17: HiBob publishes no price list, their machine-readable site index lists no pricing page, and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. Pricing is per employee per month with modules bolted on, and third-party estimates cluster in the mid-teens per employee per month, plus a one-off implementation fee of roughly 10-20% of the annual contract. Those are estimates, not HiBob's numbers, and the whole thing is negotiated. Get it in writing, including what happens to the per-employee rate as headcount changes mid-term.
tools.honest_knock: Opaque pricing and an implementation fee mean the real cost only surfaces in a sales call — and it's built for scaling mid-size companies, so it's heavy and expensive for a small team.
tools.best_for: growing mid-size companies (roughly 50-500 staff) that have outgrown spreadsheets and want a modern, culture-focused HRIS
tools.skip_if: you're under about 25 employees — a lighter, transparently priced HR tool covers you without the implementation project
compare_with: simpler, more transparently priced HR platforms

tools.name: Hive
tools.what_it_does: Project management and team collaboration in one workspace. Plan projects, assign tasks and centralize communication so work keeps moving.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-03) Free forever for up to 10 workspace members, with 1,000 AI credits a month and 200MB of storage; Starter $5 per user a month and Teams $12 per user a month on yearly billing, which the page states saves 33% against monthly; Enterprise is custom. Read the Starter row before you pay for it: it lifts storage to unlimited and AI credits to 3,000 a month, but it keeps the same 10-member cap as Free and adds a 10-project cap. Only Teams, at $12 with 5,000 AI credits, gives unlimited workspace members. The add-ons are the part to budget: proofing and approvals, timesheets, team resourcing, advanced dashboards, SSO and enterprise controls, and external users each cost $5 per user a month on top, which their own calculator confirms. Two further add-ons, CRM and Finance, are listed on the page with no price at all. The external-user add-on includes 5 external licences per seat.
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is honest bait, the add-on grid is the business model: switch on three add-ons and your $12 seat becomes $27 — a la carte flexibility that punishes teams who need the full toolkit. List your must-have modules first and compare the DRESSED price against all-inclusive rivals; for teams needing only core PM, though, Hive is genuinely cheap and pleasant.
tools.best_for: project teams that want flexible PM (Gantt, Kanban, forms, chat) and only pay for the modules they actually use
tools.skip_if: you need most of the add-ons anyway (all-inclusive tools price better), or your org demands one standardized suite
compare_with: the PM heavyweights — ClickUp bundles more per dollar, Asana wins polish; Hive wins if your module list is genuinely short

tools.name: Hopp
tools.what_it_does: Business travel management from Bolt, branded Hopp: book and control company rides from one dashboard, with per-person and per-group spend limits, automated ride reports, expensing integrations and a single consolidated monthly invoice. No activation cost and no minimum commitment — you pay per ride.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-02 on gethopp.com/en/business/) Hopp Business publishes no subscription price because it does not charge one: the page states there are no activation costs and no minimum commitment, and billing is per ride on a single consolidated monthly invoice. Ride fares vary by city, vehicle class and demand and are not published as a rate card. The site cites 50,000+ businesses; the equivalent Bolt for Business page cites over 70,000 companies.
tools.honest_knock: The honest note is that the platform is free and the rides are not. Hopp Business charges no activation fee and no minimum commitment, so the whole cost is ride pricing, which moves with city, vehicle class and demand — and coverage thins out wherever Bolt does not already run. Check both on your own routes before you move a travel budget across.
tools.best_for: teams that already travel by ride-hailing and want the spend on one invoice with per-person limits instead of expense claims
tools.skip_if: your team travels where Bolt has thin driver coverage, or you need a published per-ride rate card to budget against
compare_with: the obvious comparison, and it turns on coverage — check which of the two actually has drivers in the cities your team travels to, because that decides more than the dashboard does

tools.name: Hostinger
tools.what_it_does: Affordable, fast hosting with an AI website builder built in. Free domain, free SSL and 24/7 support — perfect for founders launching their first MVP or side project.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own web-hosting and VPS pages) Shared and WordPress hosting runs four tiers on a 48-month term. Premium is $2.99/mo ($143.52 up front, 3 sites, 20 GB SSD) renewing at $10.99. Business is $3.99 ($191.52, 50 sites, 50 GB SSD) renewing at $16.99. Unlimited is $4.99 ($239.52, unlimited sites, 50 GB NVMe) renewing at $17.99. Cloud Startup is $7.99 ($383.52, 100 GB NVMe) renewing at $25.99. VPS is a separate ladder on a 24-month term — KVM 1 at $6.49/mo (1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe, 4 TB bandwidth) renewing at $11.99, then KVM 2 $8.99 renewing $14.99, KVM 4 $12.99 renewing $28.99 and KVM 8 $25.99 renewing $49.99. Every plan is paid upfront for the whole term, the monthly figure being the total divided by the months, and every plan carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. Both the shared plans and the VPS plans include a free domain for one year.
tools.honest_knock: The headline price only holds if you prepay years up front — renewals run several times the intro rate, the number-one complaint. Budget for the renewal, and be realistic that budget shared hosting isn't managed-grade performance.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious owners and side projects that want cheap, decent hosting and will prepay a multi-year term
tools.skip_if: you run a business-critical, high-traffic site — the renewal jump and shared-tier limits make managed hosting the better long-run value

tools.name: Housecall Pro
tools.what_it_does: Field service management for home-service businesses. Schedule jobs, dispatch techs, send quotes and invoices, and take payments from one app.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-04) Basic $59/month billed annually ($79 month-to-month, advertised as 'save $20/mo') for ONE user, with no GPS tracking and no QuickBooks Online sync; Essentials $149/month ($189) for five users; MAX $299/month ($329) for eight users, sold through a demo booking. Extra users beyond those counts are $100/month each on Essentials and $75/month each on MAX — a seat, not a small add-on. There is a 14-day free trial and no credit card is required. Card processing is quoted as 'as low as' 2.59% and bank payments carry a separate 1% fee, so the sticker is the smaller half of the bill: on $40,000 a month of card revenue the processing alone is at least $1,036.
tools.honest_knock: The Basic tier is a trap for real field teams — it omits GPS tracking and QuickBooks sync, so most businesses need Essentials or up. And the seats are the expensive part: users beyond the five on Essentials cost $100 a month each ($75 on MAX), on top of card processing quoted as 'as low as' 2.59% and a 1% fee on bank payments. Price the tier and the headcount you'll actually need.
tools.best_for: home-service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, cleaning) that want scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and payments in one app
tools.skip_if: you're a solo operator who just needs simple invoicing — the field-service features are more than you'll use

tools.name: HubSpot
tools.what_it_does: CRM platform with marketing, sales, service and content hubs on one contact database. Free for up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts; Starter is advertised at $7 per seat a month against a $20 list price, and Professional starts at $800 a month with a mandatory $3,000 onboarding fee on top.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-18, read in a live browser on their own marketing pricing page, USD view) Free is $0 for up to 2 users and 1,000 marketing contacts, with no time limit. Starter is advertised at $7 per seat a month against a list price of $20 per seat a month, under a banner reading “Save up to 65% on Starter — new customers only, select offers available for a limited time”. It includes 500 HubSpot Credits and 1,000 marketing contacts. Professional starts at $800 a month paid annually, or $890 a month billed monthly, and includes 3 Core Seats with additional Core Seats from $45 a month, 3,000 credits and 2,000 marketing contacts. On top of that comes a required one-time Professional Onboarding fee of $3,000 that the headline price does not include. Enterprise starts at $3,600 a month with 5 Core Seats, extra seats from $75, 5,000 credits and 10,000 marketing contacts, and a required one-time onboarding fee of $7,000. HubSpot AEO, their answer-engine visibility tracker, is sold separately at $50 a month or $45 annually for 25 prompts across 3 engines, with a 28-day trial.
tools.honest_knock:
Three numbers on this pricing page are not what they look like, and they compound.

The first is the $7. It is the number in large black type on the Starter card, and the $20 beside it in small grey type is the list price. The banner above the table explains why: up to 65% off Starter, new customers only, for a limited time. So $7 is an introductory rate and $20 is what the seat costs afterwards — a 186% step for a system that by then holds your contact database, which is the single most painful kind of software to leave.

The second is the $800. Professional carries a required one-time onboarding fee of $3,000, disclosed in a footnote under the card rather than in the price. Year one on Professional is therefore $800 × 12 + $3,000 = $12,600 if you pay annually, or $890 × 12 + $3,000 = $13,680 month to month. The onboarding adds roughly a third to the first year, and no amount of shopping around removes it — it is mandatory. Enterprise does the same thing at $7,000 on top of $43,200 a year.

The third is the seat count, because it is not the meter that usually bites. Professional includes 3 Core Seats and 2,000 marketing contacts. For a marketing platform, contacts are the axis that grows on its own: your list gets bigger whether or not you hire anyone, and the contact tier moves the bill without anyone deciding to upgrade. Price your next two years on the list you expect to have, not the team you have now.

One more thing worth knowing before you start on Free. The free tier is genuinely usable — two users, 1,000 contacts, no expiry — and that is exactly how the ladder is designed to work. The step from Starter to Professional is not incremental: at list prices a three-seat team goes from $60 a month to $890 plus $3,000 once, which is roughly fifteen times the monthly cost. Whatever you build on Free, build it knowing where the next rung is.
tools.best_for: teams that want marketing, sales, service and content on one contact database and will actually use more than one hub — that shared database is the real product, and it is what makes the price defensible when you use the breadth
tools.skip_if: you need one job done well and cheaply, because a dedicated tool will almost always beat the equivalent HubSpot hub on price; or your contact list is growing fast and your budget is not, since contacts are the meter that moves without you touching anything
compare_with: the honest comparison is not feature-for-feature but shape-for-shape. Pipedrive and Close are sales tools that do one job and publish a per-seat price you can multiply in your head. HubSpot is a database with hubs bolted around it, priced on two meters at once — seats and contacts — with a mandatory onboarding fee at the Professional rung. If you want a CRM, the dedicated tools are cheaper and simpler. If you want marketing, sales and service reading from one contact record, that is the thing HubSpot sells and they do not really compete. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 18 August 2026.

tools.name: Hubstaff
tools.what_it_does: Time tracking with screenshots, activity levels, GPS and payroll integration for distributed teams.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-29, read on their own pricing page) Priced per seat, with both billing columns published. Billed annually: Starter $4.99, Grow $7.50, Team $10, Enterprise $25 per seat per month. Billed monthly: Starter $7, Grow $9, Team $12; Enterprise is sold annually only. The annual column is labelled 'Annual (2 months free)'. Starter, Grow and Team each carry a 2 seat minimum, so the smallest bill Hubstaff will issue is $9.98 a month rather than $4.99. Their FAQ is explicit about what a seat means: 'Hubstaff charges per seat. This means that even if only two out of your three team members are using its tracking features, you will still have to pay for all three members.' Seats added mid-term on an annual plan are prorated — their example is $60 for a seat added in July on a January-to-December plan. Six add-ons are sold per seat per month: Insights, More screenshots, Tasks and Silent app from $2.50, Locations from $3.33, Data retention from $1.67. VIP Support is $29 a month per organisation for accounts spending $275-$400 a month and $59 above $400. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card, a 30-day money-back guarantee excluding that trial, and a free Project Viewer role for people who only read reports.
tools.honest_knock: The seat definition is the whole story and they state it plainly, which deserves credit: you pay for every seat you have created, not every person actually being tracked. So an account that grew with your headcount and never got tidied up is billing you for people who left. Audit your seat list before renewal, not after. The second thing is that features on the lower tiers are add-ons rather than inclusions — Insights, Tasks, Silent app and extra screenshots at $2.50 a seat a month, Locations at $3.33 — so the plan you priced and the plan that does what you watched in the demo may differ by ten dollars a seat. And be clear with yourself about why you are buying it: screenshots and activity levels change how a team feels about their work, and that cost does not appear on any pricing page.
tools.best_for: agencies and distributed teams that bill clients for hours and need defensible time records — the proof is the product, and per-seat is fair when every seat is a person you invoice for
tools.skip_if: you want to know whether your team is working — that is a management problem and surveillance software makes it worse; also skip it if seats churn a lot, since you pay for every seat you forget to remove
compare_with: the direct time-tracking peers — both are cheaper and neither takes screenshots by default, so decide first whether you actually need the monitoring

tools.name: Iconosquare
tools.what_it_does: Social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking, deepest on Instagram and the core networks. Free for one user and two profiles, then Launch around €33/month and Scale €69. Tiers gate on seats and profiles, so agencies managing many brands climb faster than the entry price suggests.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on iconosquare.com/pricing over a US connection, at their default of 5 social profiles) Launch is $39 a month, Scale $79 and Excel $139, all billed yearly; the page puts the yearly saving at $84, $192 and $336. Above 20 profiles it becomes a custom plan. The profile count is the dial that moves the price, so a quote taken at five says little about what a team managing thirty will pay — and the tiers differ in users and groups, not just in profile allowance.
tools.honest_knock: Its depth is strongest on Instagram and the core networks; if your priority platform sits outside its best-supported set, coverage thins. Analytics is where it shines — scheduling and community features exist but aren't always as deep as dedicated publishers. And the per-seat, per-profile tiering means agencies managing many brands climb toward the Excel tier quicker than the headline Launch price suggests.
tools.best_for: agencies and brands that want deep social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking alongside scheduling, especially Instagram-first teams
tools.skip_if: you need a heavy-duty publishing workhorse across many niche platforms, or a single free native analytics view already answers your questions
compare_with: Sprout is a pricier all-in-one, Later is scheduling-first — Iconosquare's edge is analytics depth per dollar

tools.name: iContact
tools.what_it_does: Straightforward email marketing for growing businesses. Build campaigns and automations with drag-and-drop design and deliverability support.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No permanent free plan — a 30-day free trial, then paid tiers by contact count, with 15% off for paying yearly. At 500 contacts Standard is $9/mo and Premium $16/mo; the ladder then climbs with list size, with Standard running $14, $28, $45, $73, $110, $180, $250 and $350 a month at successive contact bands and Premium starting from $16 and $27 at the equivalent steps. Standard covers templates, landing pages and automations; Premium adds unlimited users, social posting and the AI content assistant. Larger lists are quoted.
tools.honest_knock: Pricing feels a touch high for what you get, and the Standard plan's hard caps on automations and landing pages push growing teams to upgrade sooner than expected. Set against ActiveCampaign the automation builder is the thinner half of the deal; what iContact sells instead is a product you can hold in your head, deliverability that holds up, and a human on support included rather than sold as a tier.
tools.best_for: small businesses and nonprofits who want a simple, reliable email tool with strong deliverability and a real marketing advisor included on every paid plan
tools.skip_if: you need advanced multi-branch automation (ActiveCampaign does more) or you're chasing the rock-bottom cheapest option

tools.name: IDrive
tools.what_it_does: Cloud backup across many devices, with versioning, snapshots and physical seed-and-restore shipping. Personal is 5 TB at $9.99/month, shown at $6.99 on annual billing — but that discount is first-year only and the renewal step is about 43%, so budget on year-two rates.
tools.pricing: (2026, re-verified 4 Sep 2026) Free 10 GB Basic tier. IDrive Mini is $0.25/month for 100 GB ($0.83/month for 500 GB). IDrive Personal is $9.99/month for 5 TB, shown discounted to $6.99/month with annual billing (save 30%), scaling up to $99.99/month ($69.99 discounted) at 100 TB. Those are the yearly-billing figures the page opens on; switch it to the Monthly tab and the same Personal 5 TB plan is $11.99/month, and a two-year plan is advertised at up to 50% off the first year. Team starts at the same $9.99/month ($6.99 discounted) for 5 computers and 5 users on 5 TB; Business starts at $19.99/month ($13.99 discounted) for 500 GB with unlimited users. Add-ons: server backup $5/month/server, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace backup at $20/seat/year. The honest catch is on the pricing page in IDrive's own words: the discounted price applies to the first year of the selected plan, and standard pricing applies from the second year onward. Two further conditions sit in the same footnotes: going over your storage limit costs $0.25/GB/month on Personal and $0.50/GB/month on Team and Business, and the discount is for new signups only and is not available if you sign up from IDrive's mobile apps. Every figure above read the same on 4 September 2026 as on 27 August 2026.
tools.honest_knock: The first-year price is a teaser and the renewal is the price — IDrive says so itself under the plan table, and on the current numbers the step from discounted to standard is about 43% (Personal 5 TB goes from $6.99 to $9.99 a month). Budget on year-two rates, not the banner, and note that the discount is for new signups only and not available through their mobile apps. Overrun your storage and there is a further $0.25/GB/month on Personal, $0.50 on Team and Business. Beyond that, the honest backup fundamentals apply: a backup you never test-restore is a hope, not a backup, and the first full backup of multi-TB data takes weeks over the wire unless you use their physical Express seed shipping.
tools.best_for: individuals and small businesses that want cheap multi-device cloud backup with versioning, snapshots and physical seed/restore shipping
tools.skip_if: you need real-time sync-and-collaborate storage (that's Drive/Dropbox territory, not backup), or you won't tolerate the year-two renewal jump
compare_with: Backblaze is simpler flat-rate per computer; Acronis adds security suites — IDrive wins on multi-device flexibility per dollar, as long as you price in the year-two step-up

tools.name: InboxAlly
tools.what_it_does: Email deliverability tool that trains your sender reputation: engagement-based signals keep your campaigns and cold outreach out of spam and in the primary inbox — works alongside any ESP or email platform.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Every amount unchanged and confirmed on the plan comparison table, which states 'Pricing in USD, billed monthly': Starter $149/mo (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile), Plus $645/mo (500/day, 5 profiles), Premium $1,190/mo (1,000/day, 10 profiles), Enterprise custom (custom volume, unlimited profiles, dedicated deliverability experts). 10-day free trial, no card. No annual billing option is offered. Premium's sessions, more precisely than the previous dossier: a 1-hour setup/strategy session plus weekly 30-minute progress reviews. VENDOR SELF-CONTRADICTION, confirm before relying: the tier cards give Starter 'Email support' and reserve live chat for Plus and above, while the comparison table lower on the same page ticks 'Live chat support' and 'Dedicated CSM' for all four tiers including Starter. Phone & Zoom support, the setup session and the weekly reviews are consistently Premium-and-above in both places. Every plan includes IA Score, IA Reputation, Adaptive Autowarmup, the in-app IA Assistant, the full REST API, native CRM integrations and inbox placement testing.
tools.honest_knock: This is a premium, seed-list-based deliverability tool, and the price reflects it — Starter alone is well above casual warm-up apps, so it only makes sense if inbox placement is genuinely costing you real revenue. It improves sender reputation through engagement signals, but it's not a magic fix for bad content or a purchased list: deliverability still depends on how you actually send. Buy it when the math (lost revenue from spam-foldering) clearly beats the monthly fee.
tools.best_for: serious senders — email marketers and cold-outreach teams — whose deliverability problems are costing measurable revenue and who need active reputation repair
tools.skip_if: you're a small sender who just needs basic list hygiene (cheaper warm-up tools suffice), or your inbox issues stem from content and list quality you haven't fixed
compare_with: lower-cost warm-up alternatives — InboxAlly is pricier and more hands-on; justify it by the revenue your spam-foldered mail is losing

tools.name: Increff
tools.what_it_does: Warehouse management plus algorithm-driven merchandising and inventory optimisation for omnichannel retail. There is no public pricing and no flat fee — every deal is quoted case by case against warehouses, users and modules, so budget for an enterprise implementation.
tools.pricing: No public pricing, re-verified 2026-08-17 and consistent across every reading we have. Increff's own /pricing URL returns a 404, and our monthly captures of the site in July and August 2026 produced no amount at all. Increff prices every deal case by case, scaled to the operation — warehouses, users and which modules you take (WMS, merchandising) — which their partnership team confirmed to us directly on 28 Jul 2026. There are no published tiers to compare, so budget for an enterprise implementation and ask for a tailored quote.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise omnichannel supply-chain software, and the opaque, quote-based pricing signals the target customer: retail brands with real scale, not small stores. The value — algorithmic merchandising and inventory optimization — only pays off at a catalog and volume large enough for those optimizations to move money. For a small or mid seller, it's likely more platform (and cost and implementation) than the problem warrants. For a scaling omnichannel brand, it's built for exactly that.
tools.best_for: retail brands and omnichannel sellers at real scale needing warehouse management plus algorithm-driven merchandising and inventory optimization
tools.skip_if: you're a small or single-channel store where simpler inventory software suffices, or you can't commit to an enterprise implementation
compare_with: comparable inventory/warehouse platforms — Increff leans algorithmic merchandising for scaled retail; get quotes and weigh implementation

tools.name: Insightful
tools.what_it_does: Workforce analytics and productivity monitoring — time tracking, workflow optimization and insider-threat detection, priced per seat.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Per seat, billed annually. Workforce Analytics $8/seat/mo, Workflow Optimization $12/seat/mo (a beta open to selected customers), or both bundled at $16/seat/mo (saves 20%); Enterprise custom, and that is where audit logs and SSO sit. Add-ons: Workspace Security $4/seat/mo, screen recording $4, on-demand screenshots $4, higher-frequency screenshots $3 (up to 120 an hour), data-warehouse integration $0.50 for the whole bundle of custom API access, BigQuery and Snowflake. A 7-day free trial gives full access except Automatic Time Mapping, no card. Admin, manager and client users are not billed unless you also track them, and users added mid-cycle are prorated. On-premise deployment requires at least 250 licences.
tools.honest_knock: This is employee-monitoring software, so weigh the culture cost, not just the price: the advertised $8-16 rates are per seat AND assume annual billing, security features like insider-threat detection are a paid add-on, and monitoring tools can damage trust if rolled out without transparency.
tools.best_for: operations leaders who want transparent, consent-based workforce analytics — time tracking, productivity insight and workflow data — across in-office and remote teams
tools.skip_if: you value a low-surveillance culture, run a tiny team, or want month-to-month billing — the headline rates are annual and per seat
compare_with: Time Doctor is the established time-tracking incumbent; Insightful leans into workforce analytics and workflow optimization — similar per-seat model, so decide on features and how much monitoring your culture can carry

tools.name: Instapage
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise landing-page and conversion platform: build, personalize and A/B-test post-click landing pages at scale, with ad-to-page mapping, heatmaps and fast AMP pages — built for paid-ads and demand-gen teams.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 4 Sep 2026) Instapage does publish plan prices; they are not on the URL we had recorded. instapage.com/en/pricing redirects to the homepage at instapage.com/lp, and the plan table sits at instapage.com/plans. Our 26 August reading landed on the redirect, found no figures and concluded that prices had been withdrawn; the figures below match the last published rates this dossier already held, so the more likely explanation is a moved page rather than a withdrawal. Three tiers sit there. Create is $99 a month month-to-month or $79 billed annually, for 15,000 unique monthly visitors. Optimize is $199 or $159 annually for 30,000 unique monthly visitors, with selectors for 50,000 and for a custom volume — the custom option defaults to 50,000 and hands you to sales. Convert is quote-only. Annual billing is advertised as 'save up to 20%', and every tier carries unlimited contacts. The 14-day free trial asks for a credit card and is capped at 2,500 unique monthly visitors; Instapage's own FAQ states that exceeding that cap ends the trial automatically and moves you onto the paid plan you selected.
tools.honest_knock: It's premium-priced and only justified by serious ad spend — Create is $79 a month billed annually for 15,000 unique monthly visitors, and the price per thousand barely improves as you climb, so the higher tiers buy features rather than cheaper traffic. The 14-day trial needs a card and carries its own cap of 2,500 visitors; crossing it ends the trial and starts the paid plan by itself. And there's the ownership question the feature list does not raise: publishing to your own domain means pointing a CNAME at Instapage — their help centre carries a per-registrar guide for exactly that — so the page is served by them and lives as long as the subscription does. Their own docs add a second catch worth knowing before you standardise on it: “we lock domains under the first Instapage account that uses them”. Treat these pages as rented campaign infrastructure, not as part of your site, and keep the copy somewhere you control.
tools.best_for: marketing teams running significant paid ad campaigns who need post-click optimisation — AdMap ad-to-page personalisation, A/B testing and heatmaps
tools.skip_if: you run limited ad campaigns or want budget pricing — at $99+/mo it's overkill below real paid-traffic volume
compare_with: the other premium and the budget landing-page builders

tools.name: Intelis
tools.what_it_does: Monitors competitor prices on Google Shopping and direct competitor sites and reprices your Shopify catalogue automatically with AI matching rules. Priced by tracked products or variants: $49 a month for 100, $179 for 1,000, $249 for 2,000 and $399 for 5,000, each with a 14-day trial.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/ecoprice-analytics and on intelis.ai/pricing) Four tiers on the Shopify listing, priced by how many products or variants you track, each with a 14-day free trial. Basic $49 a month or $490 a year, a 17% saving: up to 100 products or variants, Google Shopping competitor monitoring, AI automatch for unlimited competitors, dynamic pricing, unlimited competitor URL tracking, reports, pricing history and chat support. Professional $179 a month or $1,790 a year: up to 1,000, adding variant tracking, sales analysis, live feed export, pricing strategy monitoring and premium chat support. Premium $249 a month or $2,490 a year: up to 2,000, adding Shopify Markets support per market, Google Analytics integration and API access. Business $399 a month or $3,990 a year: up to 5,000, adding a custom labels feed for Google Merchant Center, MAP monitoring, a customised AI matching algorithm, pricing consultation and A+ support. Intelis's own pricing page does not agree with the listing above Premium. It shows Business at $499 a month and $4,990 a year on its annual toggle, $399 on its monthly toggle, and an Enterprise tier for up to 10,000 SKUs at $849 a month. The company homepage prints that same Enterprise tier as $749. The listing is what Shopify billing charges you, so treat everything above Premium as unsettled and get the tier confirmed in writing. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Intelis; the app launched 6 July 2021.
tools.honest_knock:
The ladder counts variants, not products, and that is where stores get caught. A catalogue of forty garments in five sizes and three colours is six hundred variants, so a shop most people would call small lands on the $179 tier rather than the $49 one. Count your variants, not your line items, before you read the price.

Above Premium the vendor cannot keep its own numbers straight. The Shopify listing says Business is $399 a month. Intelis's pricing page says $499 with a $4,990 annual rate, and its monthly toggle on the same page says $399. Its homepage prices Enterprise at $749 while the pricing page says $849. Three published figures for the same tier usually means the tier is negotiated rather than listed, which is fine, but it means the number you were quoted is the only one that counts.

And automatic repricing is not a switch you leave alone. The matching is AI-driven across Google Shopping and competitor sites, and a mismatched listing quietly reprices the wrong product, while an unbounded rule set on a busy category is how a store races itself to the bottom. Set floor prices before you turn dynamic pricing on, and audit what the automatch decided in the first fortnight.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with hundreds to a few thousand variants that genuinely compete on price on Google Shopping and want competitor monitoring and repricing handled automatically
tools.skip_if: your catalogue is small, you do not compete primarily on price, or your variant count sits just above a tier boundary and would push you to the next rung for a handful of SKUs

tools.name: InVideo
tools.what_it_does: Turns a prompt or script into a first-draft video with AI voiceover, templates and stock footage. Plans are monthly credit allowances that do not roll over: Plus $20 a month, Max $100, Generative $200, Elite $1,000, roughly 15% cheaper paid yearly. The pricing page no longer lists a free tier, so Plus is the cheapest way in.
tools.pricing: Four paid tiers plus a free plan, read on invideo.io/pricing on 5 September 2026. On annual billing: Plus $17 a month (750 AI credits a year), Max $85 a month (3,900 credits), Generative $170 a month (8,000 credits) and Elite $900 a month (42,500 credits); month-to-month the same tiers are $20, $100, $200 and $1,000. Credits are the meter: every AI generation, avatar minute and export draws them down, and the annual pool is what you actually buy.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the credit model — each plan is a fixed monthly credit allowance that different models consume at different rates, and unused credits do not roll over, so a heavy month can exhaust an allowance long before it renews while a slow month simply wastes what you paid for. There is also no free way in any more: on 31 August 2026 the pricing page published no free tier at all, so the cheapest route to trying it is the Plus plan at $20 a month. AI video is fast but generic by default: templated output needs real editing and brand direction to not look like everyone else's. Treat it as a first-draft engine, not a finished-studio replacement.
tools.best_for: marketing teams and creators who want to turn a prompt or script into a publish-ready first-draft video fast, using templates, AI voiceover and stock
tools.skip_if: you need frame-level creative control, long-form or highly bespoke production, or your usage would blow past the monthly credit allowance
compare_with: Pictory is a close text-to-video peer; Synthesia leans avatar/presenter video — pick by whether you need a talking head

tools.name: involve.me
tools.what_it_does: Interactive funnel builder: quizzes, calculators, assessments and payment pages with built-in email sequences — free tier to start, paid tiers priced by live-funnel count from $19/mo annual.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 7 September 2026 — the paid figures on the public page, the free plan measured inside the product, because involve.me publishes nothing about it) There is a free plan, and this is what it actually gives: 2 live funnels, publishing on a daanV.involve.me subdomain (or one of ten alternatives such as quizzes.cx, forms.ac and calculators.cx), the AI funnel builder, and involve.me branding on every page. No team seats at all. Paid, per person per month, annual against monthly: Start $29 / $49 with 3 live funnels and 1 user, Grow $69 / $99 with 5 funnels and 2 users, Scale $139 / $199 with 25 funnels, 5 users, A/B testing and lead verification. Enterprise is from $499/mo on annual contracts only. In the app the same tiers are priced in euros — €29, €69, €139 — and the annual toggle says “save up to 41%” where the public page says 40%. The tier pages also hide three meters that decide more than the funnel count does: funnel visits a month (10,000 / 25,000 / 100,000), contacts collected a month (300 / 1,000 / 3,000) and AI credits a month (50 / 100 / 300). Each is toppable: +5,000 visits €8.33, +200 contacts €8.33, +250 AI credits €7.50, +1 seat €7.50, +5 live funnels €7.50. Prices exclude EU VAT. Every tier is higher than at the 17 Jul 2026 reading, when Start was $19/mo annual and $29 month-to-month.
tools.honest_knock: The tier pages sell live funnels, but the meter that empties first is contacts. Start collects 300 contacts a month against 10,000 funnel visits — so a funnel converting at 3% hits the contact ceiling and the visit ceiling in the same week, and the next 200 contacts cost €8.33 on top. That trio (visits, contacts, AI credits) appears only in the in-app comparison table, not on the public pricing page. The free plan is worse than undocumented: involve.me offers it ten times across the pricing page, the comparison table and the in-app upgrade screen, and specifies it nowhere. We measured it — 2 live funnels, involve.me branding, no team seats — and you only learn any of that by hitting the wall, because a free account has no usage panel at all: “Plans & Billing” goes straight to the upgrade page. And the honest fundamental for any interactive-funnel tool: quizzes and calculators convert traffic you already have — they don't create it, so validate on the free plan before the subscription outruns the pipeline.
tools.best_for: marketers building interactive lead-gen — quizzes, calculators, assessments and payment funnels with built-in email sequences — who want a free tier to validate the concept first
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple form (lighter tools do that free), or you don’t yet have the traffic to feed an interactive funnel
compare_with: FlexiQuiz is the graded-quiz specialist — exams, certificates, question banks; involve.me plays the marketing game with funnels, lead capture and payments. Pick by whether you’re testing knowledge or generating pipeline

tools.name: Jibble
tools.what_it_does: Time and attendance tracking with facial recognition, GPS and payroll-ready timesheets.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-30 on jibble.io) There is no published price for anything above the free plan. The pricing page has been retired: jibble.io/pricing returns a 301 to /upgrade-plans, which returns a 301 to the homepage, and /plans does the same. What the homepage claims is a free forever plan with unlimited users, described as '100% free', with no credit card required and setup 'in under 2 minutes'. Where a price table would be, an impact calculator projects annual savings on three published assumptions — 40 hours a week, 48 working weeks a year, 5.5% payroll leakage — and labels the cost of Jibble Free as $0. The enterprise page names no figure either; its only call to action is a demo booking. (2026-09-02) Jibble's partnerships team confirmed to us in writing, through the PartnerStack programme, that there is no external pricing page. Jibble states an average of 4.8 out of 5 across major review platforms and app stores on more than 20,000 verified reviews.
tools.honest_knock: Free forever with unlimited users is a real claim and unusual in this category, where per-seat pricing is the norm — that alone makes it worth a look for a team on a tight budget. Two things to establish before you rely on it. First, what the free tier actually excludes, because 'unlimited users' and 'unlimited features' are different promises and the paid tiers exist for a reason. Second, note that their pricing page leads with a calculator showing what you supposedly save rather than what you pay. That is a marketing choice, and the number it produces rests on assumptions about payroll leakage that are theirs, not measured in your business.
tools.best_for: teams that need attendance records without a per-seat bill — if the free tier covers your case it is genuinely free, which nothing else in this category offers
tools.skip_if: you need the paid features, because you will have to get those prices from them directly; also skip facial recognition without checking your local rules on biometric data, which is a legal question rather than a pricing one
compare_with: the direct time-tracking peers — both have free tiers too, so compare on what each free plan excludes rather than on the headline

tools.name: Joiin
tools.what_it_does: Financial consolidation and group reporting for multi-entity, multi-currency organisations — connects Xero, QuickBooks and Sage, with unlimited users and reports on every plan.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Joiin's own machine-readable pricing page) 14-day free trial, no credit card; unlimited users and reports on every plan. Priced by the number of companies you consolidate, with the page showing both columns: monthly against annual, per month. 1 company $28 / $23, 2 $36 / $29, 5 $70 / $57, 10 $111 / $92, 20 $167 / $139, 50 $217 / $174, 100 $336 / $252. Above 100 companies it starts from $336/mo plus $2.80 per additional company. Paying monthly runs roughly 20% above the annual rate at every step.
tools.honest_knock: The $23 headline covers a single company on annual billing — but consolidation is the whole point of Joiin, and a real group of 10-20 entities lands at $92-139 a month. Month-to-month billing adds roughly two months per year, and it consolidates what its integrations reach: Xero, QuickBooks and Sage, plus spreadsheet imports for everything else.
tools.best_for: finance teams and accountants consolidating multi-entity, multi-currency group reporting from Xero, QuickBooks or Sage without hand-built spreadsheets
tools.skip_if: you run a single entity (your accounting platform's own reports cover it), or your ledgers live outside the supported integrations and you'd be importing spreadsheets anyway
compare_with: Fathom leans into analysis and presentation-grade reporting; Joiin is the leaner consolidation specialist with per-entity pricing and unlimited users

tools.name: Jotform AI Agents
tools.what_it_does: Build AI chatbots and customer-service agents in minutes — no code required. Handles leads, support tickets and bookings 24/7. Integrates with your existing forms and CRMs.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 4 Sep 2026 on jotform.com/ai/agents/pricing, on the yearly tab; the same figures were read from a US exit on 26 Aug 2026. The page localises its currency — it quotes $34 / $39 / $99 to a US visitor and €34 / €39 / €99 to a Dutch one, the same numerals either way.) Starter is free. Bronze is $34 a month, Silver $39 and Gold $99, each billed annually, with 'save up to 20%' against monthly billing; Enterprise is quoted. On the AI Agents page the ladder is drawn in agents and conversations, not in forms and submissions: 5 agents and 100 monthly conversations on Starter, 25 and 1,000 on Bronze, 50 and 2,500 on Silver, 100 and 10,000 on Gold. Sessions, voice-call minutes, SMS and knowledge-base characters are metered alongside — 10,000 / 100,000 / 1,000,000 / 2,000,000 monthly sessions and 50 / 100 / 200 / 300 voice minutes across the same four tiers. Jotform defines a session as a chatbot view, a page refresh or a phone call starting, whether or not anyone interacts.
tools.honest_knock: The gating detail is conversations, not features — Starter's 100 a month is a few days on a live site, and an agent that actually gets used will push you up a tier. Sessions are metered separately and Jotform counts a chatbot view or a page refresh as one, so a busy page burns allowance without ever holding a conversation; voice minutes and SMS meter on top as well. It's also tightly bound to the Jotform ecosystem: brilliant if you already live in Jotform forms, less compelling as a standalone chatbot if you don't. For form-driven support and lead capture, it's a fast, low-code win.
tools.best_for: teams already using Jotform (or wanting no-code) that need AI chatbots and service agents to handle leads, support and bookings tied to their forms
tools.skip_if: you need a deeply customizable, standalone conversational-AI platform, or your conversation volume would make the per-tier caps expensive
compare_with: dedicated AI-support platforms — Jotform's edge is no-code and form integration; compare on conversation limits at your real volume

tools.name: Jubilee
tools.what_it_does: Bankruptcy petition preparation, document automation and case management for legal practices. $95 per case pay-as-you-go, or annual plans from $995 for up to 36 filings to $4,995 for 500. Size the tier to your real filing volume; sporadic filers do better per case.
tools.pricing: Pay As You Go is $95 per case. The alternative is an annual subscription billed by yearly filing volume. Jubilee 36 is $995/yr (up to 36 filings, 2 users, $34.99/case over) and Jubilee 150 $2,495/yr (up to 150, 3 users, $26.99 over). Jubilee 300 is $3,995/yr (up to 300, 3 users, $17.99 over) and Jubilee 500 $4,995/yr (up to 500, 5 users, $12.99 over). Prices are for annual billing; above 500 filings a year the vendor quotes custom pricing (re-verified 2026-08-26).
tools.honest_knock: It's a focused vertical tool — bankruptcy petition preparation and case management — so its whole value is bounded by that practice area; a general legal practice won't get much from it. The case-count tiers are the thing to size correctly: pick 36 vs 300 by your real annual filing volume, and check whether the pay-per-case option is cheaper if you file sporadically. For a bankruptcy practice, the automation and court-form handling are exactly the point.
tools.best_for: bankruptcy attorneys and legal professionals who want streamlined petition preparation, document automation and case management for filings
tools.skip_if: you don't practice bankruptcy law, or you file so few cases that a general practice-management tool plus manual forms is enough
compare_with: Best Case (Stretto) or general practice-management software
the established bankruptcy-software peer — Jubilee competes on price and cloud access; size the case tier to your volume

tools.name: Kartra
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one platform for selling online: landing pages, email automation, funnels, memberships and checkout in one tool — no plugins to stitch together.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, monthly against yearly: Essentials $59 / $52, Starter $119 / $99, Growth $229 / $189 and Professional $549 / $429, with yearly billing advertised as saving up to 22% and a 14-day trial. The tier names moved since our August reading — the $119 plan is now called Starter and the $229 plan Growth — while every amount stayed the same. The line that changes the arithmetic and is missing from most summaries: Essentials charges a 5% transaction fee on your sales, and the tiers above it charge 0%. On $10,000 a month of sales that fee is $500, which makes the $60 step from Essentials to Starter trivially worth taking. Contacts are capped at 500, 2,500, 12,500 and 25,000 across the four tiers; Essentials sends 10,000 emails and texts a month against unlimited above it and includes 1 custom domain. Kartra never blocks new leads: it upgrades you automatically to the tier that fits and charges a mid-cycle reconciliation fee for the move — two answers above that one, the same FAQ says a Kartra subscription is flat-rate and there are never any extra fees.
tools.honest_knock: If your core need is polished course delivery, Kajabi's creator features are stronger; Kartra wins on all-in-one breadth, not course depth.
tools.best_for: creators and coaches who want funnels, email, checkout, memberships and scheduling under one roof instead of five subscriptions
tools.skip_if: you only need one of those pieces — a dedicated tool does that piece better and cheaper than an all-in-one

tools.name: Katana MRP
tools.what_it_does: Cloud manufacturing and inventory platform for product businesses. Live inventory control, production scheduling and order syncing across your sales channels — know exactly what to make and when.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A Free plan covering 30 SKUs with unlimited users, integrations and locations plus full features and API, then Core starting at $299/mo with unlimited SKUs and users and 24/7 support, and an Advantage tier on custom pricing. The add-ons are where the real cost sits and they are priced separately: manufacturing routings and insights $199/mo, end-to-end traceability via batch or serial numbers $249/mo, warehouse management with bin locations and pick-and-pack $149/mo, plus an optional $2,000 item on the page. Higher monthly sales-order volume also raises the effective cost.
tools.honest_knock: The $299 headline is the floor. Production routings and traceability are paid add-ons on top, and those are exactly the features most manufacturers need, which is why real bills often land two to three times higher. Cost also rises with sales-order volume, so a busy month is a bigger month. It's genuinely capable manufacturing software; just price the add-ons you need, not the base plan.
tools.best_for: product makers and small manufacturers who need live inventory, production scheduling and multi-channel order sync in one cloud platform
tools.skip_if: you're a simple reseller who doesn't manufacture (a plain inventory tool is cheaper), or your volume is too low to justify the add-on-driven real cost
compare_with: comparable manufacturing/inventory platforms — weigh by which add-ons you'd actually enable and your order volume

tools.name: Keap
tools.what_it_does: CRM, sales and marketing automation built for small businesses. Capture leads, automate follow-up and manage your pipeline in one place.
tools.pricing: Starting at $299/mo billed monthly for the whole platform, with no feature-based tiers and no free plan (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page). That $299 is what the calculator quotes for its own minimum: 2 users and 1,500 contacts. Raising only the contact count on the same calculator gives $335 at 2,500, $449 at 5,000, $539 at 10,000 and $719 at 25,000, and users beyond the first two are $39 a month each. Keap also requires paid implementation services — strategy consulting, data import and migration — quoted separately before you go live.
