Text marketing is bundled at Tier 1 (500 messages and 100 voice minutes) and steps to $24, $39, $79, $139 and $279 a month above that, with overages at $0.015 a message and $0.01 a voice minute; it is US-only. Cancelling an annual contract before its term ends carries a $299 early termination fee, and cancellation must be started by phone at least ten days before the next invoice date. Keap has been acquired by Thryv; its own pages now route training to Thryv Academy.
tools.honest_knock: Cost is the big one (56% of reviewers flag it), the interface feels dated, and there's a real 2–4 week learning curve on the automation builder. Billing and cancellation complaints are common — their own terms carry a $299 early termination fee on an annual contract and require ten days' phone notice — and email design is thinner than dedicated email tools.
tools.best_for: service-based small businesses, coaches and solopreneurs who want CRM, email, payments and automation in one tool — and will invest the time to learn it
tools.skip_if: you're price-sensitive, want a modern UI, or only need simple email — the cost and learning curve bite
compare_with: the more modern all-in-one and the automation specialist

tools.name: Keeper Security
tools.what_it_does: Password manager and privileged access management for teams, with a zero-knowledge architecture.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-06 on their own business and add-on pricing pages) Three business tiers, all billed annually: Business Starter at $2.00 per user per month, described as protection for 5–10 users; Business at $4.00 per user per month; Enterprise at $6.00 per user per month, sold through Request a Quote. The amounts are injected by script, so a page fetched without rendering shows the tiers with the figures missing. Personal and family plans are priced on their own page: Personal $4.34 per month ($52.02 billed annually) and Family $9.28 per month ($111.31 billed annually). The add-ons carry their own list: BreachWatch and KeeperChat $24 per user per year, Advanced Reporting & Alerts and Compliance Reports $12 per user per year, Endpoint Privilege Manager $36 per endpoint per year, Secure File Storage from $132 per year, Professional Services from $270 per year, with Connection Manager and Keeper Secrets Manager quote-only.
tools.honest_knock: The per-user price is the smallest part of the bill. Read the add-ons page next to the plan page and the shape becomes clear: BreachWatch and KeeperChat are $24 per user per year each, Advanced Reporting & Alerts and Compliance Reports $12 per user per year each, endpoint privilege management $36 per endpoint per year — so a Business seat at $4.00 a month can quietly double once you add the monitoring and reporting most buyers assume is included, and Connection Manager and Secrets Manager are not even priced. Annual billing is stated on every tier, so there is no month-to-month option to test with, and Business Starter is scoped at 5–10 users. Ask for the base plan and each add-on you need as separate lines, because a bundled quote here hides which part is actually costing you.
tools.best_for: teams that need shared credentials with real admin control and audit, and that will genuinely use the provisioning and role-based access that separate this from a consumer password manager
tools.skip_if: you are under five people wanting a shared vault, since Business Starter is scoped at 5–10 users and Keeper's own Personal plan at $4.34 a month, or Family at $9.28, covers that case for less
compare_with: the direct team password-manager comparison — both publish per-user prices, so use those as the anchor for Keeper's quote

tools.name: Kinsta
tools.what_it_does: Managed WordPress hosting on Google Cloud, with free migrations and 24/7 support. From $35/month for one site (10 GB, metered on 20 GB bandwidth or 35,000 visits), or $30/month billed annually at $350 a year. Overage bills per 1,000 extra visits; Kinsta gives no partner-only discount codes.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own plans page, USD, tax excluded) Managed WordPress hosting from $35/mo for a single site, or $30/mo billed annually $350 a year, with the first month free on top — Kinsta advertises annual as two months off. That entry plan carries one WordPress install, 10GB storage, 125GB CDN bandwidth and 14 days of backup retention, and you choose whether it is metered on bandwidth (20GB) or on visits (35,000), which is a real change from the visit-only plans older reviews describe. Multi-site plans start at $59/mo $700 a year for two installs, and agency plans start at $340/mo, or $284/mo billed annually at $3,400 a year. It is a premium tier — cheaper shared hosts exist. There is no exclusive discount code to look for: Kinsta confirmed to us on 28 Jul 2026 that it gives no partner-only or affiliate-only discounts.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying a premium for managed speed, Google Cloud infrastructure and expert support — worth it if performance and hands-off management matter, wasteful on a low-traffic hobby site a $5 shared host would carry fine.
tools.best_for: business-critical WordPress sites where speed, uptime and expert support directly affect revenue
tools.skip_if: you run a small, low-traffic site on a tight budget — entry-level shared hosting or a caching plugin gets you most of the way for a fraction of the price

tools.name: Kit
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing built for creators (formerly ConvertKit). Grow your list with landing pages and forms, then automate newsletters and sell digital products from one place; a beta Kit MCP connects AI assistants like Claude directly to your account. Recent additions: a new landing-page editor, Dynamic Content, Newsletter Sponsorships, and App Store integrations on paid plans — SMS via SlickText, Patreon member sync (tier and support data in automations), Luma/Eventbrite event sync, and two-way HubSpot CRM sync on Pro.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-02) The free plan is $0/mo and covers up to 10,000 email subscribers, with unlimited landing pages and forms, unlimited email broadcasts, audience tagging and segmentation, and digital products and subscriptions. Kit renamed the old Newsletter plan to Free and took automation out of it: Visual Automations and email sequences are now Creator-and-above, and Kit's affiliate briefing of 2 September 2026 adds that new free accounts open with a 14-day Creator trial and that accounts already on the Newsletter plan keep what they had. Creator is $39/mo billed monthly, or $33/mo billed yearly ($390 a year, saving $78), and adds unlimited Visual Automations, unlimited email sequences, Kit MCP, SMS marketing and branding removal. Pro — the tier that adds Subscriber Signals, engagement analytics, deliverability reporting, a newsletter referral system and unlimited users — is $79/mo billed monthly, or $66/mo billed yearly ($790 a year, saving $158). Paying yearly saves 17%. Every paid price on the page is quoted for 1,000 email subscribers and Kit bills by list size, so read the tier for your own list before you budget. Paid plans open with a 14-day free trial without a card, and migrations are free.
tools.honest_knock: Three honest notes. Subscriber-based pricing counts everyone on your list — cold subscribers cost the same as fans, so prune before you price. The free plan changed shape in 2026: it now runs to 10,000 subscribers rather than 1,000 (re-verified 2026-09-02), but Visual Automations and email sequences came out of it, so the free tier sends and captures without automating anything — what puts you on Creator at $39/mo, or $33/mo paid yearly, is wanting a welcome sequence rather than list growth. And the 35% price hike in 2025 changed the value math: the free tier is still arguably the best in creator email, but paid tiers now deserve comparison shopping rather than default loyalty. The creator-first features (tip jars, paid newsletters, recommendations) remain the real differentiator.
tools.best_for: creators, writers and coaches building an audience-first business who want email, landing pages, digital products and a creator network in one
tools.skip_if: you're an e-commerce store (commerce-native email tools fit better) or your list is big-but-cold — clean it before paying per subscriber
compare_with: the creator-email rivals — Beehiiv leans newsletter-growth mechanics, MailerLite undercuts on price; Kit wins on creator-commerce maturity

tools.name: Kite
tools.what_it_does: Shopify discount toolkit (by Skai Lama) built on native Shopify Functions: free gift with purchase, buy X get Y, tiered and volume discounts, progress bars and bulk codes. Free to install for the first 50 discount orders a month, then $29; Starter $29, Growth $49, Pro $99.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/kite-free-gift) Four plans, billed in USD every 30 days. The Free plan is free to install and covers the first 50 discount orders each month; the listing states that $29 a month is billed only if you go over 50 orders. Starter is $29 a month, or $299 a year at a stated 14% saving, and adds unlimited discount orders, combined offers, progress bars and up to 10K bulk codes. Growth is $49 a month, or $499 a year at 15%, and raises bulk codes to 100K with multiple rules per offer and campaign links. Pro is $99 a month, or $999 a year at 16%, and adds custom discount functions, checkout gifts (Plus only) and segment targeting. The three paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Free and Starter both say 'Not for Shopify Advanced and Plus'.
tools.honest_knock: 'Free to install' is doing a lot of work on this listing. The free plan covers the first 50 discount orders a month, and the same panel says $29 a month is billed once you pass them — so it is a threshold with an invoice behind it, not a free tier you can settle on. A store running one decent promotion will cross 50 discounted orders in days and be on Starter money without choosing to upgrade. The second catch is written on the plans themselves: Free and Starter are both labelled 'Not for Shopify Advanced and Plus', so if you are on either of those Shopify plans your real entry price is the $49 Growth tier, not the $29 the listing leads with. And the feature most likely to sell the app to a large merchant — free gifts added at checkout — is marked Plus only and sits in the $99 Pro tier, which means the Plus stores it is built for pay $1,188 a year to reach it.
tools.best_for: shopify stores that want the discount mechanics themselves — gift with purchase, buy X get Y, tiered and volume pricing, with progress bars pushing the cart toward the next reward — built on native Shopify Functions rather than theme edits
tools.skip_if: your promotions are simple enough for Shopify's own discount engine, or you are on Advanced or Plus and unwilling to start at $49 — and if all you need is a pile of unique codes, a code generator does that for a third of the price
compare_with: Both sit on Shopify's native discount plumbing, and the split is between combining discounts and creating them. Stackable is about redemption: several discounts — order, collection, shipping — under a single code, plus a progress type, from $19.99 a month with no free plan. Kite is about the offers themselves: free gifts, BOGO, tiered and volume pricing, bulk codes and storefront widgets, opening at a metered free tier that turns into $29 past 50 discount orders. So if your promotions already exist and customers keep having to pick which code to use, that is Stackable's problem. If the promotion is the thing you cannot build — a gift that appears at a cart threshold, a tier that rewards the bigger basket — Kite is the one with those mechanics, and it has the far longer record: 1,161 reviews against Stackable's 54.

tools.name: Kiwi Sizing
tools.what_it_does: Shopify size charts and AI fit recommendations, built to cut returns. Free plan carries a Kiwi watermark; Premium is $7.99 a month and the only paid tier without order-volume charges. From Staytuned.
tools.pricing: (read 5 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/kiwi-sizing) Four tiers, and the interesting line is not the price but the sentence under it. Free publishes up to three size charts with 22 templates and unlimited CSV import, and puts a Kiwi watermark on your storefront. Premium is $7.99 a month for up to ten charts, removes the watermark, adds Google Analytics and auto-translation into English and Spanish, and states plainly: no additional monthly charges. Plus, the tier the store marks Popular, is $14.99 for up to twenty charts, ten size recommenders and six languages. Ultimate is $26.99 for unlimited charts and recommenders and 22 languages. Both Plus and Ultimate carry the same caveat that Premium does not: additional charges apply based on order volume, and the listing does not say what those charges are. Import credits are an optional add-on on every paid tier, and all three come with a 14-day free trial. The listing adds that all charges are billed in USD and that recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. So the cheapest paid plan is the only one whose bill you can predict, and the one the store pushes is not.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is not limited by the chart count most people assume. Three charts is generous for a small catalogue; the real limit is the Kiwi watermark sitting on your storefront, and removing it is what the $7.99 buys. Judge the free tier on whether you can live with that watermark in front of customers, not on how many charts you get. And read the small print above Plus and Ultimate before you upgrade: both add order-volume charges that the App Store listing never quantifies, while Premium says in writing that it has none.
tools.best_for: apparel and accessory stores where sizing drives returns, and that want charts plus an AI fit recommender without building either — 4.7 stars from 1,188 reviews on 4 September 2026 is a genuinely strong base, though the recent ones read differently from the aggregate
tools.skip_if: you sell one-size or non-wearable products, where a size chart answers a question nobody asks, or you need more than ten charts and would land on a tier whose order-volume charges are not published
compare_with: Fast Bundle or the native Shopify size guide
the alternatives are a general merchandising app or building the chart into your theme — Kiwi earns its place when the recommender, not the chart, is what you are after

tools.name: Kixie
tools.what_it_does: Power dialer with SMS and CRM integration for outbound sales teams. Kixie publishes no seat price: three tiers separated by how many lines they dial, with the multi-line AI voice detection, ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence and DNC compliance all sold as add-ons on top.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-18, read on their own pricing page) No seat price is published. Three plans are listed — Professional, Single-Line PowerDialer and Multi-Line PowerDialer — with a quarterly/yearly toggle but no amount rendered anywhere on the page. The core phone system is identical on all three; what separates them is dialling. There is no PowerDialer on Professional, one line on Single-Line, and up to four simultaneous lines on Multi-Line — also the only tier offering AI human voice detection, as a premium add-on. ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence and DNC compliance are add-ons at every tier. The plan cards claim unlimited US/Canada minutes while the FAQ prices unlimited US and Canada minutes at $30 a month per user, so which of the two applies belongs in writing in your quote. First US/Canada number free, extra local numbers $5.00 a month, porting in free. Texts from $0.011 each on a registered 10DLC number, inbound free. 7-day trial, no credit card.
tools.honest_knock: Plan for 30-60% above the sticker: minutes, the multi-line dialer and AI human-voice-detection all bill separately, and the quarterly auto-renewing contract only allows downgrades in its final 30 days — read that clause before signing. The dialer itself is genuinely fast and CRM-native; just buy it with the full basket priced and the calendar reminder set (our Renewal Radar exists for exactly this).
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams living in their CRM that want a serious power dialer with local presence, SMS and automation
tools.skip_if: low call volumes (per-seat + minutes math won't pay back), or you want monthly flexibility without contract fine print
compare_with: dialer peers with simpler pricing — compare all-in per-seat including minutes, and the contract terms

tools.name: Koongo
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that syncs product feeds, stock and orders across Amazon, eBay, Bol, Zalando, Allegro and 500-plus channels from one dashboard. Free tier for 100 items; paid plans from $39 a month, separated by refresh frequency, with surcharges beyond the included limits.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/koongo, listed as “Koongo: Sell on Marketplaces”, and on koongo.com/pricing) Four tiers on the listing, separated by update frequency rather than by capability. Free covers one store language, 100 items or SKUs, 5 product feeds, one marketplace wizard and up to 10 orders a month, updating once a day. Lite is $39 a month and updates every 6 hours, Starter is $79 and updates every 30 minutes, and Pro is $119 and updates every 15 minutes. All three include 1,000 items, 5 feeds, two marketplace wizards with the second free on a summer promotion, and 100 orders a month. All three also carry a 7-day free trial. Every paid tier states surcharges for extras used — items, feeds, marketplaces and orders — and each is also sold in a feed-manager-only form, from $14.50 for Lite, $29 for Starter and $41 for Pro. All charges on the listing are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page sells the same four plans in euros at €0, €35, €69 and €99 a month, and states that all prices exclude VAT. Each plan is broken into Core, Marketplace Manager, Feed Manager and Ads Manager modules with separate prices. There is also a surcharge table for extra stores, items, orders, marketplaces, feeds and team seats, where an extra 100 orders runs from €10.00 down to €2.00 as volume grows. Developer Koongo, a product of NoStress Commerce s.r.o., Prague; the app launched on 5 November 2014 and had 98 reviews at a 4.4 average at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
The headline price is a base, not a bill. Each paid plan includes 1,000 items, 5 feeds, two marketplace wizards and 100 orders a month, and the listing says plainly that surcharges apply for extras used across all four of those dimensions. For a store with a real catalogue selling on several European marketplaces, every one of those limits is one you pass in week one. Price your own numbers on koongo.com's surcharge table before you take $39 seriously.

The two pricing pages also do not quote the same bill. The App Store lists $39, $79 and $119 and bills in USD. koongo.com lists €35, €69 and €99 and states that all prices exclude VAT. Depending on where you trade and how you are registered, those are meaningfully different amounts for the same plan, and nothing on either page reconciles them.

Then the record, which is the most useful thing on this listing. 4.4 from 98 reviews is the lowest average in this category among the apps Shopify shows beside it, and the breakdown explains why: 84 five-star ratings sit alongside six one-star ones. The critical reviews are specific rather than vague, which makes them worth reading in full. In July 2026 a Belgian merchant described a repricer set to Monitoring Mode that still blocked updates to live Bol offers because of MinimumPrice errors, so a delivery-promise change never reached the marketplace. In January 2026 a UK merchant described unresolved integration errors on OnBuy and a refused refund, with Koongo replying publicly that they had reached out several times without response. Neither is disqualifying on its own. Together they describe an app whose complexity is real and whose marketplace integrations sometimes need support to untangle — which is consistent with the vendor's own listing offering personal onboarding for complex setups.

One more line to read before you install: the listing states the app views sensitive customer data as well as device and activity data, and can view and edit products, orders and custom data. Marketplace order sync needs customer details to work, so that is expected, but it makes this a processor of personal data on your behalf rather than a feed formatter.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants selling across several European marketplaces — Bol, Zalando, Allegro, Cdiscount, Miinto and the rest — who need inventory and order sync to run automatically, and who have priced their own item, feed and order counts against the surcharge table rather than the headline
tools.skip_if: you sell on one channel or need product feeds only, where the feed-manager-only form from $14.50 or a dedicated feed app is cheaper; or your catalogue and order volume sit far enough above the included limits that the surcharges, not the plan, become the price

tools.name: KrispCall
tools.what_it_does: Virtual numbers across 100+ countries with a shared dashboard, dialer and CRM hooks, from about $12/user/month on annual billing. Calls and SMS are pay-as-you-go from a separate credit balance, so compare per-country call rates at your volume rather than the seat price.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against the vendor's own pricing page) Essential $12 per user/mo billed annually or $15 monthly, for solo agents and teams up to 5 people; Standard $32 per user/mo annually or $40 monthly, for teams scaling up to 50 users; Enterprise custom. Annual saves 20%, which the page puts at $36 per user a year on Essential and $96 on Standard, and each plan comes with $1 of free calling and SMS credit. Calls and SMS are otherwise pay-as-you-go from a separate credit balance, and numbers carry their own one-off and monthly charges (from $4.50 one-off and $1.50 a month at the time of reading).
tools.honest_knock: Same honest math as most budget VoIP: the plan buys the platform, the meter buys the conversations — per-minute and per-SMS charges land on top of every seat, so the comparison that matters is call-rate-per-country at your volume. The 100+ country number coverage is genuinely the draw; verify number availability and local regulations for your specific target countries before committing.
tools.best_for: sales and support teams that need virtual numbers across many countries with a shared dashboard, dialer and CRM hooks at a budget seat price
tools.skip_if: your calling is domestic-only at low volume (simpler tools suffice), or you need enterprise reliability guarantees over price
compare_with: the direct budget-VoIP set — differences live in per-country rates and number availability, so price your actual destinations

tools.name: Landingi
tools.what_it_does: Landing page builder with 400+ templates, from $29/month for unlimited pages and 5,000 visitors; A/B testing and pop-ups start at $49. Roughly half what Unbounce and Instapage charge, and the trade is no AI traffic routing, no real-time collaboration and thinner technical control.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17; the English page quotes USD while the same page served from a Dutch address quotes euros at the same numerals, so check your own currency) Four plans, billed annually: Build $24/month, Optimize $119/month, Scale from $229/month and Enterprise from $1,199/month. Annual billing includes two months free against monthly. Custom domains are metered: 1 on Build, 3 on Optimize, 10 on Scale and 100 on Enterprise, with extras at $5 a month each. AI credits come with the plan (2,500, 10,000, 20,000 and 60,000 a month) and top-ups are pay-as-you-go at $15 for 5,000, $25 for 10,000 and $40 for 20,000. A promotional rate roughly half the Build price appears periodically — it is a limited-time offer rather than the standard rate.
tools.honest_knock: You trade away the high-end optimisation: no AI traffic routing like Unbounce's Smart Traffic, no real-time collaboration, and thinner technical control (script containers). Excellent value, but not the conversion-optimisation powerhouse.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious teams, international businesses and anyone needing bulk or programmatic page generation across 29 languages
tools.skip_if: you need AI traffic routing, real-time collaboration or deep technical control — that's where Unbounce earns its higher price

tools.name: Later
tools.what_it_does: Visual social media scheduler and planner. Plan, preview and auto-publish posts across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and more from one calendar.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Starter $18.75/month, Growth $37.50 and Scale $82.50, all billed yearly, which Later advertises as three months free and 25% off against monthly. Every plan opens with a 14-day trial, and on the page as we read it on 31 August 2026 that trial is the only no-cost route offered: three paid tiers, nothing beneath them, and an FAQ that discusses users per plan rather than any zero-price option. Our earlier note here also described a permanently free option, which we could not source; Later has historically run a no-cost link-in-bio product that may still sit behind the signup flow, but the pricing page does not sell it. The add-ons are where a growing team pays more: extra Social Sets are $11.25 a month each, extra users $3.75 a month each, and extra AI credits $3.75 a month per 100 credits. Starter covers casual scheduling; Growth adds the inbox, approvals and longer analytics; Scale is aimed at enterprise-level analytics without an enterprise contract.
tools.honest_knock: The Starter caps are where the price really lives: 30 posts per profile and 3 months of analytics run out fast for an active brand, pushing real users toward Growth — so compare at the tier you'll actually need, not the entry price. Later's visual-first planning (born from Instagram) is still its strength; if your world is link-in-bio commerce and grids, that focus earns its seat.
tools.best_for: creators and visual-first brands (Instagram/TikTok-centric) that want drag-and-drop visual planning, link-in-bio and scheduling in one
tools.skip_if: you need deep multi-network publishing, listening and team workflows at agency scale (suite-class tools fit), or the post caps chafe immediately
compare_with: Buffer is the lean generalist, Vista undercuts on breadth — Later wins on visual planning UX for Instagram-first work

tools.name: Leadfeeder
tools.what_it_does: Website visitor identification for B2B sales. See which companies visit your site and what they viewed, and turn anonymous traffic into a warm pipeline.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on leadfeeder.com/pricing over a US connection) Lite is free forever with a 14-day full trial, seven days of visitor history and the last 100 companies a month. Discover starts at $79 a month, Activate at $369 and Scale at $599, all billed annually, which the page marks as 30% off. Worth knowing: the page carries both currencies with the same figures — $79 for an American is €79 for a European, not a converted amount — so the euro price is the more expensive of the two.
tools.honest_knock: The words doing the work are 'starting at'. What actually sets your price is how many companies you identify a month, and the page shows that allowance as 'Tiered' with no figures at any level. So €79 is the floor of the smallest bucket, and you cannot tell from the page which bucket your traffic puts you in. Get that table before you talk price. Two other things: month-to-month costs 43% more than annual on the same plan (€113 against €79), and Scale is annual-only, so the tier most growing teams land on cannot be tried for a month.
tools.best_for: B2B teams with real website traffic and a sales team that will actually work the list — the free tier is enough to find out whether your traffic contains anyone worth calling
tools.skip_if: your traffic is mostly consumer or very low volume, because company identification needs business networks to match against and thin traffic produces a thin list
compare_with: the direct visitor-identification peers — compare the identified-company allowance at your traffic level, since that is the number that sets the bill

tools.name: Leadpages
tools.what_it_does: Landing pages, pop-ups and alert bars, with unlimited traffic on every Leadpages plan where metered rivals count visitors. Conversion plans run $99 (Grow) to $399 (Scale), alongside a separate HTML Pub publishing line at $10–49. The value pick rather than the optimisation pick.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Leadpages' own machine-readable pricing file, which they last updated 2026-07-10; USD) Two lines, six paid plans, no free plan, and a 7-day free trial that requires a credit card and converts unless you cancel. Publishing plans: Starter $10/mo or $8 billed annually ($96 a year), 5 pages, 1 site, no third-party integrations; Pro $29/mo or $23 annually ($276), 25 pages, 1 blog, API access; Business $49/mo or $39 annually ($468), 50 pages, 2 sites. Optimization plans add testing and personalisation: Grow $99/mo or $79 annually ($948), unlimited pages, 4 sites, manual A/B testing; Optimize $199/mo or $159 annually ($1,908), 6 sites, multivariate testing and Smart Traffic; Scale $399/mo or $319 annually ($3,828), 10 sites, heatmaps, auto-personalisation and 10 seats. Annual billing is 20% off across the board. No plan has a traffic cap. Add-ons: $20 a month per extra seat or extra custom domain, $40 per extra client workspace on Scale, and AI credit top-ups from $2.50 for 2,000 credits down to $0.60 per thousand at the largest pack.
tools.honest_knock: It's the value pick, not the optimisation pick — if you're spending big on ads, Unbounce's Smart Traffic and Instapage's 1:1 personalisation go deeper.
tools.best_for: small businesses building landing pages and simple funnels who want unmetered traffic — no per-visitor anxiety, unlike metered rivals
tools.skip_if: you need deep A/B experimentation or enterprise features — the Conversion tier jumps to $299/mo fast

tools.name: LearnWorlds
tools.what_it_does: Create, sell and scale online courses. Build a branded school with interactive video, assessments, certificates and a built-in checkout.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page, which now carries the browser title New Pricing 2026) Starter $29/mo (or $24 annually) but with a $5 fee per paid enrollment — still the single most important number in this ladder; Pro Trainer $99/mo, or $79 billed annually, with no enrollment fee; Learning Center $299/mo, or $249 annually; Corporate quoted. The High Volume tier we recorded in August is gone: the ladder is now Starter, Pro Trainer, Learning Center and Corporate. Annual billing saves 20% and the trial is 30 days. Limits published alongside: 1,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 monthly active learners, 1 / 5 / 25 admins, 300 / 500 / 1,000 AI credits a month, email support 24/5 on Starter against 24/7 above it, and a 99.90% uptime commitment (99.95% on Corporate). All prices exclude VAT, which is added for EU customers unless a valid EU VAT number is given, and your payment gateway (Stripe at about 2.9% + $0.30) charges on top regardless of tier. A branded mobile app is still a separate add-on, but the page now lists it as having multiple price options and prints no amount, so the roughly $149/mo we carried in August is no longer confirmable. Two reading notes: the page opens by asking which of four goals brings you there and recommends a plan on that basis — the figures above were read with the branded-academy goal selected — and the plan cards print their numbers with no currency symbol at all, the only dollar signs on the page sitting on the $5 enrollment fee and the Stripe example.
tools.honest_knock: The detail most people miss is Starter's $5-per-paid-enrollment fee — at any real sales volume it quietly makes Starter more expensive than the flat Pro Trainer plan, so the "cheap" tier often isn't. Starter also runs on a single admin seat and 24/5 email support against 24/7 above it, and the branded mobile app is a separate add-on whose price the pricing page no longer states. Price it against your expected enrollment volume, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: course creators and training businesses that want a branded school with interactive video, assessments, certificates and a built-in checkout
tools.skip_if: you sell only occasional courses (a lighter or transaction-fee-only platform may cost less) or you just need to host a few videos behind a paywall
compare_with: close course-platform peers — LearnWorlds leads on interactivity and branding; compare transaction-fee structures at your volume

tools.name: Leavo
tools.what_it_does: Team time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing and a 30-day free trial.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against leavo.com) (2026) 30-day free trial with unlimited members (a trial, not a permanent free plan). Professional $2.49/user/mo billed yearly (about $448/yr for 15 users) adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15). Priced per user, annual billing.
tools.honest_knock: The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat — every employee you track adds to the bill, with no volume break shown. And the “free” is a 30-day trial, not a permanent free tier: budget for the paid plan from day 31.
tools.best_for: teams that want straightforward time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing
tools.skip_if: you need a permanent free plan (this is a 30-day trial), or you're a tiny team where a shared spreadsheet already covers hours
compare_with: Toggl is the established time-tracker with a genuinely free tier for small teams; Leavo leans into attendance and overtime banking — richer there, but per-seat and trial-only at the free end

tools.name: lemlist
tools.what_it_does: Cold email outreach and sales engagement. Build personalized multichannel sequences (email, LinkedIn, calls) with built-in deliverability tools, and trigger them off buying-intent signals its agents surface. An MCP server at app.lemlist.com/mcp puts the same actions inside Claude or ChatGPT: create, update, start and pause campaigns and sequences, manage leads, enrich emails and read team analytics in plain language - the enrichment calls spend credits like anywhere else in the product.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17; the page served us DOLLARS today where our previous reading was in euros, with the same numerals — check your own checkout) No free plan, 14-day trial. Email is $69/month, or $55/month on yearly billing, covering unlimited users and 50,000 emails a month. Multichannel is $109/month per user, or $87/month yearly, with unlimited emails and messages and 5 senders per user. Quarterly billing saves 10% and yearly 20%. Enterprise (5+ users) is quote-only. Contact data is billed separately through rechargeable credits where 1 credit = $0.01: a 1,000-credit pack is $10 and buys roughly 200 email lookups or 50 phone numbers, with a phone number costing 20 credits.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat plus per-email-account model makes total cost unpredictable as you scale, and reviews flag support response times and the LinkedIn Chrome-extension's reliability.
tools.best_for: outbound teams that live in cold email and want multichannel sequences, warm-up and a big template community in one per-seat tool
tools.skip_if: you send occasional one-off campaigns — the entry plan starts at 69€/month and only pays off with steady outbound volume

tools.name: LettrLabs
tools.what_it_does: Automated direct-mail marketing: design, personalise and send physical mailers — handwritten letters, postcards — at scale, synced with your digital campaigns and tracked for ROI.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Postage is included in every per-piece rate. Three published tiers: Starter is free and pay-as-you-go; Premium is $399/month billed annually or $449 month-to-month; Enterprise is custom-priced. On Starter, postcards are $0.76 (4x6), $0.79 (6x9), $0.85 (6x11) and $1.15 (11x18 tri-fold), and handwritten pieces are $1.56 (handwritten envelope with printed letter), $1.66 (handwritten postcard), $2.86 (card and envelope) and $3.11 (bi-fold card and envelope). Premium's card shows $0.54-$0.88 for postcards and $0.85-$1.71 for handwritten, Enterprise's $0.56-$0.88 and $0.81-$1.52 — but both are labelled 'as low as with spend commitment', so those floors need volume as well as the subscription. Handwritten insert media (a card with no envelope, shipped inside a package rather than mailed) is listed from $0.49 and is not offered on Starter. New accounts get $30 in free credit.
tools.honest_knock: Direct mail only pays off with a tight list and a real offer — it's a leverage channel, not a cheap thing to test blindly.
tools.best_for: local businesses and e-commerce brands using robotically handwritten mail (~$0.49/piece incl. postage) to stand out where email gets ignored
tools.skip_if: your audience or offer doesn't justify ~$0.49 per contact — direct mail only pays at decent response rates and order values

tools.name: Lindy.ai
tools.what_it_does: An AI teammate that lives in Slack: @mention it and it works across your other tools, sits in meetings for shared context and runs jobs on a schedule. Sold per user — Plus $29.99/month for 3k credits, Pro $99.99 for 15k — so cost tracks headcount, and a removed seat runs to the end of the cycle.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-04, read on their own pricing page; the 12 August figures were unchanged) Now sold per user, and the credit allowance is published again. Plus is $29.99/mo per user (3k credits per user per month), Pro $99.99/mo per user (15k credits, 5x Plus) and Max $199.99/mo per user (35k credits, ~12x Plus). Enterprise is quote-only. Every seat's credits pool into one workspace balance, refresh each billing cycle and do not roll over; the page sizes work as 2-250 credits for an everyday ask, 250-1,000 for deep work and 1,000-2,500 for a big build. Anyone who uses Lindy takes a paid seat, including colleagues who only @mention it in Slack — those who join that way get a 7-day free trial first, direct signups are billed straight away. All four tiers connect up to 5 inboxes, and computer use, model selection and MCP support are no longer tier-gated.
tools.honest_knock: Cost tracks headcount rather than output: every colleague who so much as @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a paid seat, and a seat you remove runs to the end of the cycle with no mid-cycle proration. Credits are published now, but as ranges: an everyday ask is 2-250, a big build 1,000-2,500. So a month is still an estimate. And when the shared pool runs dry there is no top-up — Lindy pauses credit-using actions until the reset, unless an admin moves the workspace to a bigger plan.
tools.best_for: teams that live in Slack and want one shared teammate that sits in their meetings, runs scheduled routines and drafts replies inside the tools they already use
tools.skip_if: you want flat, predictable automation costs across a large team — Lindy charges for every seat that touches it and the credits expire each cycle, so you pay for people whether or not they used their allowance
compare_with: trigger-based automation tools with flatter pricing

tools.name: Livestorm
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based webinars with registration, automated emails, polls and analytics. There is no plan price: Pro sells attendee credits at €2.50 each, bought a year up front, and one credit is spent per unique participant per session — a four-part series to 200 people costs 800 credits.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) There is still no plan price. Pro is sold as attendee credits, bought as a yearly pack up front, with sessions up to 4 hours and unlimited team members; Enterprise is quote-only with sessions up to 12 hours. The rate depends on the currency you pick on the page, and the two are not conversions of each other: €2.50 per attendee in euros, $3.00 in dollars. Their own definition, worth reading twice because it decides your bill: one credit is spent for each unique participant, per session, over a 12-month period. Someone attending two different sessions costs 2 credits; the same person joining live and later watching the replay of that session counts once. Registrants who never show up cost nothing, and your own team members never consume credits. New since August: the FAQ now says what happens when the pack runs out — you get alerts as you approach the limit, and once you reach it new attendees cannot join a session until you move to a higher yearly tier. What still is not answered anywhere on the page is what becomes of credits you have not used at the twelve-month mark.
tools.honest_knock: This is a bet on attendance that you place a year in advance. You buy credits up front — €2.50 each in euros, $3.00 in dollars, set separately rather than converted — and a credit is spent per unique participant per session, so a four-part series to the same 200 people is 800 credits, not 200, which is €2,000. A webinar that does better than expected runs you out, and the page is now clear about what that means: new attendees cannot join until you buy a higher tier. The page publishes the per-attendee rate but never a total. Before you commit, count sessions times expected attendees for the whole year, and ask what happens to unused credits at the twelve-month mark, because the page does not say.
tools.best_for: teams running a predictable programme of webinars to a known audience size, where buying a year of attendance up front is cheaper than a per-seat platform
tools.skip_if: your webinar schedule is irregular or experimental, because paying a year ahead for attendance you cannot forecast is the wrong shape; a per-month platform is safer while you find out what works
compare_with: the usual alternatives — both price per host per month, so compare that against your credits divided across a year

tools.name: Logome.ai
tools.what_it_does: Generates a logo and basic brand assets from a prompt. Designing and previewing is free, but downloading requires a paid plan — Basic at around $29/month gives one file without a transparent background. Their public site including pricing returned 404 at last check, so verify what you are charged.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-06) Nothing is on sale here. Every route on logome.ai — homepage, /pricing, /app, /dashboard, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml — returned HTTP 404 on 6 September 2026, and the response is Webflow's own default error page served from Webflow's edge, which indicates no published site behind the domain rather than an outage. app.logome.ai does not resolve in DNS. Our earlier and never-confirmed reading had design and preview free with downloads paid, and tiers at roughly $29/mo ($19 annually), $99 ($49) and $199 ($99), all paid plans including commercial rights. Those are last-known figures from before the site disappeared and are not confirmable.
tools.honest_knock: Update, 6 Sep 2026: logome.ai no longer answers at all. Every route — homepage, pricing, app, dashboard, robots.txt, sitemap.xml — returns Webflow's default 404, and there is no app subdomain: app.logome.ai does not resolve in DNS. Our July note said the public site was down but the app still loaded; that is no longer the case. Treat every figure below as last-known rather than confirmed, and if you are already paying, cancel through your card or PayPal rather than through a site that will not load. The honest catch, when the service was reachable, was the free-to-design, pay-to-download model, with the entry tier giving one file without a transparent background. AI logos are also a starting point rather than a trademark: check distinctiveness before you build a brand on one.
tools.best_for: founders and small businesses that want a professional-looking logo and basic brand assets generated fast and cheaply, without hiring a designer
tools.skip_if: you need a truly bespoke, trademark-safe brand identity (hire a designer), or the single-file Basic tier won't give you the formats you actually need
compare_with: close AI logo generators — compare download formats, ownership terms and how much the transparent-background/brand-kit features cost

tools.name: Lucrovox
tools.what_it_does: AI phone agent for local service businesses — answers missed calls, books jobs and captures leads 24/7 for trades like HVAC, plumbing and roofing.
tools.pricing:
(re-verified 2026-08-24 on lucrovox.com/#pricing and lucrovox.com/lucrochat, both read in a real browser with the pages fully loaded) The phone agent has three published tiers and the plan table is back on the page: Starter $199 a month for up to 100 AI-handled calls, Pro $499 for up to 500 calls with CRM integration and advanced lead qualification, Enterprise $999 for up to 2,000 calls with white-label branding and multi-location support. Higher volume is quote-only. Starter and Pro carry a 14-day trial, Enterprise 30 days. On our previous reading, 17 August, the pricing page opened with a missed-call ROI calculator and the tier list could not be retrieved at all; it is worth knowing that the plan table on this site comes and goes, and that the calculator's outputs ($500 average job value producing $750 a week and $39,000 a year of lost revenue) are illustrations rather than prices.

LucroChat, the website chat product from the same vendor, sits on lucrovox.com/lucrochat with its own table metered on monthly conversations rather than calls: Starter $29 for up to 1,000 conversations on one website, Growth $59 for up to 3,000 conversations on up to three websites, Professional $199 for up to 10,000 conversations on unlimited websites, each with a 14-day trial and no card required. Its own FAQ agrees, describing pricing as starting at $29 a month for 1,000 conversations. One number on that page does not agree with the rest: the ROI calculator above the table reports its result “Based on Growth plan ($99/mo)” while the table prices Growth at $59. Read the plan table, not the calculator. Two products, two meters, one domain — price them separately.
tools.honest_knock:
The meter is AI-handled calls: Starter’s 100 calls a month is roughly three a day, so a genuinely busy shop outgrows it quickly — and the steps are steep ($199 → $499 → $999). The ‘callers can’t tell it’s AI’ claim is the vendor’s own: they offer a live demo number, so test that before you commit.

One more thing to read carefully on the sibling product's page. LucroChat's ROI calculator reports its return “Based on Growth plan ($99/mo)”, while the plan table on the same page prices Growth at $59 a month (both read 24 August 2026). The $99 is the higher of the two, so nobody is being lured with a low number, but a page that quotes two different prices for one plan is a page whose figures you check at checkout rather than take on trust.
tools.best_for: local service businesses — HVAC, plumbing, roofing, med spas — losing revenue to missed calls who want a 24/7 AI receptionist that books jobs straight into Google Calendar, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan or Jobber
tools.skip_if: your call volume is tiny (100 Starter calls is the whole point) or your callers expect a human — ring their live demo line first and judge the voice yourself
compare_with: Ruby is the established human-receptionist service; Lucrovox is the AI route with published per-plan pricing from $199/mo — cheaper per call at volume, so decide how much ‘human’ your callers actually need

tools.name: ManyChat
tools.what_it_does: Comment-to-DM and chat funnels for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and SMS. Flows are button-and-script based, so an unexpected reply falls back. The free tier holds 25 active contacts and paid plans are banded by list size — $14/month at 250 contacts, $139 at 25,000.
tools.pricing: Read on their own pricing page, 6 September 2026. Free: $0, 25 active contacts, 2 channels, 1 user. Paid tiers are banded by active contacts and priced two ways — month to month, or the lower rate if you pay for the year. Essential $17/mo or $14/mo billed annually ($168, 18% off), 250 contacts, 2 channels, 2 users. Pro $39/mo or $29 annually ($348, 25% off), 2,500 contacts, 3 channels, 3 users. Business $99/mo or $69 annually ($828, 30% off), 7,500 contacts, unlimited channels, 5 users. Advanced $199/mo or $139 annually ($1,668, 30% off), 25,000 contacts, unlimited channels, 10 users. Going over your allowance does not stop your automations: each extra active contact is billed at $0.10, $0.05, $0.025 and $0.004 on monthly billing, or $0.082, $0.038, $0.018 and $0.0028 on annual. Essential and Pro carry a 14-day free trial.
tools.honest_knock: Flows are button-and-script based, not natural language — type something unexpected and the bot falls back. The AI add-on is closer to keyword-matching than real conversational AI, billing scales with contacts (a viral Reel can spike your bill), and support is email-only and slow.
tools.best_for: creators and brands running comment-to-DM and multi-channel (Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp) marketing funnels — its killer feature works reliably
tools.skip_if: you want true conversational AI support, or you have a fast-growing contact list — the flow logic is rigid and contact-based billing climbs fast

tools.name: MarketerHire
tools.what_it_does: Hire pre-vetted expert marketing talent on demand: growth marketers, paid ads specialists, email pros and more — matched to your business within days.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-01 on marketerhire.com/pricing) No rates are published. The page says there is "no plan to pick and no retainer to guess at" and that after one call you are matched with a marketer "at a budget you agreed to". The terms it does publish: a free consultation with no obligation, a match within 24-48 hours, a two-week refundable trial, and month-to-month billing you can cancel at any time. The retainer tiers reported elsewhere at roughly $5,000, $10,000 and $15,000 a month, and hourly rates of about $100-$200 with 10-20 hour weekly minimums, do not come from MarketerHire and are not on its pricing page; treat them as a historical anchor for sizing the conversation, not as a quote.
tools.honest_knock: This is expert freelance talent at expert prices — the value is speed and vetting (their pricing page promises a match within 24-48 hours, against a months-long hire), but it is a real five-figure-a-month commitment for serious engagements, not a cheap gig marketplace. Because it's talent, not software, outcomes depend on the individual and how well you brief them; the rematch guarantee helps, but you still own the strategy. Right when a great marketer would pay for themselves, wrong as a budget stopgap.
tools.best_for: companies that need a vetted senior marketer (growth, paid ads, email, more) matched quickly, without the time and risk of a full-time hire
tools.skip_if: you need cheap, task-level help (a freelance marketplace fits) or you can't yet brief and direct a senior marketer toward a clear goal
compare_with: raw freelance marketplaces are cheaper but unvetted; agencies bundle teams — MarketerHire's edge is fast, pre-vetted individual senior talent

tools.name: Marketing 360
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one marketing platform for small business. Websites, CRM, ads, email and reputation management under one roof, with a unified reporting dashboard (their 'Intelligence' analytics) that pulls every channel, lead and sale into one view — and real humans to help run it.
tools.pricing: Quote-based, and deliberately so (verified 6 September 2026 on their own site). Marketing 360 does publish a page called How Plans & Pricing Work, and it carries no prices at all: the only numbers on it are the annual-revenue bands — $0-$250K, $250K-$1M, $1M+ — in the six-question form that stands between you and a quote. Reported core software runs around $395-$419/mo with marketing consultations, but design and custom website work are separate and can run from $2,000 into five figures, and managed ad services layer on top. This review carries no pricing screenshot rather than a placeholder. Get a full written quote.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. Pricing is hidden and quote-driven, and reviewers repeatedly flag that the real cost — software plus design plus managed services — climbs well above the headline, sometimes with recurring fees for features you don't use. And it's an all-in-one "we'll do it for you" model, which is great if you want a single vendor and a human team, but it can mean less flexibility and more lock-in than assembling best-of-breed tools. Ask exactly what's included before signing.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want one vendor handling website, CRM, ads, email and reputation with real humans to help, and prefer done-for-you over DIY
tools.skip_if: you're comfortable assembling your own stack (it'll cost far less), or you need transparent, predictable pricing you can budget upfront
compare_with: HubSpot plus a freelance marketer, or a local agency
best-of-breed or agency routes — Marketing 360 bundles software and services, but compare the all-in quote against a self-assembled stack

tools.name: Meeri
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that recovers abandoned carts with AI-written web push notifications instead of email or SMS — no address or phone needed to subscribe, and no commission on recovered revenue. Free for 300 notifications a month; Pro is $4.99.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/meeripush-push-notifications, listed as “Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery”, and on meeritech.com) Two plans, and the free one is a real plan rather than a demo. Basic is free to install and covers up to 300 push notifications a month, which the listing itself translates as roughly 100 recovered carts. It carries unlimited subscribers and segmentation, the abandoned-cart recovery campaign, scheduled promotional campaigns, AI-generated campaign content, intelligent delivery timing and basic email support, and it takes no commission on recovered revenue. Pro is $4.99 a month with a 7-day free trial and adds up to 3,000 push notification impressions, unlimited campaigns and automations and premium support. All charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The plan text says Pro “upgrades as you grow” and that additional usage-based charges are billed every 30 days, without printing a rate anywhere on the listing. The vendor's own site sells the same two tiers at the same prices, calling Basic free forever and Pro's allowance 3,000 notification impressions a month, and it does not print a usage rate either. The app is English-only, works with Shopify Admin and sits in Shopify's abandoned-cart category. Developer MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ, Dubai; the app launched on 23 February 2024 and carried 9 App Store reviews at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
Start with the numbers on the vendor's own homepage, because they do not match the App Store. meeritech.com says “5.0 on Shopify App Store”, “100% five-star reviews” and “5.0 average — 8 verified reviews on Shopify”. The listing itself, read the same day, shows 4.6 from 9 reviews: eight at five stars and one at one star. The vendor's figure is what you get if you leave the one-star review out. Nothing about the app is settled by that, but a marketing page that rounds its own rating up by dropping the worst review is a useful thing to know before you weigh the rest of the page.

The review base is thin whichever number you use. Nine reviews on an app that launched in February 2024, with the three visible on the listing all from stores trading from Pakistan, and two of them carrying near-identical wording. That is not evidence of anything wrong; it is very little evidence of anything at all, and it cannot tell you how this behaves on a store like yours.

Then there is the channel itself, which is the real decision. Web push needs a browser-level subscription, and the app's own pitch is that no email or phone number is required to get one. That cuts both ways: the list is easier to build and worthless off the browser that built it. You cannot export those subscribers into an email tool, you cannot reach them anywhere else, and your recovery ceiling is set by opt-in rate rather than by the app. Measure the opt-in rate first — 300 free notifications a month is enough to find out — because it decides everything the paid plan can do for you.

One more limit worth reading before you install: the listing names English as the only language, and Shopify Admin as the only integration. There is no Klaviyo, no email platform, no SMS tool on that line, so this sits beside your existing stack rather than inside it.
tools.best_for: small Shopify stores that want a cart-recovery channel which costs almost nothing and takes no commission on what it recovers — and that are willing to treat the free 300 notifications a month as a measurement of their own push opt-in rate before paying anything
tools.skip_if: you need the recovered contacts anywhere other than the browser that opted in, you run recovery through Klaviyo, Postscript or another stack you want this to feed, or you cannot get the usage-based charge on Pro quoted as a rate before you enable it

tools.name: MeetGeek
tools.what_it_does: Meeting recorder and note-taker: transcription, summaries and searchable meeting history.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-04, read on their own pricing page in a rendered browser) The page loads on annual billing, so the figures it shows first are the annual ones; both terms are given here. Basic is free with 3 hours of transcription a month. Pro $9.99 per user per month billed annually, $15.99 billed monthly, with 20 hours of transcription. Business $17 per user per month billed annually, $27 billed monthly, with unlimited transcription and team multi-meeting analytics. Enterprise is quote-only: SSO, SCIM, org-wide settings, on-premise storage, custom retention, custom voice agents and a dedicated account manager. Extra transcription hours are $0.50 each. Downloads and exports and admin user management start on Pro, not Business; API and MCP access are listed on the free Basic plan. A 14-day free trial runs on Pro.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month, which is about an hour a working day. That sounds generous until you count the meetings you would actually record — a sales rep on four calls a day passes it in the first week, and the overage is $0.50 an hour. Unlimited transcription is the real reason to be on Business at $17, so treat Pro as a plan for occasional recording rather than a cheaper version of the same thing. Worth checking before you buy: consent. A recorder that joins every meeting changes what people say in them, and that is a policy decision rather than a pricing one.
tools.best_for: people who run many external meetings and need a searchable record — the summaries earn their keep when you cannot remember which of four calls a detail came from
tools.skip_if: your meetings are internal and few, because the note-taking in your existing conferencing tool covers that; also skip Pro if you record daily, since twenty hours will not last
compare_with: the direct meeting-recorder peers — compare the transcription-hour allowance at your real meeting load, since that is the only meter that moves

tools.name: Melio
tools.what_it_does: Bill payments for small businesses by bank transfer or card, syncing with your accounting tools. The free Go plan covers five ACH transfers a month, then $0.50 each; Core is about $25/month. Card payments carry a flat 2.9%, which only pays off when you are deliberately floating cash.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. Core is $25/mo, or $20 billed annually, with 20 free ACH a month; Boost $55/mo, or $44 annually, with 50 free ACH; Unlimited $80/mo. The detail our earlier note missed: every paid plan adds $10 a month per additional user, or $8 on annual billing, so a three-person finance team on Core is $45 a month rather than $25. Card payments carry a flat 2.9% fee and check and wire payments have their own charges. There is a 30-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is genuinely useful for low bill volume, but the value case narrows as you scale into paid tiers — and the 2.9% card fee only makes sense when you're deliberately floating cash on a card for rewards or timing.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want to pay bills by bank transfer or card and get paid, starting free with no subscription
tools.skip_if: you already run AP through robust accounting software with bill-pay built in — a second tool adds little
compare_with: the per-seat AP platform for bigger finance teams

tools.name: MigrationPro
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that imports products, customers, orders, collections, URLs and 301 redirects from WooCommerce, Wix, Magento and 30-odd other platforms. One-time payment rather than a subscription, from $29 self-service or $300 done-for-you, after a free ten-record demo.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/migrationpro-shopify-migration-app and migrationpro.io/pricing) The App Store listing prints no number at all. It shows one plan, free to install, with the line “Pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate, with no subscription fees” and a note that all charges are billed in USD. The numbers live on the vendor's own pricing page, which is a calculator: you enter your product, customer and order counts and it quotes you. Two routes are sold there, both as one-time payments rather than subscriptions. The Automated app plan, where you run the migration yourself, starts at $29 based on store size, with add-ons selected and paid individually. The Done-for-you plan, where their team handles mapping, testing and go-live with a dedicated specialist, starts at $300 with every add-on included. Both carry a 30-day guarantee and need no credit card to start, and every migration begins with a free demo of up to 10 products, customers and orders. Their homepage puts a typical store at $49 to $299 based on actual record counts. The app is English-only, migrates from WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, BigCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Shopware, Etsy, Amazon, CSV and Excel among others, and covers products, customers, orders, collections, images, URLs and 301 redirects, with Smart Sync to re-import changed data after the main run. Developer Migrationpro, LLC, Dover, Delaware; the app launched on 10 May 2022 and had 178 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
The listing tells you nothing about what this costs. “Free to install. Additional charges may apply”, and a single plan block saying pricing is tailored to the entities you migrate. To learn a number you have to leave the App Store for the vendor's calculator, and the first number you find there — $29 — is the floor for the smallest store on the self-service route, not the price for yours. Their own homepage says most stores land between $49 and $299. Run the calculator before you form an opinion about value.

The add-on structure is the part to pin down in advance. On the automated plan the add-ons are chosen and paid for individually, and the page that says so does not price a single one of them. That is the difference between a $29 migration and an unknown one, and the only way to close it is to ask which add-ons your specific source platform needs before you start.

The vendor's marketing also runs ahead of the evidence in one place. migrationpro.io says “TRUSTED BY 250,000+ STORES”. The App Store record behind it is 178 reviews, and excellent ones: a 5.0 average with 173 of them at five stars. But 178 is the number that is independently visible, and a quarter of a million is a claim only the vendor can see. Weigh the reviews, not the banner.

One practical limit sits in the reviews themselves rather than the marketing: a merchant migrating a very large catalogue in July 2026 noted plainly that large volumes take a very long time, and that the team helped speed it up. That is a fair description of what data migration is, but if you are moving tens of thousands of records, plan for elapsed days rather than an afternoon, and plan for the trial migration to be the thing that tells you which.
tools.best_for: merchants moving an existing store into Shopify who want products, customers, orders and — critically — URLs and 301 redirects preserved, and who would rather pay once than subscribe to a tool they will use for a week
tools.skip_if: you are migrating away from Shopify or between two other platforms, since this only imports into Shopify; or you need a final price before you start and cannot get the add-ons for your source platform quoted up front

tools.name: MindStudio
tools.what_it_does: Visual builder for AI agents and workflows across 200+ models, with model usage passed through at provider cost and no markup. The real bill is therefore subscription plus model spend: Individual is about $20/month, and a looping agent burns provider credits until you set caps.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on mindstudio.ai/pricing) The subscription is a floor, not the bill: every tier reads “+ usage”, so model calls are charged on top. Free is $0/month plus usage and caps you at one agent and 1,000 runs a month. Individual is $20/month plus usage, or $16/month plus usage billed yearly, and lifts both caps to unlimited agents and unlimited runs. Business is quote-based. Because the metered part is uncapped, the tier you pick says little about what you will actually pay - the run volume does.
tools.honest_knock: The no-markup model pass-through is genuinely fair — but it also means your real cost is subscription PLUS model spend, and an agent that loops or processes big documents burns provider credits invisibly until you set limits. The honest build discipline: start every agent with usage caps, and treat 'no-code' as no-code for the plumbing — the logic design and prompt quality are still entirely on you.
tools.best_for: operators and teams that want to build and deploy real AI agents and workflows visually, across many models, without engineering time
tools.skip_if: you need one simple chatbot (simpler tools exist) or deeply custom logic that ends up easier in actual code
compare_with: adjacent agent-builders — MindStudio's edge is the multi-model router and transparent model pricing; compare on the integrations you need

tools.name: Miro
tools.what_it_does: Visual collaboration platform: an infinite online whiteboard for brainstorms, diagrams, workshops and planning — with templates, voting and AI that generates diagrams and summaries, built for real-time and async teamwork.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-02 on miro.com/pricing/) Free plan: 3 editable boards workspace-wide, unlimited members, AI published as a limited trial rather than a credit count. Starter $8/member/mo and Business $20/member/mo, both billed yearly; Enterprise custom priced from 30 members. The yearly toggle is marked save 20%, which puts the monthly rates at $10 and $25. AI credits are published per plan: 25 per member per month on Starter, 50 on Business. MCP calls are a separate published meter: 500 a day on Starter, 2,000 on Business. Currency note: the served page defaults to USD, but rendered from a Dutch connection the same numerals appear as €8 and €20, so the symbol follows the visitor region.
tools.honest_knock: Per-member pricing charges for every member added to the workspace, so an org-wide rollout multiplies at full headcount — and the free plan's 3-board cap is workspace-wide, not per person, so real teams outgrow it in days. Model who truly needs to edit before you buy seats.
tools.best_for: teams that think visually — brainstorms, flowcharts, retros, workshops and planning on an infinite shared canvas with strong templates and facilitation tools
tools.skip_if: your work is mostly documents or task tracking (a doc or PM tool fits better) or most of your company would only ever need to view, not edit
compare_with: FigJam wins if your designers already live in Figma, Lucidspark on diagram-heavy work; Miro wins on breadth: templates, integrations and workshop facilitation

tools.name: Mktg.ai
tools.what_it_does: Always-on AI marketing analyst: unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over your own spend data — no public pricing, demo-first.
tools.pricing: No public pricing (re-verified 6 September 2026): mktg.ai/pricing still returns 404 and the navigation carries no pricing item, so every route ends at 'Book a Demo'. The tiers themselves are no longer secret, though — the FAQ names Growth and Enterprise above the entry level and describes what they add (dedicated onboarding on both; a dedicated customer success manager, SLA-backed response times and quarterly business reviews on top of that). Email support is on every plan; custom integrations and EU data residency are Enterprise-only, with US data centres the default. The machine-readable llms.txt is Wix boilerplate advertising an MCP endpoint and carries no price either. Rates require a sales conversation.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. First, the price is still hidden — a 404 where the pricing page should be, and no pricing item in the navigation — which for a tool that promises spend transparency is an irony worth noticing, and the FAQ makes it sharper: its own introduction says it covers what the platform costs, and then no answer in it names a figure. What the FAQ does publish is the tier names, Growth and Enterprise, and the fact that EU data residency is Enterprise-only. Second, the ROI story is the vendor's own: the homepage tile assumes a $5M budget and puts a 3% efficiency gain at $150K alongside $100K of reallocated spend, which is 2% of the same budget. Ask for verified case numbers at your spend level on the demo call.
tools.best_for: marketing teams with real media spend across channels who want an always-on AI analyst — unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over their own data. It layers on top of your existing platforms rather than replacing them, with the vendor putting real-time data in week one and full onboarding at two to three weeks
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is modest (the value scales with budget waste, and yours is small), or you want transparent self-serve pricing before a sales call
compare_with: Diginius manages PPC and e-commerce performance hands-on with published pricing; Mktg.ai sells the always-on AI-analyst layer on top of your channels — but with no public prices, you’re comparing a sticker against a sales call

tools.name: Modelize
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that generates on-model, lifestyle, studio and flat-lay product photos in bulk from your existing catalogue images, using Google's Gemini image models. Free tier is 3 one-off images; Starter $19 a month buys 100 images, Pro $49 buys 250 at up to 4K, Enterprise $99 buys 500 with extras at $0.20 each.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/modelize, listed as “Modelize: AI Product Photos”) Free plan available, then Starter $19, Pro $49 and Enterprise $99 a month. The free tier is 3 AI images once, not per month. Starter covers 100 images a month with 3 AI custom presets and 3 custom models, at standard 2K resolution and email support. Pro at $49 covers 250 images, 10 custom presets and 10 custom models, resolution up to 4K and priority support. Enterprise at $99 includes 500 images with $0.20 per additional image, unlimited custom presets and models, maximum 4K and dedicated support. On modelize.studio the same tiers are also sold annually at two months free, but only on Free, Starter and Pro — Enterprise is monthly billing only. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 5.0 from 13 App Store reviews. Developer Optify, Lyon, France; the app launched 20 April 2026 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: The economics are flat: at roughly $0.19 to $0.20 an image on every tier, moving up the ladder buys resolution, custom presets and support, never a cheaper image. Read it that way and the pricing is honest; read it as a volume discount and you will overbuy. Two other things deserve a clear head. The output quality rides on Google's Gemini image models rather than on anything Modelize owns, so results and consistency can shift when Google ships a new version, and that is outside the vendor's control as much as yours. And the app is genuinely new — launched 20 April 2026, 13 reviews at the time of writing — so the five-star average is a small sample, not a track record. Finally, an on-model photo generated by AI shows a person who does not exist; check what your ad platforms and marketplaces require you to disclose before you build a catalogue on it.
tools.best_for: Shopify fashion, jewellery and homeware sellers who need consistent on-model, lifestyle or flat-lay imagery across a large catalogue and cannot justify a photographer per drop
tools.skip_if: you need art direction a preset cannot express, photography of the actual physical item in its real texture, or a vendor with a long public track record — this app is four months old

tools.name: Modge
tools.what_it_does: Desktop time tracking and workforce analytics for remote and hybrid teams: automatic hours, app and URL classification, shift adherence, leave, payroll-ready timesheets and Stripe invoicing. Basic $4 per seat per month on annual billing ($5 monthly), Pro $5.50, Premium $7; screenshots are optional and off by default. 14-day trial, no card.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-03 on modge.com/pricing, both billing toggles and the comparison table) Per-seat plans with a full-feature 14-day trial and no card. Basic is $5 per seat per month billed monthly or $4 billed annually: app and URL tracking with AI productivity classification, workforce dashboards, automatic time tracking with optional screenshots, timesheets, approvals and payroll exports, invoice creation, email and chat support. Pro is $7 monthly or $5.50 annually and adds shifts, scheduling and adherence, leave, breaks and overtime, client billing through Stripe, on-demand screenshots with 12-month retention, and custom roles, teams and project budgets. Premium, marked popular, is $9 monthly or $7 annually and adds automated project and task time tracking, workflow analysis, suspicious-activity and mouse-jiggler detection, burnout-risk and profitability insights, contract signing, 24-month screenshot retention and a dedicated account manager. Enterprise is custom, on annual billing with volume pricing, custom retention, customised onboarding and an SLA. Two add-ons are priced per seat: More Screenshots at $2 a month lifts capture from 18 to 60 an hour on Basic, Pro and Premium; Extended Data Retention at $2 a month or $1.67 annually keeps records for six years on every tier. The comparison table lists screenshot retention as 3 months on Basic, 12 on Pro and 24 on Premium, and marks SSO (SAML 2.0), SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 as soon.
tools.honest_knock: The numbers on Modge's own pages do not agree with each other. The homepage says trusted by 1,000+ teams, the affiliate page says 1,800+ teams, the pricing page says over 2,000 users; the pricing page also shows three star ratings, 4.6 from 1,500 reviews, 4.8 from 2,000 and 4.2 from 800, without naming a single platform they come from. None of that touches the product, but it is the kind of copy a buyer should not repeat in a business case. What does touch the product is the comparison table: SSO through SAML 2.0, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 are all marked soon, and HIPAA compliant appears with no report behind it. If your security review needs a document today, there is none to hand over. The desktop agent is macOS and Windows only, and the pricing page mentions no mobile app or GPS, so field teams are out of scope.
tools.best_for: desk-bound remote or hybrid teams of a few to a few hundred people who want time tracking, app classification, shift adherence, leave and payroll-ready timesheets in one seat priced between $4 and $7 a month, and who are happy to run screenshots as an opt-in rather than a default
tools.skip_if: you need SSO or a SOC 2 report today, both are marked soon; your people work in the field, since the agent is desktop-only with no mobile or GPS on the page; or your security team will not accept a compliance claim without a document
compare_with: The obvious comparison. Hubstaff's annual column starts at $4.99 a seat with a two-seat minimum and its monthly column at $7; Modge starts at $4 annual or $5 monthly with no minimum on the page. Hubstaff has the longer record, a mobile app with GPS and a far larger integration list; Modge's pitch is shift adherence, leave policies and Stripe invoicing built into a cheaper seat, with screenshots off by default. Pick Hubstaff for field teams, Modge for desk-bound teams that also need rotas.

tools.name: Momence
tools.what_it_does: Booking and business management for class-based businesses — yoga and fitness studios, gyms, salons and schools: scheduling, memberships, payments, marketing automations and a member app in one place.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-06 on the vendor's own pricing page) The tiers render in plain text again: Basic $0/mo with a 5% Momence fee on every transaction plus 4% passed to the client; Pro $60/mo with your fee halved to 2.5%; Custom $199/mo with no Momence fee, unlimited add-ons and dedicated support. Basic and Pro carry an identical exclusion list in their card tooltips — no add-ons, no phone number, no inbox, no retail products, no reporting or insights, no staff members, no locations — so Pro buys a lower commission and nothing else. Card processing is charged separately and published per country: US 3.9% + $0.30 online, 3.7% + $0.05 in person, 1.8% ACH; UK 2.5% + 20p, 2.4% + 10p, 2% + 20p BACS; Australia 2.75% + A$0.30, 2.75% + A$0.10, 2% + A$0.30 BECS; Canada 3.9% + C$0.30, 3.7% + C$0.05, 2% + C$0.40. One change since our August readings: on 15 and 19 August 2026 these cards were rendered and then covered by a lead form and a blur filter, so the figures existed in the page but were unreadable until you handed over your details. That gate is gone.
tools.honest_knock: The 'free' plan is the most expensive one once you have real volume: a 5% commission on every sale overtakes Pro's $60 flat fee around $29k a year in processed revenue, and Pro in turn loses to the $199 Custom plan above about $67k a year. Pick your tier by volume, not by sticker — and note what the middle tier does not include. The tooltip on the Pro card lists the same exclusions as the free plan: no add-ons, no phone number, no inbox, no retail products, no reporting or insights, no staff members, no locations. Pro halves your commission and adds no features.
tools.best_for: class-based businesses — studios, gyms, salons, schools — that want scheduling, memberships, payments and marketing in one system with a member app
tools.skip_if: you only need a simple calendar-booking link (a lightweight scheduler is cheaper) or you won't accept platform fees on top of card processing
