Skip it as well if you need a firm budget before committing: with no country-level rates published, a like-for-like comparison against another provider is not possible from public information — you have to get quotes from both. And if you are already at scale with a dedicated account manager elsewhere, the Flex tier is not aimed at you and Plus removes much of the flexibility that makes Flex interesting
compare_with: the comparison worth doing, and our Deel dossier makes it checkable. On published floors: EOR $199 against $599 a month, contractor of record $199 against $325, US PEO $99 against $125, contractor management $29 against $49. Remote People is cheaper on every line we can compare. What Deel has is scale and a product surface that goes well beyond employment — and, in fairness, both are demo-led at the point where it matters, so neither publishes what your particular hire will actually cost. Get a written quote from both for the same country and the same salary; that is the only comparison that survives contact with reality. Our Remote People figures were read on 2026-08-07, the Deel figures are dated in that dossier.

tools.name: Replit
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based coding environment with instant deploys and an AI agent. Billing is effort-based: Core is $20/month including $25 of credits, Pro $95/month billed annually including $100. Credits expire monthly and a complex agent session burns them fast, which makes production costs hard to budget.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-02 on their own pricing page) Starter is free, with daily Agent credits, a built-in database and the slides/video/animation tools. Core is $17/month billed annually, shown against a struck-through $20; the $25 monthly figure of our summer captures is no longer on the page. It includes $20 of monthly credits towards the most powerful models (down from $25), up to 5 collaborators and up to 2 agents working in parallel. Pro is $100/month, or $95/month billed annually, and includes $100 of monthly credits, up to 15 collaborators and up to 50 viewers. Enterprise is separate. The number to watch is not the seat but the credits: since Replit moved to effort-based pricing the Agent decides how much work a request is worth, so the monthly credit allowance is a starting balance rather than a budget.
tools.honest_knock: The credit model on AI-heavy building is unpredictable — a complex agent session can burn credits fast, and they expire monthly, so heavy AI users hit surprise costs. Great for learning and prototyping; watch the meter for production work.
tools.best_for: developers, learners and tinkerers who want a zero-setup, browser-based coding environment with AI assistance
tools.skip_if: you need a stable, cost-predictable production environment — the expiring-credit model makes AI-heavy usage hard to budget
compare_with: GitHub Codespaces or a local IDE

tools.name: Reply.io
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven sales engagement platform. Automate your cold outreach across email, LinkedIn, and calls while keeping the human touch. Now includes a mobile app (Jason AI) for iOS and Android to run outreach on the go.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Reply's own machine-readable plan breakdown) Three separate tracks, and the one you pick changes the arithmetic completely. Email Volume is pay-as-you-go by active contacts: 1,000 for $49/mo, 2,000 for $59, 3,000 for $69, 5,000 for $89, 10,000 for $159, 25,000 for $259 and 50,000 for $459, with 100,000+ quoted. Multichannel is all-inclusive from $89/month billed annually ($99 monthly) with unlimited active contacts, adding LinkedIn, SMS, calls and WhatsApp, 10 mailboxes (5 on monthly) and 50 live data credits. AI SDR (Jason) runs $500 to $1,000 a month billed annually at Starter (1,000-3,000 contacts) and $1,500 to $3,000 at Growth (5,000-10,000), with Enterprise quoted. Agency Core starts at $210/month and Agency AI SDR at $500 per client. Add-ons on top of the Email track: LinkedIn automation $69/month per account, calls and SMS $29/month per account, AI/live-data credits from $39/month and email validation from $20/month.
tools.honest_knock: The advertised $89 is the lobby, not the building: use LinkedIn and calling — the whole point of multichannel — and the real per-seat price roughly doubles. Budget 1.5-2x the sticker, plus sending infrastructure (domains, warmup) that any cold-outreach stack needs. The platform is genuinely capable; the pricing just rewards reading this paragraph before the demo call.
tools.best_for: sales teams running structured multichannel outbound (email + LinkedIn + calls) who want sequences, warmup and a B2B database in one platform
tools.skip_if: you only send plain email sequences (cheaper single-channel tools exist), or your list is too small to justify per-seat-plus-add-ons math
compare_with: Instantly is cheaper email-first, Apollo bundles a bigger database — Reply's edge is mature multichannel sequencing; compare real per-seat totals

tools.name: respond.io
tools.what_it_does: Shared inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, email and live chat, with workflow automation, broadcasts and AI agents on top. Priced per monthly active contact rather than per seat: $79 Starter, $159 Growth and $279 Advanced, around 20% off paid yearly, with a 7-day trial and no card. The catch is where the line sits: automation, broadcasts, AI agents and the API all start at Growth, so the entry plan is the inbox without the engine (read 13 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-13, read off respond.io/pricing) Four tiers, billed on monthly active contacts rather than seats: Starter $79/month, Growth $159, Advanced $279, and Enterprise on quote. Paying yearly takes roughly 20% off — $948, $1,908 and $3,348 a year against $1,188, $2,388 and $4,188 monthly. The trial is 7 days and takes no card. What separates the tiers is not volume but capability, and the line matters: Starter buys team and custom inboxes, the mobile app, AI Prompt, AI Assist, basic reports and 2FA. **Workflows automation, broadcasts, AI Agents, advanced reports, the developer API and the Zapier and Make integrations all start at Growth.** Advanced adds multiple workspaces, SSO, webhooks, HTTP requests in workflows and phone-number masking, and although a figure is shown its button says “Talk to Sales”. One thing we could not pin down. The page carries a selector for 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / more than 10,000 monthly active contacts under the heading “pay only for the contacts you talk to”, but the prices we read did not move between those settings. Ask what your contact volume actually costs before you sign — that is the meter you are buying.
tools.honest_knock: The entry plan is the inbox without the engine. At $79 you get shared inboxes across WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS and live chat, and that alone solves the “five people answering from one phone” problem. But workflow automation, broadcasts, AI Agents and the API — the things most people picture when they read “omnichannel platform” — begin at $159, so the real entry price for an automated setup is double the headline. Work out which side of that line you sit on before comparing it with anything else. And note the meter: you pay per active contact per month, so cost follows how many people message you, not how many staff you add. That is kinder than per-seat pricing for a small team fielding a lot of chats, and harsher if you have a big list you talk to often.
tools.best_for: a small team that already lives in WhatsApp and Instagram DMs and has outgrown a shared phone — retail, clinics, travel, local services. Per-contact pricing suits you if headcount grows faster than conversation volume, and the seven-day trial without a card lets you check that before committing
tools.skip_if: you only need one channel: a plain shared inbox or a helpdesk will cost less than an omnichannel platform you use a fifth of. Skip the Starter plan specifically if automation is the reason you are looking — you will be on Growth within a month. And if your monthly active contacts run into the tens of thousands, get the number in writing first, because that is the meter and the published ladder stops being informative
compare_with: the comparison most WhatsApp-first teams will make, and one we have already researched. Both put a shared team inbox on top of the WhatsApp Business API; the practical difference is how the meter runs and where automation starts. respond.io reaches wider across channels — Instagram, Messenger, SMS, live chat and email in the same inbox — which is worth paying for only if you genuinely answer on more than one

tools.name: Restream
tools.what_it_does: Multistreaming studio: broadcast one show to YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook and Twitch at once from the browser, with guests and local recordings. The channel caps are the business model — 3 on Standard at $190 a year, 5 on Professional — and extra seats start at Professional, at $25/month; the Standard column offers none.
tools.pricing: Re-read on restream.io/pricing on 7 September 2026, with both the Creator/Business tabs and the Monthly/Annually toggle operated. Free: 2 channels with Restream branding, 1 seat. Standard $19 a month, billed as $190 a year (3 channels, 1 seat). Professional $49 a month, billed as $470 a year (5 channels, Full HD 1080p in Studio, 2 seats). Business $239 a month, billed as $2,390 a year (8 channels, website player to 1,000 viewers, 2 seats). Enterprise is quoted. Annual therefore saves 16.7% on Standard and Business and 20.1% on Professional, not the flat 'Save 20%' the toggle advertises. Add-ons are monthly on top: Clips +$19/+$29/+$59 and Webinars +$99/+$99/+$299 across the three tiers, extra team seats $25 a seat on Professional and Business only, and extra workspaces $49 (Professional) or $239 (Business).
tools.honest_knock: The channel caps are the business model -- each tier buys a few more destinations. Seats are the second meter: Free and Standard include one and cannot buy another at all, while Professional and Business include two and sell extras at $25 a month. Price it at your real destination count and team size, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: creators, podcasters and marketing teams who broadcast one show to many platforms at once, without extra encoding hardware
tools.skip_if: you stream to a single platform (its native studio is free) or you need broadcast-grade production control — an OBS-style tool fits better
compare_with: StreamYard wins on beginner-friendly guest shows, OBS on free pro-grade control; Restream wins on multistream breadth and scheduling

tools.name: Retouch4me
tools.what_it_does: AI retouching plugins for photographers (Photoshop-compatible, Mac/Windows) — perpetual licences per plugin ($145 for most, $179 for Dodge & Burn and Clean Backdrop), full-suite subscriptions from $169 a year with 2,400 retouch credits, or cloud retouching in credit packs at $24 for 100, $59 for 300 and $179 for 1,200. Free to try first: two free plugins, three free apps and a demo on every paid plugin (site, read 7 Sep 2026).
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-07 on retouch4.me/pricing and retouch4.me/products/retouch-plugins) Three ways to pay. (1) Perpetual plugin licences, one-time. The photo collection is fifteen plugins: $145 for Heal, Crop, Face Make, Portrait Volumes, Skin Tone, Skin Mask, Mattifier, White Teeth, Eyes Bundle, Stray Hairs, Fabric, Dust and Color Match; $179 for Dodge & Burn and Clean Backdrop. Outside that collection: Lab $145, Mask Anything $29, the Vectorscope panel $30, video plugins from $124 and 3D LUT Creator Pro from $99. A four-plugin portrait stack (Heal, Crop, Dodge & Burn, Clean Backdrop) is $648 at list. Time-boxed sales run alongside the list: on 7 Sep 2026 Heal showed $108.75 (25% off $145) under a 'Workflow Revamp' promotion putting a different plugin on 25% off each Tuesday of the month. (2) Subscriptions, which include the full plugin set: Start $169 a year, Pro $299, Business $759 — a 'limited offer' against list rates of $20/$35/$90 a month, restated on the cards as $14.08/$24.92/$63.25 a month. They carry 2,400/6,000/18,000 retouching credits and 108,000/300,000/1,200,000 culling credits a year, 20/40/100 GB of MyShot storage, unlimited AI colour correction with batch processing, and a 14-day money-back guarantee that holds while you have used up to 500 retouches. 1 retouch = 1 credit regardless of how many plugins run on the image, and unused credits roll over up to 5 years while the subscription stays active. (3) Credit packs without a subscription: $24 for 100 retouching credits (plus 9,000 culling credits), $59 for 300 (25,000) and $179 for 1,200 (100,000) — $0.24, $0.20 and $0.15 a retouch, each with unlimited AI colour correction for 30 days after purchase. Free: the Frequency Separation and Color Match Free plugins, the Apex, Photoshop Panel and Arams applications, a Try Demo on every paid plugin, and free cloud retouches for uploading RAWs to their RAW Bank.
tools.honest_knock: Work out which lane you are in before you pay, because the three lanes price the same photo very differently. One plugin forever at $145 is honest value — but a working portrait stack means four plugins at $145-$179 each, $648 in total, while the Start subscription hands you the entire set for $169 a year with 2,400 retouches included. The catch cuts the other way too: own-forever versus keep-paying is the real decision, since the credits' 5-year rollover only holds 'while the subscription is active' — stop paying and the suite and the stockpile are gone. Low volume? Cloud retouching without a subscription is sold in packs, $24 for 100 retouches, and at $0.15 to $0.24 a photo it is the dearest lane per image, not the cheapest.
tools.best_for: high-volume portrait, school and wedding photographers who already live in Photoshop and want repetitive retouching (skin, stray hairs, dust, teeth) automated — owning the plugins outright or renting the whole suite on credits, whichever their volume favours
tools.skip_if: occasional editors — the two free plugins, the free applications and a $24 pack of 100 cloud retouches cover light use; or anyone unwilling to do the three-lane maths, because picking the wrong lane here easily doubles what the same workflow costs
compare_with: the credit-based AI retouching desktop app — Evoto bundles everything in one interface paid per export credit, Retouch4me offers lifetime plugins, a credit subscription or pay-per-photo; high volume favours owning the plugins, low volume favours credits. Verify both current price lists yourself.

tools.name: Rippling
tools.what_it_does: Workforce platform that unifies HR, IT and Finance in one system of record: run payroll and benefits, manage hiring, onboarding and time tracking, and provision devices and app access automatically — with policy-driven automation across employee data, approvals and compliance.
tools.pricing: (verified 2026-08-27) Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The pricing page is a 'request a custom quote' form with no public numbers — you tell it which of HR, IT and Finance you need and your headcount, and a price comes back through sales. The one figure Rippling publishes is a floor: its global-payroll page advertises 'Starting at $8 per month per user' for the platform (HR, payroll, benefits, spend, devices and apps). That $8 is an entry point, not a quote — the buttons beside it read 'Get a free quote' and 'Contact Sales', and the real bill depends on which modules you switch on and how many employees you run. Some product pages show no price at all. Decide the exact module mix you need before you compare vendors, because Rippling's cost scales with how much of it you adopt.
tools.honest_knock: The published '$8 per user a month' is real but it's only the floor, and it's the HR-and-payroll entry — not the price of the platform. Rippling sells HR, IT and Finance as separate, separately-quoted modules, so you can't comparison-shop without a sales call, and a single-module deployment pays platform prices for a point tool. You're buying a system of record; the value only shows up once you consolidate several systems onto it.
tools.best_for: growing companies that want HR, IT and Finance on one employee record — so a single hire can trigger payroll, a provisioned laptop and app access at once, and offboarding claws it all back automatically
tools.skip_if: you need only one function, like standalone payroll or device management, where a focused and transparently-priced point tool is cheaper and simpler — or you need firm pricing before committing to a sales conversation
compare_with: Gusto is the simple, transparently-priced US payroll-and-HR incumbent for domestic teams; Rippling is the broader system of record that also runs IT and Finance and scales internationally. Choose Gusto for straightforward payroll, Rippling to consolidate systems onto one record

tools.name: Riverside
tools.what_it_does: Records podcasts and video locally at each end, so guests on poor connections still come out broadcast-quality. Recording hours are unlimited; the meter is separate-track download time, 15 hours a month on Pro ($35 monthly or $24 on annual billing, re-read 7 Sep 2026), and hitting that cap stops new separate-track downloads until the next cycle rather than billing you more.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-07 on riverside.com/pricing; riverside.fm now redirects to riverside.com. Amounts are region-priced: the page returned euros from a Netherlands exit on this date, with the same numerals our 26 August 2026 US reading returned as dollars, so the dollar figures are given here) Pro $35 a month or $24 on annual billing; Grow $45 or $34; Webinar $99 or $79; Business quote-only. What separates the tiers is studios and separate-track download hours — 1 studio and 15 hours on Pro, 2 and 20 on Grow, 3 and 25 on Webinar, unlimited on Business — while recording hours are unlimited on all four. Up to 4K desktop capture, 44.1/48 kHz audio and 10 people in a session are on every tier; the mobile apps cap at 1080p below Business, and frame rates are 24 FPS except on Business. Webinar registration is 100 on the Webinar plan and up to 10,000 on Business. AI credits: Pro starts with 2,000 and Business with 12,000, and Magic Clips, Magic Audio and the AI Co-Creator do not consume them. The page contradicts itself: its FAQ says annual billing saves 'up to 20%' with Pro dropping from $29 to $24 and Grow from $39 to $34 — the pre-increase monthly rates — while against the $35/$45/$99 on the cards the annual saving is 31%, 24% and 20%.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is not recording time, it is separate-track download time — and separate tracks are the entire reason to use this rather than a video call. Recording itself is unlimited. Their own FAQ on hitting the cap: you can still access your content but cannot download new separate tracks until the next billing cycle or you upgrade. So a busy interview month does not cost you more money, it quietly stops you delivering, which is worse. Fifteen hours on Pro is about seven or eight hour-long interviews once you count retakes and the recording that runs while you set up. There is a 14-day trial rather than a published free plan.
tools.best_for: podcasters and interviewers who need broadcast-quality audio and video from guests on bad connections — local recording at each end is genuinely the thing that solves it
tools.skip_if: you record alone, or your guests are always in the room with you, because then a local recorder does the same job once; also skip Pro if you download more than about eight hours of separate tracks a month, since that cap is what will stop you
compare_with: the direct local-recording peers — compare the monthly hour allowance for separate tracks, not the headline price

tools.name: RocketReach
tools.what_it_does: Contact data and prospecting: look up verified work and personal email addresses plus direct and mobile phone numbers, filter on 50+ criteria, then push the result into Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft or Bullhorn. Sequences, an AI email writer and Autopilot jobs that keep a saved search running come with the paid plans, with technographics, org charts and intent topics higher up. The database size (700 million professionals, 60 million companies) and the 98% accuracy figure are RocketReach's own.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-01 on rocketreach.co/pricing) A free account exists: signing up takes no credit card and gives a limited number of lookups. Above that are three paid plans, all quoted per month on an annual term. Essentials is $19/month, billed $229 USD annually, and is email only: unlimited personal and professional email lookups, 1,200 exports a year and a send limit of 500 emails a day. Pro is $52/month, billed $619 USD annually, and adds unlimited mobile and direct phone numbers, 3,600 exports a year, technographics, news and org charts, 10 active Autopilot jobs and the Salesforce, Outreach, HubSpot, Salesloft and Bullhorn integrations. Ultimate is $115/month, billed $1,379 USD annually, with 20,000 exports a year, 25 active Autopilot jobs, Salesforce custom mapping, intent data and healthcare data. Above those, enterprise plans are quote-only and the page says they start at $6K annually. Read the headline figures as the annual rate: the plan-features table lists searches as unlimited on the annual term but capped at 100, 250 and 1,000 a month on monthly billing, with exports capped at those same numbers instead of the yearly allowances. RocketReach says a lookup is refunded when it returns no verified email or phone number, and that cancelling takes effect from the next term, so you keep access for the term you have already paid for.
tools.honest_knock:
The published prices are annual rates, and the annual term is doing more work than the page lets on. RocketReach's own feature table lists searches as unlimited on the annual term but caps them at 100, 250 and 1,000 a month if you bill monthly, and caps exports at those same numbers instead of 1,200, 3,600 and 20,000 a year. So the $19 on the card is $229 up front, and the flexible-looking monthly option is the one that rations the product. Their FAQ adds that cancelling takes effect from the next term, so a year is a year.

The plan boundary matters more than the price. Essentials is email only: mobile and direct phone numbers start at Pro, and so do the Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft and Bullhorn integrations, technographics and org charts. Above Ultimate the ladder stops being a ladder, with enterprise starting at $6K annually against $1,379 for Ultimate.

And the numbers that sell it are all RocketReach's own, printed on their pricing page: 700 million professionals, 60 million companies, 98% accuracy, 30 million users, 95% of the S&P 500. We have measured none of them. Contact-data accuracy is the thing that varies most by territory and by seniority, and a database claim is an average, not a promise about your list. The free account is the right answer to that: it costs nothing and needs no card, so run the free lookups against a slice of your own target accounts before you commit to a year. A lookup that finds nothing verified is refunded, per their FAQ, which makes that test cheaper still.
tools.best_for: sales, recruiting and BD teams whose bottleneck is finding verified direct dials and personal emails, and who can commit to an annual term - that is where the search allowance stops being metered
tools.skip_if: you need the outreach engine more than the data, or you cannot commit to a year: monthly billing caps lookups and exports at 100 to 1,000 a month, and platforms like lemlist or Amplemarket build the sequencing around the contacts instead of selling you the contacts first
compare_with: the cheaper all-rounder and the enterprise data giant

tools.name: Ruby
tools.what_it_does: Live human receptionists answering your calls, plus chat. Billed by receptionist-minute: $250/month for 50 minutes and $395 for 100, rising to $1,725 for 500, with chat bundled from $115/month. Premium rates that pay off only when a missed call is a lost client.
tools.pricing: Read on their own plans-and-pricing page, 6 September 2026. Virtual receptionist plans are sold by monthly minutes: 50 minutes $250, 100 minutes $395, 200 minutes $720, 500 minutes $1,725 — $5.00 a minute at the bottom, $3.45 at the top. Live chat is sold by monthly chats: 10 chats $143, 30 chats $335, 50 chats $520. Add chat to a receptionist plan and those become $115, $268 and $416 — the 20% the page advertises, exact at the two larger tiers and rounded up from $114.40 at the smallest. Larger volumes are quoted. Ruby states there are no extra fees for activation, onboarding, setup, customisation or out-of-hours coverage, and every feature is included at every tier — the plans differ only in the number of minutes or chats. No rate is published for minutes used beyond your plan.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying premium rates for real human receptionists billed per minute — worth it when a missed call is a lost client, but expensive if your call volume is low or an AI answering service would do the job for a fraction.
tools.best_for: client-driven service businesses (law, home services, clinics) where a live human answering every call directly wins business
tools.skip_if: your call volume is low or mostly routine — an AI answering service or a solid voicemail-to-text setup costs far less

tools.name: Runpod
tools.what_it_does: Serverless GPU compute platform. Rent high-end NVIDIA GPUs by the hour to train and deploy your own machine learning models.
tools.pricing: Pay-per-use GPU cloud (re-verified 2026-08-26 against runpod.io/pricing). Secure Cloud on-demand pods run from $0.27/hr (RTX A5000) and $0.49/hr (L4) up to $2.89/hr for an H100 PCIe, $3.29/hr H100 SXM, $4.59/hr H200, $6.79/hr B200 and $7.89/hr B300. Four of those moved up since July — L4 from $0.39, H100 SXM from $2.99, H200 from $4.39 and B300 from $7.39 — while the A5000 and the H100 PCIe did not move at all. The page's own structured data publishes the Community Cloud column beside every card, and that is where the real discount sits: RTX 4090 $0.34 against $0.74 on Secure, RTX 3090 $0.22 against $0.50, RTX A6000 $0.33 against $0.53, H100 PCIe $1.99 against $2.89. Serverless bills per second at a premium over pods in exchange for sub-200ms cold starts and autoscaling: $0.58/hr for the 16GB tier, $2.72/hr for an A100, $4.79/hr for an 80GB H100 (was $4.55) and $9.98/hr at the top for a B300. Multi-node Clusters now publish two rates — $1.79/hr per A100 SXM and $4.31/hr per H200 SXM — while H100 SXM, L40S and B200 clusters plus all reserved capacity stay quote-only. Storage is billed on top and is easy to miss: container disk $0.10/GB/month, volume disk $0.10 while running and $0.20 while idle, network storage $0.07/GB under 1TB and $0.05 over it, $0.14 for the high-performance tier.
tools.honest_knock: The honest math is utilization. On the same card serverless runs roughly 1.6-2x the pod rate per compute-hour: $4.79 against $2.89 for an H100, $2.72 against $1.39 for an A100 PCIe. That is brilliant for spiky inference and wasteful for steady training, so pick the mode per workload, not per habit. And like all GPU clouds, the meter never sleeps: an idle pod you forgot is the cloud version of the subscription graveyard. Set spend alerts before the first experiment, not after the first invoice.
tools.best_for: developers and ML teams that want cheap, per-second GPU compute for inference and experiments without committing to hyperscaler contracts
tools.skip_if: you need enterprise SLAs, compliance guarantees and managed everything (hyperscalers exist for that), or your workload is steady enough that owned/reserved hardware wins
compare_with: close GPU-cloud rivals — compare per-GPU-hour on the exact card you need and whether serverless cold-start speed matters for your workload

tools.name: Salesflare
tools.what_it_does: CRM for small B2B teams that auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar. $29–99/user/month with no caps on contacts or pipelines. Deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and basic reporting unless you export.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against salesflare.com) $29–99/user/mo (Growth ~$29–39, Pro ~$49); 30-day free trial, no card, no onboarding fees and no caps on contacts or pipelines (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and reporting feels basic unless you export. Integrations cover the essentials (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier) but niche tools lean on Zapier — and at higher seat counts the price overlaps fuller CRMs.
tools.best_for: small B2B teams whose reps hate data entry — Salesflare auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar
tools.skip_if: you need deep customisation, a big integration marketplace, or built-in calling and invoicing — Pipedrive or a fuller CRM fit better
compare_with: the more customisable, bigger-integration pipeline CRM

tools.name: Salesflow
tools.what_it_does: LinkedIn outreach automation for outbound sales teams — connection requests, follow-up sequences and Open InMails, with email steps for multichannel campaigns, plus admin panel, seat management and shared templates for agencies. Priced per seat, from about $79 per user per month billed annually.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02) Their own pricing page returns a 403 to us, so these figures come from independent reviews read on 2 August 2026 rather than from Salesflow directly — verify on their site before you buy. Single User is reported at $99 per user per month, or $79 per user per month billed annually, plus VAT where it applies, including 400 LinkedIn invites, up to 2,000 follow-up messages and 800 Open InMails a month. Team tiers are reported as Starter from $70 per seat at 5+ seats, Pro from $39.95 per seat at 20+ seats and Agency from $29.98 per seat at 50+ seats, with discounts of 15% at six months and 30% at twelve.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price falls steeply with team size — roughly $79 alone against $29.98 at fifty seats — so a solo operator pays two to three times what an agency pays per seat for the same product. And the monthly quotas are the real ceiling: 400 invites and 800 Open InMails is a fixed budget, not a starting point.
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn sequences across several seats, where the per-seat price drops and the admin panel earns its keep
tools.skip_if: you are one person sending a handful of connection requests a week — the quotas are far above what you need and the seat price is at its highest

tools.name: Salesmessage
tools.what_it_does: Business texting and SMS marketing in one shared inbox. Reach customers where they actually reply — two-way texting, automation and team collaboration.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-08, re-verified on their own pricing page) Repackaged since our last check into two named plans plus Enterprise, metered in message credits. Monthly billing: Basic is $25 a month for 500 credits a month; Pro is $329 a month for 10,000 credits a month; Enterprise is contact-for-pricing with custom credits. Both plans carry a credits dropdown that raises the allowance for a fixed add-on. On Basic, 1,000 credits is +$24, 2,500 is +$74, 5,000 is +$154 and 7,500 is +$224 a month. On Pro the ladder runs from 15,000 credits at +$150 up to 50,000 at +$1,170 a month, in 5,000-credit steps. Annual billing is shown as two months free. Basic is $21 a month billed yearly for 6,000 credits a year (12,000 credits +$252, 30,000 +$756, 60,000 +$1,560, 90,000 +$2,268), and Pro $277 a month billed yearly for 120,000 credits a year (180,000 +$1,512, rising to 600,000 at +$11,796). Seats and numbers are priced apart from the plan: the first seat is free and each additional seat is $10.00 a month or $100.00 a year; the first number is free and each additional number is $5.00 a month or $50.00 a year. The page defines the meter itself: SMS is 1 credit per 160 characters, MMS is 2 credits, calling is 1 credit a minute and call forwarding is 2 credits a minute. A 14-day free trial runs, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered, refunded less the message credits used. The page no longer publishes a per-credit overage rate, nor terms for taxes, carrier fees or country availability, so we quote none.
tools.honest_knock: Two things changed here and both cost money. First, calling now runs on the same meter as texting — 1 credit a minute, 2 a minute when forwarding — so voice minutes eat the allowance you budgeted for messages. Second, the plan ladder is a canyon: $25 to $329 a month with nothing between them, and the credits dropdown raises your allowance without adding a single seat. Size the credits, not the headcount. An MMS is 2 credits, so one picture message to 1,000 contacts is 2,000 credits — four times the entire monthly allowance on Basic. Seats and numbers bill on top of every plan beyond the first of each: a five-person team on one number is $40 a month over the sticker, and the annual headline of $21 and $277 is a per-month display of a bill charged yearly. Note what the page has stopped saying since our previous check: there is no published per-credit overage rate anymore, so what happens when you run out mid-cycle is not stated where you buy — ask before you commit. And US business texting carries a regulatory layer of its own: 10DLC registration and carrier surcharges bill separately from anything quoted here, and opt-in and opt-out handling stays your legal responsibility — the platform enables compliance, it does not absolve you.
tools.best_for: sales and service teams that want two-way texting and calling in one CRM-linked inbox, and can estimate their monthly credit burn — messages plus call minutes — before they sign
tools.skip_if: your audience doesn't respond to SMS, or your volume is low enough that the fixed 10DLC overhead outweighs the sending. Also skip it if you need a lot of seats cheaply. And skip it if your real usage lands in the gap between the $25 and $329 plans, since the only bridge on offer is a bigger credit bundle on the small plan
compare_with: the business-SMS peer group — compare credits-per-dollar AND what the meter counts, now that call minutes draw on the same balance; the sticker rows look more alike than the invoices

tools.name: SaneBox
tools.what_it_does: Email triage that moves low-priority mail out of the inbox and works with any provider. From $4.54/month for one account on a two-year commitment — $9.49 month to month — up to $22.04 for four accounts with every feature. The honest catch: you are paying monthly to filter mail that modern email clients increasingly sort for free.
tools.pricing: (read in a live browser on their own pricing page, 18 Aug 2026 — the figures are rendered client-side, so a plain fetch shows nothing) Three plans, and the advertised price is the two-year rate. Snack $4.54/mo billed $109 every 2 years, $5.42/mo billed $65 annually, or $9.49 month to month: 1 email account and 2 of the Sane features. Lunch $7.46 / $9.08 ($109 a year) / $15.99: 2 accounts and 6 features. Dinner $22.04 / $26.58 ($319 a year) / $42.99: 4 accounts and every feature, plus phone support. The free trial is 7 days with all features on up to 4 accounts. Education, non-profit and government get another 25% off on request during the trial.
tools.honest_knock: It works with any email provider, which is a genuine advantage over the built-in tools in Gmail and Outlook. But you are paying monthly to filter mail that modern clients increasingly sort for free. The value is real only if your inbox is genuinely overwhelming and native filters are not cutting it. Price it on the plan you would actually keep: the headline rate is a two-year commitment, and month to month the same Snack plan is $9.49 rather than $4.54.
tools.best_for: heavy-email professionals drowning in a cluttered inbox who want AI triage that works across any mail client
tools.skip_if: your inbox is manageable or your mail client's built-in filtering already handles it — you don't need to pay for this

tools.name: Scarcity.AI
tools.what_it_does: Three Shopify urgency apps — low stock counter, countdown timer and live visitors counter — that read real data but let you choose which true number the shopper sees.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com, across all three listings) These are three separate apps from one developer, each installed and billed on its own. The Low Stock Counter is $4.99 a month or $41.91 a year at a stated 30% saving, with a 7-day trial; its free tier is Development Stores, meaning development and partner stores only rather than a working free plan. The Visitors Counter is $1.99 a month or $16.71 a year, with a genuine free plan that carries the counter itself, customisation, product-level targeting and holiday presets — the $1.99 adds an upsell banner for your most-viewed product, on a 3-day trial. The Countdown Timer listing shows a free tier and no paid ladder. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, who also publish Blocky, TiXel and Way. Ratings at the time of writing: 4.7 from 84 reviews on the low stock counter, 4.8 from 36 on the visitors counter and 5.0 from 22 on the countdown timer.
tools.honest_knock:
All three read real data, which is worth saying before anything else — the low stock counter shows inventory levels and the visitors counter reads unique visitors, live traffic and product views. Nothing here invents a number.

But the visitors counter carries two settings that shape which true number a shopper sees. It can show the counter only after a set number of views, so a quiet product simply displays nothing rather than a small figure. And the time frame is yours to set, so 'twelve people viewed this' can mean twelve in five minutes or twelve since yesterday, presented identically. Neither setting fabricates anything; together they let you present a true number that a reasonable shopper would read as something else.

That distinction is where the legal line sits. The FTC treats false urgency and scarcity as deceptive practice under section 5 of the FTC Act, and the examples in its dark-patterns guidance are close to these mechanics: a low-stock claim when stock is plentiful, or a cart-activity figure well above the real one. The test is whether a reasonable consumer would be misled about a material fact. That test does not apply to the app; it applies to how you configure it, which means the compliance question lands on your desk rather than the developer's.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who genuinely run low stock or timed promotions and want to surface that on the product page — the low stock counter is tied to real inventory, which makes it the honest one of the three when your stock actually is low
tools.skip_if: your stock is not low and your sale does not end, because a claim a shopper would read as false is one the FTC treats as deceptive; or your brand sells on trust, where a blinking counter costs more in credibility than it returns

tools.name: Scrolly
tools.what_it_does: Free Shopify app from Effectify that adds a customizable floating back-to-top button and, optionally, infinite scroll on collection pages, with no code and no paid tier. The button is a safe convenience; the infinite scroll replaces the paginated collection URLs crawlers use, so it is a merchandising decision rather than a styling one.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on apps.shopify.com/custom-scroll-to-top) Free, and free is the only plan. The listing carries no paid tier, no usage meter and no Shopify-plan surcharge — the pricing block that most App Store listings use to sell an upgrade is simply absent here. The app has been on the App Store since March 2020 and carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, which is the store's own bar for performance, design and integration.
tools.honest_knock: The two features carry very different risk and the app presents them as one install. Infinite scroll replaces the paginated collection URLs a crawler uses to walk a large catalogue, pushes your footer permanently out of reach, and on some themes collides with the load-more or filtering logic already in the theme — that is a merchandising decision, not a styling toggle. The app also edits Online Store script tags and the theme, so it adds a third-party script to every page and an uninstall can leave remnants. And because there is no paid tier, there is no support contract behind it either: what you get is the vendor's goodwill, which the six-year run on the App Store suggests is real, but it is not something you can buy more of when you need it.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who want a free, one-click back-to-top button on long collection and product pages without touching theme code
tools.skip_if: you run a large catalogue that depends on paginated collection URLs being crawled, your theme already ships its own load-more or filtering behaviour, or you need conversion work rather than navigation polish — this only changes how the page scrolls

tools.name: Seamless.ai
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact database with AI list-building, plus an MCP server so Claude or ChatGPT can run the searching and enrichment. Nothing above the free plan (1 user, 50 credits) carries a published price; the only quantity their FAQ names is a Pro floor of 10,000 annual credits (read 7 Sep 2026). Independent tests put deliverability near 74%, and contracts auto-renew with 30-60 days' notice to cancel.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-07 on seamless.ai/pricing and seamless.ai/llms.txt) Still no published amount above the free plan, in a fourth reading. Free: 1 user, 50 credits. Pro: 'Per User', unlimited exports, annual credit packages, '1 Credits = Phone + Email', Contact sales. Enterprise: unlimited users, unlimited exports, custom packages, customer success and enterprise support, Contact sales. The only quantity they publish above Free is in the FAQ: Pro plans start at 10,000 annual credits, and custom accounts get a daily allotment at five or more licence tiers. The FAQ also says there are no setup fees, and that 'the prices shown on this page reflect this annual discount' — on a page that shows none. Four capabilities are marked Add-on in every column, Enterprise included: AI Assistant, Data Enrichment, Autopilot and Buyer Intent Data. Connect (email, calling and tasks) is flagged as included on all plans for a limited time. Third-party guides report an entry around $147 a month for roughly 250 credits and up to $150-500 per user a month; those are not Seamless's numbers, and 250 credits a month is 3,000 a year against a published Pro floor of 10,000.
tools.honest_knock: Data accuracy is the recurring complaint — independent tests put email deliverability around 74% (20–30% bounce) versus ZoomInfo's ~2–3%, so real cost per usable contact climbs. The buying experience is the other weak spot: sales-led, auto-renew with 30–60 day written cancellation, and reports of charges after a 'confirmed' cancellation.
tools.best_for: teams that want a huge real-time contact database and AI list-building for less than ZoomInfo, and can tolerate cleaning the data
tools.skip_if: data accuracy is your top priority (ZoomInfo bounces far less), or you want simple no-contract pricing — the bounce rates and auto-renewal bite
compare_with: the more accurate and the cheaper data tools

tools.name: Section Library
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that adds 200+ ready-made theme sections plus AI-generated custom ones (Gemini 3.1 Pro), all inside the native theme editor so layouts change without a developer. Free plan gives 8 credits a month; paid runs $9, $19 or $29 a month for 25, 55 or 90 credits. Live since October 2023 with a single App Store review.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/section-library) Free plan: 8 credits a month, access to the free sections only, basic AI generation. Starter $9 a month: 25 credits, all sections accessible, AI section generation, email support. Pro $19 a month: 55 credits, all sections, priority support. Business $29 a month: 90 credits, all sections, priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and the listing shows no free trial on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial. One thing the pricing table never states is what a credit actually buys. Whether one credit is one AI generation, one section added to a theme, or something else is defined nowhere on the listing — and the credit count is the only thing separating the four plans. The vendor's own site, sectionlibrary.com, publishes no prices at all, so the App Store listing we link to is the only ladder on record. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 10 October 2023. It carries a 5.0 rating from exactly one App Store review, left in October 2023 by a merchant who had the app installed for four minutes.
tools.honest_knock:
Almost three years on the App Store and one review. The app launched 10 October 2023 and, as of 19 August 2026, exactly one merchant has written about it: a five-star note from October 2023 by someone who had it installed for four minutes. That is not evidence of quality and not evidence of trouble — it is an absence of evidence, and on an app that writes sections into your live theme, that absence is the main thing to weigh. On the same listing page Shopify shows Section Store with 2,760 reviews, also free to install, which is what a track record looks like in this category.

Second, the credit is undefined. Every plan is priced in credits and nothing on the listing says what one buys, so you cannot price your own usage before you commit.

Third, the AI half of the product is Google's. Sections are generated by Gemini 3.1 Pro, so output quality and consistency shift when Google ships a new model, which is outside the vendor's hands as much as yours. The library half — the 200+ pre-built sections — is the part that depends on nobody else, and it is the part worth judging the app on.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who want ready-made theme sections and the occasional AI-generated layout inside the native theme editor, and who can live with an app that has almost no public track record
tools.skip_if: you are rebuilding a store you cannot afford to break and want a page builder with thousands of merchants behind it, or you need your monthly cost known in advance — the credit unit is never defined

tools.name: Securify
tools.what_it_does: Country blocker and fraud filter for Shopify: blocks countries, IP ranges, bots, VPNs and risky emails at checkout, and holds suspicious orders automatically. Free plan; paid $5.99 to $49 a month.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/easy-block-customer-ip-country) Free plan available with a free trial on the paid tiers. Paid runs Pro $5.99, Advanced $9.49 and Growth $49 a month. Rating 4.4 from 68 reviews, and it carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. The App Store lists it as “Country Blocker Fraud Securify” from siimple.ai.
tools.honest_knock: Blocking by country and IP is a blunt instrument and it cuts both ways: every rule that keeps out a fraudster also keeps out a customer travelling, using a corporate VPN, or living behind a carrier NAT. The app is honest enough to give you a live log of what it blocked, and that log is the part to actually read — a rule set nobody reviews quietly costs sales. Also worth separating in your head: blocking bots from your analytics is a reporting fix, while blocking fraud at checkout is a money fix, and the two need different rules.
tools.best_for: stores seeing real fraud or bot traffic that want country, IP, VPN and email-risk rules plus automatic holds on suspicious orders, and who will review the block log rather than set and forget
tools.skip_if: you are blocking on a hunch rather than on measured fraud — start by reading your order data, because a blocked legitimate customer never tells you they were blocked

tools.name: Seel
tools.what_it_does: Shopper-paid returns and shipping protection for Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce. Customers add Worry-Free Purchase at checkout and Seel pays the refund instead of you — free for the merchant.
tools.pricing: Three plans on seel.com/pricing, re-read 7 September 2026: Free at $0 per store per month (no monthly platform fee), Growth at $99 per store per month, Enterprise at custom pricing. Worry-Free Purchase (formerly Return Assurance), Worry-Free Delivery and Extended Warranty are listed as included on all three, so the returns-protection product stays shopper-paid: customers who add it pay roughly $2-$5, reported elsewhere as 3-5% of order value, set by Seel's algorithm. The plans differ on the AI agencies. Free is pay-as-you-go for one agency at $0.99 per resolved ticket, $0.40 per listing, 3% of attributed GMV, $5 per store review and $29 per storefront regulation scan. Growth covers all five with capped usage — up to 100 resolved tickets, 100 listings, $500 attributed GMV, one Voice of Customer report (sentiment across your brand and three competitors), up to four 5-star reviews and one storefront regulation scan — and order tracking for 2,000 orders instead of 250; overage bills at the Free rate card. Their FAQ states the subscription is fixed per store per month and that attributed GMV does not feed it. Enterprise usage scope and commercial terms sit in the merchant agreement. Insurance benefits are provided by Seel Insurance Inc. or Arch Specialty Insurance Company, with availability varying by jurisdiction and state (re-verified 2026-09-07; on 2026-08-02 the page showed no plans or rate card).
tools.honest_knock: Two things to weigh, and neither is the price you pay — because you do not pay one. First, you cannot set the fee. Seel's algorithm prices it, so if it lands too high for your niche and shoppers stop opting in, your only lever is switching the feature off entirely. Second, the charge appears on your checkout, not Seel's: shopper-side complaints filed with the BBB describe the fee arriving in the cart with the opt-out easy to miss, and that lands on your brand. Test it as a customer before you enable it. Also check the platform list — Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce only, with no WooCommerce, Wix or custom storefront support.
tools.best_for: stores selling final-sale, high-consideration or hard-to-size products, where return anxiety is the thing killing the order — merchants report conversion lifting around 5% and shoppers taking the option roughly 24% of the time
tools.skip_if: your margin already absorbs returns comfortably, or you need control over what appears on your own checkout — the fee is set by Seel and shown to your customer either way
compare_with: the other shopper-paid model, but with merchant-side workflow control Seel does not offer

tools.name: Selixer
tools.what_it_does: Shopify profit dashboard that nets ad spend, COGS, returns and fees out of revenue and reports what you keep per product, campaign and customer, built for fashion and apparel brands. Essance $149 a month, Catalyst $299 and Aether $399, each with a 14-day trial; the profit waterfall and campaign ROAS start at $299.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/selixer) Three tiers, no free plan, each with a 14-day free trial. Essance $149 a month: one user seat, one connected ad account, a 30-day data lookback window, basic high-level profit metrics, an inventory health score teaser and total dead stock value. Catalyst $299 a month: three seats, two ad accounts, unlimited historical data, the full profit waterfall and product P&L, campaign POAS and ROAS tracking, smart reorder alerts and stockout risk, AI anomaly detection and insights, and profit-leak and low-margin SKU detection. Aether $399 a month: five seats, three ad accounts, an AI co-pilot for simulations and what-ifs, advanced demand forecasting, RFM customer scoring and cohorts, multi-touch ad attribution models, discount and transaction-fee impact, and full benchmarks and analytics. The listing publishes no annual rate, so all three are monthly. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Akaame Export Private Limited; the app launched 19 May 2026 and carries a single App Store review.
tools.honest_knock:
Read the feature lists rather than the prices and the entry tier stops looking like an entry tier. Essance at $149 a month gives you one ad account, a 30-day lookback and, in Shopify's own wording, an inventory health score teaser. The profit waterfall, the product P&L and campaign POAS and ROAS tracking, which is the reason anyone installs a profit dashboard, all start on Catalyst at $299. So the real price of what this app is sold on is double the headline.

The ad-account caps decide the tier as much as the features do: one, two, then three. If you run Meta, Google and TikTok you are on the $399 plan for connectivity alone, whatever your revenue looks like.

And this is a new app. It launched on 19 May 2026 and has one public review. There is nothing bad in the record, but there is barely any record, and this is a tool you hand your cost prices, your ad spend and your margins to. Use the 14-day trial to reconcile its numbers against a month you have already closed in your own books before you trust a dashboard you cannot yet audit.
tools.best_for: Shopify fashion and apparel brands with real ad spend that want profit per SKU and per campaign in one place, and can carry the $299 tier where those features actually live
tools.skip_if: your store is small enough that a spreadsheet still works, you need more than three connected ad accounts without paying $399, or you want a longer public track record than an app launched in May 2026 with one review

tools.name: Seller Investigators
tools.what_it_does: Amazon FBA reimbursement recovery on contingency: a free 48-hour audit, then a 25% commission charged only after Amazon deposits recovered funds. No subscription. Ask which cases Amazon would have settled automatically before you sign.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice. Once on the home page — “only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you” — and again in the FAQ: “no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”. The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover fall into five groups: inbound shipments (cancelled shipments, receiving discrepancies, carrier damage), items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, customer returns (refunds not returned within 60 days, overpayments, the wrong item returned, chargebacks), and overages and discrepancies (removal orders, incorrect weights or dimensions, overcharged orders); unfair reimbursement appears as a sub-case under both the lost and the damaged group. Re-read 29 August 2026: the 25% figure, the free 48-hour audit and the absence of any subscription are unchanged.
tools.honest_knock: Contingency pricing is the honest kind — you pay only out of money that arrived — but 25% of a recovery is not the same as 25% of a profit, and there is one question that decides whether this is worth it for you. Amazon reimburses some categories automatically, and its policies on that have changed more than once. So ask, before you sign: which of these cases would Amazon have settled on its own within the claim window, and what exactly is the 25% charged on — the gross amount recovered, or what is left after Amazon's own fees? A free audit that finds $20,000 sounds decisive until you learn how much of it was already on its way. Ask for the split, in writing, before the audit turns into an engagement.
tools.best_for: established FBA sellers with enough inventory movement that discrepancies add up and nobody in-house has time to file case-by-case claims — the contingency model means an audit costs you nothing but the access you grant
tools.skip_if: you are a small seller whose monthly discrepancies are modest, where 25% of a small recovery buys less than the hour it takes to file yourself. Also skip it until you have asked what share of the claim Amazon would have paid automatically, because that is the part of the bill that buys you nothing
compare_with: the comparison worth making, and the two are related — the Seller Investigators partner link runs through Carbon6's own domain. Carbon6 sells a suite of Amazon seller tools on published monthly subscriptions; this is a single contingency service with no subscription at all. If reimbursement recovery is the only job you need done, paying a percentage of what comes back is the cheaper shape; if you want inventory and profit tooling alongside it, the suite is the better buy

tools.name: Seller Snap
tools.what_it_does: AI repricer and seller-analytics platform for Amazon and Walmart — what the vendor calls game-theory repricing, aimed at Buy Box share rather than racing to the bottom, plus min/max profit calculation, 80+ analytics data points and imports from tools like InventoryLab and SkuVault. Starter is $100/month billed annually (annual only); month-to-month starts at $250. 15-day free trial, no credit card. A July 2026 interface release adds live Buy Box insight with SKU-level filters, multi-store management from one screen including bulk cost updates, repricing from mobile, historical inventory-value tracking, saved views, customizable columns and a dark mode.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column; every figure below was read again on that date and none of them had moved since 24 Jul 2026) There are four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features. All four list the same six feature groups: Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity and integrations. The four tiers are set out above; what the page does not tell you is what each step actually buys. Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed — while the seller ID and user counts never move at all. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The revenue ceilings themselves are printed without any period attached; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000 and $30,000 a month. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself. One thing on the page has changed and it is not a price: a banner above the plans offers 'your first month for only $1 when you subscribe before 2026', a deadline that had already passed when we read it on 26 Aug 2026, so treat it as decoration rather than an offer until support confirms it.
tools.honest_knock: Read the caps before you read the prices, because the caps are what you are actually buying. Two of them deserve scrutiny. First, the revenue limits — $15,000 on Starter, $30,000 on Accelerator — are printed with no period attached on the pricing page. We asked, and Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month. That is the reading that costs you money. $15,000 a month is roughly $500 a day, so a seller who already clears that sits above Starter before signing up — and $30,000 a month puts the ceiling of Accelerator within reach of a shop doing $1,000 a day. Measure your own monthly revenue against the tier first, because the page will not do it for you. Second, the SKU limit sits at 1,000 on both of the lower tiers, so catalog growth alone — not revenue, not users — can push you up a step. And the steps are steep: leaving Accelerator for Standard means $425/month annually or $500 monthly, roughly 2.4 times what you were paying, for capacity rather than for any feature you did not already have. The cheapest door is also not quite $100: Starter is annual-billing only, so the lowest month-to-month entry into the product is $250/month. Finally, 'Starting at' appears above every monthly price on the vendor's own page — treat all of these as floors and confirm your own quote. Worth checking first, though: Amazon already includes a rule-based repricer. Automate Pricing comes with the Professional selling plan and supports rules such as Competitive Featured Offer and Competitive Lowest Price with a seller-set price floor, so if your problem is simply matching the competitive price without going below cost, test that before paying for anything. And note what sets your tier: their FAQ says pricing follows the total number of SKUs in your Seller Central account, not the active ones, so a dormant catalogue costs you money. One more thing to time correctly. In September 2026 Seller Snap began telling affiliates that its most advanced repricing engine yet had just launched, built on the premise that Amazon no longer awards one Buy Box but thousands of local ones, buyer by buyer and city by city. Their own repricing-engine page, read on 3 Sep 2026, is more careful than that: it says a redesigned app today, a new repricing engine coming soon, and it offers a waitlist and an early-access form rather than the engine itself. What has actually shipped is the redesigned app — a live Buy Box filter at SKU level, one preset across every store, repricing from a phone, and historical inventory value tracked over time. The local Buy Box logic sits behind that, still ahead of the product rather than in it. So judge the subscription on what the app does today; if the local pricing engine is the reason you are signing up, ask support for a ship date in writing before you pay for a year of it.
tools.best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers past the hobby stage who compete for the Buy Box on a catalog of up to a few thousand SKUs, and want AI repricing and deep seller analytics in one place. The 15-day no-card trial makes it cheap to test against your own listings before any commitment
tools.skip_if: you sell mainly outside Amazon and Walmart, since those are the only two marketplaces supported. Also skip it if your catalog and revenue are small enough that a rules-based repricer at a fraction of the price does the same job, or if what you actually need is multi-channel competitor price monitoring rather than marketplace Buy Box repricing
compare_with: the other AI-first Amazon repricer we cover: Feedvisor's real platform (Feedvisor360, with ad optimization and dedicated analysts) starts around $1,500/mo, while Seller Snap sits in the $175-$425/mo band on published, self-serve pricing with a no-card trial. If you need multi-channel price monitoring rather than marketplace repricing, compare Pricefy instead — and verify every current price list yourself before you sign.

tools.name: Sellfy
tools.what_it_does: No-code store builder for creators to sell digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand merch — with zero transaction fees and built-in social-media selling.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-07) Starter is $29/mo billed monthly or $22/mo billed yearly, for up to $10k of sales a year; Business $79 or $59, up to $50k; Premium $159 or $119, up to $200k; above that Sellfy quotes you. Yearly billing saves 25%, there is a 14-day trial, a 30-day money-back guarantee and no free tier. 0% transaction fees on every plan, though PayPal or Stripe still take roughly 2.9% + 30c per transaction. The revenue limits are soft: Sellfy's own pricing.md says the store is never suspended and you are never forced to upgrade, while the page's FAQ says you are expected to upgrade and that Sellfy may instead charge a 2% overage fee on revenue above the limit. Read in US dollars from a Netherlands connection.
tools.honest_knock: The honest mechanic is the revenue ladder: plans cap by your ANNUAL SALES, so success moves you up. But the caps are soft - Sellfy's FAQ says it may charge 2% on revenue above your limit rather than forcing an upgrade, so ask whether that applies to you before jumping a tier. The 0% transaction fee is genuinely rare and beats percentage-taking platforms at volume; below a few hundred in monthly sales the flat subscription is the tax instead, and your processor still takes about 2.9% + 30c regardless.
tools.best_for: creators selling digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand who want a simple store with zero platform commission
tools.skip_if: you sell occasionally (percentage-fee platforms like Gumroad cost nothing idle), or you need a full e-commerce ecosystem (Shopify territory)
compare_with: the creator-store trio — Gumroad takes ~10% but no subscription; the crossover math is simple: past ~$300-400/mo in sales, Sellfy's flat fee wins

tools.name: Sendcloud
tools.what_it_does: European e-commerce shipping platform: connect 160+ carriers, print labels in batches, show delivery options at checkout, send branded tracking (email, WhatsApp, SMS) and run a self-service returns portal — with rules-based shipping automation. Available to online retailers in 8 countries (Netherlands, Belgium, UK, France, Germany, Austria, Italy, Spain). Free plan available.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Free plan €0/mo: up to 20 parcels a month, no courier contract, no subscription, €0.50 a label beyond that. Paid tiers at the monthly rate: Lite €28/mo + €0.10 per label, Growth €87/mo + €0.09, Premium €175/mo + €0.08, Pro €639/mo + €0.07. Every tier also has a MONTHLY label cap (Lite 400, Growth 1,000, Premium 10,000, Pro 30,000) and past it each extra label costs €0.15 on top of the plan rate. Users: 1 free, 3 Lite, 5 Growth, 10 Premium, unlimited Pro. 14-day free trial, no card. The page advertises a yearly option at -20% but the discounted figures are not in the served HTML. You can only ship FROM eight European countries. (2026)
tools.honest_knock: The pricing has layers — a per-label fee on top of the subscription, plus carrier surcharges that can land on invoices weeks later. It's built out-of-the-box, so deep customisation is limited, there's no inventory management (ShipStation has it), and high-volume shippers (€12k+/mo) plus pickup-reliability complaints suggest it's happiest with small-to-mid EU stores.
tools.best_for: European e-commerce stores that want easy multi-carrier shipping (DHL, PostNL, Colissimo, GLS, DPD), branded tracking and a returns portal live in under 30 minutes
tools.skip_if: you ship mainly in the US, need inventory management and complex fulfilment, or you're a very high-volume shipper wanting deep customisation — ShipStation fits that better
compare_with: the US-focused fulfilment platform with inventory management

tools.name: Sentaro
tools.what_it_does: Email threat detection that flags phishing, risky and malicious messages right in your inbox. Surfaces the dangerous emails that look perfectly normal — before anyone clicks.
tools.pricing: (read 5 September 2026 on sentaro.com, pricing section) Two plans. Professional is $6 per user per month billed monthly, or $5.50 per user per month billed annually — the toggle labels that discount as -8%. A currency switcher sits beside the billing toggle and offers the identical numerals in euros: €6 and €5,50. That is not a conversion, so a European buyer pays roughly 15% more for the same seat. Enterprise publishes no figure at all, only 'Custom pricing'. What Professional includes: real-time email risk analysis, Threat / Suspicious / Safe labels in the inbox, phishing, spoofing and impersonation detection, working directly inside Gmail and Outlook, and organization-wide deployment. What sits above it on Enterprise: SSO / SCIM, advanced admin controls, API access, custom policies, dedicated support, and compliance and audit support. Sentaro connects to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 through the API rather than by changing MX records. History: until August 2026 no price was published at all.
tools.honest_knock: The category claim (AI catches what filters miss) is plausible — Microsoft/Google native filtering misses sophisticated BEC — but any vendor's accuracy percentage is measured on their own test set, not your mail flow. The honest procurement move: run their trial alongside your current filtering, count real catches and false positives for two weeks, and price per mailbox against the incumbents with that data in hand.
tools.best_for: SMBs on Google Workspace/M365 that want an extra AI layer against phishing and BEC without infrastructure changes
tools.skip_if: you already run a mature email-security stack (Ironscales/Abnormal-class), or nobody internally will review the flagged-mail queue
compare_with: the established API-based email-security players — compare detected-in-YOUR-inbox counts from parallel trials, not brochure accuracy

tools.name: SEO Space
tools.what_it_does: SEO tool built exclusively for Squarespace, delivered as a Chrome extension paired with a web dashboard. The extension runs inside the Squarespace editor and on live pages, scoring each page and saying in plain language what to change and where the setting lives; the dashboard adds site-wide audits, keyword rank tracking, backlink and competitor data, local SEO tools and scheduled white-label PDF client reports. Pricing is keyed to the number of websites rather than seats, which is why it suits freelancers and studios managing client sites. There is a genuinely usable free plan — a scan of up to 50 pages without a card; paid pricing is keyed to the number of websites, with the most-popular position (5 sites) at $33.33/month billed annually, read 17 Aug 2026.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-17, re-verified on their own homepage pricing block) One figure is published: Pro, the default position on their website slider, is $33.33/mo billed annually, labelled MOST POPULAR and covering 5 websites. The slider runs 1, 3, 5, 10, 20 and unlimited websites, but the amounts for the other positions are rendered per selection and do not appear in the delivered page, so we do not quote them. Yearly billing is sold as "4 Months Free", which means the equivalent monthly rate is higher than the headline — the page does not print it next to the plan. Pricing is by number of websites, not per seat, and their own line "All Plans Include Every Feature" means a higher position buys site slots rather than extra capability. Free entry is real: a scan of up to 50 pages with no card, plus a 7-day trial of Pro, also with no card. An earlier reading (21 Jul 2026) recorded named Starter/Pro/Expert tiers at 1/3/5 sites with their own amounts; the page no longer shows that structure, so those figures have been withdrawn rather than carried forward.
tools.honest_knock: Squarespace has been quietly absorbing the job this tool was invented for. The platform's own SEO panel, checklist, sitemaps and structured data are free, and its AI-suggested titles, descriptions and alt text are available on Fluid Engine 7.1. On 7 July 2026 it announced AI Visibility, brand tracking across AI search, included on 7.1 plans with no extra subscription. It is metered against plan-varying AI credits rather than unlimited. If you own a single Squarespace site, a large share of what you would pay for here is now a friendlier wrapper around something the platform already does. The tool earns its keep on volume and client work, not on one site. Note too what their own pricing block says out loud — 'All Plans Include Every Feature' — so moving up the ladder buys site slots, not a better tool.
tools.best_for: Squarespace freelancers and studios billing for several client sites. Pricing by number of websites rather than per seat, multi-site dashboards and white-label PDF reports are things the big per-seat SEO suites never bothered to build for Squarespace. And the extension tells you where the setting actually lives in the editor
tools.skip_if: you run a single Squarespace 7.1 site and have no clients. Squarespace's own free SEO panel, AI-generated descriptions and AI Visibility now cover much of what you would be paying for. And the free plan here will tell you whether the paid layer adds anything for your site before you spend
compare_with: SEO Space wins on translation, not data: it knows where each setting lives in the Squarespace editor, while Ahrefs and Semrush have vastly deeper indexes and cost several times more. Pick by whether your bottleneck is knowing what to fix or knowing where to fix it

tools.name: SEOmatic
tools.what_it_does: SEO suite for Shopify from Aheadworks: unlimited image compression with alt text, AI-generated meta titles and descriptions, SEO audit, schema markup and both XML and HTML sitemaps. Free up to 10 products; the paid ladder is priced purely by catalogue size — $15, $25 or $40 a month for 500, 2,000 or 5,000 products, with a 14-day trial. Live since 2015, rated 4.4 over 114 App Store reviews.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/minifier and on seomatic.io) Four tiers, and the only thing that changes between the three paid ones is how many products they cover. Free: 10 products, 50 image optimisations, AI SEO audit, auto-pilot AI meta title and description, schema markup, HTML sitemap. Starter $15 a month or $144 a year (save 20%): 500 products, unlimited image optimiser, broken links, XML and HTML sitemaps, 14-day free trial. Basic $25 a month or $240 a year: 2,000 products. Advanced $40 a month or $384 a year: 5,000 products. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page at seomatic.io publishes the identical ladder, which is worth noting because the two often disagree — here they do not. There is no plan above 5,000 products on either page, so a larger catalogue has no listed price at all. Developer Aheadworks, 12495 S Parkland Bay Trail, Parkland, Florida; the app launched 18 August 2015 and carries a 4.4 average over 114 App Store reviews, and it holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge.
tools.honest_knock:
This app is eleven years old and has 114 reviews. That is the number to sit with. On the same listing page Shopify shows three direct rivals. SEOLab is 5.0 over 2,368 reviews and free, Tiny SEO 5.0 over 2,261 and free to install, and Smart SEO 4.9 over 851 with a free plan. All three carry between seven and twenty times the review volume, all are rated higher, and none of them charges by product count. SEOmatic's 4.4 is a real rating from real merchants, but it is the weakest track record on its own page.

The distribution behind that 4.4 matters too: 81% five stars against 8% one star, with almost nothing in the middle. The most substantial recent review, from March 2025, is a merchant of six months saying it appears to work on images and nothing else, and that support is difficult and slow. The vendor replied that the reports do exist, and asked them to get in touch. An older one-star from a merchant who lasted seventeen minutes reads 'Paid for it to tell me 0% savings'. Both are about the same thing — what the app actually did after installation was not visible to the person paying for it.

And the product cap is a hard ceiling, not a soft one. There is no tier above 5,000 products on the listing or on seomatic.io, so if your catalogue is larger than that, the published ladder simply does not have a row for you.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores under 5,000 products that want image compression, alt text, auto-generated meta tags, schema and sitemaps from one app on a flat monthly fee, and would rather not pay per AI credit
tools.skip_if: your catalogue is larger than 5,000 products, or you want the safest bet in a category where three rivals on the same page carry 850 to 2,400 reviews at 4.9-5.0 against this app's 4.4 over 114

tools.name: Serpstat
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one SEO platform — keyword research, competitor analysis, rank tracking, site audit and backlink data — from $50/month on annual billing ($69 month-to-month), with a 7-day trial that takes a card and auto-renews.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four plans, and the page opens on the annual view — so the first number you see is not the month-to-month price. Individual $69/month, or $50 on annual billing. Team $129, or $100 annually. Team x2 $209, or $169. Agency $499, or $410. There is a hidden middle step: two dropdowns inside the Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000) move Team to $169/month monthly or $135 annually, so Team is really three price points. Seats are capped rather than sold: Individual is single-user, Team 3, Team x2 6, Agency 30, and no per-seat price is published anywhere — a fourth user means the next tier. The limits matter more than the prices: 100 searches a day on Individual (500 / 1,000 / 5,000 above it), export rows 50,000 a month, and no API at all on the entry plan. The 7-day trial takes a card, charges $1 to verify, turns on auto-renewal and bills the plan after seven days unless you cancel. Re-verified 2026-08-26: the four annual prices are unchanged, and the page now heads the table with 'save up to 27% with annual discount' and prints the saving per plan — $228, $348, $484 and $1,068 a year. That is the arithmetic that turns $50, $100, $169 and $410 back into $69, $129, $209 and $499, which matters because the monthly column itself is not in the page's HTML at all; only the annual one renders. The comparison table still carries the two-value Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000), so the hidden middle step is still there, but its price is printed nowhere on the page today. Three limits worth reading before anyone picks Individual: Site Audit does no JavaScript rendering on that plan, it scans at most 5,000 pages, and its data retention figure is 2 where Team gets 10 and Agency 100.
tools.honest_knock: The thing you are actually buying is data coverage, and that is the one thing you cannot verify — Serpstat's own published figures do not agree with each other. Re-read on 24 July 2026, their homepage says 529 billion backlinks, their data hub says 1.1 trillion, and their backlinks page says 1.7 trillion in the prose while its own spec block on that same page says 1.1 trillion. The keyword count reads 8.62 billion on one page and 7.46 billion on another. That is not evidence the data is thin; it is evidence that these numbers cannot serve as a basis for your decision. Judge it on your own searches during the trial instead. Two other things to weigh.
