Backlink reports are capped at 10,000 results per report on Team, Team x2 and Agency alike, so paying from $129 to $499 buys more of everything except a deeper backlink report. And 'maximum pages to scan' in a single crawl (5,000 / 25,000 / 50,000) is a far smaller number than the monthly 'pages to audit' allowance it sits next to.
tools.best_for: solo SEOs and small in-house teams who want the whole workflow — keywords, rankings, audit, competitors — under one subscription at roughly a third of what the incumbents charge, and who will judge the data on their own market during the trial
tools.skip_if: your work depends on deep backlink analysis, since the 10,000 results per report ceiling does not move no matter which tier you buy; or you need more than three seats, because seats are not sold separately and the next tier roughly doubles the bill
compare_with: the closest self-serve rival on price and scope — both sell the full workflow well under what the incumbents charge, so the decision comes down to which one's data holds up on your own market and how each counts its limits. Compare the units carefully: a daily allowance and a monthly stock are not the same number, and both vendors mix them. Verify both current price lists yourself.

tools.name: ServiceM8
tools.what_it_does: Job management for trades and service contractors: scheduling, quotes, job cards and invoicing.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit, USD) Priced by jobs per month, with unlimited users on every paid tier. Free $0: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, 10 AI uses a day. Starter $29: unlimited users, 50 jobs, unlimited AI uses a day. Growing $79: 150 jobs. Premium $149: 500 jobs. Premium Plus $349: 1,500+ jobs. A 14-day free trial is offered. The plan amounts sit in the page markup rather than in its flat text, so a plain text scrape of this page returns no prices.
tools.honest_knock: Unlimited users on every paid tier is genuinely unusual in this category and worth saying first: put your whole crew in without the bill moving. The meter is jobs instead, and jobs are the thing you least control. Fifty a month on Starter is roughly two a working day, which a two-van operation passes in a busy month — and the next step is not a small one, it is $29 to $79. Count your jobs in your best month rather than your average, because that is the month that will bump you, and a seasonal trade will spend part of the year paying for a tier it does not need. The free tier at 30 jobs and one user is a real trial, not a plan.
tools.best_for: trades and service businesses with a crew, where per-user pricing elsewhere punishes you for having enough people — this is one of the few tools in the category that does not
tools.skip_if: you are a sole trader doing a handful of jobs a month — the free tier covers that, and at low job volume the paid tiers are buying capacity rather than features
compare_with: the direct job-management peers — compare on jobs included versus users included, because that is the axis these differ on

tools.name: Shiftie
tools.what_it_does: Rota building, clock-ins, leave and shift swaps for shift-based businesses. Charged per active employee — £2.75 a month for the first 30 and £1.50 for each one above that, with no minimum and a custom quote past 200 staff. Not an HR or payroll platform, so those stay separate purchases.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-05) £2.75 per active employee per month for the first 30, then £1.50 for each employee above 30 — the reduced rate is marginal, not retroactive. Measured on the vendor's own pricing slider: 1 employee £2.75, 5 £13.75, 10 £27.50, 15 £41.25, 30 £82.50, 31 £84.00, 50 £112.50, 100 £187.50, 150 £262.50, 199 £336.00. At 200 employees the slider stops quoting and switches to Custom Pricing. There is no minimum and no entry-plan floor: one employee costs £2.75. Monthly billing only — no annual option is offered anywhere on the page. Billing is in arrears: at the start of each month you are charged for users marked active during the previous month. 28-day free trial, no card details required, and 7-day UK-based support included. Note the domain move: shiftie.co.uk now redirects to shiftie.co.
tools.honest_knock: It's focused, affordable rota software — which means it does scheduling, clock-ins, leave and swaps well, but it isn't a full HR or payroll platform, so a growing business will still bolt on payroll and HR tools around it. Pricing is genuinely low, but the per-active-employee model means a large seasonal team in a busy month costs more than the headline suggests. For shift-based scheduling specifically, it's a clean, cheap fit.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses (hospitality, retail, leisure) that want quick rota building, clock-ins and leave management without spreadsheet pain
tools.skip_if: you need full HR, payroll and performance management in one system, or your team doesn't work in shifts at all
compare_with: comparable scheduling platforms — Shiftie tends to undercut on price; compare on payroll/HR features you actually need

tools.name: Shipdock
tools.what_it_does: Shopify pickup points, multi-carrier label printing and cash-on-delivery tracking, strongest on the Central European carrier networks.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/packeta) Three tiers, no free plan, and the entry tier names its own limitation. Lite is $9.99 a month or $107.88 a year and is labelled 'only CSV': pickup point and home delivery, an email reminder, the pickup-point widget on the thank-you and order-status pages, unlimited carriers across more than twenty, and an order export to custom CSV. Basic is $14.99 or $161.89 a year and is the first tier that prints shipping labels, adding parcels created automatically after fulfilment and cash-on-delivery payment tracking. Shopify Plus is $24.99 or $269.89 and moves the pickup-point widget into the checkout itself rather than the pages after it. Annual billing saves a stated 10% on each. Trials are five days on Lite and Basic and ten on Plus. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer happyapps.cz; the app sits in Shopify's delivery and pickup category and had 42 reviews at a 5.0 rating at the time of writing, 41 of them five-star.
tools.honest_knock:
Read the carrier list against your own country before anything else. The listing slug is 'packeta', the developer is happyapps.cz, and cash-on-delivery tracking is a headline feature — all three point at Central and Eastern Europe, where Packeta and Zásilkovna are everyday carriers and COD is a normal way to pay. More than twenty carriers are supported, but a US or UK merchant should confirm theirs is among them before the five-day trial starts.

The second thing is the trial length against the job. Five days on Lite and Basic is short for a shipping integration, because the test that matters is a real order going out with a real label to a real address. Install it on a day you are actually shipping, not on a quiet Sunday.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants shipping in Central and Eastern Europe who want pickup points, multi-carrier label printing and cash-on-delivery tracking in one app rather than one integration per carrier — and who are on Shopify Plus, where the pickup-point picker sits inside checkout instead of after it
tools.skip_if: your carriers are not in its list, which is the first thing to check, since the app's centre of gravity is Packeta and the Central European networks; or you need a label only occasionally, when a CSV export and your carrier's portal cost nothing

tools.name: Shippo
tools.what_it_does: Multi-carrier shipping software for e-commerce. Compare rates, print discounted labels and automate tracking across carriers — shipping that scales with your store.
tools.pricing: Read on their own pricing page, 6 September 2026. Starter is free: up to 30 labels a month, discounted USPS, UPS, FedEx and DHL Express rates, 1 user login, and 5¢ per label if you connect your own carrier account. Pro is banded by monthly label volume, priced monthly or annually: 1-200 labels $19/mo or $205/yr; 201-500 $29 or $313; 501-1,000 $54 or $583; 1,001-2,500 $79 or $853; 2,501-5,000 $139 or $1,501; 5,001-10,000 $199 or $2,149. Annual billing saves about 10% at every band. Labels beyond 10,000 a month cost $0.08 each. Pro makes your own carrier accounts free and adds branded tracking, chat and phone support. Premier is contact-us: unlimited shipments, 15+ logins, a dedicated account manager. Non-US address validation is metered separately at 9¢, 8¢ and 6¢ per validation on Starter, Pro and Premier. API calls not tied to a Shippo label, and the Estimate API, bill at API Starter rates.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is honest but layered. The free tier stops at 30 labels a month, and its 5¢ per label on your own carrier accounts quietly adds up. Pro looks like a flat $17 a month until you read the comparison table: it covers up to 10,000 shipments and then bills $0.08 for every label beyond that, so a good sales month adds a variable line to a subscription that reads as fixed. Address validation outside the US is metered too, at 9¢, 8¢ or 6¢ depending on plan. The real money is elsewhere anyway — in the carrier rate discounts, which vary by lane and weight. Run your five most common shipments through it against your current rates; that comparison decides, not the subscription price.
tools.best_for: e-commerce sellers shipping across multiple carriers who want rate comparison, label printing and tracking in one place with genuine rate discounts
tools.skip_if: you ship a handful of packages monthly through one carrier (their native tools are fine), or you're big enough for direct carrier contracts to beat aggregated rates
compare_with: the direct shipping-software peers — compare discounted rates on your actual lanes and the workflow features your volume needs

tools.name: Shoeboxed
tools.what_it_does: Turn paper and digital receipts into organized, IRS-ready expense data with OCR plus human verification — syncs with QuickBooks and Xero.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Four plans, each quoted both yearly and monthly: Starter $97/yr or $9/mo (30 digital scans/mo, 20 paper scans/yr, 1 Magic Envelope/yr, 1 user, 3 years of scan storage); Pro $297/yr or $29/mo (200 digital scans/mo, 20 paper scans/mo, 1 Magic Envelope per quarter, Gmail receipt sync, QuickBooks Online/Xero, 3 users); Plus $797/yr or $79/mo (750 digital scans/mo, 50 paper scans/mo, 1 Magic Envelope/mo, 10 users); Paper Plus $1,997/yr or $179/mo (500 digital scans/mo, 200 paper scans/mo, 2 envelopes/mo). Overages by tier: $0.30/$0.15/$0.10 per digital scan, $2.00 or $1.50 per paper scan, $9 per extra envelope. Unlimited mileage tracking on every plan. A 30-day money-back guarantee rather than a free trial — the card is charged at signup, and the vendor asks you not to claim the refund once a Magic Envelope has shipped.
tools.honest_knock: Its unique trick is the Magic Envelope, where you literally mail a stuffed envelope of paper receipts and humans digitize them. That trick is also the meter to watch: envelope frequency defines the tiers, and heavy paper businesses land in the $179/mo bracket quickly. If your receipts are already digital, cheaper scan-only apps exist; Shoeboxed earns its price precisely when physical paper is the problem.
tools.best_for: businesses drowning in PAPER receipts — trades, field crews, owners with shoeboxes of history — who want them humanly digitized, verified and IRS-ready
tools.skip_if: your receipts are mostly digital already (lighter OCR apps cost less), or your accountant's tooling ingests receipts natively
compare_with: app-first expense tools — Shoeboxed's differentiator is the mail-in human digitization; if you don't need that, compare on OCR quality alone

tools.name: Shorby
tools.what_it_does: Link-in-bio pages and short links, with messenger deep-links into WhatsApp or Telegram and retargeting pixels firing on every click. It charges from about $15/month where Linktree does not charge at all, so the gap only pays off if messenger selling or ad retargeting is genuinely your funnel.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-06 at dash.shorby.com/pricing) Three paid plans, no free plan on the table. Rocket $15/mo, or $12/mo billed annually ($36 off the year); Pro $29/mo, or $24/mo annually ($60 off); Agency $99/mo, or $82/mo annually ($204 off). Pages included: 5 on Rocket, 50 on Pro, 250 on Agency, with Agency adding Projects and Teams from three up. Direct messenger buttons, Click Insights and Shor Rewards are on all three; Google Analytics, custom domains (per project) and Dynamic Feeds (5 per page) start at Pro. The table states all prices are in USD and all sales are final. Note that the marketing site's own /pricing/ page renders nothing — this table is only reachable at dash.shorby.com.
tools.honest_knock: In a category where the market leader has a generous free plan, Shorby charges from day one, so it has to earn the gap. Its case rests on two genuinely differentiated features: messenger deep-links, one tap into WhatsApp/Telegram chats, and retargeting pixels firing on every click. If you use neither, Linktree's free tier wins; if messenger-first selling or ad retargeting is your funnel, the $15 pays for itself.
tools.best_for: creators and businesses that sell via messenger conversations or retarget link-in-bio traffic with ad pixels
tools.skip_if: you just need a links page (free tools abound), or your audience doesn't click through to chat apps
compare_with: the free-tier giants — Shorby's paid-only stance is justified only by its messenger and pixel features; decide on those

tools.name: Shore
tools.what_it_does: Booking and business software for local service businesses (salons, barbers, wellness, coaches): 24/7 online appointments via your website, Google and Instagram, calendar and staff scheduling, client profiles, automated reminders that cut no-shows, plus email marketing and POS. Fixed monthly price with unlimited bookings — no per-booking commission.
tools.pricing: (2026-09-07, read on their own pricing pages in English and German, in euros) Three packages, each showing two figures that are a billing choice rather than a discount: the higher is the monthly-billing rate, the lower is the rate per month when you pay for the year. Starter EUR 59.90 / EUR 49.90 with 2 employees included, Growth EUR 89.90 / EUR 79.90 with 4, and Team EUR 129.90 / EUR 119.90 with unlimited employees. The toggle reads 'Yearly (Save EUR 120)' against 'Monthly', and EUR 120 is exactly the EUR 10 monthly gap over twelve months. Card payments run at up to 1.35% on every tier. There is a 14-day free trial. POS hardware is published separately: the Shore Complete bundle is EUR 1,499, with a card reader at EUR 69, dock EUR 49, stand EUR 199, cash drawer EUR 99 and Epson receipt printer EUR 269. Add-ons: a professional website at EUR 65/month and a branded web app at EUR 40/month. The POS is only sold in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Paying yearly carries a 12-month initial term; monthly billing cancels with 14 days' notice to the end of the period.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for local appointment businesses, and that's also the boundary: the integration list is short (calendar, Google, Instagram, Meta), and once you add POS and payments the monthly total climbs well past the entry price. If you only need a booking link, this is more machine than you need.
tools.best_for: salons, barbers, spas, wellness studios, physical therapists, craftspeople and local retailers that want bookings via Google and Instagram, no-show-reducing reminders, marketing and (optionally) POS in one fixed-price system
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple scheduling link (a Calendly-class tool is lighter) or you run a business without appointments at all
compare_with: commission-based salon platforms or lighter pure-scheduling tools

tools.name: Signal House
tools.what_it_does: SMS and Voice API positioned as a Twilio alternative. Usage-based with no platform fee: $0.0065 per SMS segment with no minimum, down to $0.0030 above 10m, and $1.00 a month per local number. A2P 10DLC fees are published; voice rates are not.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Usage-based, no platform subscription. SMS on a 10DLC local number costs $0.0065 per segment with no minimum, falling on volume: $0.0050 from 500k segments a month, $0.0045 from 1m, $0.0040 from 2m, $0.0035 from 5m and $0.0030 from 10m. Numbers are $1.00 a month, dropping to $0.50 between 500 and 1,000 numbers and $0.25 above 1,000. MMS is $0.0200 per segment, $0.0170 above 500k. Toll-free numbers are $1.00 a month with SMS from $0.0079 down to $0.0050. Number lookup is $0.005. A2P 10DLC registration is billed separately: $4.50 for the brand, $15 one-time per campaign, then $1.50 a month for a low-volume campaign or $10 a month for a standard one. Carrier fees are passed through on top: outbound AT&T $0.0035, Verizon $0.0045, T-Mobile $0.0045. A2P approval is quoted at 72 hours or less, dropping to 48 hours above 500k segments a month.
tools.honest_knock:
Two things are missing from a page that is otherwise unusually specific. The first is voice. The product is sold as an SMS and Voice API and the pricing page publishes no voice rate at all — nor short code pricing. If the voice half is why you are looking, you cannot budget it from public information and will have to ask.

The second is the arithmetic behind the Twilio comparison, which is the whole pitch. Take the entry rate with no minimum. Signal House is $0.0065 a segment against Twilio’s $0.0083, which reads as a 22% saving. But carrier fees are a pass-through and identical either way: add T-Mobile’s $0.0045 to both and you get $0.0110 against $0.0128 — about 14%, not 22%. Numbers narrow it further, $1.00 against $1.15. So the saving is real and it is worth having at volume, but it is a discount on the platform margin rather than on your bill, and the headline does not make that distinction. On a million segments a month that difference is roughly $1,800 a month against Twilio’s list — worth switching for, provided the voice side does not turn out to be where the money goes.

Worth noting on the other side: Signal House prints its A2P 10DLC registration fees on the pricing page, and Twilio’s equivalent page says only that fees apply and points elsewhere. Being able to see the whole bill before you sign is not nothing.
tools.best_for: teams sending real SMS volume in the US who already know what an A2P 10DLC campaign is and want a cheaper per-segment rate than Twilio’s list without giving up published pricing. The volume ladder is genuinely steep — from $0.0065 down to $0.0030 — so the case gets stronger the more you send, and the number discounts above 500 numbers suit anyone running many local presences
tools.skip_if: you are mainly buying voice, because there is no published rate to compare and no way to model the cost. Skip it too if your volume is small: at a few thousand messages a month the per-segment saving against Twilio is a few dollars, and you would be trading a mature ecosystem and documentation for that. And if you are not already registered for A2P 10DLC, budget the brand and campaign fees plus the approval wait before you compare anything — those apply wherever you send from
compare_with: the comparison Signal House invites, and it is checkable. On the entry tier Signal House charges $0.0065 a segment against Twilio’s $0.0083, and $1.00 a month for a local number against $1.15. Carrier fees are pass-through and the same on both, so the all-in gap is nearer 14% than the 22% the message rate alone suggests. What Twilio has that does not show up in a rate table is depth: a far larger ecosystem, more documentation and a longer track record, plus voice pricing you can actually read. Both price lists here were read on 2026-08-07 — verify them yourself, because usage-based rates move and neither vendor publishes every fee in one place.

tools.name: Signeasy
tools.what_it_does: E-signature and contract management for SMBs — unlimited signing and sending, templates, audit trails and integrations, priced per seat.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against signeasy.com) (2026) Free trial. Personal $10/mo billed yearly ($120) — single seat, built around signing. Business $20/mo per seat billed yearly ($240/seat) adds unlimited sending and collaboration; Business Pro $30/mo per seat ($360/seat) adds end-to-end contract management with roles.
tools.honest_knock: The $10 Personal plan is annual-billed and single-seat — and note that sign-unlimited is not send-unlimited: proper unlimited sending starts at Business, $20 per seat on a yearly commitment, while contract-management features gate at Business Pro, $30 per seat.
tools.best_for: small teams that want straightforward unlimited sending and signing per seat, with contract management one tier up
tools.skip_if: you only sign occasional documents, or you are a solo sender at volume — Personal is single-seat and sending-limited
compare_with: DocuSign is the enterprise default with the deepest integration catalog; Signeasy is the simpler, cheaper-per-seat alternative for SMB sending and signing

tools.name: SignNow
tools.what_it_does: Electronic signatures and custom eSignature workflows by airSlate. Send, sign and manage documents on any device — legally binding and team-friendly.
tools.pricing: Three seat plans, read on signnow.com/pricing.md on 7 September 2026: Business at $8 per user a month on annual billing, Business Premium at $15 and Enterprise at $30, with month-to-month priced higher (read at EUR 20 / EUR 30 / EUR 50 from the EU on 5 September 2026). A Site License is billed at $1.50 per signature invite instead of per seat, aimed at organisations sending 1,000+ documents a year, and is where SSO, full API access and phone support appear; HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11 and QES are add-ons on top. airSlate Business Cloud is $50 per user a month and bundles signNow with airSlate, pdfFiller and US Legal Forms. signNow states unlimited users on all paid plans and no envelope cap. Free 7-day trial, no credit card required.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for straightforward everyday signing — if you need deep contract-lifecycle (CLM) features, a heavier platform fits better.
tools.best_for: teams that sign at volume and want unlimited users at a flat rate — roughly 60% under DocuSign for the same core job
tools.skip_if: you need the deepest enterprise integrations and workflows — that's where the incumbent still earns its premium

tools.name: Similarweb
tools.what_it_does: Competitive intelligence on web traffic, search and ads — what your competitors' visitors do.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on their own pricing page) The entrepreneur plans are published: $125 per month on annual billing for Competitive Intelligence, $333 for Competitive Intel & SEO & AEO, and $542 for Competitive Intel, SEO & AEO & Ads — or $199, $399 and $649 respectively on monthly billing, each for a single user. Included history differs by plan and is easy to miss: 3 months on the entry plan, 6 months on the two above it. What is not published is the business and enterprise tab: it carries no figure at all and routes every tier to 'Talk to sales' for a custom package, and the FAQ repeats that premium features require one. A free trial is offered without a stated length. Up to 37 months of data history is sold as an add-on rather than an inclusion, and API access is either standalone or inside a custom package.
tools.honest_knock: Similarweb does publish a price — $125 a month for one seat on annual billing, or $199 if you pay monthly. What it does not publish is anything above one seat: the business and enterprise tab carries no figure at all and routes straight to a sales call, where the number depends on what they think you can pay. So the decision splits in two. One analyst can price this today and start a trial without speaking to anyone. A team walks into a negotiation, and should walk in with a ceiling already written down — plus the two line items priced apart from the seats: 37 months of data history is an add-on, and API access is quoted separately.
tools.best_for: a single analyst or marketer who needs competitor traffic and channel estimates often enough to justify $125 a month, and teams who are prepared to negotiate an annual contract for more than one seat
tools.skip_if: you want a quick check on one competitor — the free tier and public estimates cover that, and the cheapest paid plan is $125 a month for a single user
compare_with: the tools people weigh this against — all three publish a single-seat price, so the comparison comes down to scope per dollar

tools.name: SimpleTexting
tools.what_it_does: SMS marketing and business texting: run mass-text campaigns, two-way conversations and automations with compliance built in.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Credit-based by monthly volume, from $39/mo (500 credits) up to about $909/mo (50,000), with SMS = 1 credit and MMS = 3. Yearly billing saves 20% — the entry plan is $39 a month billed yearly at $398.40 — and unused credits roll over. Extra credits beyond your plan run 5.5 cents each. Every paid plan includes three user seats, with additional seats at $20/mo each and additional numbers at $10/mo; a local number is $10/mo plus a $4 activation fee, and there is a one-off $4 carrier (10DLC) registration. Toll-free and short-code options sit above that, with short codes beginning at $1,000/mo. Nonprofits, churches and other tax-exempt organisations get 15% off any monthly plan.
tools.honest_knock: The credit model plus US carrier (10DLC) fees and per-number/per-seat add-ons mean the sticker isn't the whole bill — and SMS marketing only works with genuine opt-in and a real offer, not blasting a cold list.
tools.best_for: US businesses that want straightforward, compliant SMS marketing and two-way texting with rollover credits
tools.skip_if: you don't have a real opted-in list or a compelling offer — texting a cold audience burns money and trust

tools.name: SimplyBook.me
tools.what_it_does: Online booking and scheduling system for service businesses — booking website and widget, provider calendars, automated reminders and online payments. Free plan for 50 bookings a month with one provider; paid plans from EUR 11.90 a month billed annually.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02, read on their own pricing page, in euros) Free EUR 0: 50 bookings a month, 1 custom feature, 1 provider, no card needed. Basic EUR 11.90/month billed annually or EUR 13.90 monthly: 100 bookings, 3 custom features, 5 providers. Standard EUR 24.90 annual or EUR 29.90 monthly: 500 bookings, 8 custom features, 15 providers. Premium EUR 49.90 annual or EUR 59.90 monthly: 2,000 bookings, unlimited custom features, 30 providers. Enterprise is quote-only. Annual billing saves a stated 17%. Their own page says no setup fees, no transaction fees and no per-user charges — payment processors bill their own rates separately. A 14-day trial of premium features runs without a card.
tools.honest_knock: The plan ladder is set by bookings per month and by how many custom features you may switch on, and those two ceilings move independently — so you can outgrow a plan on features while nowhere near the booking cap, or the reverse. Free and Basic also carry SimplyBook.me branding on your booking page; white-label starts at Premium.
tools.best_for: service businesses that take appointments and want a booking page, reminders and online payment without building one
tools.skip_if: you only need a simple calendar link for one person — a free scheduling link does that without a booking system on top

tools.name: Smartli
tools.what_it_does: AI writing suite for e-commerce: product listings, ad copy, SEO text and brand assets. Monthly runs $39 (Starter) to $299; on annual billing Starter disappears and Pro drops to about $24/month. Each of the nine tools is competent rather than deep, so leaning hard on one job means outgrowing it.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 5 Aug 2026, on smartli.ai) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 7-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Starter was $29/mo when we first checked, so the entry price has gone up.
tools.honest_knock: Smartli bundles nine AI tools — copy, SEO, images, logos — into one suite, and that breadth is also the honest catch: each individual tool is competent rather than best-in-class, so a team that leans hard on one job may outgrow it toward a specialist. And like all AI copy, its product descriptions and ad copy need a human edit and a fact-check — never publish specs or claims it invents about your product. For a store that wants many content jobs handled cheaply in one place, it's efficient.
tools.best_for: e-commerce sellers who want an affordable all-in-one AI suite to draft product listings, ad copy, SEO text and basic brand assets in one place
tools.skip_if: you need best-in-class depth in one area (a specialist copy or image tool), or you won't edit and fact-check AI output before it ships
compare_with: Jasper or Copy.ai plus a separate image tool
specialist AI-content tools — Smartli's edge is bundling many jobs cheaply; compare on the one job you'll use most

tools.name: SmartSuite
tools.what_it_does: One flexible work management platform to plan, track and automate any process. Projects, CRM and operations side by side — replace a stack of scattered tools with a single source of truth.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No free plan — a 14-day trial of Professional with no credit card. Team is $15 per seat a month billed annually, or $20 billed monthly, with a minimum of 3 billable users, 5,000 records per solution and 50 GB of storage. Professional is $32 per seat annually, or $36 monthly, with a minimum of 5 billable users, 100,000 records and 100 GB. Enterprise is custom-priced. The minimums matter more than the rate: a three-person team on Team pays for three seats whether or not all three log in, and Professional cannot be bought for fewer than five.
tools.honest_knock: It's a broad, do-everything work-management platform, so the power comes with a learning curve and a per-seat cost that adds up for bigger teams — a single source of truth if you commit, overkill if you just need a task list.
tools.best_for: teams consolidating projects, CRM and operations into one flexible, database-driven work-management platform
tools.skip_if: you need a lightweight to-do or a single-purpose tool — SmartSuite's breadth is wasted and its learning curve isn't worth it

tools.name: Smarty Discounts
tools.what_it_does: Shopify discount engine for the rules the native one cannot express: capped and fixed-amount discounts that hold up across currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts and mix-and-match, targeted by product, customer, cart, market, country or company. Free plan available; Lite $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, Pro $25.99 or $259.99. Each tier includes two discounts at the level above. Launched January 2025, six reviews as of 4 Sep 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/smarty-discount) Three tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Forever Free costs nothing, Lite is $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, and Pro is $25.99 a month or $259.99 a year; the annual price on both paid tiers saves 17%, and both carry a 7-day free trial. What you are buying is capability, not volume: there is no order cap, no revenue meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan anywhere in the block. Free covers product and order discounts with basic targeting and what the listing itself calls low support. Lite adds shipping and mix-and-match discounts, enhanced targeting and priority support. Pro unlocks every discount type, every targeting rule, active time periods and free shipping on a single rule. One detail in the plan table is worth reading twice, because it is unusual and it is in your favour: each tier gives unlimited discounts at its own level plus up to two at the level above. On Free you can build two Lite-grade discounts, on Lite two Pro-grade ones. That is a working trial of the next tier rather than a locked door, and it means you can prove the rule you actually need before you pay for it.
tools.honest_knock: The evidence base is thin. The app launched on 14 January 2025 and carries six reviews as of 4 September 2026 — all five stars, but six is not a track record, and the vendor, Neezon, is a small developer in Ho Chi Minh City rather than a company with a support contract behind it. The listing is unusually candid about what that means at the bottom of the ladder: the free plan's own feature list says low support. Add to that what the app needs to do its job. The data-access panel says it reads customer data flagged as sensitive and can view and edit customers, products, discounts and the Online Store, which is the access any discount engine needs but is still broad. And because the ladder gates discount types rather than volume, the plan you land on is decided by the one rule you cannot live without: if the campaign you have in mind needs time-period scheduling or free shipping on a single rule, you are on Pro at $25.99 regardless of how few discounts you run.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants whose promotions have outgrown the native discount engine — capped amounts, a fixed amount that behaves correctly in several currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts, mix-and-match — and who want to build them with rules rather than with a developer, targeting by product, customer, cart, market, country or company
tools.skip_if: your promotions are ordinary percentage or fixed-amount codes, which Shopify's built-in discounts already do for free; or you want a long support and reliability record before a young app gets write access to the discounts in your checkout
compare_with: the honest comparison is not another app but the discount engine already sitting in your admin. Shopify does percentage, fixed-amount, buy-X-get-Y and free-shipping discounts at no cost, and for most stores that is enough. Smarty Discounts starts earning its $9.99 or $25.99 at the point where you need a cap on the discount, a fixed amount that converts properly across markets, tiers built on weight or subtotal rather than quantity, or targeting by company or market — the rules the native engine cannot express at all

tools.name: SMTP.com
tools.what_it_does: Reliable transactional and bulk email delivery via SMTP relay and API: high-deliverability sending for app notifications, receipts and campaigns, with real-time analytics and dedicated IPs — built for volume senders.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-05) Fixed-volume plans, all billed monthly: Essential $25 (50,000 emails, shared IP), Starter $80 (100,000, dedicated IP begins here), Growth $300 (500,000), Business $500 (1,000,000). Above that, High Volume Senders is quote-only and starts at a minimum of 250 million emails a month, with a dedicated platform instance, dedicated IP and MTA and no shared mail queue. Reputation Defender and Insight Engine are optional add-ons at 20% of plan cost each, available on all plans. No free tier or published trial. Payment by card or PayPal. The site is operated by J2 Global Canada, a Ziff Davis company.
tools.honest_knock: It's a veteran, reliable relay, but two honest notes. Pricing is volume-tiered, so a shared IP on the cheapest plan is fine for low volume while serious senders need the dedicated-IP tiers (and the IP warm-up discipline that comes with them). And the value-add features — reputation and verification — are metered on top at ~20% of plan cost, so the real bill is higher than the base tier. It's infrastructure, not a marketing suite; you bring the campaigns.
tools.best_for: businesses and developers needing dependable high-deliverability transactional or bulk email via SMTP relay and API, with dedicated IPs at scale
tools.skip_if: you send low volume and a free/cheap SMTP tier covers you, or you want a full marketing-email platform with templates and automation built in
compare_with: close relay/API peers — Postmark leans transactional-fast, SendGrid broader; compare on IP options and deliverability at your volume

tools.name: SMTP2GO
tools.what_it_does: Reliable transactional and bulk email delivery. Send via a simple SMTP relay or API with strong deliverability, real-time analytics and global sending infrastructure.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-07 on smtp2go.com/pricing with the volume slider walked through all nine stops; the plan cards carry the amounts in their data-rate-monthly and data-rate-annual attributes) Free: 1,000 emails a month, 200 a day, 5 days of reporting, ticket support only (toll-free phone and live chat limited to 14 days), extra emails not permitted. Starter: $15/mo or $150/year for 10,000 (overage $1.20 per thousand); $30/mo or $300/year for 50,000 ($1 per thousand). Professional: $75/$750 for 100,000 ($0.85), $170/$1,700 for 250,000 ($0.70), $280/$2,800 for 500,000 ($0.60), $520/$5,200 for 1,000,000 ($0.50), and it adds a dedicated IP address and email-testing tools. Premier: custom, over 3,000,000 a month. Annual is exactly ten months' money at every step (their 'two months free'). All invoices are billed in US dollars; EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD are shown as approximations. 30-day money-back promise.
tools.honest_knock: It's the pragmatic middle of email infrastructure: simpler and better-supported than the hyperscale APIs, cheaper than most, with genuinely useful reporting — but sending reputation is still yours to earn. A relay delivers what your domain deserves: without proper SPF/DKIM/DMARC and list hygiene, no provider saves you. Check the overage rate for your tier before you size up: on the 10,000 plan an extra thousand emails costs $1.20 against the $1.50 a thousand you already pay, and the 50,000 plan at $30 works out cheaper per email than Professional at $75.
tools.best_for: businesses that want dependable transactional/bulk sending via SMTP or API with human support and clear per-volume pricing
tools.skip_if: you're inside a marketing platform that already sends for you, or you need advanced template/campaign tooling bundled in
compare_with: close relay peers — Postmark leans transactional purity; SMTP2GO wins on support reputation and price at SMB volumes

tools.name: SocialBee
tools.what_it_does: Social media management and scheduling with content categories. Plan, recycle and publish posts across all your channels from one calendar.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, read on their own pricing page) Bootstrap $29/month ($290 a year, 16% off): 5 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Accelerate $49/month ($490 a year): 10 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Pro $99/month ($990 a year): 25 profiles, 5 workspaces, 3 users per workspace. Agency tiers billed monthly: Pro50 $179, Pro100 $329, Pro150 $449 for 50, 100 and 150 profiles, with 10, 20 and 30 workspaces and 5 users per workspace; billed yearly they are $149.20, $274.20 and $374.20 a month. Add-ons: 5 extra profiles $15/month or $150/year, an extra user $10/month or $100/year, an extra workspace $10/month or $100/year. AI generation is unlimited on every tier.
tools.honest_knock: You are billed per social profile, not per person, and a profile is one brand account on one network. A single business posting to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok has used the whole Bootstrap allowance before a second brand or a client exists. The second thing is that people cost extra on top: Bootstrap and Accelerate are single-user plans, so a two-person team on eight profiles is $49 plus $10, not $29. Count your profiles across every network first — that number, not your team size, decides the tier.
tools.best_for: solo marketers and small agencies who post to several networks on a schedule and want evergreen recycling rather than a queue that empties
tools.skip_if: you post to one or two networks by hand and are happy doing it, because the value here is category-based recycling across many profiles and that only pays back at volume
compare_with: the standing comparison — count your profiles across every network and price all three on that number

tools.name: Softr
tools.what_it_does: Build custom AI business apps, client portals and internal tools without code. Connect Airtable, Google Sheets or your data and launch in an afternoon.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-07) A free plan with unlimited apps, up to 3 builders, 5 app users, 5,000 database records, 500 workflow actions and 5 AI credits a month. Paid on yearly billing: Basic $19/month, Pro $99/month and Business $329/month, with Enterprise on custom limits; the pricing page opens on the Yearly tab and advertises two months off, so month-to-month costs more. App-user allowances are published per tier: Team 5 + Client 5 on Basic, Team 10 + Client 50 on Pro, Team 30 + Client 100 on Business, where Team users share a business email domain with one of your builders and everyone else counts as a Client user. Extra app users beyond the allowance start at $1/month on Pro and $2/month on Business. Extra builder seats are $5/month on Basic, $10 on Pro and $20 on Business, and builders can be added as app users free. Records run 50K / 500K / 1M and workflow actions 2.5K / 10K / 25K a month. Non-profits and education get a stated 50% discount. Refunds: in full within 14 days of a first monthly payment, 30 days of a first yearly one.
tools.honest_knock: Builder seats are billed on top of the plan, and pricing counts builders and app users separately, so a public-facing app with a lot of end users gets expensive fast. Watch the overage rate as well as the plan: extra app users are $1 a month on Pro but $2 on Business, so the dearer plan meters growth at double the rate. It fits internal tools and client portals with a known audience, not an open signup.
tools.best_for: teams building internal tools, client portals or member apps on top of Airtable or Google Sheets without code
tools.skip_if: you're building a public consumer app with unpredictable, high user counts — the per-user model works against you there

tools.name: Spiky.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI meeting intelligence for revenue teams — records and analyses sales calls, tracks keywords and talk patterns, and coaches reps. Free tier at 3 meetings per user, then $15 to $40 per user per month on annual billing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 28 Aug 2026 on their own pricing page; unchanged since 31 Jul 2026) Read across both billing toggles. There is a genuine free tier, capped at 3 meetings per user per month. On annual billing Plus is $15, Pro $24 and Premium $40 per user per month; switch to monthly and the same three read $18, $29 and $49. Annual saves up to 18%. Trials need no card. Meeting allowances: 3 on Free, 30 on both Plus and Pro, unlimited on Premium.
tools.honest_knock: The number to check first is the meeting cap, not the price. Plus and Pro both stop at 30 meetings per user per month, so the step from $15 to $24 buys features, not capacity. A rep taking two calls a day passes 30 in three weeks, which pushes you to Premium at $40 — nearly triple the entry price — for volume rather than capability. Price this from your team's actual call count and you will land on the right tier; price it from the feature table and you will not.
tools.best_for: sales and customer-facing teams that already run most conversations on video and want the coaching layer — talk-time, keyword tracking and call review — without buying a full revenue-intelligence platform
tools.skip_if: your team's calls are mostly ad hoc or on the phone rather than video, or the meeting volume per rep sits well above 30 a month, in which case only the top tier fits and the cheaper plans are a false economy
compare_with: the other conversation and outreach tools we cover — Spiky's angle is coaching from the recording rather than sequencing the outreach; compare on meeting volume, because that is what sets your tier

tools.name: Spocket
tools.what_it_does: Dropshipping platform with vetted US and EU suppliers. Find fast-shipping products, add them to your store in a click and automate order fulfillment.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-07) Four monthly plans, metered on unique products: Starter $39.99 (25 products), Pro $59.99 (250 products, 25 premium), Empire $99.99 (10,000 / 10,000) and Unicorn $299.99 (25,000 / 25,000). Annual billing is advertised as eight months free and the annual rates are printed on the cards: Pro $24 a month, Empire $57 and Unicorn $79, with stated savings of $432, $516 and $2,563. Unicorn's two figures do not reconcile - $299.99 a month for a year less $79 a month for a year is $2,651.88, not $2,563. There is a 7-day trial and 0% transaction fee on every tier. Multiple-store support is listed on all plans, but the page states a separate subscription is required for each store. Unicorn carries the MOST POPULAR badge.
tools.honest_knock: Spocket's pitch is faster-shipping US and EU suppliers, and that's real — but you still pay twice: the monthly subscription and the wholesale product cost, so margins depend on picking items with room to mark up. Catalog breadth is narrower than giant AliExpress-based tools (that's the trade for vetting and shipping speed), and the low Starter product cap pushes serious stores up to Pro quickly. It reduces, not removes, the usual dropshipping risks.
tools.best_for: dropshippers who want vetted US and EU suppliers with faster shipping and one-click store integration, prioritizing delivery speed over raw catalog size
tools.skip_if: you want the widest possible catalog at the lowest sourcing cost (AliExpress-based tools fit), or your margins can't absorb both subscription and wholesale cost
compare_with: AliExpress-oriented alternatives with bigger catalogs but often slower shipping — Spocket trades breadth for US/EU speed

tools.name: Stackable
tools.what_it_does: Shopify discount app (by Optizio) that folds several discounts into one code: order, collection and shipping discounts combined, a progress type that raises the discount as the cart grows, and checkout upsells on the top tier. No free plan — Growth is $19.99 a month, Unlimited $99.99, both with a 7-day trial.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/stackable-discounts) Two paid tiers, billed in USD every 30 days, and no free plan. Growth is $19.99 a month, or $199.99 a year with the annual saving the listing puts at 17%, and covers unlimited combined discounts; that plan carries the label 'For Non-Plus'. Unlimited is $99.99 a month, or $999.99 a year on the same 17%, and adds unlimited checkout upsells and unlimited linked discounts on top of the same combined discounts. Both tiers come with a 7-day free trial. The plan table lists no order caps, credit allowances or per-use charges, so what the tier costs is what the app costs.
tools.honest_knock: The two halves of the pitch are priced five times apart. Discount stacking — order, collection and shipping discounts redeemed with a single code — is the $19.99 Growth plan, the one the listing labels 'For Non-Plus'. The checkout upsells and linked discounts the app leads with sit in the $99.99 Unlimited tier only, so a merchant who came for the upsells is reading $1,199.88 a year rather than $239.88. There is no free plan to settle whether the stacking alone lifts an order, so the seven-day trial is the entire evaluation. One more thing to check before you commit: the Website link on the listing, www.stkbl.app, now redirects to the documentation for Discount Kit — a different, pricier Optizio app — and that documentation does not mention Stackable anywhere (checked 6 September 2026). For an app that launched on 13 October 2020 and has collected 54 App Store reviews since, ask support where the current documentation lives before the trial clock starts.
tools.best_for: shopify stores running several promotions at once — an order discount, free shipping and a collection deal — that want shoppers to redeem them with one code instead of choosing, or that want the progress type which raises the discount as the cart fills
tools.skip_if: you run one promotion at a time, because Shopify's own combined discounts already cover that at no cost — or the checkout upsells are the part you actually want, since those only exist in the $99.99 tier here
compare_with: Both extend Shopify's native discount engine, and the money separates them more than the feature lists do. Smarty Discounts has a free tier and tops out at $25.99 a month, and it aims at rules the native engine cannot express — capped and fixed-amount discounts that survive currency conversion, tiers by quantity and subtotal. Stackable aims at combination instead: several discounts under one code, a progress type that raises the discount as the cart grows, and checkout upsells in its top tier. So if the problem is 'this rule cannot be built', start with Smarty and pay nothing to find out. If the problem is 'my customers have to pick which code to use', that is Stackable's job — but there is no free tier here to test it on, only the seven-day trial.

tools.name: Stamped
tools.what_it_does: Reviews, ratings and loyalty platform for e-commerce: collect product reviews and user-generated content, run rewards and loyalty programs, and show social proof to lift conversions on Shopify and other stores.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-11, read on their own pricing page with the bundle toggle on and all three products ticked) There is no free plan, and the bill is driven by your monthly order volume rather than by a flat plan fee. Bundled, all three products came to about $18/month at the 200-order step and $79/month at 1,000 orders; $798/month is the figure at the 5,000-order step, not the price of the suite. Standalone, Reviews is around $23/month at 200 orders and $99 at 1,000. Plans include up to two domains and each additional store is $100/month after a first free month. Overage charges were dropped. A re-read on 12 August 2026 was not possible: the pricing page returns 403 to non-browser clients from both of our networks.
tools.honest_knock: The $798/month figure that circulates for the full suite is the 5,000-order step, not an entry price — at 200 orders the same three-product bundle came to about $18/month when we read it. Read the order band, not the headline. What does bite is the shape: each product is its own subscription and the price steps hard with volume, so a good month raises the bill in several places at once, and a second storefront is another $100/month. Start with one product and price the step above the volume you actually expect.
tools.best_for: mid-market Shopify brands that want reviews and loyalty in one platform instead of juggling separate apps
tools.skip_if: you're an early-stage store — the removed free plan and $199+/product pricing are steep before you have the volume to justify them
compare_with: other reviews and loyalty apps, some far cheaper

tools.name: Stampezee
tools.what_it_does: Digital stamp cards for local businesses, replacing paper punch cards. Stamp Start is free for one branch, one card and up to 100 stamps; Stamp Lite is $29.99/month for two branches and three cards. Public pricing stays thin, so re-check the tiers before committing.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-30 on stampezee.com/en/pricing from a US exit) Four tiers, all now named and priced on the public page. Stamp Start free: 1 branch, 1 stamp card, up to 100 customers or 100 stamps, whichever comes first. Stamp Lite $29.99/month: 2 branches, 3 stamp cards, unlimited customers and stamps, signup rewards, EzeeCodes, birthday/anniversary/referral automations. Stamp Pro $49.99: 3 branches, 6 cards, spend-based stamping, tiered and exclusive rewards, 4 push notifications. Stamp Elite $99.99: 10 branches, 12 cards, scratch-card campaigns, email marketing, 1 custom stamp card design, dedicated account manager. The page advertises 17% off on the annual term but does not print the annual amounts. StampEzee prices by region and the European rates are materially lower, not just relabelled: the same page read from the Netherlands gives EUR 19.99, 39.99 and 69.99. Note the entry tier's own contradiction: the plan card frames Stamp Start as a 14-day free trial, the comparison table on the same page lists it as Free with no time limit.
tools.honest_knock: The category is honest and proven (digital stamp cards beat lost paper cards), and the platform is young with limited public pricing and review coverage — so start on the free plan, run one real campaign, and measure repeat-visit lift before paying. The deeper truth of loyalty programs: the mechanics are 10% of the outcome; a reward worth returning for is the other 90%.
tools.best_for: local businesses (cafés, salons, retail) that want a simple digital stamp-card loyalty program starting free
tools.skip_if: you need POS-integrated loyalty with CRM depth (bigger platforms exist), or your offer isn't repeat-visit shaped
compare_with: the digital-stamp peer set — compare per-location pricing and whether Apple/Google Wallet passes are included

tools.name: StoreFAQ
tools.what_it_does: Builds SEO-friendly FAQ pages and product FAQ accordions with JSON-LD schema on Shopify, plus an AI chatbot, instant answers and live chat. Free plan covers 100 FAQ page views; Professional $7.99 a month, Growth $14.99 and Enterprise $49.99, all metered on page views and AI conversations.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/storefaq) Four tiers, metered on FAQ page views and AI chatbot conversations rather than on the number of FAQs. Free: 100 FAQ page views, unlimited FAQs and FAQ groups, the AI chatbot and AI-written FAQs, 25 AI conversations for the lifetime of the account, AI training on up to 50 products, export and import, instant answer with live chat and standard support. Professional $7.99 a month: 500 FAQ page views, 50 AI conversations a month, training on 150 products, multilingual FAQs and dedicated support, with overage at $0.0159 per extra page view and $0.30 per extra AI conversation. Growth $14.99 a month: 2,000 FAQ page views, 100 AI conversations a month, 300 products, with overage at $0.0075 a view and $0.30 a conversation. Enterprise $49.99 a month or $479.90 a year, a 20% saving: unlimited FAQ page views, 500 AI conversations a month, 2,000 products, priority support and $0.30 per extra conversation. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Storeware, 124 Broadkill Rd #599, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 3 January 2024 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock:
The meter is FAQ page views, and that is the thing this app exists to increase. You install it to get SEO-friendly FAQ pages that rank and get read; every read is a billable unit. The free plan stops at 100 views and Professional at 500, which a product-page FAQ on a store with any traffic burns through in days, and then it is $0.0159 a view. Unlimited views arrive only on the $49.99 tier. Success on the cheap plans costs you money, which is an odd shape for a pricing page and the first thing to model before you install.

The AI allowance is the second meter and it is tight. Twenty-five conversations for the entire life of a free account, fifty a month at $7.99, a hundred at $14.99, and $0.30 each after that. Two hundred extra conversations in a month is $60, more than the top tier costs outright, so if the chatbot is the reason you are here, price the conversations rather than the subscription and jump straight to the tier that fits.

And know the boundary of the tool. This builds FAQ content, schema and a light chat layer. It is not a helpdesk: no ticketing, no agent queues, no multichannel reporting. Anything a shopper asks that an FAQ cannot answer still lands in whatever inbox you had before.
tools.best_for: small Shopify stores that want SEO-tagged FAQ pages with JSON-LD schema and a light AI chatbot for deflection, without standing up a full support stack
tools.skip_if: you have real traffic, because the page-view meter charges you for the FAQ pages doing their job, or you need ticketing, agent workflows and multichannel support reporting

tools.name: StoreSEO
tools.what_it_does: SEO suite for Shopify: bulk meta titles and descriptions, image compression and alt text, JSON-LD schema, sitemap submission, instant indexing requests and Search Console reporting, with AI credits for generated copy. Free forever for 25 products; paid runs $14.99, $39.99 or $249.99 a month by product count.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/storeseo) Free Forever covers 25 products with SEO scoring, 200 AI credits, 25 image optimisations, up to 5 tracked keywords, an LLMs.txt generator and Agents.md editor, an SEO migrator, alt-text optimisation and 24/7 chat support. Paid tiers are Lite $14.99, Essential $39.99 and Advanced $249.99 a month, each with a 7-day free trial. Lite covers 100 products, 500 image optimisations and 1,000 AI credits and adds one-click schema markup, instant indexing requests, Google Analytics and Search Console and automatic sitemap submission. Essential covers 250 products, 2,000 images and 5,000 credits. Advanced covers 10,000 products, 50,000 images, 50,000 credits and adds multilingual SEO. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing: storeseo.com sells a Growth plan at $99.99 a month (1,000 products, 5,000 images, 12,500 AI credits, 200 keywords) that does not appear on the App Store listing at all, and also sells credit top-ups from $10 for 5,000 credits and $50 for 25,000. Rating 5.0 from 674 App Store reviews. Developer Storeware, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 19 October 2021 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: Know what an SEO app can and cannot do before you buy any tier. This one fixes the mechanical layer well — meta titles and descriptions in bulk, alt text, compressed images, JSON-LD, sitemaps, indexing requests — and none of that creates demand for products nobody is searching for. It is maintenance, not marketing, and on a catalogue of 25 products the free tier already does most of it. Two specifics worth a raised eyebrow. The pricing gap between Essential at $39.99 for 250 products and Advanced at $249.99 for 10,000 is filled by a $99.99 Growth plan. That plan lives on the vendor's own site but not on the App Store listing our link points to, which is a strange place to hide a tier. And the AEO/GEO features — the LLMs.txt generator, the Agents.md editor, the separate “agentic” ranking — are a bet, not a channel. No major search or AI vendor has committed to reading llms.txt, so treat those numbers as a hypothesis you are testing rather than traffic you are buying.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a few hundred products and no in-house SEO help, who want metadata, schema, alt text and indexing handled in bulk and reported against Search Console
tools.skip_if: you have fewer than 25 products, in which case the free tier is the whole product, or you expect an app to fix a demand problem rather than a metadata one

tools.name: Storista
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that turns TikTok, Reels and UGC clips into shoppable video widgets — carousels, stories, grids and spotlights — with auto-sync from TikTok and Instagram. Free for 10 videos, $15 for 50, and AI product tagging from $49.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/storista-stories, listed as “Storista Shoppable Video UGC”) Four tiers. Free covers 10 videos with unlimited views, TikTok Shop and Shop app integration, GEO/SEO optimisation and the Carousel and Spotlight widgets, and it keeps Storista branding on the widget. Basic is $15 a month for 50 videos, unlimited views, basic analytics and videos on any page. Business is $49 a month for unlimited videos, AI Smart Tagging, advanced analytics and all widget types. Scale is $199 a month for Shopify Plus stores and adds VIP support and multiple stores. Every paid tier carries a 14-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The app is English-only, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and works with Checkout, Shopify Admin, TikTok Shop, the Shop app, Instagram Reels, TikTok Videos, GemPages, Rebuy, Skio, Shogun and Subscriptions. Developer Storista LLC, Sheridan, Wyoming; the app launched on 19 February 2021 and had 49 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing. Note that storista.io, the vendor's own domain, sells a different product on a different meter — AI-generated UGC video at roughly $1 to $4 a render, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan — and not the widget ladder above.
tools.honest_knock:
The first thing to know is that the brand sells two different products, and the one you find by searching the name is not the one this link installs. storista.io is an AI UGC video generator priced per render, roughly $1 to $4 a video, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan. The Shopify app is a shoppable-video widget priced at $0, $15, $49 and $199 a month. Same company, same name, unrelated ladders, and nothing on either page maps one to the other. If you arrive at a price expecting the other product, you will be wrong by a factor of ten in either direction.

Second, read the headline against the pricing table. AI Smart Tagging is one of four bullets in the app's own pitch and one of the four features named in the listing summary. It appears on Business at $49 and above. On Free and Basic you tag products to videos yourself.

Third, the rating deserves its detail. 5.0 from 49 reviews is excellent, and the breakdown is 47 five-star, one four-star and one one-star — so the round number is a rounding, not a perfect record. That is a small point, but it is the kind of thing worth checking on any app whose average sits exactly on the ceiling.

Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views customer device and activity data and can view and edit customers, products, store analytics, custom data and Shopify admin. That is a wide grant for a widget that displays video, and it belongs in your processing register whatever you decide about the product.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that already produce TikTok or Reels content and want it on the storefront as shoppable video, with the free tier's unlimited views making it cheap to test whether social video converts on your product pages at all
tools.skip_if: you have no UGC or short-form pipeline to feed it — the widget displays content, it does not create any — or you want automatic product-to-video tagging without paying $49 a month for it

tools.name: Storylane
tools.what_it_does: Interactive product demos you can embed, with analytics on who watched what.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0: 1 seat, 1 published demo live at a time, unlimited views. Starter $50/month ($40 annual), 1 seat, extra seats $40 each, unlimited demos, de-anonymises 250 visitors/month. Growth $625/month ($500 annual), 5 seats, extra seats $100 each, 2,500 visitors/month. Premium $1,500/month ($1,200 annual), 10 seats, 10,000 visitors/month. Enterprise quote-only. Their RepX chat product is separate again, starting at $2,000/month for up to 10,000 monthly visitors.
tools.honest_knock: The jump from Starter to Growth is $50 to $625 a month — twelve and a half times — and the free tier is capped at one live demo, so the moment you want a second demo published you are on the ladder. What is actually being sold at each step is visitor de-anonymisation: 250 a month on Starter, 2,500 on Growth, 10,000 on Premium. Price that against what you already pay a separate tool to do, because it is the meter that decides your tier, not the number of demos. Extra seats are charged on top at $40 to $100 each, which means a five-person sales team on Starter is not $50 a month, it is $210.
tools.best_for: sales and marketing teams who show a product before a call and want to know which prospects clicked what — the free tier is genuinely usable for one demo
tools.skip_if: you need more than one live demo but nowhere near 2,500 identified visitors a month, because that is exactly the gap the price ladder does not serve; a screen recording and a calendar link may do the job for less
compare_with: the direct interactive-demo peers — compare the visitor-identification allowance at your tier, since that is what you are really buying

tools.name: Streak
tools.what_it_does: CRM built directly inside Gmail: manage pipelines, leads and deals from your inbox with email tracking, mail merge and shared views — ideal for teams that live in Google Workspace.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Pro $49/user/mo annual or $59 monthly; Pro+ $69 annual or $89 monthly; Enterprise $129 annual or $159 monthly — a flat 20% annual discount, with Enterprise available on annual billing only and only to teams of 10 or more. Everyone on a team must be on the same plan. AI credits are a second meter: 20 per user per month on Pro, 150 on Pro+, 500 on Enterprise, pooled across the team and expiring each period; top-ups run $100/mo for 1,000 credits up to $1,000/mo for 25,000. The free CRM tier was eliminated in 2024-25, but the free email tools remain — email and link tracking, snippets, Streak Share, a thread splitter, and mail merge at 50/day against 1,500/day on the paid plans. Pro+ has a 14-day free trial.
tools.honest_knock: The pitch — CRM living inside Gmail — is also the ceiling: everything happens in the inbox, which power users love and growing teams outgrow (reporting, permissions, cross-team process). And note the trajectory: the free tier is gone and per-seat prices sit at real-CRM levels now, so the 'lightweight Gmail add-on' framing no longer matches the invoice. If the inbox is truly where your deals live, few tools feel this natural.
tools.best_for: solo founders and small Gmail-native teams whose pipeline genuinely lives in email threads and who want zero context-switching
tools.skip_if: your team needs shared process outside the inbox (a standalone CRM scales better), or you're price-sensitive — the Gmail convenience now costs full CRM money
compare_with: standalone SMB CRMs at similar or lower per-seat — Streak's edge is literally living in Gmail; that's the whole trade

tools.name: Success.co
tools.what_it_does: Strategy execution and OKR platform. Turn goals into action: set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, run meetings and align teams so strategy actually gets executed rather than just planned.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 in Success.co's own structured data on success.co/pricing) There is a Free Forever plan at $0, and the paid product is tiered per user with the rate falling as the team grows. Monthly billing: $12 per user a month for 1-25 users, $11 for 26-75, $9 for 76-125, $7 for 126-250 and $6 for 251-1,000. Annual billing takes roughly a dollar to two off each step: $11, $10, $8, $6 and $5 per user a month paid annually. Two enterprise add-ons sit outside that ladder and are quoted on the page itself at $250 a month each: Single Sign-On (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or any SAML/OIDC provider) and Directory Sync via SCIM for automatic provisioning and de-provisioning. A 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits get 50% off.
tools.honest_knock: The ladder rewards size rather than commitment: moving from 25 to 26 users drops the rate a dollar, and the annual discount is worth about the same single dollar per user. So the number that decides your bill is headcount, not billing term — and at the small end, where most teams start, $12 a user is the least favourable rate on the whole page. The two capabilities a security team will ask for first, SSO and SCIM, are not in any plan: they are $250 a month each, which on a 20-person account doubles the bill.
tools.best_for: leadership teams that already run on goals and want one place to set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, and keep strategy execution on cadence
tools.skip_if: your team won't commit to a regular goal-review rhythm (the software alone won't create it), or a simple shared doc already keeps you aligned
compare_with: close OKR/EOS-style execution platforms — compare on how well each fits your existing operating rhythm and per-user cost

tools.name: Sunsama
tools.what_it_does: Daily planning that pulls tasks from your other tools into one deliberate schedule.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) The page gives two different numbers and it is worth knowing both. The plan card says $17 a month billed yearly, or $22 billed monthly, for the Pro plan, with unlimited usage and integrations; Enterprise is quote-only. The FAQ on the same page says Sunsama costs $25 a month per person, or $20 a month on yearly plans, and gives a worked example of $50 a month for two people. There is a free trial with no card required. The page also explains, unprompted, that they price at $25.00 rather than $24.99 because they consider the latter 'deceitful psychological trickery'. Their own llms.txt, read the same day, lists Pro at $17 per person a month billed yearly and $22 billed monthly, plus a 14-day trial at $0 with no card required — so the machine-readable file agrees with the plan card and not with the FAQ.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page contradicts itself: the plan card says $17 yearly and $22 monthly, the FAQ on the same page says $20 yearly and $25 monthly. One of those is stale, and until you know which, treat $25 as the number you might actually be charged. That is an odd thing to have to say about a company that goes out of its way on that same page to explain why it refuses to use $24.99 pricing — the transparency is real and so is the inconsistency. The other thing to be clear about is that this is per person with no team discount mentioned: two people is two subscriptions, and their own example says $50.
tools.best_for: people whose problem is deciding what to do today rather than tracking what exists — it pulls from your existing tools and forces a daily plan, which is the whole product
tools.skip_if: you already plan your day and just want a task list, because that is free everywhere; also skip it for a team, since there is no team pricing and the per-person cost multiplies straight through
compare_with: the direct daily-planning peers — all three are per person, so compare on which one actually gets you to close the planning ritual each morning

tools.name: SupaEasy
tools.what_it_does: No-code Shopify Functions generator (by Nextools): build and migrate custom discount, checkout, payment, shipping and validation logic from the Shopify Admin, with a migrator for deprecated Scripts and an AI generator that writes functions from a plain-language brief.
tools.pricing: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/supaeasy and supaeasy.com/pricing) A free plan plus three paid monthly tiers, each with a 7-day trial. The catch is in the free plan: it works only on a development store, not a live one. Premium is $49 a month ($470 a year), Advanced is $99 a month ($950 a year) and Ultimate is $399 a month ($3,830 a year). The headline feature — the AI Functions Generator, which writes a function from a plain-language description — does not appear until Advanced at $99, alongside the Scripts Editor and Functions Wizard. So using SupaEasy the way it markets itself, on a live store, realistically starts at $99 a month.
tools.honest_knock: Two things the marketing glosses over. First, the 'free' plan is development-stores only, so any live use is paid, and the AI generator that headlines the app is not in Premium ($49) but in Advanced ($99), possibly plus metered AI credits as an add-on — so the AI promise realistically costs $99+ a month. Second, the rating is suspiciously spotless — 5.0 across 205 reviews, all five-star — and the praise dwells on fast human support (Andrea, Fabio) more than on the no-code AI running unattended, which hints the tool can need hand-holding.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants — especially non-Plus stores — who want custom discount, checkout, payment and shipping logic without hiring a developer, and above all those forced to migrate deprecated Shopify Scripts to Functions before the cutoff
tools.skip_if: you only need a simple volume discount (a dedicated discount app is cheaper), you are comfortable writing Shopify Functions in code yourself, or you will not pay $99 a month to use the AI generator on a live store — the free plan runs on a dev store only
compare_with: SupaEasy is a no-code layer over Shopify Functions — the same platform capability a developer would code by hand. With engineering time, native Functions cost nothing but your developer's hours; SupaEasy is for merchants who would rather describe the logic than write it, and who need the Scripts migrator. Weigh the subscription against a freelancer's one-off build

tools.name: Superfiliate
tools.what_it_does: Creator-led growth for D2C brands: run influencer, affiliate and referral programs in one platform across Shopify, Meta and TikTok Shop — discovery, automation, gifting and revenue tracking.
tools.pricing: (read 25 August 2026, re-checked 5 September 2026) Superfiliate publishes no price on its own site. superfiliate.com/pricing returns 404 with and without www, /llms.txt returns 404, there is no pricing item anywhere in the navigation, and the only commercial call to action is Book Demo. Their Shopify App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/superfiliate) publishes the shape rather than the amount: a single plan named Custom, 'Free to install. Additional charges may apply', the note that the app 'Requires an active Superfiliate subscription for app activation and use. Contact Superfiliate for plan details', and one hard fact — 'All charges are billed in USD.' So the free-to-install label covers the app, not the platform. Our dossier has carried a range of roughly $299 to $999 a month which we cannot trace to their site or to any dated reading; treat it as an unverified order of magnitude rather than a price, and ask for the number in writing on the demo call.
tools.honest_knock: The price is the part you cannot check. Their pricing page returns 404 with and without www, the homepage carries no figure at all, and the only route to a number is a sales call — so the honest warning is not that it is expensive, but that you cannot compare it against anything until you have spoken to them. Ask for the figure in writing on that call, and ask what separates the ends of whatever range they quote. On fit rather than price: this is built for brands already running creator and affiliate programs, and it is overkill if you are testing your first affiliate offer.
tools.best_for: e-commerce brands turning customers and creators into affiliates with branded co-branded storefronts — if the volume justifies a demo-quoted platform fee
tools.skip_if: you're testing affiliate marketing for the first time — there is no self-serve entry and no published price, so the first step is a sales call about a program that is not yet producing

tools.name: SupportBee
tools.what_it_does: Email ticketing for collaborative customer service: a shared team inbox where every agent has their own login, plus an integrated knowledge base and, on the upper tier, a customer portal. Per seat, no free plan.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-27 on supportbee.com/pricing) Two plans, both priced per seat, and no free tier. Month to month, Startup is $20/seat/month and Enterprise is $25/seat/month. Switch the toggle to annual and the page shows a total of $204 per seat billed annually on Startup and $252 on Enterprise, a saving it advertises as 20 per cent, which works out at effective rates of 17 and 21 dollars a seat a month. Startup covers the shared inbox, snippets, filters, basic integrations, API access, unlimited email inboxes and tickets, customer satisfaction ratings, customer management, audit trails and one knowledge base with one team. Enterprise is described as everything in Startup plus five things: enterprise integrations, business hours, the customer portal, an audit log with data history, and portal access for customer groups. The trial is 14 days and the home page says no credit card is required. Billing runs through Stripe, you can switch between monthly and annual at any time with a prorated credit, and plan changes take effect immediately.
tools.honest_knock: It is an email helpdesk and only an email helpdesk. There is no live chat, no phone, no WhatsApp and no social inbox, and the integration list confirms it: Asana, Trello, ClickUp, Linear, Notion, GitHub Issues, Pipedrive, Insightly, Capsule, Customer.io, QuickBooks, PostHog, Slack and webhooks are all places to push a ticket outward, not channels a customer can arrive on. Read the two published plans as printed and neither lifts the cap of one knowledge base and one team, even though the vendor's own FAQ describes teams as the way you mirror departments. Enterprise is listed as everything in Startup plus five named items, and more teams is not one of them. Watch the seat count too. The pricing FAQ defines users as everyone with access across all three permission levels, collaborators included, and the docs add a collaborator through the same add-a-user flow. So the invite-the-whole-company pitch runs through the same per-seat meter, and collaborator activity does not even show up in reports. And the two pages disagree about leaving: the pricing FAQ says you can cancel your subscription anytime, while the billing doc routes cancellation through contact us, which is the one billing action on that page that is not self service.
tools.best_for: small support teams working out of a shared email inbox who want assignment, internal comments and a knowledge base without dragging customers into a portal or learning a helpdesk suite
tools.skip_if: your customers reach you on chat, phone or WhatsApp, or support and billing need separate queues with their own rules; this is one channel, one team and one knowledge base on both published plans

tools.name: Surfer (SurferSEO)
tools.what_it_does: Content optimization against live SERP data, and since 2026 a tracker for how often a brand is cited in AI answers like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Billed yearly at four tiers.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on surferseo.com/pricing over a US connection; first read 2026-08-25 from the Netherlands) Billed yearly: Discovery $49/mo, Standard $99/mo, Pro $182/mo and Peace of Mind $299/mo, with Enterprise at $999/mo and AI Search Analytics sold on its own at $158/mo. Every listed rate assumes the annual commitment. The page publishes what that commitment saves you — $120, $240, $444, $720 and $324 a year — and working those back gives monthly-billing rates of about $59, $119, $219, $359 and $185; Surfer does not print those figures itself, so treat them as arithmetic on theirs rather than a reading. Worth knowing if you are outside the US: we read this page from both sides and the numbers do not convert. A European is quoted €49 to €299 where an American is quoted $49 to $299, which at today's rate makes the same subscription materially more expensive in Europe.
