tools.honest_knock: Every tier quotes its monthly rate on annual billing, so the number you see is a year's commitment rather than a monthly one. The meter that actually forces an upgrade is documents: 120 to 360 optimizations depending on tier, which a working content team passes faster than it expects. And the AI-visibility tracking that the product now leads with is capped by prompt count per tier, so watching more of your market costs a step up rather than an add-on.
tools.best_for: content marketers, SEO specialists and agencies that need on-page optimization against live SERP data and want to start tracking how often they are cited in AI answers
tools.skip_if: you are a solo blogger who needs keyword research rather than document-level optimization, or you cannot commit to a year — every listed rate assumes annual billing
compare_with: the WordPress plugin people weigh this against — Rank Math optimises inside your site for a far smaller fee, Surfer works document by document against live SERP data and adds AI-answer tracking; the split is whether you are optimising a site or writing at volume

tools.name: SurveyMonkey
tools.what_it_does: Survey and feedback platform: build surveys, collect responses at scale and analyze results for market research, CX and employee feedback. A native Salesforce integration pushes responses straight into Salesforce, triggers workflows off the answers themselves (churn-risk follow-up or an NPS detractor landing on a rep's desk, for instance) and ties feedback back to accounts and pipeline, so sales and CS read it inside the tool they already work in rather than in a separate reporting dashboard.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on surveymonkey.com/pricing over a US connection, on the Team plans tab) Team Advantage is $30 per user a month and Team Premier $92, both starting at three users and billed annually — so the real entry price is three seats, not one. Advantage carries 50,000 responses a year and Premier 100,000, with $0.15 per response beyond that. Enterprise is quote-only from five users. Individual plans sit behind a separate tab, so the figure a solo user sees is not the one quoted here.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is a teaser. Response caps trigger $0.15-per-response overages that become a hidden cost on big studies. Branding and customisation are limited, and a lot of the good analytics and logic sit behind higher tiers.
tools.best_for: teams that need research-grade survey logic (skip logic, randomisation, quotas) with compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2) and 200+ integrations
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple form (Google Forms is free) or you're cost-sensitive with high response volumes — the overage fees add up
compare_with: the free-basic and the design-led form tools

tools.name: SurveySparrow
tools.what_it_does: Conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience. A limited free plan, then roughly $19–39/month on Basic up to $149 on Business. Response limits on the lower tiers and a contact-sales wall on API and higher volume make budgeting fiddly, and there is no true monthly billing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) The plan prices are not in the page itself — they render only after the plan selector loads, and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. What the page does publish is the discount structure: yearly billing saves up to 40%, students and education get 50% off, nonprofits 15%, and a startup programme offers $2,000 of credit for $500. Our earlier reading put paid survey plans at roughly $19-39/mo (Basic), Starter around $59 and Business around $149, with the CX and reputation suites quoted, billed quarterly or annually rather than monthly — treat those as indicative and take your figure from the selector.
tools.honest_knock: The conversational-survey UX is the draw, but response limits on lower tiers and the 'contact sales' wall on advanced features (API, higher volume) make budgeting fiddly — and there's no true monthly billing.
tools.best_for: teams that want engaging, conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience
tools.skip_if: you just need a quick, occasional form — a free tool like Google Forms or Tally covers it without a subscription

tools.name: Survicate
tools.what_it_does: Customer feedback platform for continuous surveys: NPS, CSAT and in-product micro-surveys across web, in-app, email and link — with templates, audience targeting and native integrations (Segment and RudderStack among them) that pipe feedback straight into your CRM and analytics.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on survicate.com/pricing) A 10-day trial of all features, no card. Growth starts at $114/mo billed annually and is metered on feedback, not seats: 250 survey responses and 1,000 data points a month, 10 user seats across 2 teams, one dashboard. Pro starts at $349/mo billed monthly or annually, with a custom yearly response pool, advanced survey logic and 10 dashboards. Enterprise starts at $569/mo. Note that the entry price moved up during 2026 - we had $89 on this page before this read - so check the current figure before you budget.
tools.honest_knock: The plan is metered by response volume, not by surveys — a viral NPS month can push you a tier up, and the free plan's 30-day retention quietly deletes your history. Mind the billing asymmetry too: Starter is monthly-only while Growth and up expect an annual commitment.
tools.best_for: product and CX teams running always-on feedback — NPS, CSAT and in-app surveys — piped into the CRM and analytics stack they already use
tools.skip_if: you just need an occasional one-off questionnaire (a simpler form tool covers that) or your response volume is huge — response-metered pricing punishes scale
compare_with: Typeform wins on beautiful long-form forms, SurveyMonkey on cheap general-purpose surveys; Survicate wins on continuous product feedback with deep integrations

tools.name: Switcher Studio
tools.what_it_does: Multi-camera live production and streaming from iPhones and iPads you already own, with overlays and pay-per-view monetisation. Studio runs around $45/month on annual billing. iOS-only — no Android or desktop app — and wireless multi-cam is only as reliable as the venue's Wi-Fi.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against switcherstudio.com) (2026) Studio around $45/mo on annual billing (about $65 monthly) and Suite around $69–$71/mo annual (about $99 monthly); a Studio Seasonal tier near $55/mo runs on a 3-month commitment for event users. 14-day trial, no free plan.
tools.honest_knock: It's iOS-only — iPhones and iPads, no Android and no desktop app — so your whole capture setup lives in Apple's ecosystem. And wireless multi-cam is only as reliable as your venue's Wi-Fi; a shaky connection is the failure mode nobody markets. The monetization features (pay-per-view, subscriptions) are genuinely strong, but only matter if you're actually selling access.
tools.best_for: creators, churches, events and small businesses that want multi-camera live production and streaming using iPhones and iPads they already own — no broadcast hardware
tools.skip_if: you're on Android or Windows, you need rock-solid wired production for high-stakes broadcasts, or a single-camera stream is all you'll ever need
compare_with: OBS is free but desktop and technical; Switcher trades that for wireless iPhone simplicity at a subscription price

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.what_it_does: AI avatar video for training, explainers and onboarding: type a script, no camera or actors needed. Priced in video-minute credits — Basic is free with about 10 minutes a month and no downloads, Starter $18/month billed yearly for 120 minutes a year. Re-generating an edit spends the minutes again.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Basic is free. Starter $29/mo billed monthly or $18/mo billed yearly; Creator $89/mo monthly or $64/mo yearly; Enterprise is custom with unlimited minutes. The page currently carries a NEW LOWER PRICES banner claiming plans from $18 a month, a 38% saving. Priced by video-minute credits, so the minute allowance rather than the sticker is what decides which plan you need, and a Studio Express-1 avatar is a paid add-on at $1,000 a year available only on annual plans. One caution we can document. The FAQ block lower down that same page states Starter costs $29 a month or $264 a year, and Creator $89 a month or $804 a year. That works out at $22 and $67 a month — not the $18 and $64 shown on the plan cards above it. Both readings were present in our July and August 2026 captures too, so check the figure at checkout rather than trusting either block.
tools.honest_knock: The video-minute caps are tight — 10 min/mo on Starter goes fast when you iterate, and re-generating edits burns minutes. Fantastic for avatar-led training and explainers without a studio, but not for high-volume or cinematic production.
tools.best_for: teams making talking-head training, explainer and onboarding videos without cameras, actors or editing
tools.skip_if: you need lots of video or cinematic, human-shot production — the minute caps and avatar style won't fit

tools.name: Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder
tools.what_it_does: AI blog builder for Shopify: generates SEO-oriented posts with titles, images and keyword suggestions, embeds your products, and schedules bulk publishing from a drag-and-drop editor. Free with 50 one-off credits; Pro is $9.99 a month on Shopify Basic but rises with your Shopify plan to $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder) Free plan available: unlimited blog posts, 50 credits that do not recur, extra credits at $0.06 each, unlimited SEO audits, the drag-and-drop editor with autosave, author, product and table-of-contents blocks and 24/7 live chat. Pro is $9.99 a month or $101.89 a year, a 15% saving, and adds 250 AI credits a month, publish scheduling, content strategy suggestions, one-click multi-language AI translations, AI keyword suggestions, weekly idea suggestions and hands-on help fixing SEO issues. The headline price applies on Shopify Basic only: the listing states +$5 on the Grow plan, +$30 on Advanced and +$60 on Shopify Plus, so Pro is $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99 a month depending on which Shopify plan you are on. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.9 from 450 App Store reviews. Developer Tapita; the app launched 14 February 2022 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: Publishing volume is the trap this tool makes cheap. It generates posts quickly and schedules them daily or weekly in bulk. And a Shopify blog filled with unedited AI articles is precisely the pattern search engines have spent the last two years demoting: the app lowers the cost of production, not the bar for ranking. Used the other way round, as a drafting and structuring tool for posts you actually edit, it is sensible and cheap. Two practical points on the price: the $9.99 headline holds only on Shopify Basic, and the surcharge takes it to $69.99 a month on Shopify Plus, which is the sort of detail that belongs in a headline rather than a footnote. And the listing never says how many of the 250 monthly credits a single post costs, so the allowance cannot be planned against until you ask.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that want structured, product-linked blog drafts and a publishing schedule, and that will edit what comes out before it goes live
tools.skip_if: you intend to bulk-publish AI articles unedited, or you are on Shopify Plus and can buy a full content tool for what the surcharge takes this to

tools.name: Tapita SEO Optimizer
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one Shopify SEO app: site audits with LLMs.txt for AI search engines, bulk and AI-written metadata, image alt text and compression, JSON-LD schema, broken-link auto-redirects and one-click speed fixes. Free plan available; Basic is $9.99 a month and Pro $39.99 on Shopify Basic, plus $5, $30 or $60 more a month on Grow, Advanced and Plus.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/google-seo-schema-meta-data) Three tiers. Free: SEO audit and LLMs.txt on basic pages, unlimited on-page SEO audit, essential JSON-LD schemas, and image compression 900 a month capped at 30 a day. Also bulk and AI metadata optimisation, bulk image alt text and file names for 50 products, one-click page speed and 24/7 support chat. Basic $9.99 a month or $101.88 a year, a 15% saving, adds SEO audit and LLMs.txt on main pages, auto image optimisation 100 a day, 100 AI metadata credits a month, full JSON-LD schemas, broken-link detection with auto-redirects and advanced speed features. Pro $39.99 a month or $408 a year adds all main pages, 500 images a day, 500 AI credits a month, higher speed capacity, full automation of image alt text and file names, unlimited keyword research and hands-on help fixing SEO and Search Console issues. Both paid tiers carry the same surcharge line, and it is the number that decides what this costs: +$5 on the Shopify Grow plan, +$30 on Advanced and +$60 on Shopify Plus. So Basic is $9.99, $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99, and Pro is $39.99, $44.99, $69.99 or $99.99, depending on which Shopify plan you are on. Extra audit pages and extra AI credits are billed on top and the listing does not print a per-credit rate. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Tapita, M5 Building, 91 Nguyen Chi Thanh, Hanoi; the app launched 15 March 2023 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock:
The price on the listing is a Shopify-Basic price, and almost nobody reads the line underneath it. The same Pro plan is $39.99 on Shopify Basic, $44.99 on Grow, $69.99 on Advanced and $99.99 on Shopify Plus, because Tapita adds $5, $30 or $60 on top depending on your Shopify plan. That is a two-and-a-half-fold spread on identical software, and it is the single largest factor in what this app costs you. Work out which row you are on before you compare it to anything else.

The second meter has no published rate at all. Basic gives you 100 AI metadata credits a month and Pro gives you 500, and beyond that the listing says only that more audit pages and more credits carry an extra charge. It does not say how much, and it does not say how many credits one product's metadata consumes. Tapita's own sister app publishes $0.06 a credit on its listing; this one publishes nothing, so you cannot price a month of AI metadata before you install.

And the free tier is a demonstration rather than a plan: 50 products for bulk alt text and file names, 30 images a day, and the SEO audit and LLMs.txt limited to basic pages. Any real catalogue is on a paid tier within a week, which is fine as long as you know that going in.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants on the Basic or Grow plan who want SEO audits, bulk metadata, image alt text and speed fixes out of one app instead of hiring a specialist
tools.skip_if: you are on Shopify Advanced or Plus, where the same tier costs $30 to $60 a month more, or you need a published per-credit rate before you build a month of AI metadata around it

tools.name: Tapstitch
tools.what_it_does: Fashion-first print-on-demand for brand-builders: premium heavyweight blanks (streetwear tees, oversized hoodies), bigger print areas and made-to-order apparel with no inventory — integrates with Shopify.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No subscription and no monthly fee — you pay per item, production plus shipping, so there is no plan price to compare. Our monthly captures of the catalogue put item prices roughly between $2.99 and $23 depending on the blank. The honest catch is margin rather than fees. Printify's lower product and shipping costs mean noticeably higher profit per sale, while Tapstitch's premium heavyweight blanks — around 250 GSM tees and 350-380 GSM hoodies — sit at retail-grade prices, roughly $35-50 for a finished tee. Price the finished garment against your retail price, not the platform.
tools.honest_knock: Printify is cheaper, higher-margin and has a far bigger catalogue — if you're optimising for profit per sale or product breadth, that's the real trade-off. Tapstitch earns its place when garment quality and brand feel matter more than squeezing the last point of margin.
tools.best_for: creators building a real apparel or streetwear brand who care about fabric, fit and how the product feels in hand
tools.skip_if: you want the cheapest option or the widest catalogue — for pure margin and product breadth, traditional POD like Printify wins

tools.name: Tax1099
tools.what_it_does: Per-form e-filing of 1099s, W-2s and related forms, falling to about $0.68 a form at high volume, with an eFile Plus subscription near $249/year for frequent filers. TIN matching, W-9 requests, state filing and corrections can each carry their own charge, so tally the add-ons.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) This is pay-as-you-go per-form e-filing that drops with volume. Our dated reading puts it as low as about $0.68 a form at high volume. There is a free Essential account for creating payers and recipients and running TIN matching, and an eFile Plus subscription around $249 a year for teams that file often. Those tiers are not published in a form our capture can read, so verify the current per-form bands on their own page before budgeting a season. The structure to understand is that the price per form falls as your count rises, so the effective cost depends entirely on volume rather than on a plan.
tools.honest_knock: Per-form pricing is genuinely cheap for a handful of 1099s, but it's metered: TIN matching, W-9 requests, state filing and corrections can each carry their own charge. A business filing across many recipients and states should tally the add-ons, not just the headline per-form rate. It's a filing tool, not a bookkeeping system; it assumes your payee data is already clean.
tools.best_for: businesses and accountants who need to e-file 1099s, W-2s and related forms accurately and cheaply, especially seasonal or higher-volume filers
tools.skip_if: you only file one or two forms a year (the IRS's own free options may suffice) or you want full bookkeeping rather than just the filing step
compare_with: TaxBandits or the IRS IRIS portal
TaxBandits is a close paid equivalent; IRIS is free but barer — Tax1099 wins on integrations and bulk workflows

tools.name: TaxCycle
tools.what_it_does: Professional tax preparation and CRA e-filing for Canadian accountants and bookkeepers. Quote-based and priced by module and firm size, with reported figures ranging from roughly CAD 1,680 into five figures for full suites. Canada-only, and not a consumer filing app.
tools.pricing: Prices are published on taxcycle.com (read 5 September 2026, Canadian dollars before tax, per year): Tax Basics 2026 is $1,600 for one user (regular $1,680) and $540 per additional user; the Complete Tax Suite is $2,625 (regular $2,800) with extra users at $756; the Complete Tax Suite plus TaxFolder is $2,752 (regular $3,102) with extra users at $944. TaxFolder on its own (client portal and e-signatures) is $375 plus $215 per additional user. Larger multi-office licences are quoted.
tools.honest_knock: This is professional preparer software priced for firms, not a consumer filing app: the cost only makes sense if you're preparing returns for clients at volume. The suites start at about CAD $1,600 a year for one user and each extra seat adds several hundred dollars, so a two- or three-person practice should budget the suite price plus seats, plus GST or HST, before comparing it with per-return alternatives.
tools.best_for: Canadian accountants and bookkeepers who prepare and e-file client returns and want fast, checked, CRA-integrated professional tax software
tools.skip_if: you're an individual filing your own personal return (consumer software is far cheaper), or you're outside Canada
compare_with: the established Canadian preparer suites — TaxCycle competes on speed and UX; compare on the specific modules your practice files

tools.name: Team Pulse
tools.what_it_does: Projects, tasks, chat, files and a light CRM pipeline in one tool. The tiers gate on members and projects at once, and the pipeline does not exist below the $79 Growth plan — Starter at $29 is a single seat with five projects. The listed rates assume annual billing.
tools.pricing: (2026) Genuinely free tier: $0/mo for 1 member, 2 projects, unlimited collaborators, chat/tasks/files. Paid (billed annually): Starter $29/mo ($348/yr) — 1 member, 5 projects, NO pipelines; Growth $79/mo ($948/yr) — 3 members, 10 projects, 1 pipeline, AI; Pro $159/mo ($1,908/yr) — 10 members, 20 projects, 2 pipelines; top tier $299/mo ($3,588/yr) — 40 projects, 1,500 AI credits.
tools.honest_knock: The tiers gate on TWO axes at once — member count and project/pipeline count — so you can hit a wall on either. The CRM pipeline is a big part of the pitch, but it doesn't exist below the $79 Growth plan (Free and Starter have none), and member limits are tight: Starter is a single seat, Growth just three. The listed rates also assume annual billing.
tools.best_for: solo operators and small teams who want projects, tasks, chat AND a lightweight CRM pipeline with AI in one simple tool, and value the real free tier to start
tools.skip_if: you need more than a handful of team members (seat caps climb the tiers fast), or you only need project management — dedicated PM tools give far more generous member limits
compare_with: ClickUp is the established all-in-one work platform with generous free seats; Team Pulse bundles a CRM pipeline plus AI in a simpler package — cleaner to start, but the member and project caps are tighter as you grow

tools.name: Teikametrics
tools.what_it_does: Advertising optimisation for Amazon and Walmart sellers, with inventory and catalogue signals.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) Essentials, for up to $10K a month in ad spend: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Advanced, for over $10K a month in ad spend: custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. Enterprise, for over $100K a month in ad spend: also custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. A free trial and a free opportunity assessment are offered.
tools.honest_knock: Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription — it is a subscription plus a percentage. Three per cent of ad spend above $10,000 means a seller spending $40,000 a month pays an extra $900 on top of whatever the custom base is, and that line scales with the thing the product is supposed to make more efficient. That is not automatically wrong — it aligns them with your growth — but it does mean your bill rises when your advertising does, and you should model it at your expected spend rather than your current one. The $10K threshold is the number to watch: crossing it changes the pricing model, not just the price.
tools.best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers spending enough on ads that a few points of efficiency covers the fee — under $10K a month the flat $149 is straightforward
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is small or seasonal, because the flat fee at low spend is a large share of your budget and the percentage model at high spend needs modelling before you commit
compare_with: the direct marketplace-advertising peers — compare total cost at your real monthly ad spend, including any percentage component

tools.name: Tellent
tools.what_it_does: Modular people-management platform — applicant tracking (Recruitee), core HR and performance management with AI automation, for hiring and managing teams.
tools.pricing: Tellent publishes no prices. Its pricing page (read in a browser on 5 September 2026) lists three ATS tiers for Recruitee, Start, Advance and Optimize, and the HR modules Manage and Grow, but every tier ends in 'Get a demo' rather than a figure; agencies are told to ask for a custom quote. What the page does state is scope: Start covers 5 active job posts and a single-page careers site, Advance unlimited posts, referrals and 100 AI screening credits a month, Optimize SSO, API, onboarding support and a dedicated CSM. Free trial available.
tools.honest_knock: The modular pricing is honest — buy only the ATS, or only HRIS — but note the ATS floor: ~€270/mo prices it for teams that hire continuously, not for the company filling two roles a year. And as with every ATS, the workflow fit (approval chains, career-site needs, integrations with your assessment tools) matters more than the feature list; the 18-day trial is enough to run one real vacancy through it — do that.
tools.best_for: European scale-ups hiring continuously that want a collaborative ATS (and optionally modular HRIS/performance) with transparent per-module pricing
tools.skip_if: you hire occasionally (job boards + a spreadsheet honestly suffice), or you want one all-in-one HR suite rather than modules
compare_with: Greenhouse is the ATS benchmark at higher cost; Personio bundles HR-first — Tellent sits between on price with EU roots

tools.name: Tenable
tools.what_it_does: Exposure and vulnerability management (makers of Nessus): scan, prioritize and remediate security weaknesses across IT, cloud and OT — for security teams of any size.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-30 on tenable.com/buy and the Nessus Essentials page) Nessus Essentials is free — a 30-day licence for 5 IPs, non-commercial only, with plugin updates delayed 30 days and no reporting, data export, compliance checks or support. Essentials Plus $199/year: 20 IPs, real-time plugin updates, basic PDF/HTML reporting, still non-commercial, free for verified students and instructors. Nessus Professional $4,790/year, $9,330.95 for two years, $13,637.54 for three — the first tier licensed for commercial use. Nessus Expert $6,790/year, $13,208.13 for two, $19,304.19 for three. Advanced Support (24x365 phone, email, community and chat) is a $400/year add-on on both. Training: $275 for a year of the Nessus Fundamentals course for one person, $385 with Nessus Advanced added. Cloud Tenable Vulnerability Management $3,500/year for 100 assets ($6,825 for two years, $9,975 for three); $3,700/year buys up to 250 assets online. Web App Scanning $6,790/year, or $3,578 for 5 FQDNs. Anything larger is a quote.
tools.honest_knock: Note on how we link this one, updated 28 Jul 2026: between 21 and 28 July our partner link was dead — Tenable's shop subdomain stopped resolving, so we pointed the link at Tenable's own product page and earned nothing from it. Tenable confirmed on 28 July that the links are repaired; we re-tested them that day and the link now works again, lands on the same Nessus product page, and does pay us a commission. This is serious, enterprise-grade security tooling with an enterprise price and a learning curve — not a set-and-forget scanner. You need someone who can act on the findings, or you're paying for reports nobody reads.
tools.best_for: security teams and IT-mature companies that need continuous, authoritative vulnerability scanning and can remediate what it finds
tools.skip_if: you have no one to triage and fix findings — a managed security service or a lighter scanner fits a small team better

tools.name: TestGorilla
tools.what_it_does: Pre-employment skills testing: assessment library, custom questions and candidate scoring.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat. Core $142/month on an annual commitment, $1,704 billed annually, with the full test library, analytics and 2 full-access seats; the Core card carries a credits selector and its sign-up link defaults to a 400-credit tier. Plus starts from $400/month with an annual commitment starting at $4,800, described as scaling with your hiring needs. The page also sets out what a credit buys: 0 for resume scoring, qualifying questions and custom questions, 1 per candidate for skill tests, video questions, ID verification or a talent-pool invite, and 2 per candidate for AI interviews. Prices are shown in USD with GBP, EUR, AUD and INR available.
tools.honest_knock: Both paid tiers are annual-commitment only. Core is not $142 a month in any meaningful sense — it is $1,704 up front, and there is no monthly option to test it with real candidates first. That matters more here than in most categories, because hiring is lumpy: a company that hires in two bursts a year is paying for ten quiet months. Plus is worse to budget for, because it 'starts from' $400 and the page will not say what moves it. The free tier is credit-metered rather than feature-limited, which makes it a genuine trial — use it on a real vacancy before you sign a year.
tools.best_for: companies hiring steadily enough that a year of testing is cheaper than one bad hire, and who will actually use the library rather than writing their own questions
tools.skip_if: you hire a few people a year — the annual commitment is the whole problem, and the free tier plus a well-designed take-home task covers occasional hiring
compare_with: the direct skills-testing peers — compare on whether a monthly plan exists at all, because that is where these differ most

tools.name: TextExpander
tools.what_it_does: Text-expansion tool: you type a short abbreviation and it expands into a stored snippet system-wide on macOS and Windows and in Chrome, with fill-in fields, nested snippets, date maths and scripting. The real product is the team layer — a shared snippet library with permissions, sign-up by email domain, auto-subscribe for new hires, usage statistics and SSO — aimed at support, clinical-admin, recruiting and sales teams that need everyone sending the same approved wording. The vendor self-attests SOC 2/SOC 3 and HIPAA compliance with a BAA available, which is the clearest argument for paying rather than using a free expander. There is a free plan (5 active snippets); paid tiers start at $5 per user/month billed annually, and the 30-day trial of the full product needs no credit card.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-18 on the vendor's own pricing page; USD per user/month billed annually, excluding tax) The line-up was rebuilt since our July reading and it now starts at free. Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted. Annual billing is sold as two months free against paying monthly; the page does not print the monthly amounts next to the plans, so we do not quote them. The free plan is real but deliberately narrow: 5 active snippets out of an unlimited library, one snippet swap every two weeks, 3 teams, 5 team members and no snippet activity history at all. That history — what lets you see changes and restore deleted snippets — is 24 hours on Pro, 7 days on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. Team members stay capped at 5 on Free and Pro; unlimited members start on Business, which is also the first tier with single sign-on (Google SSO on Business, all providers plus SCIM on Enterprise). A 30-day trial with full access to every feature and no credit card sits alongside the free plan. The page still carries an important pricing note for international customers, which we could not open on this reading, so treat the listed USD amounts as pre-tax.
tools.honest_knock: On a Mac the operating system already does the basic job free: Apple's built-in Text Replacement syncs static snippets across your Apple devices, though Apple's own documentation notes it is not available in every app. And Espanso covers the power-user case free and open source on Mac, Windows and Linux. On Windows there is no built-in equivalent (contrary to a widely repeated claim, PowerToys has no text-expansion utility), so the case for paying is genuinely stronger there. Do not buy it for mobile. The vendor's own mobile page is an early-access signup form for Android and iOS betas, not a shipping product — even though the surrounding copy is written in the present tense. Then add the snippet activity history: nothing at all on the free plan, only 24 hours on the $5 Pro tier, 7 days on Business, and unlimited only on Enterprise. Add the vendor's own note that buyers in VAT/GST countries including the EU, UK and Australia may see an estimated 20% uplift on the listed USD price (read 21 July 2026). For one person with a few dozen fixed snippets, the honest answer is usually don't.
tools.best_for: support, clinical-admin and recruiting teams that need everyone sending identical approved wording — the shared library, permissions, auto-subscribe and SSO are what the paid tiers actually buy, and the SOC 2 and HIPAA-with-BAA posture is the one thing no free expander offers a compliance-bound team
tools.skip_if: you are one person on a Mac with a couple of dozen fixed snippets. macOS Text Replacement is built in and free, Espanso is free and open source across all three desktop platforms, and TextExpander's own free plan now covers 5 active snippets. A subscription only starts earning its keep when you need fill-in fields, scripting, or a second person editing the same library
compare_with: Both have a free tier now, and Text Blaze still undercuts every paid rung: Pro $2.99 and Business $6.99 per user per month billed annually, read on their own plans page on 18 August 2026, against $5 and $10. So TextExpander has to win on OS-level expansion outside the browser, and on the SSO, SCIM and HIPAA-BAA paperwork a procurement team asks for — not on price

tools.name: Textline
tools.what_it_does: Business SMS for support and sales teams: shared inboxes, automations and compliance tooling.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Amounts unchanged since 2026-08-01. Add-on message credits $0.03 each, bought in advance; backup message credits $0.04 each, Textline's automatic fallback when you run out mid-conversation. A $15 monthly 10DLC campaign fee applies if you use a 10DLC long code; the same page states that toll-free numbers do not carry a monthly registration fee. NEW since the last reading: the page now names three tiers with their inclusions but still no prices — Essentials (600 minimum included message credits a month, three agents, three-year conversation history), Pro (2,000 minimum credits, five agents, unlimited history, Salesforce, custom roles) and Enterprise (quote). HIPAA-compliant plans are charged an additional fee. Note for future readers: the per-feature tooltips on this page are unfilled placeholder copy, so the feature names carry no explanation.
tools.honest_knock: Two costs are easy to miss and both are monthly. The credit system has two rates: $0.03 for credits you buy deliberately and $0.04 for backup credits that fire automatically when you run out — a 33% premium for not noticing. And a $15 monthly 10DLC campaign fee appears on your bill if you use a 10DLC long code, charged by the carrier registry rather than by Textline, so no plan removes it; the same page notes that toll-free numbers carry no monthly registration fee, so the number type is the lever, not the tier. Plan prices are still not published — the page names Essentials, Pro and Enterprise and what they include, but no dollar figures.
tools.best_for: support and sales teams that already text customers from personal phones and need a shared, compliant inbox with a record of who said what
tools.skip_if: you send marketing blasts rather than conversations — that is a different product and priced per message elsewhere; also skip it if your volume is low enough that a shared inbox on your existing helpdesk covers it
compare_with: the direct business-texting peers — compare on the per-message rate plus the 10DLC fee, since the platform fee is only part of it

tools.name: TheTop
tools.what_it_does: An AI 'chief of staff' that pulls Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Microsoft 365 and RSS feeds into one ranked morning brief, then drafts the replies and quick actions the brief calls for. Essential is $15/month for two connected sources; the enrichment, smart reply and five-source cap that let it act rather than summarise sit on Pro at $30.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on thetop.com/pricing) Two paid plans, both month to month with no contract. Essential is $15/month and covers the full morning brief, two connected sources, AI-powered summaries and insights, basic conversation memory and a daily email digest. Pro is $30/month and adds adaptive memory and learning, five brief refreshes a day, automatic data enrichment, quick actions and smart reply, and five connected data sources. Switching the billing toggle to yearly drops the effective rates to $12 on Essential and $25 on Pro. Both plans open with a seven-day free trial of Pro. The pricing page shows no free tier, although its own FAQ answers a question about starting on Free and upgrading later.
tools.honest_knock: Out-of-the-box integrations stop at Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Microsoft 365, and RSS or news feeds, so anything else in your stack sits outside the brief. The tier caps bite before the feature list does: two connected sources on Essential, five on Pro, and Gmail plus Calendar alone uses up Essential. Automatic enrichment, quick actions and smart reply — the parts that do something rather than summarise something — are Pro only, which makes the realistic price the $30 tier rather than the advertised $15. The pricing page also shows no free plan while its own FAQ answers a question about starting on Free, so ask before you count on one.
tools.best_for: professionals and small-business owners who lose the first hour of the day triaging Gmail and a calendar, and want one ranked brief instead of five open tabs
tools.skip_if: your day runs through Slack, a CRM, a ticket queue or a project tracker — the integration list does not reach them, and a brief built from email and calendar alone will miss what actually moved

tools.name: Thordata
tools.what_it_does: Proxy infrastructure and scraping stack — residential, mobile, ISP and datacenter proxies plus SERP/web-scraper APIs, priced per GB, IP or 1K requests.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Usage-metered, with free trials on the APIs. Every advertised "from" rate is the largest package on its ladder: residential $0.65/GB at 5,000 GB ($3,250) against $2.00/GB at 1 GB, $1.50 at 50 GB and $0.80 at 350 GB; mobile $2.20/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB; SERP API $0.70 per 1K at 1M responses against $1.20 at 15K; Web Scraper API $0.50 per 1K at 3M against $1.00 at 30K; Web Unlocker $1.00 per 1K at 200K against $1.30 at 10K; Scraping Browser $2.50/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB. Static ISP and datacenter proxies advertise $0.75/IP against a $1.50 list, while the ISP packages themselves list at $1.50 and $4.50 an IP.
tools.honest_knock: Everything is a meter — per GB, per IP, per 1K responses — so the bill scales with usage. And every rate the site advertises is the largest package on its ladder: $0.65 a GB means buying 5,000 GB, while 1 GB of the same product costs $2.00. Budget at your own volume, not at the headline. Plus the category-wide caveat we'd give any residential-proxy vendor: those '100M+ real residential IPs' come from consumer devices, so check sourcing ethics and your target sites' terms before building on it.
tools.best_for: data teams scraping at scale — price intelligence, SERP tracking, AI-training data — who want proxy infrastructure plus ready-made scraping APIs at aggressive per-unit rates
tools.skip_if: you need predictable flat pricing, or your use case skirts site terms — residential proxying carries compliance questions no discount fixes
compare_with: Bright Data is the enterprise incumbent with strict compliance vetting; Thordata undercuts hard on per-unit price — decide whether compliance depth or unit cost matters more for your pipeline

tools.name: Thryv
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one platform for small service businesses: CRM, scheduling, invoicing, reviews and marketing.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on their own pricing page) Starter is $99 a month and Signature $399 a month on monthly billing. Annual billing is stated to save 15%, which our 1 August reading put at $85 and $340, with Signature billed $4,068 a year. Amplify is custom-priced. A free trial is offered, and the growth add-ons sold alongside these plans are not priced on the page.
tools.honest_knock: Two published tiers, $85 and $340, and nothing between them. That makes the decision unusually blunt: not which plan fits, but whether a fourfold step is worth taking all at once. Signature is billed annually at $4,068 — that is a year committed up front, and the monthly figure is a division rather than a payment option. Before that call, list which of the bundled parts you would otherwise buy separately: Thryv's case rests on replacing four or five tools, and if you only want two of them the arithmetic usually favours keeping them.
tools.best_for: small service businesses — trades, salons, clinics — that currently run on a diary, a spreadsheet and a separate invoicing tool, and would genuinely retire all three
tools.skip_if: you already have a CRM you like, because this is an all-in-one and its value is the bundle; buying it alongside what you have is paying twice for the overlap
compare_with: the direct small-service-business peers — compare on which of your existing tools each one actually replaces, not on the feature count

tools.name: TicketTailor
tools.what_it_does: Low-fee event ticketing and box-office software: sell tickets online, manage check-in and keep more of your revenue without per-ticket booking fees.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) No subscription and no contract: pay-as-you-sell $0.85/ticket, or prepaid credits from $0.30/ticket — 500 credits cost $300, which is $0.60 each. Free events are genuinely free up to 5,000 tickets a year, your first five paid tickets cost nothing, and charities, B Corps, PTAs and not-for-profits get 50% off, as do very low-priced tickets. Seat reservations cost an extra credit per reserved seat. Prices switch by currency (GBP, EUR, USD, AUD, CAD) — these are the US ones. Stripe, PayPal or Square processing fees apply separately and Ticket Tailor never touches the payment.
tools.honest_knock: The fee honesty is the product — flat cents per ticket instead of percentage skims makes it dramatically cheaper than the big platforms on higher-priced tickets (a $0.30-0.85 fee on a $50 ticket vs a percentage is no contest). The trade: you bring your own audience. There's no discovery marketplace pushing your event, so if you rely on a platform's browsing traffic to sell out, the cheap fees won't fill seats.
tools.best_for: event organizers with their own audience (venues, communities, creators) who want flat low per-ticket fees, full branding and no subscription
tools.skip_if: you depend on marketplace discovery to sell tickets (Eventbrite's traffic is the fee you're paying for), or you run two events a year at tiny volume
compare_with: Eventbrite trades higher percentage fees for discovery traffic; Humanitix routes fees to charity — Ticket Tailor wins on raw cost per ticket

tools.name: Tidio
tools.what_it_does: Live chat, ticketing and the Lyro AI agent in one platform: AI answers routine questions from your own data, hands the rest to the team with context, and Flows chase leads proactively. Lyro also plugs into Zendesk, Intercom, Salesforce and 20+ platforms without migration, but only on Premium.
tools.pricing:
(read 2026-08-24 on www.tidio.com/pricing/ with both billing columns clicked, and on www.tidio.com) The plan table opens on the annual column, so the first figures on the page are not what month-to-month costs. Starter is 24.17 a month billed annually against 29 paid monthly, Growth starts at 49.17 annually against 59 monthly, and the two stand-alone add-ons follow the same 20 percent step: the Lyro AI Agent from 32.50 annually against 39 monthly, Flows from 24.17 against 29. Plus is 300 a month in both columns and adds usage on top; Premium is contact-for-pricing. Tidio's own homepage quotes the higher, monthly number (“Paid plans from $29/mo, no surprise upgrades”), which makes the marketing page the more conservative of the two places you can read a price. The table rendered in euros on our reading while the same numerals appear with dollar signs on other retrievals of the same URL, so treat the figure rather than the symbol as the fact and confirm the currency at checkout.

What you pay is decided by three separate meters, not by the plan name. The free plan carries 50 billable conversations, 100 Flows visitors reached and 50 Lyro AI conversations, and the comparison table's own footnote makes that last allowance a lifetime one rather than a monthly one. Starter covers 100 billable conversations, Growth starts at 250 and the table caps it at 2,000, both with 10 seats and a 7-day free trial. Lyro conversations are upgradable from 50 to 1,000 and Flows visitors from 2,000 to 100,000. Two things the page does not say: what a conversation over the cap costs, and what the “discounted usage rates” next to Plus's “+ monthly usage” actually are. On Plus that unquoted rate is the whole variable, because the 300 is only the entry fee.
tools.honest_knock:
The AI number on the homepage and the AI number on the pricing page do not agree, and the pricing page is the lower of the two. The homepage, read 24 August 2026, says Lyro “resolves 67% of conversations instantly” and repeats it as a statistic: 67% of conversations resolved instantly. The pricing table, read the same day, lists “Guaranteed 50% Lyro AI resolution rate” as a Premium feature — the most expensive tier on the page. So the figure the marketing quotes is 17 points above the figure the company is willing to guarantee, and the guarantee is only available if you talk to sales about the top plan. Both numbers can be true at once; a typical result and a contractual floor are different things. But it does mean that if you are buying on the strength of 67 percent, you are buying an average someone else achieved, not a commitment to you.

Second, the plan table opens on annual billing. The headline 24.17 and 49.17 become 29 and 59 the moment you click Monthly, and the two add-ons move 32.50 to 39 and 24.17 to 29. Nothing is hidden — the toggle is right there and the annual column is honestly labelled “2 months free” — but the number you remember from the pricing page is about 20 percent below the number you pay unless you commit for a year. Tidio's own homepage quotes the monthly figure, so the two pages leave a buyer with two different first impressions of the same plan.

Third, “Free plan forever” is true for the help desk and not for the AI. The free tier's 50 Lyro AI conversations are one-off: the comparison table footnote reads that your first 50 conversations are free (lifetime), and the same applies to the 100 Flows visitors. The live chat and ticketing side really does keep working at zero, but the AI agent that the whole homepage is built around stops after 50 conversations ever, which for a shop with any traffic is a matter of days. Read the free plan as a trial of Lyro inside a permanently free help desk, not as a free AI agent.
tools.best_for: support teams that want an AI agent and a help desk from the same vendor and can size all three meters — billable conversations, Lyro AI conversations and Flows visitors — against their own volume before they commit, and Shopify, WordPress or Wix stores that want to run live chat at zero and treat the 50 free Lyro conversations as a measurement of whether the AI answers their questions at all
tools.skip_if: you need the AI agent to keep answering past the first 50 conversations without paying, you cannot get the over-cap rate and the Plus usage rate quoted before signing, you want one per-seat price rather than three independent meters, or you are buying on the strength of the 67 percent resolution figure and need it as a commitment rather than an average

tools.name: TiXel
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app for Meta and TikTok pixels, with unlimited pixels, product-level scoping and server-side Events API tracking on one flat plan.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/tixel) One paid plan and no ladder to climb. Unlimited Plan is $19.99 a month, or $119.94 a year at a stated 50% saving, and carries unlimited pixels, server-side Events API pixels, regular pixels via pixel code, pixels scoped to specific products, automatic event triggers with no manual event configuration, and online support. The trial is three days. The other tier, Development Stores, is free but only for development and partner stores, and billing activates on upgrade — the same shape as this developer's Blocky listing, where the advertised free plan is also development stores rather than a working free tier. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched 19 October 2020 and had 78 reviews at a 4.1 rating at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock:
The 4.1 rating is the most useful number on this listing, but not for the reason an average usually is. The shape behind it is 67 five-star reviews, 4 four-star, none at three or two, and 7 one-star. Nothing sits in the middle. That is not a mediocre product; it is a binary one — it works immediately, or it installs cleanly and then tracks nothing at all.

The one-star reviews describe the same failure in the same words: the pixel is set up by the instructions, no page views or add-to-carts ever arrive, and support does not reply. One reviewer reports being charged for a service they say never worked and being refused a refund, after three days of use. We cannot verify what happened in any individual account, but the consistency of the complaint is itself information.

Set against that, the trial is three days. For a tracking tool that is short, because you need enough traffic through the store to see whether events actually land. Treat those three days as a test with a deadline, not a trial period.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants running Meta and TikTok ads who need more than the free channel apps give them — several pixels on one store, pixels scoped to individual products, or server-side Events API tracking alongside the browser pixel to recover events that ad-blockers and Safari strip
tools.skip_if: you run one pixel for one brand, since Shopify's Meta and TikTok channels do that for nothing; or you cannot put real traffic through the store within three days, because that is the whole trial and the reported failure is a pixel that tracks nothing

tools.name: TnC
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that puts a mandatory “I agree to the terms” checkbox on the cart and on the Buy It Now, PayPal and Apple Pay express buttons, logs the consent timestamp against the order, and can show it only for chosen products or countries for GDPR and age gates. From $7.99 a month, with the consent timestamp starting at $12.99; the checkbox inside Shopify's own checkout page needs Shopify Plus and a $19.99 tier the App Store listing does not show.
tools.pricing:
(read 2026-08-25 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article on effectify.help) Every paid tier costs more than it did a day earlier: read on 24 August 2026 the ladder was $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99, and read again on 25 August 2026 the same three plans, carrying the same feature lists, showed $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99. Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $7.99 a month or $67.12 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $12.99 a month or $109.12 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $14.99 a month or $125.92 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing article, last updated 25 August 2026, carries the same raised rates and lists a fifth plan the App Store listing does not: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one rate that did not move, so the gap between the top listed plan and the hidden one narrowed from $7 to $5. That article puts the annual saving at approximately 30% on every plan, which the listed annual rates match to the cent, and answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above” — while being the only page where the Plus Plan appears at all. It also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge.

Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and had 514 reviews at a 4.9 average at the time of writing. The listing names English, Vietnamese, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Chinese (Simplified) as supported languages.
tools.honest_knock:
Start with the badge at the top of the listing, because it is the one thing on this page that misleads. “Free plan available” is displayed twice, and the free plan is Development Stores — for development and partner stores only, with payment activated on upgrade. A store that takes real orders has no free tier here. It is the same shape as this developer's Blocky and TiXel listings, where the advertised free plan is also development stores rather than a working free tier, so read it as a house pattern rather than an oversight.

Second, the App Store's pricing table is incomplete. The vendor's own help-centre article lists a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month, Shopify Plus only, and describes it as the plan that shows the checkbox in the actual checkout page. The App Store listing shows four plans and not that one. The same article answers its own hidden-fees question with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above”, which is true of that article and not of the listing most buyers will read first. If you are on Plus and you want consent captured in checkout rather than in the cart, the price is two and a half times the headline.

Third, the feature that makes the app defensible costs extra, and what it costs is not stable. Basic at $7.99 shows the checkbox; it does not record when anyone ticked it. Consent-date logging starts on Advanced at $12.99. Read a day earlier, on 24 August 2026, those same two plans were $6.99 and $9.99 with identical feature lists, so the step from checkbox to audit trail went from $3 to $5 overnight while the listing said nothing about it. For an app whose pitch is chargebacks and legal risk, an audit trail as a paid upgrade is worth knowing before you compare $7.99 against anything else.

Fourth, be clear about what this can and cannot enforce. On a store that is not on Shopify Plus the checkbox lives in the cart and on express-checkout buttons, not inside Shopify's checkout, because Shopify does not open that page to apps below Plus. The listing is honest about the surfaces it does cover — cart drawers, Buy It Now, express checkout buttons, floating carts, PayPal and Apple Pay — but a shopper who reaches payment by another route has not passed a gate. Whether that is sufficient consent is a question for your own counsel rather than for an app listing.

Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views device and activity data including geolocation, IP address, browser and operating system and browsing behaviour, and can view and edit customers, products, orders for the last 60 days, store analytics, web pixels and the Online Store script tags and theme. Geolocation is what the country targeting on Advanced and above runs on, so the scope is explicable, but an app installed for compliance reasons that itself processes IP addresses and browsing behaviour belongs in the same register as everything else you had to write down.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants on a standard plan who need a recorded “I agree” gate before payment — for GDPR, an age gate, digital-goods withdrawal rules or chargeback defence — and who go to Advanced at $12.99 for the consent timestamp rather than stopping at the $7.99 headline
tools.skip_if: you are on Shopify Plus and want the checkbox inside the real checkout page, where the plan you need is the $19.99 Plus tier the App Store listing does not show; you expected a free tier from the listing's badge, which covers development and partner stores only; or a checkbox on the cart and the express buttons is not the enforcement your legal requirement actually asks for

tools.name: Todoist
tools.what_it_does: Task manager for individuals and small teams: quick capture, due dates and projects across devices. The free plan caps you at five projects and has no reminders, which moves most regular users to Pro at about $5/month billed annually. A to-do app, not a project suite with timelines or dependencies.
tools.pricing: Free (up to 5 projects, no reminders); Pro about $5/mo (annual, ~$7 monthly), Business about $8/user/mo (annual, ~$10 monthly) (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The free plan's 5-project cap and missing reminders push most serious users to Pro quickly — but Pro is genuinely cheap. It's a personal/team task manager, not a full project platform, so don't expect Gantt-level PM.
tools.best_for: individuals and small teams who want a fast, elegant task manager that gets out of the way
tools.skip_if: you need full project management with timelines, workloads and dependencies — this is a to-do app, not a PM suite

tools.name: Toggl
tools.what_it_does: Time tracking for freelancers, consultants and agencies, with budgets, rates and profitability per project. Free up to five users; Starter about $9/user/month on annual billing. The paid line is drawn at whether you bill clients — track time for personal discipline and the free tier covers it.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) Free covers a limited number of users, Starter is $9 per licence a month and Premium $14. But read the asterisk: that $14 applies to your first year of Premium annual, and then renews at $18 per licence a month. Enterprise is quoted. The renewal step is the thing to budget: a ten-person team on Premium goes from $1,680 in year one to $2,160 in year two, and it is stated on the page rather than hidden.
tools.honest_knock: Toggl's honesty problem is the good kind: the free tier is so capable that many teams never need to pay — the paid line is drawn exactly at 'do you bill clients' (budgets, rates, profitability). If you do, Starter earns itself fast; if you track time for personal discipline, resist the upgrade. Time tracking's real cost everywhere is adoption: the tool is frictionless, but the habit still has to be built.
tools.best_for: freelancers, consultants and agencies that bill by the hour and want frictionless tracking with budgets, rates and profitability per project
tools.skip_if: you need surveillance-style monitoring (screenshots, activity scoring — deliberately not Toggl's philosophy), or free-tier tracking already covers you
compare_with: the classic trio — Clockify undercuts on price, Harvest bundles invoicing; Toggl wins on tracking UX and reporting depth

tools.name: Top Echelon
tools.what_it_does: Recruiting software for agencies and staffing firms: TE Recruit is an ATS and CRM with resume parsing, pipeline management, hotlists and job-board integrations, while TE Network is a split-placement network for sharing roles and candidates with other recruiting firms.
tools.pricing: TE Recruit (the ATS and CRM) runs $75 per seat per month billed annually or $89 month-to-month on Standard, and $89 billed annually or $110 month-to-month on Professional. TE Network, the split-placement network, is priced per agency rather than per seat: $135 per month billed annually with the $350 startup fee waived, or $150 per month billed monthly plus a $350 one-time startup fee (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Almost everything people shop for sits in Professional, not Standard: Smart-TE AI, automations, sequences, inbound email sync and API access are all one tier up, so Standard is a competent but plain ATS. The bigger thing to price honestly is that TE Recruit and TE Network are two separate subscriptions. The network is billed per agency on top of your seats, so "Top Echelon" can mean two bills. And taking the network month-to-month adds a $350 one-time startup fee that annual billing waives.
tools.best_for: recruiting agencies and SMB staffing firms that want an applicant tracking system and CRM in one place, especially ones that would actually work split placements with other recruiters
tools.skip_if: you are an in-house talent team hiring for your own company — this is built around agency and split-placement workflows, so you would carry a network you never use

tools.name: Tradify
tools.what_it_does: Specialized job management software for trade businesses. Handle quoting, scheduling, and invoicing from the field.
tools.pricing: Per user, per month, quoted in USD on their own pricing page and re-verified 2026-08-16: Lite $47, Pro $51 and Plus $61 per user, plus a Custom tier for large teams that is priced on request. The 14-day free trial includes all features. The Instant Website add-on is $12 a month. There is no free plan and no volume ladder published on the page — the per-user rate is flat within a plan.
tools.honest_knock: Per-user pricing is honest and simple, but it means the cost scales linearly with headcount — a ten-person crew is a real monthly number, not the single-seat sticker. It's purpose-built for trades job management (quoting, scheduling, invoicing), so it's not a general project-management or accounting suite; you'll still run Xero or QuickBooks alongside it. For a trades business that's a feature, not a flaw.
tools.best_for: electricians, plumbers, HVAC and other trades businesses that want quoting, scheduling, job tracking and invoicing from the field in one simple app
tools.skip_if: you're a solo operator who invoices from a spreadsheet happily, or you need heavy project-management/accounting depth rather than trades job management
compare_with: close trades/field-service peers — compare on per-user cost and which accounting integrations you already run

tools.name: Trainerize
tools.what_it_does: Personal training and fitness-coaching platform. Deliver workout and nutrition plans, message clients and take payments from one branded app, so trainers can coach more clients online.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free for 1 client; Grow ~$9/mo (2 clients); Pro scales by client count (~$23/mo at 5 clients to ~$275/mo at 200); Studio Plus ~$248/mo per location. The add-ons are the real bill: nutrition $20-45/mo, payments $10/mo, video coaching $10/mo, branded app ~$169 one-time + $99/yr.
tools.honest_knock: The client-count ladder looks gentle, but working trainers switch on nutrition, payments and video — and the real monthly lands 30-50% above the sticker (a Pro-50 at ~$120 becomes ~$165+ dressed for work). Price the stack you'll actually coach with. That said, the client experience and ABC ecosystem are genuinely mature; churn-prone coaches lose more to a clunky app than to a fair subscription.
tools.best_for: personal trainers and studios delivering structured workout/nutrition coaching through a polished client app, scaling by client count
tools.skip_if: you coach a handful of clients over WhatsApp and sheets happily, or you want one flat price without add-on shopping
compare_with: the coaching-platform peer set — all use client-tiers plus add-ons; compare your fully-dressed stack price, not entry rows

tools.name: Trainual
tools.what_it_does: Documents SOPs and runs new-hire onboarding, with AI that drafts and updates training docs from your own account context. Not publicly priced: all four plans are quote-gated behind a demo, and the only figure the pricing page publishes is a one-time implementation fee of $1,000.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on trainual.com/pricing) No prices at all. The page lists four plans — Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise — and every one of them carries a "Get a demo" button where a rate would be. The only figure the page publishes is a one-time implementation fee of $1,000, stated in its own FAQ alongside a 4-6 week engagement with an implementation specialist. The FAQ also answers the sizing question directly: "Trainual is best suited for companies with 25 - 1000 employees", and says pricing varies with team size and the features you need. Pricing is quote-only. An earlier version of this entry carried monthly figures attributed to unnamed third-party sources; those are not on the vendor's page and could not be traced to a named source, so they have been removed rather than repeated.
tools.honest_knock: You cannot find out what it costs without booking a demo. All four plans — Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise — are quote-gated, and the single number the pricing page publishes is the one-time implementation fee of $1,000. The same page answers the sizing question plainly, best suited for companies with 25 to 1000 employees, so a small team is being told twice that it is not the buyer here: once by the fit range and once by a setup fee that arrives before the subscription does. Under a handful of staff, a shared doc may do.
tools.best_for: growing teams (roughly 10+ staff) that need to document SOPs and onboard new hires consistently instead of training by osmosis
tools.skip_if: you're a team of two or three — a well-organized Notion or Google Doc captures your processes without the seat-band pricing

tools.name: Tresorit
tools.what_it_does: End-to-end encrypted cloud storage and secure file sharing. Protect sensitive business documents with zero-knowledge security and granular access controls.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own business and personal pricing pages) There are three business plans: Professional for 1 user, Business from 3 users and Business Pro from 5 users. Priced from our location in euros, they run €29.99, €20 and €25 per user per month on monthly billing, and €23.99, €16 and €20 on yearly — which the page badges as 20% off. Personal runs a permanent free Basic tier plus Lite, Essential and Pro (€4.99, €11.99 and €29.99 a month from here). Our dollar reading of the same plans on 4 August 2026 gave Professional $33.99, Business $24 and Business Pro $30 per user per month. Storage runs 4 TB on Professional, from 6 TB on Business and from 15 TB on Business Pro, with maximum file sizes of 10, 15 and 20 GB. Every plan carries a 14-day trial with no feature limits, but Tresorit requires payment details up front to start it. Enterprise is quote-only.
tools.honest_knock: You pay the Swiss-E2EE premium — noticeably above mainstream clouds and above Proton Drive per GB — and the encryption trade-offs are inherent: no server-side content search, more deliberate sharing flows, and credential/recovery discipline is on you. For regulated teams that's exactly the deal; for casual storage it's over-engineering.
tools.best_for: businesses and professionals with confidentiality obligations (legal, health, finance) that need end-to-end-encrypted storage, granular sharing controls and compliance features
tools.skip_if: you want cheap bulk storage or deep app integrations (mainstream clouds win), or a personal-grade E2EE like Proton Drive covers your needs at lower cost
compare_with: Proton is the value E2EE pick for individuals; Tresorit's edge is enterprise admin, compliance and data residency — priced accordingly

tools.name: Turbotic
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise automation orchestration. Manage your entire ecosystem of RPA, AI, and scripts from a single control tower.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own product page) The Turbotic AI Assistant is $25 per seat per month and includes 1,500 credits a month, with additional credits bought as needed. The broader orchestration platform is not priced publicly at all: turbotic.com/pricing is now a demo-booking form with no figures on it, so everything above the assistant seat is quoted after a sales conversation. No free plan is mentioned.
tools.honest_knock: It's a newer, enterprise-leaning automation platform, so it's less proven with a smaller community than the big names — and the credit-per-execution model means heavy volume needs cost-checking. Verify it integrates with your actual stack first.
tools.best_for: teams that want an AI-assisted way to discover, document and run automations without deep RPA expertise
tools.skip_if: you need a huge, battle-tested integration ecosystem right now — an established platform has more connectors and community

tools.name: Typewise
tools.what_it_does: AI agents for customer service that resolve requests end to end and take action in the systems you already run — CRM, ERP, billing, commerce — configured in plain language instead of flowcharts. Pricing starts at $1 per resolution on their own site (read 2026-08-17) and there is no published plan table, so what counts as a resolution is the number to pin down before a pilot.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-05 on typewise.app/pricing, a page that did not exist in August) A base plan plus a per-resolution rate. Starter is $99 a month or $999 a year with 1 user, email and chat, a $20 monthly AI Operator budget and pay-as-you-go resolutions at $2 each. Growth is $599 a month or $5,999 a year with 5 users, all digital channels, a $100 AI Operator budget and volume packages that bring resolutions down to $1. Business is $2,000 a month billed annually with unlimited workspaces, a $1,500 AI Operator budget, a custom DPA and a success consultant. Additional users are $89 a month. Every plan starts with a 14-day trial of 100 resolution credits and $10 of AI Operator credit, no card. The page defines the meter: a full resolution counts once, and unresolved tickets are free. Prices are in USD and shown in EUR, GBP or CHF at parity depending on your location. History: in August 2026 the only published number was 'starting from $1 per resolution' on the home page and /pricing returned a 404.
tools.honest_knock: The bill has two parts now and both are published: a base fee from $99 and a resolution rate from $2 (pay as you go) down to $1 with volume packages. What the page defines is that a full resolution counts once and an unresolved ticket is free; what it still leaves to you is where the line falls in practice — whether a conversation handed to a human counts as resolved, and whether a reopened ticket counts again. Get those two answers in writing before the trial, because they decide whether the tool bills you most on the tickets it handles worst. The ROI calculator on their site is the vendor's own arithmetic; the pilot is where you replace it with yours.
tools.best_for: customer-service teams with real ticket volume that want AI agents to resolve requests end to end and act inside the systems they already run — CRM, ERP, billing, commerce — with approval steps and human handover as they raise the automation level
tools.skip_if: your helpdesk's built-in AI answers already absorb the volume, or your channel mix leans on phone support — their home page lists voice among the channels while their own SMB page still marks it "coming soon", so pin that down before you sign
compare_with: Intercom Fin or your helpdesk's native AI

the honest comparison is where the work happens: Fin lives inside Intercom's own desk, while Typewise sells itself as a layer above the stack you already run, reading and writing in CRM, ERP and commerce systems. Already on Intercom? The native option starts ahead. Support work spread across several systems? That layer is the argument — ask both what counts as a resolution before you compare the price

tools.name: UENI
tools.what_it_does: A done-for-you small-business website, built for you rather than a builder you have to learn: a one-time build fee (promoted at $79 against a usual figure near $599) plus $24.99/month, including domain, email and a launch call. DIY editing is limited and the seven-day promise often slips.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-22, read in a live browser on their own US pricing page) A done-for-you website, now sold in four tiers rather than one. Every tier carries the same setup fee of $599, currently promoted at $79. Launch is $24.99/mo and covers a custom-designed site, domain and SSL, hosting, one professional email address and 30 days of done-for-you edits. Plus is $59.00/mo and adds unlimited done-for-you edits, four email addresses, advanced SEO, integrations such as live chat and lead forms, promotion on Google, Facebook and Instagram, and VIP phone support. Ecommerce is $99.00/mo and adds a full online store with abandoned cart recovery, social selling, subscriptions and courses, advanced bookings and deposits, automated sales tax and a loyalty programme. Growth is $124.99/mo and adds a dedicated VIP Growth Team, a custom marketing plan, monthly one-on-one sessions and 2,000 words of fresh content a month. A yearly toggle advertises about 17% off: our August capture records $20.83 a month ($249.90 billed annually) on Launch and $49.17 ($590) on Plus, with two-year rates of $18.74 ($449.82) and $44.25 ($1,062). Transaction fees are 0% on every tier and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: It's done-for-you, which is the appeal and the catch. DIY editing and customisation are limited, e-commerce and integrations are basic, and the most common complaint is the gap between the 7-day promise and reality — slow design turnaround and patchy communication with the team. Expect some upselling.
tools.best_for: small-business owners with no time or tech skills who want a professional site built for them, not another tool to learn
tools.skip_if: you want full control over design, run a real e-commerce store, or need deep customisation and integrations — a DIY builder gives you more freedom
compare_with: a DIY builder like Wix or Squarespace

tools.name: UltaHost
tools.what_it_does: Budget-friendly web hosting across shared, VPS, WordPress and dedicated plans — NVMe SSD storage, free SSL and migration, DDoS protection and 24/7 multilingual support, from 30+ global data centers.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Term toggles are Monthly, Yearly (-30%), 2 Years (-40%) and 3 Years (-50%), and the pages default to the 2-year rate. Shared Starter is $3.44/mo (from $6.89) for 1 domain and roughly 10,000 visits a month, with the wider shared range running about $3.29 to $11.95 and VPS from about $10.99. The line to read on every card is the renewal: our August capture records plans renewing at $4.39 and $6.89 a month rather than at the promotional rate, so the advertised price buys the first term and the second term costs more.
tools.honest_knock: It's the classic budget-host trade-off, with one thing in its favour. The sticker price is a term commitment, not a monthly rate: the headline figures are the 2-year prices, the discount ladder runs -30% yearly, -40% for two years and -50% for three, and paying monthly gives all of it back. What has changed is the renewal. Each plan card now states it renews at the same rate for another 2 years, so the usual trap of a cheap first term followed by a dear one is at least written down. Read that line on the plan you actually pick, because it is quoted per plan. The headline rates also sit under a running 40%-off sale, so treat the crossed-out price as marketing rather than a baseline. Support is generally fast but can be hit-or-miss depending on which agent picks up your ticket, and it's a smaller, less-established brand than the big managed hosts. It's a value play, not a premium-SLA one.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious owners, developers and small businesses that want cheap, fast NVMe hosting (shared or VPS) with free migration and DDoS protection, and will prepay a multi-year term
tools.skip_if: you run a business-critical, high-traffic site that needs premium managed hosting with guaranteed enterprise support, or you don't want to lock into a multi-year term to get the good rate
compare_with: the comparable budget-to-mid hosts — Hostinger is the better-known value pick, SiteGround leans premium-managed; judge on the renewal rate and the support you'll actually need, not the intro price

tools.name: Unbounce
tools.what_it_does: Landing page builder for paid campaigns, with A/B testing and Smart Traffic routing each visitor to the best-converting variant. From $74/month (Build) to $187 (Optimize), and the visitor caps — around 20,000 a month on Build — push you up a tier when a campaign takes off.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page, USD) Five published levels, monthly against yearly at 25% off: Starter $29 / $22, Build $99 / $74, Experiment $149 / $112, Optimize $249 / $187, plus custom pricing above that. The Starter tier is missing from most summaries, ours included until this update, which described the range as beginning at $74. Pages are unlimited on every plan; what pushes you up a tier is the visitor cap, so a traffic spike rather than a page count is what changes your bill.
tools.honest_knock: The entry price is high for a landing-page tool, and the visitor caps bite if a campaign takes off. It's also oddly behind on basics — no URL import, limited file/code management, and still no true AI page generation in 2026.
tools.best_for: PPC specialists and agencies running paid campaigns who want A/B testing and Smart Traffic (AI routing each visitor to the best-converting variant)
tools.skip_if: your traffic or budget is small, or you want cheap unlimited pages — Landingi starts around $29/mo for similar basics
compare_with: the other premium and the budget landing-page builders

tools.name: Uniqode
tools.what_it_does: Dynamic QR codes and digital business cards with real-time scan analytics — connect offline touchpoints to measurable results and capture leads.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page) The plan cards are rendered in the browser and invisible to a non-browser client. So what we can hold Uniqode to is its own pricing FAQ, read on 12 August 2026. Static QR codes are free, and dynamic QR codes start at a stated minimum of $9/month. A custom domain is a Plus add-on at $2,000 per domain per year. Your first digital business card is free, with extra seats on a Team plan at $6 per user per month. Billing is annual. Third-party listings quote a $5 entry tier; that is not what Uniqode's own page says, and we are not repeating a Lite or Pro figure we could not read at the source.
