tools.honest_knock: The tier jumps are steep and a lot is gated: analytics are capped at 60 days on the entry plan, scan limits apply across all tiers, and custom domains sit behind higher pricing. It's a real QR platform — but overkill if you just want the occasional code.
tools.best_for: marketing teams that need dynamic QR codes with real analytics and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, optional HIPAA)
tools.skip_if: you only need the occasional static QR code — a free generator does that, and Bitly is better if link-shortening is your main job
compare_with: the link-shortener that bolted QR on

tools.name: UniTel Voice
tools.what_it_does: Virtual business phone system for small teams. Get a toll-free or local number with auto-attendant, call routing and a mobile app — no hardware.
tools.pricing: Four plans, no contracts (re-verified 2026-08-17): Start-Up $9.99/mo, Unlimited $24.99/mo, Office $29.99/mo and Office-Max $69.99/mo, with a stated saving of over 30% on annual billing and a 30-day money-back guarantee. The line to read before you size a team: additional users on the Office plans are $9.99 per user per month on top of the plan, added any time after signup. Support is US-based and included.
tools.honest_knock: It's a virtual phone layer, not a full unified-comms suite — you won't find the deep team messaging, video meetings and contact-center features pricier platforms bundle. For a solo founder or small team that just needs a professional number, auto-attendant and call routing, that focus is exactly the point; for a larger org wanting one platform for everything, it will feel thin.
tools.best_for: solopreneurs and small teams that want a professional toll-free or local number, auto-attendant and call routing on their existing phones — no hardware
tools.skip_if: you need integrated video meetings, team chat and a full contact center, or you have no need for a separate business line at all
compare_with: Grasshopper is a close, pricier equivalent; Google Voice is cheaper but barer — UniTel's Unlimited tier is the value play

tools.name: Unleashed Software
tools.what_it_does: Inventory and MRP software for manufacturers and wholesalers — real-time stock across warehouses, purchasing, sales orders and batch or serial tracking. The entry price covers 3 users and 100 sales orders a month; past that the bill stacks up.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on unleashedsoftware.com/pricing) Two bundles, in USD and excluding tax. Unleashed Core is $399 a month, or $4,389 a year which the page itself puts at $366 equivalent monthly. Unleashed Pro is $729 a month, or $8,019 a year at $668 equivalent monthly. The toggle promises “Save up to 10%”; the actual saving works out at 8.3% on Core and 8.4% on Pro. Both bundles come with a 14-day free trial with all features enabled. What the headline covers is the part worth reading twice: Core includes 3 user licences, Pro 5, and both include just 100 sales orders a month and 250,000 or 500,000 API calls. Everything past that is priced separately. Extra users are $69 a month on Core and $89 on Pro. Sales-order upgrades run $70 (up to 500), $200 (up to 1,500), $320 (up to 3,000) or $490 (unlimited) a month. And support is a paid add-on at $99 a month for Standard or $239 for Premier. Onboarding is a one-off fee on top: $449 self-service, $799 standard, $5,549 full. Optional modules start at $119 a month for Advanced Inventory Manager, $262 for Marketing Accelerator and $450 for CRM.
tools.honest_knock: The 100 sales orders a month included on both bundles is the number that decides your bill, not the $399. A wholesaler running 1,500 orders with six users who wants phone support pays $399 for Core, $200 for the order tier, $207 for three extra seats and $99 for Standard support. That is $905 a month, or 2.3 times the headline, before a one-off onboarding fee of at least $449. Support being a paid add-on rather than part of the plan is the detail most comparison tables miss. Price the bundle you will actually be on: count your busiest month's orders, your real seat count, and decide whether you can live without phone support, then compare that total against the alternatives rather than comparing entry prices.
tools.best_for: manufacturers and wholesalers who have outgrown spreadsheets and need real-time stock across multiple warehouses, with batch and serial tracking, landed costs and purchase-to-sale visibility in one system
tools.skip_if: your order volume is low or steady enough that the included 100 a month covers it and a lighter tool would do — at that size you are buying capacity you do not use, and the per-order tiers only pay back once volume is there

tools.name: Upsell.com
tools.what_it_does: Shopify upsell app, formerly ReConvert: AI-driven cart, checkout and post-purchase upsell and cross-sell funnels, frequently-bought-together and product page recommendations, A/B testing and analytics with segmentation. The free plan is development stores only, and the three published tiers — $4.99, $9.99 and $19.99 a month — stop at 200 orders or $200 of upsell revenue; above that the listing only says charges rise.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-02 on apps.shopify.com/reconvert-upsell-cross-sell) Billed in USD, with a 14-day free trial. The free plan is for development stores only, not a live shop. The three listed paid tiers all carry the same feature set — AI upsells, bundles and cross-sells, AI product recommendations, the full funnel across product page, cart, checkout and post-purchase, A/B testing, advanced analytics and segmentation, and 24/7 live chat support — and differ only in volume: Upsell Basic is $4.99 a month for up to 50 orders or $50 of upsell revenue, Upsell Growth $9.99 for up to 100 orders or $100, and Upsell Business $19.99 for up to 200 orders or $200. The listing adds that charges increase as monthly order volume or upsell revenue increases and points to a full pricing table it does not show, so what a store above 200 orders a month pays is not published on the app page.
tools.honest_knock: The prices on the listing are the bottom three rungs of a ladder that keeps going. Upsell Business, the most expensive tier shown, tops out at 200 orders or $200 of upsell revenue a month — a ceiling most stores worth installing an upsell app on will pass — and the page then says only that charges rise with volume, referring you to a full pricing table it does not display. The app page therefore cannot tell you what the app will cost you. Two smaller things compound it: the free plan is restricted to development stores, so there is no way to try it on a live shop without paying, and checkout upsells require Shopify Plus, which puts the checkout stage of the funnel out of reach on a standard Shopify plan.
tools.best_for: shopify merchants who want one funnel covering product page, cart and post-purchase offers with AI recommendations and A/B testing, and whose monthly order volume is still low enough that the published tiers apply
tools.skip_if: you do more than 200 orders a month and want to know the price before you install, because that part of the ladder is not on the app page — or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells
compare_with: Both cover the post-purchase and checkout upsell ground on Shopify, and AfterSell publishes what it costs across its whole range. Upsell.com, formerly ReConvert, publishes only its bottom three rungs — $4.99, $9.99 and $19.99, stopping at 200 orders a month — and refers everything above that to a pricing table the app page does not show. On features the two are close enough that for a growing store the deciding factor is the one thing Upsell.com will not put on the page: what it charges once you are actually busy.

tools.name: UpsellPlus
tools.what_it_does: Upsells, cross-sells and free gifts across Shopify product pages, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS, with AI recommendations and A/B testing in 23 storefront languages. Free plan runs one offer; Launch is $49/month, the Shopify Plus tier $119 and Scale $199 — each capped by how much upsell revenue it may generate ($500, $2,000 and $5,000 a month).
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-31 on apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout) Four tiers, billed in USD, with a 14-day free trial on the paid ones. Free runs one offer, opens all twelve upsell types plus analytics, and allows up to $500 in upsell revenue. Launch is $49 a month or $500 a year (the listing says that saves 15%) and also allows up to $500 of app-generated revenue a month, adding cart, pop-up and drawer upsells, product page and post-purchase upsells, multivariate A/B testing, progress bars and free gifts. The Shopify Plus tier is $119 a month or $1,149 a year (save 20%), raises the ceiling to $2,000 a month and adds checkout customization, checkout upsells, thank-you page customization and AI recommendations. Scale is $199 a month or $1,899 a year (save 20%) for up to $5,000 of upsell revenue a month, live support and multivariate A/B testing.
tools.honest_knock: The plans are capped by the revenue they are allowed to earn you, and the first paid step does not raise that cap: Free and the $49 Launch plan both stop at $500 of upsell revenue a month. The $49 buys offers and features, not headroom — headroom starts at $119. The listing also never says what happens when a store passes Scale's $5,000 ceiling, which is precisely the moment the app is working, so ask before you build a checkout flow around it. And read the feature list closely: checkout upsells are marked Plus-only, meaning your store has to be on Shopify Plus, so on a standard Shopify plan the checkout half of an app called Checkout Upsell is not what you are buying.
tools.best_for: shopify merchants who want one app covering product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS offers rather than three, especially Shopify Plus stores, where the checkout half of the product actually unlocks
tools.skip_if: your upsell revenue sits near the $500 ceiling that Free and the $49 plan share — the first paid step buys features, not headroom — or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells
compare_with: Both are Shopify upsell apps and both are strongest around the checkout. AfterSell is the tighter, better-known post-purchase and checkout play; UpsellPlus spreads wider — product page, cart drawer, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and Shopify POS in one app, with 23 storefront languages and integrations into Klaviyo, Recharge, Appstle, Skio and Smartrr. The catch is the revenue ceiling on each UpsellPlus tier, so compare on the plan you would actually need rather than on the entry price: free and $49 stop at the same $500 a month.

tools.name: UptimeRobot
tools.what_it_does: Uptime monitoring with a generous free tier — website, port, keyword and API checks down to 60-second intervals, status pages, integrations and mobile apps.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-26 on uptimerobot.com/pricing over a US connection) Free is $0. Solo starts at $144 a year, Team is $468 and Scale starts at $948 — the page quotes yearly, not monthly, which makes it look cheaper per line than it is against monthly-priced rivals. Login seats are the upsell: none on Solo, three on Team, five on Scale, and more at $15 or $19 each a month. Data retention runs three months on Free, twelve on Solo and twenty-four above that. They publish a machine-readable version of this page for AI agents, which is rare enough to be worth noting.
tools.honest_knock: The famous free tier is real — but the paid ladder has quiet extras: extra login seats cost $15-19 per month EACH beyond the included ones, and SMS or voice-call alerts are pay-per-credit on every plan. The Solo tier includes no team seats at all.
tools.best_for: solo builders and small teams monitoring sites, ports and APIs at 60-second resolution with status pages — and honestly, the free 50-monitor tier covers most hobby stacks
tools.skip_if: you need many teammates in the dashboard (seats are a paid add-on) or heavy SMS alerting — credits stack on top of the subscription
compare_with: Pingdom is the enterprise-polish incumbent at a higher entry price; UptimeRobot's free tier and cheap solo plans win for small stacks — watch the seat and SMS add-ons as the team grows

tools.name: VEA
tools.what_it_does: AI built for entrepreneurs, not enterprises: VEA learns your business like a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it — then finds the next one.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-02 on VEA's own pricing page) Four tiers now, per user per month, monthly against annual: $30 / $25, $50 / $40, $150 / $120 and $597 / $497. The three-tier ladder we read in August ($31.95 / $24.95, $49.95 / $39.95, $77.95 / $59.95) was replaced between our 2 August and 1 September 2026 captures: the two lower tiers were rounded to whole dollars, the old top tier at $77.95 is gone, the new third tier costs roughly double it, and a fourth tier sits above that. The page's marketing line still says 'Starting at $24.95 per user per month', a figure no longer on the plan cards. Annual billing saves roughly 17% to 20%. The tiers are separated by how much the AI does rather than by seats: the entry plan is task tracking and team alignment, First Class adds AI agents handling routine work, and Private Jet adds AI analysis and decision guidance.
tools.honest_knock: The pitch is unusually bold: an AI that learns your business the way a great employee would, finds the constraint keeping you stuck, and helps you solve it. That ambition is also the honest caveat — it's a young product making a big promise, its price ladder was rebuilt in August 2026 with a top tier at $597 per user a month, and independent review coverage is still thin. Judge it in the trial on one measurable question: did it identify a constraint you recognize as painfully real? If yes, it earns the next month. If its advice stays generic — the thing its own positioning promises to avoid — walk.
tools.best_for: hands-on entrepreneurs and small-business owners buried in operational detail who want AI that learns their specific business and helps surface what's actually holding it back — explicitly not enterprise software
tools.skip_if: you run a larger organization with established teams and processes (VEA itself positions against that), or you need a task-specific tool rather than a business-level advisor
compare_with: a generic AI assistant or a human business coach
VEA's bet is business-specific context and constraint-finding — evaluate whether its advice concretely beats what a generic assistant gives you for free

tools.name: Velora
tools.what_it_does: Unified operations platform for nonprofits: Keela (donor CRM), Aplos (fund accounting) and Raisely (online fundraising) as one connected suite — donor management, campaigns and finances built for charities instead of adapted from business software.
tools.pricing: Quote-only. joinvelora.com (read in a browser on 5 September 2026) has no pricing page and no amount anywhere; every call to action is 'Talk to sales'. Velora bundles Keela (CRM), Aplos (accounting) and Raisely (fundraising) for nonprofits, and the individual product prices we recorded earlier (Keela from about $134 a month, Aplos from about $79) are no longer shown on the unified site, so treat them as historical until sales confirms.
tools.honest_knock: Velora is three acquired products (Keela, Aplos, Raisely) being unified into one platform, and that's the honest watch-out: integration between them is newer than the marketing suggests, so check how deeply the pieces actually connect for your workflow before committing. Costs also stack per product and per contact count — a growing donor base raises the CRM bill. For nonprofits though, purpose-built beats adapted business software in fund accounting specifically.
tools.best_for: nonprofits that want donor CRM, fund accounting and online fundraising from one vendor, purpose-built for charities rather than adapted business tools
tools.skip_if: you're a tiny charity that only needs a donation page (free tools cover that), or you're deeply invested in one best-of-breed piece already
compare_with: the legacy giant vs a DIY stack — Velora sits between: integrated and nonprofit-native without Blackbaud's enterprise weight

tools.name: Vida AI
tools.what_it_does: Deploy autonomous frontline voice agents. Let AI answer calls, book appointments, and handle FAQs 24/7 without sounding robotic.
tools.pricing: Quote-oriented (2026): agency/reseller plans from about $750/mo (a starter tier carries 5 agents and ~2,500 AI voice minutes; growth tiers advertise unlimited agents and minutes) and platform/service-provider plans from ~$2.5k/mo. Verify current tiers with sales.
tools.honest_knock: This is priced for agencies and telecoms reselling AI phone agents, not for a single small business wanting one receptionist bot — if that's you, the entry price buys far more platform than you need. And the universal truth of voice AI: demo calls are rehearsed, your callers aren't. Pilot it on your real call types (accents, interruptions, edge requests) and measure containment rate before betting the front desk on it.
tools.best_for: agencies, MSPs and service providers that want to deploy and resell white-label AI voice agents at volume, with unlimited-minute economics at scale
tools.skip_if: you're one business wanting one AI receptionist (single-business voice-AI tools are far cheaper), or your call flows are too high-stakes to automate yet
compare_with: builder-oriented voice-AI platforms — Vida's edge is the reseller/white-label model; compare per-minute economics at your projected volume

tools.name: VidPal
tools.what_it_does: Autonomous content engine for faceless and topic-based channels: it discovers trending stories in your niche, auto-generates short-form videos and carousels with AI voiceovers, and auto-publishes them across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and more.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Free: 4 lifetime credits, standard-quality exports, "Made with Vidpal.ai" watermark, no card. Starter $12/mo billed annually ($144/yr) or $24 monthly, 15 credits/mo; Pro $23/mo annually ($276/yr) or $46 monthly, 40 credits, auto-publish and scheduling, 2K exports; Business $41/mo annually ($492/yr) or $82 monthly, 100 credits, 4K, three daily slots; Enterprise on quote. One credit is a Reel, a carousel, an editing upload or ten minutes of clip source; an AI Avatar or long-form video is five. Monthly credits do not roll over, annual credits arrive as a yearly pool, and top-up packs expire after 60 days. Refunds cover the unused credit balance within 30 days.
tools.honest_knock: Credits don't carry over month to month, and a few users report slow support/account responses — so run the free plan through a full create-and-publish loop before you pay.
tools.best_for: creators and small brands running faceless or topic-based channels that want the trend-find, generate and auto-publish loop handled in one tool across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube
tools.skip_if: you want hands-on creative control over every video, or your brand can't afford auto-published AI content going out without a human check

tools.name: Vista Social
tools.what_it_does: Unified social media management and publishing. Schedule posts, manage conversations, and track analytics across all your brand accounts.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Professional $79/mo ($758/yr) — 15 profiles, 2 users, 10,000 DM contacts, 1,000 AI credits/mo; Advanced $149/mo ($1,430/yr) — 30 profiles, 4 users, 25,000 contacts, 2,000 credits, Zapier/Make/MCP; Scale $349/mo ($3,638/yr) — 70 profiles, 8 users, 100,000 contacts, 3,500 credits, white label and client connect; Enterprise custom with unlimited profiles and users. Yearly billing is 20% off on Professional and Advanced but 13% on Scale. Add-ons on every tier: listening across social, web and news from $75/mo, X (Twitter) $29/mo, Employee Advocacy free for 3 advocates then from $199/mo for 25. 14-day trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: It undercuts the big suites convincingly. The honest check is coverage depth: platform APIs change constantly, so verify the specific networks and features YOUR clients need (particularly newer TikTok/threads capabilities and approval workflows) inside the trial rather than trusting the comparison table. Agencies stepping up from Professional hit the Scale tier for white-labeling — price that step into client contracts from day one.
tools.best_for: agencies and multi-brand teams that want scheduling, listening, reviews and reporting across many profiles at a notably lower price than legacy suites
tools.skip_if: you manage one or two profiles (free/native tools suffice), or you need enterprise-grade approval chains and support SLAs the big suites specialize in
compare_with: the premium incumbents — Vista's pitch is 80-90% of the feature set at a fraction of the seat price; verify your critical 10% in the trial

tools.name: Volza
tools.what_it_does: Export-import trade intelligence: search customs-level shipment records to find verified buyers and suppliers. Startup is $1,500 a year for 182 countries and 2 users; the 200-country coverage and 10 users start at $4,500 (read 2026-09-01). Downloads run on a published credit allowance, from 360,000 full-shipment credits a year.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-09-01 on volza.com/pricing) Three paid annual plans and a free trial. Startup is $1,500 a year: 182 countries (44 export and 50 import detailed databases, 160 export and 158 import mirror databases, 7 export and 7 import one-side databases, premium countries excluded), data from 2014 onward, 6,000 searches, full shipment view, 360,000 full-shipment download credits and 2 users. SME is $4,500 a year: 200 countries, adds the statistical databases (46 export, 48 import), unlimited searches under fair use, 1,040,000 download credits and 10 users. Corporate is $9,600 a year: the same 200-country coverage, unlimited searches under fair use, 2,400,000 download credits and 15 users. The free trial runs 7 days with no card, is advertised as "$50 On sign up + Unlimited Volza credits", shows the last three years in full view with a six-month preview, and carries no full-shipment download credits. An annual and a 2-year value plan are offered as billing terms. The page also states a refund promise: if you find no profitable opportunity, Volza will help you find one or refund in full.
tools.honest_knock: Three honest catches. The entry plan is narrower than the marketing implies: $1,500 a year covers 182 countries and two users, while the 200-country coverage and ten seats start at $4,500. Downloads run on a credit allowance — 360,000 a year on Startup — and an earlier reading of the catalogue put the cost per record at one credit for US or India shipments and up to ten in thinner markets; that per-country rate is not stated on the current pricing page and we could not re-verify it on 1 September 2026, so treat it as a question for sales rather than a fact. And the update cycle is slow, with some datasets taking up to two months to refresh, which suits structural questions far better than reactive ones. There is a learning curve too; it rewards analysts, not casual users.
tools.best_for: import-export businesses and sourcing teams that want global customs-level trade data plus verified buyer/supplier contacts at a fraction of enterprise pricing
tools.skip_if: you only need US shipment data with fast daily updates (ImportGenius refreshes daily), or you're not doing import/export — this is a niche intelligence tool
compare_with: the US-focused faster-updating one and the pricey enterprise incumbent

tools.name: Voye
tools.what_it_does: Pooled eSIM data for travelling teams, billed on actual usage rather than prepaid bundles, with per-user spend controls. Coverage and speed vary by country and carrier partner, so pilot your heaviest routes first — the vendor's roaming-savings figures stay claims until your invoice confirms them.
tools.pricing: Published plans (read 6 September 2026 on their plans page). Monthly, 30-day validity: $9.99 for 5 GB, $19.99 for 12 GB, $39.99 for 30 GB, $69.99 for 55 GB, $119.99 for 100 GB — $2.00 down to $1.20 per gigabyte. Yearly, a single payment, 365-day validity: $500 for 200 GB, $1,000 for 450 GB, $2,000 for 950 GB, $3,500 for 1,800 GB — $2.50 down to $1.94 per gigabyte. Three-month billing is exactly three times the monthly price, with no discount. Enterprise — unlimited eSIMs, priority support and onboarding — is quoted by their sales team.
tools.honest_knock: eSIM data pooling genuinely beats classic roaming for traveling teams, but the honest homework is coverage-and-speed on YOUR corridors: quality varies by country and local carrier partner, so pilot with two or three of your heaviest travelers before migrating everyone. And note the vendor-cited savings numbers are marketing math until your own invoice confirms them.
tools.best_for: companies with regularly traveling teams that want one pooled global data contract, per-user controls and an end to roaming bill surprises
tools.skip_if: travel is rare (per-trip consumer eSIMs are simpler), or your destinations are few enough for local SIM discipline
compare_with: the business-eSIM field — compare per-GB rates on your actual destination list, not the global average

tools.name: VWO
tools.what_it_does: A/B testing and conversion optimization platform. Run experiments, heatmaps and personalization to lift conversions without developers.
tools.pricing: No price is published any more. Read in a browser on 4 September 2026, vwo.com/pricing lists Growth, Pro and Enterprise as feature tables only: every tier's button is 'Schedule a Demo' and no amount, MTU tier or traffic slider appears anywhere on the page, nor in vwo.com/llms.txt. The ~$314/mo for 10k MTUs this dossier carried until that date was a published figure the vendor has since withdrawn. There is a 30-day free trial, no credit card required.
tools.honest_knock: The jump from Growth to Pro is steep — small businesses get priced out of MVT and complex targeting — and the UI is dense with options. Some users note the reporting breaks more often than pricier tools (though it doesn't affect the tests themselves). The part that costs people money later is what happens to a winner. VWO applies page changes through its SmartCode — their own page says the asynchronous SmartCode “loads page changes asynchronously when the web page loads” — so a variant left running in the editor is rendered by VWO rather than built into your site. Fine while you pay, gone when you stop. Their server-side testing changes the arithmetic here, because those changes live in your own stack; the client-side ones do not.
tools.best_for: teams that want an all-in-one experience-optimisation platform (A/B testing + heatmaps + personalisation) with friendlier Bayesian stats and transparent pricing
tools.skip_if: you're a small business wanting advanced targeting/MVT on the entry tier (you'll be priced up), or an enterprise running massive concurrent experiments — Optimizely handles that scale

tools.name: Warmup Inbox
tools.what_it_does: Standalone email warm-up service — automated inbox warming, deliverability monitoring and integrations for Google, Outlook, Zoho and SendGrid.
tools.pricing: (re-read 2026-09-05 on warmupinbox.com/pricing, both billing toggles) Three tiers, priced per inbox. Billed monthly: Basic $19 an inbox a month for 75 warmup messages a day, Pro $59 for 250 a day, Max $99 for 1,000 a day. Billed yearly the same three read $15, $49 and $79 a month ($180, $588 and $948 a year), which is the 20% saving the page advertises. The tiers also differ on the reply rate to your warmup mail — up to 25% on Basic, 45% on Pro and 50% on Max — and Pro adds your own templates, chosen warmup topics, language warmup and scheduled warmup. There is a free trial with no credit card, and the vendor states more than 30,000 real inboxes in the network.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is published and readable — three tiers, per inbox, with both billing toggles printing a rate: $19, $59 and $99 monthly, or $15, $49 and $79 on the yearly plan. The bigger caveat is structural: warmup is priced per inbox, so a team running twenty sending addresses pays twenty times the headline. And warmup is a floor, not a ceiling — it builds sender reputation, but no amount of it rescues a bad list or a bad offer.
tools.best_for: outbound teams warming new sending domains and inboxes before campaigns, with integrations across Google, Outlook, Zoho and SendGrid
tools.skip_if: you want to compare costs before creating an account — the public page will not let you — or your sending volume is too low to need dedicated warm-up
compare_with: lemwarm comes bundled with lemlist outreach seats; Warmup Inbox is the standalone warm-up specialist with broader inbox integrations — but check its in-app pricing first, the public page shows none

tools.name: Wati
tools.what_it_does: WhatsApp Business API platform for sales and support: shared team inbox, bulk broadcasts and no-code chatbots — plus Astra, its AI agent builder for agents that actually resolve conversations (orders, refunds, bookings, lead qualification) across WhatsApp, web and voice. Its omnichannel inbox now also carries TikTok DMs natively (all plans, no extra cost) alongside Instagram and RCS — with ad-to-chat context that shows exactly which TikTok ad triggered a conversation. It now ships its own MCP server as well: connect Claude or ChatGPT once and manage contacts, send WhatsApp campaigns, read past chats and build agents in plain language, while sends still run on your own approved templates and the full history stays in the Wati dashboard. Wati's own page puts the cost like this: free for current paid Astra customers with no usage cap during launch, and full MCP access on every Astra plan for new customers (checked 4 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page — which served us euros, not dollars) Growth €59/mo, Pro €119/mo and Business €279/mo billed annually, with a 7-day free trial and no setup fee. Users are capped per tier: Growth includes 3 and lets you add none at all; Pro and Business include 5, with extra seats at €39 and €89 per user per month. Add-ons are separate again — 1,000 automation triggers €35/mo, 1,000 AI co-pilot credits €25/mo, Shopify $4.99/mo, each extra WhatsApp number €29/mo. Our dollar reading of the same page on 23 July 2026 gave Growth $39, Pro $79 and Business $199 annually, so which currency and which figure you see depends on where Wati places you — check your own checkout before you budget. On top of all of it sit Meta's own per-conversation message fees, which Wati bills through at its own rate card.
tools.honest_knock: The plan price is the smallest part of the bill. Growth is capped at three users and you cannot buy a fourth at any price, so growing past three people forces the jump to Pro; from there extra seats are $24 each, and $69 each on Business. Automation triggers, AI credits, the Shopify link and every additional WhatsApp number are all separately metered, and Meta's per-conversation fees land on top of the lot. Model your real message volume and seat count before committing — that is where the money actually goes.
tools.best_for: businesses that want to run WhatsApp support and broadcasts at scale with a shared team inbox and automation
tools.skip_if: your customers aren't on WhatsApp or your volume is tiny — the platform fee plus per-message costs aren't worth it for a trickle
compare_with: Interakt or a direct Meta BSP

tools.name: Way
tools.what_it_does: Shopify store locator on Google Maps with no API key needed, priced by location count rather than by feature.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on apps.shopify.com/sticky-navigate-to-store) Four tiers, and above the first one the ladder is a location counter rather than a feature list. Free carries one store location, the floating Google Maps locator, appearance customisation and online support, with the app's own branding shown on your storefront. Basic is $9.99 a month or $95.90 a year and removes that branding, raising the limit to 50 locations and adding the map widget as an app block, a pop-up modal for multiple locations, full customisation with custom CSS, and bulk import and export. Advanced at $19.99 or $191.90 a year and Pro at $39.99 or $383.90 list exactly the same eight features as Basic; what they add is headroom, 500 locations and 2,000. Annual billing saves a stated 20% on every paid tier and each carries a 7-day free trial. No Google Maps API key is required on any plan. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps; the app sits in Shopify's store locator category and had 126 reviews at a 4.7 rating when the pricing was re-read on 25 August 2026.
tools.honest_knock:
The pricing page reads like a feature ladder and behaves like a counter. Basic, Advanced and Pro list the same eight capabilities, so the $10 and $20 steps above Basic buy nothing but a higher location limit, and the jump from 50 to 500 leaves no tier in between. A chain with 60 or 80 shops pays the 500-location price and uses a tenth of it.

The free plan is genuinely usable on a live store, which is worth saying plainly — the same developer's Blocky and TiXel listings advertise free plans that turn out to be development stores only, and this one is not that. What it does carry is the app's branding on your storefront and a hard limit of one location, so it is a real free tier for a single shop rather than a trial in disguise.
tools.best_for: retailers and brands with physical stockists who want a Google Maps locator on their Shopify storefront without setting up a Maps API key or paying Google directly — the app handles the key on every tier, including the free one, which removes the developer step
tools.skip_if: you have one shop and do not mind the app's branding under your map, because the free tier already covers you; or you need routing, appointment booking or stock-by-location, since this maps and directs and does not do any of that

tools.name: Weave
tools.what_it_does: Phone, texting, payments and reviews unified for the front desk, tuned to dental, optometry and small healthcare practices. Quote-based per location: owners commonly report $400–700 per location per month plus a one-time setup fee near $750. Get the all-in number in writing.
tools.pricing: Weave sells a per-location monthly subscription and its pricing page (weavehq.com/pricing, read 5 September 2026) now states plans start from $199 per location a month, though the exact tier ladder is still only shown after a demo. Practice owners commonly report all-in costs of roughly $400 to $700 a location once phones, payments and add-ons are bundled, plus a one-time setup fee of about $750. Quote-driven above the floor.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. The $199 starting price is a floor, not the bill: add-ons, setup and per-location fees land on top, and the full tier ladder is only shown in a demo, so get everything in writing. And it's deeply tuned for healthcare and appointment-based practices; a general small business will find much of the workflow assumes a front desk and a patient schedule.
tools.best_for: dental, optometry and small healthcare practices that want phone, texting, payments and reviews unified for the front desk
tools.skip_if: you're outside healthcare/practice verticals, or you're a single small office where a simple VoIP line and a separate review tool cost far less
compare_with: Podium or a standalone VoIP plus review tool
Podium is a close communications peer; a DIY stack is cheaper but less integrated — weigh the all-in quoted cost

tools.name: WebCatalog
tools.what_it_does: Turn web apps into tidy desktop apps and manage multiple accounts side by side. Less tab chaos, more focus — your whole stack organized in one place.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-25 on their own pricing page, re-read 2026-09-05 from a European connection where it prices in euros: Pro €4.31 and Business €6.89 per user a month billed annually, plus local taxes) Basic is free and no card is required: 2 desktop apps, 2 profiles, 1 space, 1 page and 5 links. Pro is $5 per user per month billed annually, plus local taxes, and lifts those caps to unlimited apps, profiles, spaces and pages with cloud backup and sync. Business is $8 per user per month billed annually and adds shared spaces, team management, centralised billing and an activity log, with SAML single sign-on as a paid add-on. Both paid plans carry a 7-day trial, and a legacy lifetime licence still exists without cloud sync.
tools.honest_knock: It solves a real annoyance: dozens of web apps and multiple accounts per app as tidy desktop windows. The honest question is whether you need the paid tier at all. The free plan's 2-app limit is tight, but browser profiles and PWAs solve part of the same problem for free. Pro earns its fee when multi-account juggling (several Gmail/Slack/WhatsApp identities) is daily reality.
tools.best_for: people juggling many web apps and multiple accounts per service who want them as clean, separate desktop apps with per-profile isolation
tools.skip_if: browser tab discipline or built-in PWA installs already cover you, or you use a handful of apps with single accounts
compare_with: Rambox is the direct competitor with similar pricing; PWAs are the free baseline — pay only if profile isolation is your real pain

tools.name: Webflow
tools.what_it_does: Visual website builder that writes production code — design, CMS, hosting and ecommerce in one place.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-04, read on their own pricing page with every plan accordion and billing tab open) Webflow bills in two places at once. Site plans, billed yearly: Starter free; $15/mo for a site that does not need a CMS (custom domain, 300 static pages, 10 GB bandwidth); $25/mo for the CMS tier, which the page now calls Premium. Ecommerce site plans are separate again: Standard $29/mo with 500 items and a 2% transaction fee, Plus $74/mo with 5,000 items and no transaction fee, Advanced $212/mo with 15,000 items. Workspace plans, also billed yearly: Starter free (2 staging sites, 1 full seat), Core $19/mo, Growth $49/mo, and on the freelancer-and-agency tab Freelancer $16/mo and Agency $35/mo. Seats are charged on top of the workspace plan: a full seat is $39/mo billed yearly, a limited seat $15/mo, a review-only seat $0. Platform plans start at Team $2,500/mo with an annual contract required, and Enterprise above it is quote-only. Add-ons: Optimize from $299/mo by page views, Analyze from $9/mo by sessions, Localize Essential $9/mo and Localize Advanced $29/mo by number of locales, 2,000 AI credits $20/mo billed yearly, and a published bandwidth ladder running from +50 GB at $20/mo billed annually to +2.45 TB at $974/mo, with monthly billing about half again as expensive at every step. Webflow Cloud overages run at $2 per million requests and $2 per 5 hours of CPU usage, with web app bandwidth pooled into the site plan's bandwidth. Storage is priced on that page again: on the Basic and CMS site plans the D1 and KV stores include 100 MB and then run at $2 per 500 MB, and R2 object storage at $2 per 5 GB; on the Team plan those same lines read $2 per GB. (Re-verified 2026-08-29 on the pricing page itself: every plan, seat and add-on price above was unchanged.)
tools.honest_knock: Three separate bills, and the pricing page shows them on separate tabs. A site plan is what puts your site online: $15 a month for a static site, $25 with the CMS. A workspace plan is what lets your team work on it: $19 or $49 a month. And seats are charged on top of the workspace plan at $39 a month each for anyone who can actually design. So a two-person team on a CMS site is not $25 a month — it is $25 for the site, $19 for the workspace and $39 for the second seat, which is $83, and that is before add-ons. Two more numbers to find before you commit. The entry ecommerce plan takes a 2% transaction fee on every order, which the $29 headline does not mention and which is the largest single cost for anyone selling real volume; removing it means Plus at $74. And Optimize, the conversion tooling Webflow leads with in its marketing, starts at $299 a month on top of everything else and is priced by page views. Price your team, your site and your add-ons together, because no single tab on that page shows you a total.
tools.best_for: designers and marketing teams who want to ship a real, fast site without a developer in the loop for every change, and who value that the CMS and hosting are the same product as the editor
tools.skip_if: you are one person publishing a simple site. The free tier and a $15 site plan cover that, and the reason to be here is the team workflow you are not using. Also skip the entry ecommerce plan if you sell in any volume, because 2% of every order will outrun the $45 a month that Plus costs extra
compare_with: the two directions people leave for — Framer for a simpler visual builder, WordPress for cheaper hosting and more plugins; compare the total of site plan, workspace and seats, not the entry sticker

tools.name: WebinarGeek
tools.what_it_does: European live and automated webinar platform — viewer-tier pricing, engagement tools, CRM integrations and GDPR-friendly hosting. The vendor states you can now generate a full webinar — including polls, quizzes and a registration page — from a plain-text description, with UTM tracking and post-webinar redirects on the registration page (vendor mail, August 2026).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) The plan figures render client-side, and neither our monthly captures nor a plain fetch retrieves them. The page carries a currency switch across EUR, USD, GBP, SEK, NOK and DKK, and advertises up to 50% off for annual billing. So both the number and the currency depend on where you buy. Our dated reading gives Premium €69/mo (€49 billed annually) for 50 viewers, Advanced €99/mo (€69 annually) scaling from 125 to 1,000 viewers, and Enterprise from €349/mo. Add-ons are billed separately and annually: localisation €20/mo, AI assistant €20/mo, extra workspace €59/mo, HubSpot €49/mo and Salesforce €49/mo.
tools.honest_knock: The friendly €49 headline is the annual rate for just 50 viewers, and the real cost lives in add-ons: localization, the AI assistant, CRM integrations and extra workspaces are each €20-59 a month on top. A serious webinar stack quickly doubles the base plan.
tools.best_for: marketing and sales teams running live and automated webinars in Europe who want a polished, GDPR-friendly platform with viewer-tier pricing
tools.skip_if: you run occasional small webinars (your video-call tool may cover it), or you need the CRM and localization features that sit behind paid add-ons
compare_with: Livestorm is the browser-based all-rounder; WebinarGeek is the European specialist with strong automation — watch the per-add-on pricing as your needs grow

tools.name: Wegic
tools.what_it_does: AI website builder that generates and hosts sites from a conversation — credit-based, with custom domains and code export on higher tiers, and built-in image generation powered by ChatGPT Image-2 (upload a reference or prompt, drop the result straight into your design). It can also turn a single product photo or mockup into a ready-to-sell product page. A one-click optimize pass audits a published site for SEO and site-health problems and applies the fixes itself — vendor-announced in July 2026, and not something we have tested.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-30 on wegic.ai/en/pricing from a US exit) Credit-based AI website builder, priced in US dollars. Free: 100 credits at signup only, which Wegic's FAQ describes as credits to chat with the AI — generating a site is a paid action. Trial pack $2.99, covering one full website generation. Starter $39.90/month, or $286.80 a year — $23.90/month, the advertised 40% off — for 600 credits/mo (~$0.04/credit), a permanent .wegic.net address, code export, e-commerce product display, website analytics and removal of the Wegic watermark. Premium $69.90/month, or $502.80 a year ($41.90/month), for 2,000 credits/mo (~$0.02/credit), a custom domain and up to 70% off extra credit purchases. Wegic's own Stripe catalogue also carries two- and three-year terms that the plan table does not show: Starter $525.60 and $680.40, Premium $885.60 and $1,220.40. A separate Wegic Cloud balance for AI image and video generation runs on top: $20/month of credit on Starter, $35 on Premium. Credits do not roll over — the balance is wiped at the end of every billing month, and when a subscription ends published sites stay live for 7 more days.
tools.honest_knock: Everything is credits, and generating a site burns them fast — Wegic's own page notes a single generation can cost over $10 in credits, while the free plan gives 100 credits once. The cheaper per-credit rate only kicks in on the higher annual tier, and premium AI media draws down a second 'Cloud' balance on top of your plan.
tools.best_for: non-technical founders who want an AI to build and host a simple site fast, and are comfortable with usage-based credit pricing
tools.skip_if: you want predictable flat pricing, or you'll iterate heavily — credits make redesigns expensive, and real use needs a paid plan quickly
compare_with: Hostinger's AI builder bundles hosting at a flat monthly price; Wegic is credit-metered and AI-native — faster to generate, but the meter runs on every regeneration

tools.name: WhatConverts
tools.what_it_does: Lead tracking and marketing attribution. Capture calls, forms and chats and tie every lead back to the campaign that drove it, for clear ROI.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-05 on whatconverts.com/pricing) Two ladders behind one toggle, and the page opens on the single-account one. Single account: Call Tracking $30 a month, Plus $60 (forms, chat, ecommerce), Pro $100 (HIPAA, call flows, report builder), Elite $160 (customer journey, multi-click attribution) — each including $30 of monthly usage credit. Agency, on the second tab, is three plans rather than one, all with unlimited accounts: Plus $500 a month with $250 of credit, Pro $800 with $300, Elite $1,250 with $400. Every tier carries a 14-day free trial. Past the included credit, the comparison table on the same page prints the usage rates: additional local numbers $2.50 each, local minutes 4.5 cents each, toll-free numbers $3.50 each, toll-free minutes 6.5 cents each, and white label $50 a month on every tier; call transcription is $0.02 and PCI redaction is priced separately. The billing FAQ adds that minutes are rounded up to the full minute and that a busy or no-answer call still counts once it connected to the tracking number.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is honest and the rate is invisible: every phone number, call minute, text, form, chat, appointment, email, event and transaction is charged against a monthly credit, and past that credit WhatConverts publishes no unit price anywhere on its site — the billing FAQ points to a Rates page inside the account, so a busy site cannot model its own bill before signing up. Its genuine strength versus bigger attribution suites is capturing EVERY lead type (not just calls) at a fair price; the flip side is you still need someone to read the reports and reallocate budget, or it's measurement theater.
tools.best_for: agencies and lead-gen businesses that want every lead — calls, forms, chats — attributed to its source and campaign without enterprise-suite prices
tools.skip_if: your leads flow through one channel (lighter tracking suffices), or nobody will act on the attribution data monthly
compare_with: the attribution peer group — CallRail is the call-first incumbent; WhatConverts wins on multi-lead-type breadth per dollar

tools.name: Wing Assistant
tools.what_it_does: Managed virtual assistants for founders and teams: delegate admin, inbox, scheduling and repetitive tasks to a dedicated, trained assistant.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Wing's own machine-readable pricing page) This is a managed assistant service, not software. General Virtual Assistant part-time is $699 a month and full-time $999 a month, which Wing presents as a 16% saving against the part-time rate pro-rated. Specialist roles are priced separately and enterprise is custom. The published package includes a dedicated assistant, a success manager and free replacement if the fit is wrong.
tools.honest_knock: You're renting a person, not automating a task — a good VA is real leverage, but only if you already have documented, delegatable work. Hand over chaos and you'll get chaos back, faster.
tools.best_for: founders drowning in delegatable admin who have processes to hand off and want a managed VA without recruiting one themselves
tools.skip_if: your workflows live only in your head — document or automate the repetitive work first, before paying a human to run undefined chaos
compare_with: other managed-VA services, or bringing someone in-house

tools.name: Wistia
tools.what_it_does: Video hosting built for marketing — player customisation, viewer analytics and lead capture.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0: 25 GB storage, 1 user, 200 GB bandwidth, and Wistia branding on the player. Business $79/month: 250 GB storage, 3 users, 1 TB bandwidth. Business + Lead Gen $329/month. Enterprise quote-only: 1 TB+ storage, 2 TB bandwidth. Extra users $25 each. Two overages sit in the FAQ rather than on the price card: webinar attendees beyond the allowance cost $0.20 each and extra webinar minutes $2.00 each. Some AI features (video dubbing, audio descriptions) are marked as costing extra without a price.
tools.honest_knock: Bandwidth is the meter that decides your bill, and it is the one number you cannot predict before you publish. A single video that does well can move you from Free to Business in a month, which is arguably the product working — but budget for it rather than being surprised. The free tier carries Wistia branding on the player, so it is a trial with no time limit rather than a plan you can ship a brand on. The webinar overages are the sharpest edge: $2.00 per extra minute means a session that runs long costs real money, and that rate is in the FAQ, not on the pricing page.
tools.best_for: marketing teams who want video on their own site with real analytics and lead capture, and who care that the player does not recommend a competitor's video afterwards
tools.skip_if: you just need somewhere to put videos — an unlisted upload to a free platform does that, and the reason to pay here is the analytics and the branding control, not the hosting
compare_with: the closest marketing-video peers — compare on bandwidth included and what the free tier puts on your player

tools.name: Wiz Checkout Upsell
tools.what_it_does: Shopify checkout and post-purchase app from Skai Lama: upsells, volume discounts, subscription upgrades and free gifts, plus checkout banners, trust badges, input fields and gift messages, with thank-you and order status page offers behind them. Essential is $49/month but post-purchase only; the checkout-stage editing the app is named for starts on the $99 Plus Growth plan, and $199 Checkout concierge adds A/B testing across all extensions.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-09-02 on apps.shopify.com/checkout-pro) Three tiers, billed in USD, each with a 14-day free trial and no free plan. Essential is $49 a month and covers post-purchase upsell funnels, thank-you page upsells and customization, order status page upsells and a review block, and all shipping and payment customizations; the listing marks that tier as not applicable for Shopify Plus. Plus Growth is $99 a month, or $999 a year (the listing says that saves 16%), and is the tier that opens the checkout itself: checkout upsells, subscription upgrades, checkout banners, reviews and trust badges, checkout input fields and gift messages, a checkout discount list and free gifts, on top of everything in Essential. Checkout concierge is $199 a month or $1,999 a year (save 16%) and adds custom onboarding and launch, A/B testing and analysis across all extensions, monthly performance review calls and custom extension development.
tools.honest_knock: The name says checkout, but the $49 Essential plan does not include checkout upsells. That tier is post-purchase, thank-you page and order status page only, and the listing explicitly marks it as not applicable for Shopify Plus. Everything the app is named after — checkout upsells, checkout banners and trust badges, input fields, gift messages, free gifts at checkout — starts on the $99 Plus Growth plan. There is no free plan either, only a 14-day trial, so the cheapest honest way to find out whether checkout upsells move your numbers is $99 a month. And A/B testing across all extensions, the feature you would want precisely to prove that $99 was worth it, sits one rung higher again at $199.
tools.best_for: shopify merchants who want checkout-stage upsells, banners, trust badges and gift messages alongside post-purchase and thank-you page offers from a single app, and whose order volume already makes $99 a month a rounding error
tools.skip_if: you were budgeting the $49 tier and expected checkout upsells with it — that plan is post-purchase only — or you want to test the idea at no cost first, because there is no free plan here
compare_with: Both are Shopify upsell apps, and AfterSell is the broader, longer-established name for post-purchase and thank-you page offers. Wiz splits its ladder differently: $49 buys the post-purchase half only, and the checkout-stage editing that gives the app its name starts at $99. So compare on the tier you would actually buy. If post-purchase offers are the goal, weigh AfterSell against the $49 plan; if you want to rewrite the checkout page itself, weigh it against $99 and price the difference.

tools.name: Woodpecker
tools.what_it_does: Cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform priced by contacted prospects — unlimited team seats and email accounts, built-in warm-ups, deliverability tooling and a lead finder.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-25 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Free trial. Usage-priced: $7.00 per 100 contacted prospects, and the smallest volume the slider offers is 500 — so $35 a month is the practical entry rather than the $7 headline; unlimited team members and connected email accounts included; 4 warm-ups free. Add-ons: LinkedIn account $29/mo each, managed sending addresses (Google/Microsoft) $6/mo each, extra warm-ups $5/mo per email account, Lead Finder credits from $10 per 500. The rate is real but the entry is not — the prospect slider starts at 500, so the smallest bill is 500 ÷ 100 × $7.00 = $35 a month (checked on their pricing page, 18 August 2026). Contact 200 prospects and you still pay $35; the per-100 figure only starts describing your bill once you are past the minimum.
tools.honest_knock: The $7-per-100-prospects unit reads cheap, but a real outbound motion stacks add-ons fast. Every connected LinkedIn account is $29 a month, managed sending addresses $6 a month apiece and extra warm-ups $5 per account — and contacted prospects are the meter, so scaling outreach scales the bill.
tools.best_for: outbound teams that want usage-priced cold email plus LinkedIn outreach, with unlimited seats and email accounts included instead of per-user fees
tools.skip_if: you send occasional one-off campaigns (usage pricing only wins when you actually use it), or your motion is LinkedIn-heavy — $29 per connected account adds up
compare_with: lemlist is the seat-priced all-rounder with the big template community; Woodpecker prices by contacted prospects with unlimited seats — leaner for small teams, add-ons stack at scale

tools.name: World Businesses for Sale
tools.what_it_does: International marketplace for buying and selling established businesses — restaurants, shops, services and manufacturers — free for buyers, with broker plans (listing fee plus 1-3% commission) or no-commission pay-as-you-go listings, and 24/7 guidance for sellers.
tools.pricing: (2026, re-verified 2026-08-03) Browsing is free for buyers. Sellers pick one of two tracks. Broker plans: Basic £395 (3% commission, 6-month contract), Standard £749 (2% commission, 9 months), Premium £1,500 (1% commission, 12-month contract, stays live until sold with free renewals) — every tier states commission is due only if they introduce the buyer. Or no-commission pay-as-you-go listings (inc. VAT): Basic £49, Standard £75 or Premium £99 for 30-day access. Take 10% off on a flex monthly subscription (£44.10 / £67.50 / £89.10) or 20% off on a 6-month plan (£235.20 / £360.00 / £475.20), and you keep 100% of the sale price. Free 24/7 chat guidance before you commit.
tools.honest_knock: On the broker plans you pay twice: a listing fee up front AND commission when it sells — 3% on Basic, 2% on Standard, 1% on Premium — on contracts of 6, 9 and 12 months. Only Premium stays live until sold with free renewals, so on the lower tiers a business that has not sold needs a paid renewal, and for a slow sale £1,500 once can beat £749 twice. Every tier says commission is payable only when they introduce the buyer, which is exactly the clause to read in the contract before you sign. If you want no commission at all, the pay-as-you-go plans start at £49 for 30 days — far cheaper up front, but those are listings, not broker introductions. As with any marketplace, the fee buys exposure, not a guaranteed sale.
tools.best_for: owners selling established, often brick-and-mortar businesses — restaurants, shops, services, small manufacturers — who want international buyer exposure with hands-on guidance
tools.skip_if: you're selling a small online asset (an auction-style online-business marketplace fits better), or you want a free listing — even the cheapest no-commission plan here costs £49 for 30 days
compare_with: Flippa is the online-business marketplace (sites, apps, e-commerce) with auction dynamics; World Businesses for Sale leans brick-and-mortar and international with flat listing plans — pick by what you're actually selling

tools.name: WP Rocket
tools.what_it_does: WordPress caching and performance plugin: page cache, lazy loading, file optimisation and CDN integration from one settings screen. Licensed annually from about $59 for one site to $299 for many, all tiers feature-identical. Stop paying and you keep your settings but lose updates and support.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-09-04, read on their own pricing page) These are annual licences, and the page prices in the visitor's currency. Read from Europe it sets EUR and shows Single €49.95/yr (1 website), Plus €99.95/yr (3 websites) and Multi €249.95/yr, and the 95 cents matter because an earlier reading rounded all three down to whole euros. Multi carries a site-count selector at 50, 100 or 500 websites, and anything above 500 is a custom licence. The dollar storefront reads $59, $119 and $299 a year for the same three tiers. Our own pricing screenshot on this page is that USD version, captured 12 August 2026, so the figures beside it are the euro ones from the same day. The two are not a contradiction but two storefronts of the same product. All tiers are feature-identical — you pay for the number of sites. There is no trial; the page offers a 14-day refund instead, and the licence auto-renews after a year, switchable off in your account's Billing section. What the page does not say anywhere is what it renews at.
tools.honest_knock: It's a subscription, not a lifetime license — you keep your settings if you stop paying but lose updates and support, and a technically-minded user can get most of the way there with a free caching plugin. Two things to check before you buy on price. The Multi licence is capped now: 50, 100 or 500 websites, with a custom licence above that, so there is no unlimited tier to grow into. And the renewal rate is not published — the page confirms the licence auto-renews after a year but never states at what price, which is exactly where the Trustpilot complaints cluster.
tools.best_for: WordPress owners who want near-instant page-speed gains out of the box without touching cache config
tools.skip_if: you're comfortable configuring a free caching plugin like LiteSpeed Cache or W3 Total Cache and enjoy the tinkering
compare_with: LiteSpeed Cache or W3 Total Cache

tools.name: Wrike
tools.what_it_does: Work management for mid-to-large teams running cross-functional projects: reporting, workflows, approvals and resource management. Free up to five users; Team about $10/user/month and Business $25 on annual billing, with a five-seat minimum on Business.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-05) A permanent free plan at $0 per user, with no user cap named on the plan card; Team $10 per user a month for 2 to 15 users; Business $25 per user a month for 5 to 200 users. Pinnacle and Apex publish no amount at all — both carry only a Contact us button and the line "Connect with us for pricing". Business and every tier above it is sold as an annual subscription only. Seats are bought in blocks: groups of five up to 30 seats, groups of 10 from 30 to 100, groups of 25 above 100. Self-service checkout covers Team and Business up to 15 users with no add-ons; beyond that the purchase goes through a Wrike representative. All prices are listed in US dollars and exclude local taxes.
tools.honest_knock: It's powerful and scales to complex, cross-team portfolios, but that power brings a learning curve and a per-seat cost that climbs — small teams often find it heavier than they need next to a simpler board tool.
tools.best_for: mid-to-large teams running complex, cross-functional projects that need robust reporting, workflows and resource management
tools.skip_if: you're a small team that just wants a simple kanban board — a lighter tool is faster to adopt and cheaper

tools.name: Xero
tools.what_it_does: Cloud accounting for small business: bank reconciliation, invoicing, bills and reporting.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-30, read on their own US pricing page) Every headline price is a promotion: 'Get 90% off your plan for your first 6 months when you buy by 30 September 2026'. Early is $2.50 a month for the first six months and then $25. Growing is $5.50 for six months and then $55. Established is $9 for six months and then $90. Multi-currency and project tracking are on Established only. Optional add-ons: Inventory Plus (no price shown) and Xero Payroll powered by Gusto at $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor. Prices shown are USD; Xero prices differently by country.
tools.honest_knock: Read the second number, not the first. Every plan on that page is 90% off for six months, and the price that governs the rest of your first year is ten times what the button says: $25, $55 and $90. That is not hidden — it is printed right there — but it is printed smaller, and the plan people pick on the strength of $2.50 a month is the one that becomes $25. The offer is dated too: it runs until 30 September 2026. The second thing to check before you commit is which country's page you are on, because Xero's tiers and prices differ by market and the US page is not the UK or AU one. And the entry tier is a genuine floor rather than a taster: if you need multi-currency or projects, that is Established at $90.
tools.best_for: small businesses whose bookkeeper or accountant already works in Xero — the ecosystem and the bank feeds are the real product, and the monthly price is small against what the reconciliation time costs
tools.skip_if: you invoice a handful of clients and reconcile by hand — the entry tier at $25 after the promo is buying automation you may not need yet, and simpler invoicing tools cost less
compare_with: the standing comparison in small-business accounting — compare the post-promotional price on all three, because all three lead with a discounted rate

tools.name: Zedonk
tools.what_it_does: Fashion-industry ERP for small and mid-size brands — modular sales, production, inventory and wholesale management with a B2B digital showroom, priced per module from £166/mo billed annually.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against zedonk.co.uk) (2026) Modular fashion-ERP, priced per building block and billed annually, all listed as 'prices starting from': PLM £166/mo, ERP Essential £166/mo, B2C (adds Shopify integration and barcodes) £250/mo, B2B (adds the digital wholesale showroom) £332/mo. No self-serve signup — every tier goes through a demo, and the real price depends on which modules you stack.
tools.honest_knock: The 'starting from' wording is doing real work: £166/mo is the floor of the cheapest module, billed annually, so a working setup for a brand that sells wholesale quickly stacks toward £332/mo and beyond — about £4,000 a year before add-ons. There is no trial and no public total: you find out your actual price in a demo call. Budget for the stack, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size fashion brands that need sales, production, inventory and wholesale in one system built around size curves, seasons and linesheets
tools.skip_if: you are not a fashion business — this is deliberately niche — or you want self-serve, monthly-cancellable software rather than an annual, demo-led ERP
compare_with: the closest fashion-ERP alternative with a US centre of gravity — both are modular; decide on which one matches your region's size curves, currencies and wholesale workflow, and verify both current price lists yourself.

tools.name: Zeffy
tools.what_it_does: Fundraising, ticketing and donation payments for nonprofits at genuinely $0 — no platform, transaction or card-processing fees. The model is an optional tip prompt shown to your donors at checkout, which they can set to zero. Weigh that against the 2–5% paid platforms take from every donation.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against the vendor's own pricing page) Genuinely $0 for nonprofits (2026): no platform, transaction or card-processing fees on donations, ticketing or payments. The model: donors see an optional (zero-able) tip prompt at checkout, and enough tip to fund the platform.
tools.honest_knock: The honest scrutiny of 'free': the tip prompt is shown to YOUR donors, with suggested percentages. Most give happily, but some organizations feel it inserts a step between donor and cause — and a donor who tips 10% effectively paid a fee, just voluntarily and not from your share. Compare that trade against the 2-5% the paid platforms take from every donation, and for most small nonprofits the math strongly favors Zeffy.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size nonprofits that want donations, ticketing, memberships and payments without any fee eating the mission's money
tools.skip_if: your organization objects to donor-facing tip prompts on principle, or you need enterprise CRM-grade donor management built in
compare_with: the close 'free/tip-funded' and low-fee peers — compare the donor checkout experience and what each layers on top of payments

tools.name: ZenBusiness
tools.what_it_does: US business-formation service — LLC, S corp and C corp filings at $0 plus the state's own fee, with the money in the recurring stack around it: registered agent $199/year, Worry-Free Compliance $199/year (Advanced $299/year), operating agreement $99, EIN $99. Add-ons are priced individually rather than bundled into tiers (site, verified 25 Jul 2026).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-27 on their own pricing page; unchanged since 25 Jul 2026) Formation itself is $0 plus the state's fee — that applies to LLC, S corp and C corp filings alike, and the state fee is separate, varies by state and is not shown until you pick one. Everything else is priced as its own line rather than bundled into plan tiers. The recurring items are registered agent at $199/year, Worry-Free Compliance Filing at $199/year, and Advanced Compliance Protection at $299/year. One-time filings: operating agreement $99, EIN $99, business document templates $99, rush filing $79 and DBA registration $95 plus state fees. Then business licence report $149, amendment $100, certificate of good standing $100, annual report filing $100 per report, and New York publication $200 for the state that requires it. There is a second catalogue alongside the legal one: business website $129/year, eCommerce website $279/year, business email address $25/year, domain $25/year, domain privacy $10/year, logo kit $60, business banking $5/month and Money Pro with online payments $30/month.
tools.honest_knock: The $0 is real for the filing service and it is also the whole commercial idea: what you sign up for at zero has an annual carry that is not shown next to it. A registered agent is a legal requirement in every state, and theirs is $199/year — so the realistic first-year cost of 'the $0 LLC' is the state fee plus $199, before compliance filing at another $199/year. Price the second year, not the first. The second thing to hold in view is that the state fee is the largest and most variable number in the whole exercise, and ZenBusiness cannot change it. It is set by your state, ranges widely, and their own page sends you to a lookup rather than quoting it. Anyone comparing formation services on the advertised price alone is comparing the small half of the bill.
tools.best_for: first-time founders who want the paperwork handled and are willing to pay a yearly fee to keep it handled — the a-la-carte pricing means you can start at the state fee plus a registered agent and add only what you actually need
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable filing with your state yourself and acting as your own registered agent. In that case the state fee is the only unavoidable cost, and the $199/year is buying convenience and a business address rather than anything you cannot do. Also skip it if you need legal advice rather than filing, since a formation service is not a law firm
compare_with: the standing comparison in this category — both sell formation plus a registered agent, and the decision turns on the recurring fee and what each includes at the entry price rather than on the headline. Check both current price lists yourself before choosing.

tools.name: Zendesk
tools.what_it_does: Customer service suite: ticketing, messaging, voice, help centre and AI agents.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page from two countries) Per agent per month on annual billing, US storefront: Support Team $19, Suite Team $55, Suite Professional $115. Suite Enterprise + Copilot is quote-only. The page geo-prices — read from Europe the same three tiers show €19, €55 and €115 — so check which storefront your quote came from. Annual billing carries a stated 20% discount and the monthly rate is never printed. Paid add-ons on top of the seat price: Copilot $50 per agent/month (€50), Workforce Engagement bundle $50 (€50), Contact Center $83 (€82). Copilot can be attached to Professional and higher only. AI agents are included in Suite and Support plans but metered by 'automated resolutions' beyond the plan allowance, and App Builder, Action Builder and Voice are billed on consumption above their own allowances.
tools.honest_knock: Three separate multipliers sit on top of the number you first see. The prices shown are annual-billed — the page states a 20% annual discount and never prints the monthly rate, so budgeting month-to-month means adding roughly a quarter yourself. Copilot, the AI the product is currently sold on, is a $50 per-agent add-on that their own page restricts to Professional and higher: the $19 and $55 tiers cannot have it at any price, and on the $115 Professional seat it is a 43% uplift. And the AI agents that are included are metered by automated resolutions: past the allowance you pay per resolution, so the bill moves with how well the AI works rather than with how many people you hire. App Builder, Action Builder and Voice are metered on consumption alongside it. Price the tier you need with the add-ons you actually want switched on, because the $19 entry and a working configuration are far apart.
tools.best_for: support teams past the point where a shared inbox works, who need routing, a help centre and reporting in one place and have the volume to justify per-agent pricing
tools.skip_if: you are a small team handling support out of email. The entry tier is email and ticketing only, the features people buy Zendesk for start at $55 a seat, and the Copilot AI is not available below $115. Also skip it if your case volume is low enough that per-resolution AI metering is more admin than benefit
compare_with: the usual head-to-heads — compare at the tier that includes the AI you actually want, since that is where the price gap opens

tools.name: Zendrop
tools.what_it_does: AI dropshipping and print-on-demand for Shopify: browse 1M+ products from US and global suppliers, link them to your store and let fulfilment and tracking run automatically, with custom branding, POD and 3PL as you scale. Free to install, but linking products needs a paid tier — $29, $49 or $79 a month by product count, with per-order product and shipping cost on top.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/zendrop) Free to install, with three paid tiers: Beginner $29, Pro $49 and Plus $79 a month. What separates them is not features but how many products you may link to your store. The free tier allows none at all, Beginner covers 1-20, Pro 21-100 and Plus 101 or more. The feature list on all three paid tiers is identical: trending products, Zendrop Academy, Zendrop AI access and custom branding. Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top of every plan, and the listing states that external charges may be billed by Zendrop separately from your Shopify invoice. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.5 from 1,191 App Store reviews. Developer Zendrop, based in Germany. One thing the listing does not show. When we captured the screenshot on 19 August 2026, zendrop.com itself was running a Summer Promo: 65% off the annual Plus plan for the first year, advertised as a $357 saving, plus $100 in order credits, ending 31 August 2026. That offer sits on Zendrop's own site rather than on the App Store listing, so which price you pay depends on where you sign up.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is a catalogue browser rather than a working tier: it allows no linked products, so nothing can actually be sold through it. Past that you are paying for an allowance, not for capability — Beginner, Pro and Plus carry exactly the same feature list, and the only thing $79 buys over $29 is room for more than a hundred linked products. The subscription is also the smaller half of the bill: product and shipping cost lands per order on top, and Zendrop bills that separately from your Shopify invoice, so the figure you budget is not the figure you pay. The 4.5 average covers a split verdict, with 83% five stars alongside 7% one star across 1,191 reviews.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants starting or scaling a dropshipping or print-on-demand store who want sourcing, automated fulfilment, tracking and custom branding in one app, and who can price the per-order product and shipping cost into their margins
tools.skip_if: you already have supplier relationships worth keeping, or you need the cheapest possible international shipping — the vetted US supplier network is the selling point here and you pay for it

tools.name: ZenZap
tools.what_it_does: Secure work-chat for teams — organized channels, built-in tasks and workflows, AI agents and admin controls, as easy to use as texting.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-09-01 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Free plan: unlimited group chats, unlimited built-in to-dos, WhatsApp chat migration, AI voice-note transcription and in-chat search, 1 GB storage — the page publishes no user cap for it and no promise of unlimited seats. Pro $3/user/mo billed yearly ($4 monthly); Business+ $8/user yearly ($10 monthly); Enterprise custom. Flat-rate team bundles price below per-seat: Pro is $51/mo yearly for up to 20 users and $112 for up to 50, Business+ $89 and $190, quoted in dollars and pounds. Yearly billing saves 33%. Integrations with business tools and API access start at Business+; audit logs, SSO and SAML/SCIM are Enterprise.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing genuinely undercuts Slack — the honest question is ecosystem: team chat lives or dies on integrations and habit, and ZenZap's app catalog is a fraction of Slack's, so teams glued to hundreds of integrations will feel the gap. For WhatsApp-refugee teams that mainly need organized channels, tasks and work/life separation, the free tier is a remarkably complete landing spot.
tools.best_for: small teams that run work over messy WhatsApp/personal chat today and want organized, professional chat with tasks — starting free
tools.skip_if: your workflows depend on a deep integration ecosystem (Slack's moat), or you're already paid into Microsoft Teams via 365
compare_with: the giants — richer ecosystems at higher per-seat costs; ZenZap wins on price and simplicity for chat-first small teams

tools.name: ZoomInfo
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise B2B sales intelligence and contact database. Find verified company and contact data, buying signals and org charts to fuel outbound at scale.
tools.pricing: Sales-gated, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17: no public rates, no monthly billing and no free plan, with the pricing URL refusing plain requests and neither of our monthly captures retrieving a figure. Contracts typically start around $15k and the median runs near $32k a year, climbing once seats, credits and add-ons (intent data, international coverage) stack up — but those are third-party figures, not ZoomInfo's, and every deal is negotiated annually. Expect a multi-year push and price the credits, not just the seats.
tools.honest_knock: The contract is the most-cited frustration: annual lock-in with a strict 60–90 day cancellation window and 10–20% renewal increases. Credits burn fast, data can be stale (prospects who left years ago), and it's built for enterprise — overkill and overpriced for SMBs, with weaker accuracy outside the US.
tools.best_for: enterprise go-to-market teams that need the deepest US database, buyer-intent signals and conversation intelligence — and can absorb the contract
tools.skip_if: you're an SMB or want flexible month-to-month pricing — the cost, credit burn and lock-in rarely pay off below enterprise scale
compare_with: the cheaper, more flexible data tools
